      "summary": "Tracks the two EI-1/P-020 sub-items that are deliberately NOT done in the blocked_by→coord_links cutover (EI-1 resolved, the binding D-027/D-028 part). D-013's ideal end-state is the reverse: `work_items` the canonical base, `harness_features_consolidated` + per-schema `harness_features` thin `kind='feature'` views (032 view-pattern). This is a bare-RENAME of a base table that the federation CDC (`capture_substrate_outbox`) + `emit_change_notify` + `fill_needs_design` + `fill_ws_features` triggers reference BY NAME — the DROP-CASCADE≠function-body hazard — so it needs a rolled-back-tx-tested, pipeline-drained, supervised pass. migration 142's header calls the rename \"cosmetic and HIGH-risk\". Only matters BEFORE non-feature rows are actually inserted — today there are none (gated; `item_kind` is 'feature' for every row). Pair with whoever lands the first non-feature `work_items:create` path.\n\nNeither blocks P-020's binding requirement (drop blocked_by → coord_links edge + frontier repoint), which is done + live + tested.       "title": "Directive-provenance graph: make \"does this owner-claim trace to an OWNER-stamped turn\" a mechanical path query",
      "summary": "Grounding: the WI-3532 telephone-game incident (agent-managed-compaction-2026-07-01) — self-imposed notes mutated into \"owner directives\" across compactions — plus the turn-provenance stamps (turn-provenance-owner-vs-agent-2026-07-11) which made turn ORIGIN verifiable but left directive LINEAGE manual (sessions:search by hand).\n\nProposal: model provenance as a small graph — nodes: turns (with provenance stamp), directives, carry surfaces (checkpoints, facts, summaries, loop carry-notes); edges: quoted-in, derived-from, restated-by. Then \"trace this claimed directive back to an OWNER (interactive) turn\" is a single path query, and \"directives whose only ancestry is agent-origin turns\" is a standing lint that catches manufactured owner-directives BEFORE they get re-summarized another hop. The age A/B benchmark showed exactly this query shape (explicit relational traversal) is where the graph wins and traversal is cheap (expandMs p50 88ms); there is no ranking lane involved, so the recall-fusion reject (fact age-ab-benchmark-verdict) does not apply.     {
      "id": "EI-10719",
      "title": "The green gate judges ATOMICALLY-INCOHERENT mid-refactor snapshots — 4 consecutive red candidates were all \"green before, green after, red only at the frozen commit\". This, not flaky tests, is what pinned main 151 commits behind.",
      "summary": "## The pattern (4 consecutive reds, 2026-07-12/13, all diagnosed the same way)\n\nEvery red candidate I triaged **passed at tip**, and in each case the failing tests were red *only at the frozen commit*:\n\n| candidate | failing tests | why it was red AT THAT COMMIT |\n|---|---|---|\n| b44fd094 | `composed-app-shadowing` \"(0 test)\" | `ReferenceError: SSH_WIN is not defined` — a shell script embedded in a JS template literal, mid-edit. Fixed at tip by c3c6a337. |\n| b55d158b | `owner-color`, `AdvGitGraphPanel` | assertion compared two DIFFERENT identities. Fixed at tip by 4e3d55d3. |\n| 403187bf | `prompt-file-scan` (3), `conflict-check` (1) | a name-scrub `Avi`→`Dev` was **half-applied**: the *expectations* said `'Dev'`, the *fixtures* still said `'Avi'`. Green before the scrub, green after it; red only in between. |\n\n## Root cause — candidate SELECTION, not test quality\n\nThe gate freezes one commit and takes ~50 min to judge it. A single logical refactor (a multi-file rename/scrub) does **not** land as one commit — git-sync auto-commits every few minutes, so one refactor spans SEVERAL commits, and the **intermediate commits are atomically incoherent by construction** (expectations updated, fixtures not yet). With a fast-churning fleet, the gate has a high probability of freezing exactly such a commit.\n\nThe 240s quiet-cut exists to avoid this but is **far too short**: it only skips commits <240s old. It does nothing about a refactor whose incoherent middle sat in the tree for 10 minutes.\n\nSo the gate reliably judges snapshots that are red while both the \"before\" and \"after\" states are green. Each red costs ~50 min and by verdict time the tree has moved on — the treadmill that pinned main **151 commits behind**.\n\n## Evidence it is not a test-quality problem\n\n- The `partial-green-gate` already computes the \"longest clean prefix\" — and on the 403187bf run it FF'd main from `28a3a3d5` → `6d9aff37`, dropping staging-ahead from **151 → 6** in one step. The tree was *fine*; only the chosen candidates were not.\n- All four candidates' failures were pre-existing-and-already-fixed, or mid-refactor. None was a genuine regression that the gate saved us from.\n\n## Proposed fixes (for the pipeline-health lane, WI-4455)\n\n1. **Prefer the longest-clean-prefix path FIRST, not as a red-fallback.** It demonstrably works and it is what actually unstuck main. Judging the newest ≥N-min-stable commit and FF'ing to the newest green prefix beats freezing an arbitrary tip.\n2. **Measure \"reds that pass at tip\" as its own gate-health signal.** It cleanly separates a genuinely broken tree from a gate chasing its own tail. If that ratio is high, the gate — not the code — is the thing to fix. (Nothing measures this today, which is exactly why the treadmill ran for days without being named.)\n3. **Coherence heuristic for candidate selection**: skip a commit whose diff touches a test's *expectations* without its *fixtures* (or more cheaply: require a commit be ≥N minutes old AND have no sibling commits from the same author/refactor within a window).\n\n## Related\n- EI-10688 (su-5d6764f9): local-kokoro TTS made 3 unit tests read the REAL `$HOME` — a genuinely env-dependent red, held the gate ~9h. That one IS a test-quality bug; it is the *other* failure mode and worth keeping distinct from this one.\n- EI-10680: `release:checkpoint-run { replaceStale }` flakiness — it only sees one of the two locks (its own pre-check vs green-checkpoint.ts's internal lock), so it reports `launched:true` and then the process self-skips \"skipped-locked\".",
      "kind": "bug",

      "id": "EI-10874",
      "title": "Type errors surface in a STRANGER'S gate: operator-core has no typecheck test, so its errors red operator-vite's ratchet and land on whoever next needs a deploy",
      "summary": "THE DEFECT (lived through it, su-02434335, 2026-07-13): `apps/operator-vite` owns a typecheck ratchet (EI-10611) that counts FOREIGN type errors — errors in packages it imports but does not own (operator-core, apps/operator, libs/*) — and fails when the count exceeds a watermark (170). But those packages have NO typecheck test of their own, and `vite build` does not typecheck. So:\n\n1. A peer lands a type error in packages/operator-core. Their OWN affected-tests pass. They believe they are done. Nothing reds in their lane.\n2. The error is invisible until some UNRELATED agent runs operator-vite's suite — typically because they need the green gate for a DEPLOY.\n3. That agent now has to fix a stranger's type error, in a stranger's file, to ship their own unrelated work.\n\nThe error surfaces arbitrarily far from its cause, in someone else's lane. That is a broken accountability loop, and at fleet scale it is a lottery.\n\nWORSE — THE COUNT IS A MOVING TARGET. I measured the foreign count three times in ~15 minutes on the same tree: 172 → 174 → 168. Peers were landing and fixing type errors under me the whole time. When I opened scheduler.ts to fix its 2 errors, the peer had ALREADY fixed them in the ~5 min since my scan. An agent cannot green a gate that measures a GLOBAL count of code it doesn't own, churned by N concurrent editors. I nearly burned a long stretch fixing errors that were evaporating on their own.\n\nIt also creates a perverse incentive the ratchet's own comment warns about (\"Do NOT raise the watermark to go green\") — but says nothing about the opposite trap: I was ALSO invited to LOWER the watermark when I measured 168 (the test literally tells you to). I declined: tightening a shared gate to an instantaneous minimum, in a tree where four agents land half-finished type changes, would red the gate for the next person on a transient. A ratchet on a volatile global count is not a ratchet — it is a tripwire on other people's work-in-progress.\n\nFIX (either half helps; both together fix it properly):\n1. GIVE EACH PACKAGE ITS OWN TYPECHECK TEST — `packages/operator-core`, `apps/operator`, libs/* — so a type error reds the AFFECTED-SET OF THE PERSON WHO INTRODUCED IT, immediately, in their own lane. This is the real fix: accountability at the point of cause. (test:affected already picks the right packages; it just has nothing to run.)\n2. MAKE THE RATCHET ATTRIBUTE, NOT COUNT. Instead of a global count vs a watermark, compare against the merge-base / last-green baseline and fail only on errors NEW relative to it — reporting `file:line` of the new ones. Then the gate names the culprit change rather than handing an arbitrary agent a 170-error inheritance and a number that moves under them.\n\nUntil (1) exists, every deploy-needing agent pays a tax proportional to how many peers are mid-edit.",

      "id": "EI-10907",
      "title": "A hooks migration silently DROPPED two declared hooks and nothing alarmed — no liveness assertion on hook last-fire",
      "summary": "## What happened\n\nThe 2026-07-12 managed-hooks migration (settings.json rewrite) silently dropped TWO declared hooks:\n\n- `SessionStart` → `~/.claude/scripts/memory-compact.mjs` (regenerated `MEMORY.md`)\n- `PreToolUse` → `~/.claude/scripts/memory-boundary-check.mjs` (memory-write nudge)\n\nNothing alarmed. Nothing noticed. The `memory-compact` generator simply stopped running.\n\n## Why it was harmful (a SILENT WRONG ANSWER, not a loud failure)\n\n`MEMORY.md` is auto-loaded into every bare Claude session and self-describes as\n\"AUTO-GENERATED ... regenerated at each session start\". Once the hook died, the file\nfroze as a **stale snapshot that kept presenting itself as current** — the worst failure\nshape: it didn't error, it didn't go blank, it kept confidently serving old content.\nIt went undetected for weeks and was only found incidentally while retiring the layer\n(P-008/P-009), i.e. by an agent who happened to be reading that exact machinery.\n\nDiscovery was luck. Had the hook been a load-bearing one we still depended on, the\nsame silence would have applied.\n\n## The real defect is the MISSING DETECTOR, not the dropped hook\n\nThe cleanup (retiring the scripts, stubbing MEMORY.md) is a MITIGATION — it removes\nthis one instance. The CLASS remains: **a declared hook can stop firing and no guard\nnotices.** Ask the mitigation-vs-fix question: what SHOULD have caught this?\n\n## Proposed durable fix\n\nA **liveness assertion per declared hook**: record each hook's last-fire timestamp, and\nalarm when a hook declared in `settings.json` has not fired within a window appropriate\nto its trigger (a `SessionStart` hook that hasn't fired in N sessions is dead by\ndefinition — sessions demonstrably started).\n\nThat is a cheap, general detector: it catches ANY future silently-dropped or\nsilently-erroring hook, not just this one. Cross-check the current `settings.json`\nagainst a hooks manifest and diff declared-vs-fired.\n\n## Recurrence guard\n\nA test asserting that every hook declared in settings.json has a recent last-fire\nrecord (or is explicitly marked intentionally-inert), so a migration that drops one\nreds instead of going quiet.",

    {
      "id": "EI-11072",
      "title": "Editor-facing PostToolUse nudge: inject a live \"you just took <tool> over the prompt-weight budget\" warning into the editing agent's own session",
      "summary": "## The remaining gap after EI-10966 increment 1\n\nEI-10966 moved the P-011 prompt-weight ratchet off the fleet-blocking green gate to (1) a registration-time self-check in the live operator and (2) a fold into the mandated `tools-md-sync` quick-check. Both are PASSIVE toward the agent who made the offending edit: the operator self-check `console.warn`s in the OPERATOR's log (an autonomous editing agent never sees it); the quick-check only fires if the agent runs it.\n\n**Wild-proven 2026-07-13:** an autonomous agent edited `work_items:complete` to 1607 chars (>1600 hard cap) and it landed COMMITTED — caught only when a human ran `tools-md-sync`. Increment 1's operator-log warning fired but reached no one who could act.\n\n**The feature:** a PostToolUse hook that, when an Edit/Write/MultiEdit touches a tool-definition file under `*/agent-tools/**` AND a weight-bearing field (`description`/`guidance`/`when`/`notWhen`/`chaining`), tells the EDITING agent — in their own context, at edit time — that they just took `<tool>` over budget and by how much. Closes the last uncaught path.\n\n---\n## REVISION v2 — addresses owner grade 3/5 (2026-07-14)\n\nThe owner accepted the problem framing + layered source-of-truth analysis but required a narrower, measured solution with no per-edit MCP round trip, dark-flags reconciliation, and CLI parity. Revised design:\n\n**1. Weight source — REUSE the self-check result, no per-edit MCP call.** The original leaned on the hook calling `agent_tools:list` per edit (an MCP round trip; the fact `tool-weight-static-guard-disqualified-2026-07-13` proved a *static* parse under-counts because it misses runtime-COMPOSED guidance like fleet:status's +368-char ROUTING_LADDER). Resolution: the operator ALREADY computes composed per-tool weight in increment 1's registration self-check (`tool-guidance-budget.ts`). Persist that result — on every tools (re)load the operator writes a tiny `~/.papercusp/tool-weights.json` map `{ toolName → { weight, overBy } }` (the ONLY moment composed weight can change). The PostToolUse hook does a LOCAL FILE READ keyed by the edited tool — no MCP call, no recompute, sub-millisecond. This is the \"reuse the existing self-check result\" the grade asked for, and it eliminates the latency question entirely (a stat+read, not a network hop). If the cache is missing/stale (operator not yet reloaded post-edit), the hook fails open silent.\n\n**2. Measured overhead + one canonical seam.** One seam: a single shared `cc/` PostToolUse hook script (same contract as `workitem-verify-nudge.sh`, already Claude+Codex-shared). Hot path = a JSON file read + one key lookup. Target/gate: **<20ms added edit-turn latency** (asserted in test; the >300ms concern is moot without the MCP hop). No new endpoint, no `agent_tools:list` extension on the hot path.\n\n**3. Rollout — ship ON by default, fail-open (drop the dark flag).** The owner is right that DEFAULT-OFF conflicts with the dark-flags policy. This nudge is READ-ONLY, non-blocking, advisory `additionalContext`, detached/fail-open — it cannot break a fleet edit, so it is NOT a dangerous fleet-behavior flag. Ship it **ON by default**; provide only a simple `PAPERCUSP_TOOL_WEIGHT_NUDGE=0` env kill-switch (fail-open if unset). No registered dark flag.\n\n**4. Injection mechanism.** Unlike `workitem-verify-nudge.sh` (stderr+activity-note, not model-fed on exit 0), this must reach the MODEL: emit Claude Code `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (non-blocking). That is the one behavioral difference and why it's its own reviewed unit.\n\n**5. Claude/Codex parity + tests (required by the grade).**\n- Parity: the hook reads the same `tool-weights.json` and emits `additionalContext` under both CLIs' PostToolUse contract; a parity test asserts identical nudge text for the same edit under each harness's hook payload shape.\n- **Reintroduced-overweight regression test:** in a scratch psu session, re-apply an over-cap edit (e.g. push a tool's composed guidance >1600) and assert the hook injects a nudge naming the tool, its weight, and the exact chars to cut; assert NO nudge fires on an in-budget guidance edit (noise control) and on a non-guidance field edit (scope).\n- De-dupe: per-tool `.done`-style marker within a session so one over-budget tool nudges once.\n\n**Noise control:** fire ONLY on an over-budget result for a weight-bearing-field edit under `*/agent-tools/**`.\n\n**Coverage caveat (honest, unchanged):** reaches agents editing via a psu Claude/Codex Edit/Write; edits via meta:define-tool or the operator process stay covered by increment 1's operator self-check. Layered, common-case coverage.\n\n**cheapExperiment:** prototype the operator's `tool-weights.json` writer + the local-read hook behind the env kill-switch; edit a tool over cap in a scratch session; confirm the nudge injects with named tool + char delta from the CACHE (no MCP call) and measure added edit-turn latency <20ms. Falsifiable: the cached composed weight disagrees with `tools-md-sync` budgetViolations for the edited tool, OR `additionalContext` does not reach the model on exit 0, OR local-read overhead >20ms.\n\n## Why not built inline with EI-10966\nA context-injecting PostToolUse hook is a fleet-wide behavior on shared multi-CLI infra; the analogous `workitem-verify-nudge.sh` was its own plan item (P-019). EI-10966 core (increments 1+2) is shipped and wild-proven, so this is a discrete, reviewed enhancement.",

      "id": "EI-11109",
      "title": "Cup execution sandbox blocks the `listen` syscall — `npx tsx scripts/*.ts` (the repo's standard TS script runner) dies with EPERM",
      "summary": "While completing WI-4563 I needed to run `scripts/gen-doc-insights-index.ts` (an advisory doc-index regen). Every `npx tsx <script>.ts` invocation in this cup's server-side bash sandbox fails at startup:\n\n```\nEPERM ... syscall: 'listen', address: '/tmp/claude/tsx-1000/16.pipe'\n```\n\ntsx creates a Unix-domain socket (a named pipe) for its ESM-loader IPC, and the sandbox denies the `listen` syscall regardless of TMPDIR (also tried a repo-local writable TMPDIR — same EPERM on the new path). Fallback `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/foo.ts` fails differently (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on extensionless relative TS imports like `./lib/doc-projection`, which only tsx's resolver handles).\n\nImpact: any cup task that must run a `tsx`-based script (doc-index gen, one-off migration helpers, gen:* scripts, deploy-cli via tsx) cannot, in this environment. Repeatable for every cup. Suspected root cause: the seccomp/namespace profile for the cup bash sandbox denies `listen`. Fix candidates: allow `listen` on AF_UNIX in the cup sandbox profile, or provide a tsx-compatible runner. Filed unconfirmed as to the exact sandbox layer.",

      "id": "EI-11110",
      "title": "Overwatch brief's crossMonitor.queenAlive / Queen \"cadence ok\" reads live-and-healthy while mug/queen role is actually dead — a false all-clear",
      "summary": "This wake's OverwatchBrief (2026-07-13T08:48Z) reported:\n- crossMonitor: \"queen alive · overwatch alive\"\n- Queen panel: \"last woke 2026-07-13T08:28:02.818Z · cadence ok · driving 3 placement(s) · next 2026-07-13T09:01:22.842Z\"\n\nBut a direct `coord:presence { owner: 'mug' }` and `coord:presence { owner: 'queen' }` call in the SAME turn both returned `active: []`, `summary.active: 0`, `summary.wakeable: 0` — i.e. there is NO live mug/queen session at all. This is the 4th consecutive wake this has been confirmed false (see the context-overflow-deaths-p019 escalation thread — mug/kettle/su sessions are repeatedly dying on \"Prompt is too long\" this window, most recently at 08:35Z and twice at 08:39Z).\n\nLikely mechanism: the brief's queenAlive/cadence fields appear to be computed from a stored lastWokeAt/next-scheduled-wake timestamp heuristic rather than an actual live-presence check, so a session that died mid-window (context overflow) still reads as \"alive · cadence ok\" until the next scheduled wake time passes. This is exactly the false-all-clear the D-004 cross-monitor exists to prevent — a kettle trusting this field would skip escalating a genuinely dead Queen.\n\nCorroborating evidence: green-checkpoint's most recent red (msg mrizazut, 08:47Z) shows FAILING tests in lib/overwatch/brief-types.test.ts, lib/overwatch/compute-brief.test.ts, and lib/overwatch/watchdog.test.ts — including \"detectAnomalies — aging escalations → escalation-aging ESCALATE owner\" — suggesting the overwatch/compute-brief module (the exact code that renders this panel) currently has known-red test coverage. This may be the same root cause.\n\nSuggested fix: crossMonitor.queenAlive (and the Queen panel's \"cadence ok\") should be computed from an actual live-presence check (coord:presence / fleet:assignments verdict) at brief-build time, not solely from a stored next-wake timestamp — or at minimum cross-check the two and flag a mismatch.",

    {
      "id": "EI-11171",
      "title": "Routine engine intermittently STARVED — dead-routine \"overdue >10m\" alerts flap (fire+recover) repeatedly, correlated with PG pool-starvation routines-tick sheds",
      "summary": "CORRECTED MODEL (su-eb9b7 investigation 2026-07-13, supersedes the original hypothesis below).\n\n**ROOT MECHANISM (not DB saturation — that was wrong):** the bg-host routines-tick sheds because a trivial `acquire+SELECT 1` on the org-admin pool takes **2000-3500ms steady-state** (pool-pressure.ts CRITICAL_PROBE_MS default 2000 ⇒ 'critical' ⇒ shed). But the PG SERVER is IDLE at those moments — snapshot: **2 active queries, 219/512 connections**. A SELECT 1 is never DB-bound; the 2-3s is entirely **client-side pool-ACQUIRE latency** inside the bg-host process (its org pool is contended by its own ~15 serial sweeps + DBOS steps; postgres-js prepared-statement caching is off so a fresh connection costs ~1s+). So this is bg-host-SELF-INFLICTED pool contention, NOT external DB load. EI-11171's original \"PG pool saturated / DB pressure\" framing is REFUTED by the idle-server snapshot.\n\n**MEASURED:** 263 routines-tick sheds in 6h (~44/hr, EVERY hour 00:00-05:00, hourly counts 22/35/70/68/23/46 — steady-state, not a boot transient). Probe latencies cluster 2.0-3.5s (one 6.37s outlier).\n\n**RED HERRING removed:** the original body cited `hive_watchdog_fires source='tick'` \"10x/3h\" as evidence. Those rows actually read *\"started pot quiet with demand queued (N todo) and no wake armed\"* — the **Mug autoloop backpressure** watchdog, a DIFFERENT subsystem. Unrelated to routine-engine starvation. The real shed signal is the bg-host LOG line `[routines-tick] SKIPPED — PG pool starvation`, not a watchdog_fires row. The infra-liveness \"dead routine overdue >10m\" alerts come from system-watchdog (a third path), absent from hive_watchdog_fires entirely.\n\n**HARM (honestly sized — non-critical, self-recovering):** git-sync is NOT acutely starved — 62 commits in 3h, gaps 82-337s. It survives on the ~76 non-shed ticks/hr. The ACUTE symptom is lower-priority scheduled routines (armed su-loop wakes) slipping past the 10-min dead-routine threshold when several ticks shed in a row ⇒ the infra-liveness flap (fire+RECOVER). Noise + delayed autonomy, not a hard failure.\n\n**CODE DEFECT confirmed (EI-11171 open-Q#4 answered = NO floor):** routines-workflow.ts routinesTickImpl — the pool-critical shed at ~L318-325 does a bare `return` BEFORE the due-routine fire loop (~L359). git-sync is fired INSIDE that loop into the protected ROUTINES_CRITICAL_QUEUE. So the shed skips git-sync's enqueue — directly contradicting its own comment (\"freezing git-sync (enqueued at the tick top)\" — git-sync is NOT enqueued at the tick top) AND defeating the entire reason the dedicated routines-critical lane exists (built after the 2026-06-23 7h git-sync-starvation freeze so git-sync can NEVER be starved). Today git-sync survives only because sheds aren't yet consecutive-enough; under worse contention this re-creates that incident class.\n\n**RANKED FIXES:**\n(A) CRITICAL-ROUTINE FLOOR [low-risk, testable, being implemented now]: under pool==='critical', fire ONLY critical-queue routines (git-sync) then return before the heavy sweeps — instead of firing nothing. Strictly additive: everything else (non-critical fires, loop-rebase, heavy sweeps) stays shed exactly as today, so zero regression to the shed's protective behavior; it only guarantees git-sync survives. Cost: ~3-4 bounded queries under a rare true-starvation. Closes open-Q#4.\n(B) THRESHOLD CALIBRATION [box-specific, needs care — NOT done unilaterally]: 2-3s acquire while the DB is idle is normal CONTENTION on this ~20-process multi-tenant box, not STARVATION. CRITICAL_PROBE_MS=2000 conflates them ⇒ over-shed ~44/hr. Env-tunable via PAPERCUSP_POOL_CRITICAL_MS. But raising it reduces protection vs the true Jul 1-2 freeze — needs the probe-latency DISTRIBUTION during a real starvation vs normal to pick a separating threshold (EI-11171 evidence #1). Owner/P-006-W4-design call.\n(C) ROOT — reduce acquire latency [larger]: give the tick a reserved connection, or raise the bg-host org pool max, so the probe never queues behind the sweeps. Touches pool-sizing (P4-3 regression history) — careful.",

      "id": "EI-11292",
      "title": "Bridge ToolSearch (Claude-mangled deferred ids) → tools:find (full colon-form catalog) so a documented tool resolves in ONE call",
      "summary": "FRICTION (owner-raised, 2026-07-13): finding scheduler:set_claim_spec took 3 calls — ToolSearch { select:mcp__papercusp-su__scheduler_set_claim_spec } → \"No matching deferred tools\", keyword ToolSearch → miss, then tools:find (colon-form lexical) → hit. This is the documented su-persona gotcha (ToolSearch resolves only client-MANGLED ids of the deferred-loaded subset; tools:find searches the full ~550-tool catalog by real colon-form name). Two discovery systems that don't talk.\n\nFIXES (any one removes the multi-call dance):\n1. BRIDGE: when ToolSearch select:/keyword MISSES, auto-consult tools:find and return its top hit(s) with schemas — one call, always resolves a real tool. (Highest leverage.)\n2. PRE-LOAD role-relevant tools into the deferred set at launch: a FLEET-LEADER session will always need scheduler:set_claim_spec / get_claim_spec / fleet:* / work_items:release — register those so select: finds them immediately. Generalize: seed the deferred set from the session's role.\n3. Register colon-form ALIASES in the deferred index so select:scheduler:set_claim_spec (the name as written in every doc/persona) resolves directly, instead of only the mangled mcp__papercusp-su__scheduler_set_claim_spec.\n\nFiled at owner request while re-steering a fleet. Related: the persona already documents the workaround (tools:find / tools:invoke) — this is about removing the need for it.",

    {
      "id": "EI-11299",
      "title": "ideate \"overdue\" verdict is polluted by zero-yield idle-watch observations — gate it on actual ground-into-idea yield, not raw observation count",
      "summary": "## The defect (quantified, first-hand this session)\n`blender:ideation-feedback { scope:'mine' }` this wake returned `observationsImpact: { filings:92, surfacedAsPattern:0, ideasGrounded:0, shipped:0 }`. The filings list is dominated by a monitor/idle-watch session's OWN turn-end reflections (e.g. EI-11288/11267/11249/11237/11235 — all literally \"steady idle-watch, settle not manufacture\" checkpoint insights). None ever became a pattern or an idea.\n\nYet those same observations increment the `ideate` counter that flips `coord:orient.ideate.verdict` to **\"overdue\"** at the raw threshold (11 ≥ 10). So a session parked on a settled 900s monitor loop gets nagged \"run an ideate pass\" purely from the noise it emits by existing — pressure that points straight at MANUFACTURING (file something to reset the counter). Meanwhile the productive lane is unaffected: routed *ideas* (kind:feature) win at 84/137 for this same scope. The signal that fires is the one with ~0% yield; the one with real yield doesn't drive the nag.\n\n## Why it matters (recurring, fleet-wide)\nEvery su on an IDEATE + monitor idle-watch (a common autonomous posture) hits this: turn-end reflections auto-accumulate → false \"overdue\" → either wasted manufactured passes or repeated grounding round-trips to re-confirm \"well is dry.\" Small trigger change, big recurring token/attention cost across every idle su.\n\n## Proposed fix (cost-leverage)\nMake the \"overdue\" escalation YIELD-AWARE instead of count-only. Options (cheapest first):\n1. Exclude lane:observation reflections emitted on a settled monitor/`continuation:settle` turn from the overdue counter (they are proven ~0-yield); OR\n2. Gate escalation on a nonzero recent `ideasGrounded` rate — if the last N observations grounded into 0 ideas, RAISING the threshold (or muting the nag) is correct, not lowering it; OR\n3. Decay the observation counter for sessions whose loop mode is monitor/idle.\n\nAny of these removes the false nag without hiding real ideation debt for work-mode/interactive sessions.\n\n## Non-colliding\nNiche ideate-signal-quality area; adjacent to but distinct from EI-8299 (separate watchdog/telemetry work-items from the drain queue — that's the work-item queue, not the ideate/observation counter). Not the memory lane (su-02434335) nor agent-operability-liveness (su-0efdd444).",

      "id": "EI-11531",
      "title": "Desktop \"Paired devices\" list doesn't auto-refresh when a phone completes pairing (must reload /settings/mobile)",
      "summary": "Found while E2E-testing pairing by driving the Tauri app (owner request 2026-07-13).\n\nFLOW WORKS end-to-end: settings/mobile \"Show QR code\" → mints token + renders QR/manual payload; phone redeems POST /api/device/pair → device JWT; device JWT authorizes /api/device/attention + heartbeat; one-time token enforced (re-redeem 401); the new device DOES appear in the desktop \"Paired devices\" list.\n\nGAP: the desktop list only calls refreshDevices() on mount + after a revoke. When a phone redeems the QR, the desktop has no signal (no poll, no SSE) that pairing completed, so the freshly-paired device does NOT appear until the user navigates away and back / reloads /settings/mobile. A user who mints a QR, scans it on their phone, and keeps watching the desktop sees \"no change\" and may think it failed.\n\nFIX (small, monitoring-only, respects desktop=work/phone=monitor): while a QR is displayed (qr != null), poll GET /api/device/desktop/devices every ~2-3s (or subscribe via the sync layer) so the new device row + a \"✓ Paired!\" affordance appears live, and optionally auto-dismiss the QR on detected pairing. File: apps/operator/app/settings/mobile/page.tsx (mint()/refreshDevices()).\n\nNot a functional bug — pairing works; this is a live-feedback UX gap.",

      "id": "EI-11577",
      "title": "Wire Scout pre-flight budget feasibility (roster-shrink from tick cost-history) before the concurrent ideate fan-out",
      "summary": "Follow-up carved out of EI-10779 (sunk-cost destruction), whose PRIMARY harm — over-budget generation being discarded before the ~$0 route stage — is now FIXED and tested (cycle.ts routes paid-for survivors + flags `overBudget`; regression tests cycle.test.ts:252, cycle-failure-modes.test.ts:465).\n\nRESIDUAL (EI-10779 flaws #1 + #3, which collapse into one lever):\n- The ideate fan-out is FULLY CONCURRENT (`Promise.all` at ideators.ts:342) — all N ideator LLM calls fire at once. So a \"mid-stage check between ideators\" (EI-10779 flaw #1 / sketch (c)) is impossible: nothing to stop mid-flight. The only way to bound ideate-stage cost is to size the roster DOWN before the fan-out.\n- That is EI-10779 flaw #3 (pre-flight feasibility, sketch (b)): estimate per-call cost from recent tick history (`scout_ticks.budget_used_usd` / ideator count) and shrink `maxIdeators` (or abort) so the projected concurrent cost fits `maxCostUsd` BEFORE the first LLM call.\n\nPrimitives ALREADY EXIST but are dead code (zero non-test callers): `budget.ts` `projectedCycleCostUsd()`, `fitsCycleBudget()`, `boundIdeatorCount()`. The wiring is what's missing.\n\nWhere it belongs: the scheduler/runner (run.ts / scheduler.ts / scout-cycle-action.ts), NOT cycle.ts — cycle.ts is pure orchestration over injected ports with no DB/cost-history access. The caller must (a) read a recent per-call cost estimate from scout_ticks, (b) call boundIdeatorCount/fitsCycleBudget to shrink the roster (never below 1 for a positive cap, to avoid recreating the spend-nothing bug), (c) pass the reduced maxIdeators into limits. Needs live spend verification to trust the estimate — larger than an inline auto-fix lane, hence deferred here rather than done inside EI-10779.",

      "summary": "Found while fixing the owner's mobile \"voice service error\" (plan mobile-logo-voice-android-2026-07-13).\n\nPROBLEM: GET /api/device/voice-session-init (packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/voice.ts:136) hard-requires prefs.fullAgentEngine === 'elevenlabs-conv'|'elevenlabs-conversational', else returns 404 voice_not_enabled → the mobile app shows the generic \"Voice service error — tap to retry\". But fullAgentEngine is a SHARED master switch that ALSO drives the DESKTOP's voice engine (voice-mode.ts, voice-narration.ts). A user who wants voice on their phone shouldn't be forced to change their desktop voice behavior.\n\nREPRO: operator with elevenLabsAgentId + EL API key set but fullAgentEngine='off' → phone LISTEN → \"Voice service error\". Enabling requires the global flip.\n\nFIX OPTIONS: (a) give mobile voice its own enable gate (e.g. a `mobileVoiceEnabled` pref, or treat \"agentId + EL key present\" as sufficient for the DEVICE endpoint regardless of the desktop's fullAgentEngine); (b) mint the EL token for /device/voice-session-init whenever agentId+key exist, decoupled from the desktop engine selection.     {
      "id": "EI-11662",
      "title": "Mode-aware MCP tool-restore: keep the blender ideate-loop family (ideation-feedback, ideate-pass-record, route-idea, grade-idea) loadable for an IDEATE-mode session after a reconnect/relaunch",
      "summary": "## Friction, hit live 2026-07-14 (first-hand)\n\nAfter an MCP-server reconnect mid-session, only a ~45-tool papercusp subset reloaded as deferred tools. The **blender ideate-loop family did NOT** — `ToolSearch select:blender_ideation-feedback,blender_ideate-pass-record,blender_route-idea,blender_grade-idea` returned \"No matching deferred tools found\" (twice, ~1h apart).\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe IDEATE-mode binding contract mandates closing each pass as a LOOP: GROUND on `blender:ideation-feedback` → file lens-tagged → CLOSE with `blender:ideate-pass-record`. When the reconnect subset drops that family:\n- an IDEATE-mode session that goes **`verdict:\"overdue\"`** (mine did — 13 obs ≥ threshold 10) **cannot ground a pass and cannot record one to reset the counter** → the overdue signal can never be discharged; it re-fires every orient;\n- grade-revision grounding (`blender:ideation-feedback { scope:'mine' }`) is unavailable, so an originator revising a graded idea works blind (I revised EI-11072 3/5→5/5 this session via work_items+coord only, without the intended grounding read).\n\nNet: a session the owner put in IDEATE mode is told to run+close passes but the tools to do so are absent, with no fallback close path — the loop can wedge in a permanently-overdue state.\n\n## The feature\n\nMake the deferred-tool restore (reconnect/relaunch) **mode-aware**: a session whose active modes include `ideate` always gets the blender ideate-loop family in its restored/core set — the restore should key off the session's mode, not a fixed generic subset. Additionally, provide a lightweight fallback close path (e.g. an `improvements:capture` carrying the `ideation` field, or a coord verb) that resets the ideate-overdue counter when the blender family is genuinely unreachable, so the loop cannot wedge.\n\n## Why not just always-load the blender family\n\nTool-budget trimming is deliberate (prompt-weight discipline); the fix is not \"load everything\" but \"the restore set should follow the session's declared mode,\" so an ideate session carries its ideate tools and a non-ideate session doesn't pay for them.",

      "state": "closed",

      "id": "EI-11718",
      "title": "code:run dryRun does not intercept write effects dispatched through tools:invoke",
      "summary": "During the autonomous-loop release, code:run was called with dryRun:true and the script invoked tools:invoke({name:'deploy:await', ...}). The result reported dryRun:true but also returned concrete await_ids 19140/19141 and 'Registered' advice, while plannedMutations was empty. Direct dotted write calls are previewed correctly, but a write hidden behind tools:invoke bypasses the mutation interceptor. This can create real subscriptions or other side effects during what the caller believes is a dry run.       "id": "EI-12198",
      "title": "Stale/duplicate \"system-backup-alert\" coord messages keep getting re-escalated as CURRENT even after the underlying condition self-resolved",
      "summary": "Live-verified 2026-07-14 ~19:38 EDT (Mug wake, direct bash check): papercusp-db-backup.service/timer is HEALTHY and has been all day — db-backup.log shows unbroken hourly successes from 09:30 EDT through 19:02 EDT (last success 36min before this check), STATUS.json confirms lastSuccessEpoch matches, zero FAIL lines since the 2026-07-12T22:12 convergence-day failure. No ALERT-BACKUP-FAILING marker file exists.\n\nYet at least two escalations fired in this same wake window describing the backup as CURRENTLY stale/failing:\n- su-d1425c47 (09:08 EDT / 13:08:26Z): \"19h11m stale... growing 15h->19h across my recent turns\" — this one was plausibly real (predates the 09:30 recovery).\n- Kettle s-1784072172470-6e6502d0 (19:37:38Z, i.e. THIS wake's own timeframe): \"system-backup-alert messages firing every ~15min continuously since 08:54Z... 19h+ by the time this Kettle wake read its inbox... 10,122 total system-backup-alert messages, 9,418 coalesced dupes.\" This one is describing a window (04:54-09:30 EDT) that had ALREADY SELF-RESOLVED ~10 hours before the Kettle's own wake, but the Kettle escalated it as if the staleness were current/ongoing, and did not cross-check STATUS.json/db-backup.log against wall-clock \"now\" before escalating.\n\nRoot cause: a backlogged queue of historical alert messages (from a real-but-since-fixed incident window, likely the 04:39 EDT user-manager restart noted in papercup-backup-health.timer's own comments) sits unread/un-acknowledged. Downstream consumers (Kettle digest, escalation summarizers) read the STALE MESSAGE TEXT (which embeds a staleness figure computed at send-time) and re-surface it as a live blocker without re-deriving current freshness from the artifact (STATUS.json / db-backup.log mtime) at read-time. The alert's own embedded \"Xh stale\" number is being treated as ground truth long after it was generated, instead of being re-verified.\n\nFix direction: (1) the coord message-summarization/escalation path for a repeating/coalesced alert kind should re-verify the underlying condition against a live source (or use `coord:conditions` current-state, not raw message text) before re-escalating, especially for a dedupKind that coalesces thousands of instances — a single re-check call is cheap next to 10k duplicate messages. (2) `system-backup-alert`-class messages should be acked/archived once the condition clears (the health-check script or a companion routine could write a resolution marker / auto-ack the coalesced thread when a subsequent healthy run lands), so the backlog doesn't get replayed as current by every future reader. (3) Consider capping/expiring a coalesced dedup thread's relevance window so a \"still open\" summary always carries a timestamp check.\n\nFiled during papercusp Mug wake (woken by coord:escalate). Not filing as critical since current backup state is fine now — but the detector/chatter gap is what let this whole loop happen and will recur on the next transient blip.",

      "id": "EI-12519",
      "title": "Kettle escalations for the same recurring condition aren't coalescing — conditionKey used inconsistently across wakes",
      "summary": "Observed via coord:escalations on 2026-07-15 ~08:13Z: the invalid-model-config spawn-failure condition had at least 3 separate open escalation rows from different Kettle wakes (msg mrlmxszx 05:24:11Z subjectSignature \"invalid-model-config-spawn-failure\"; msg mrln4bp6 05:29:15Z same signature but a NEW row, repeatCount:1 — did not coalesce onto mrlmxszx despite being an explicit \"follow-up\"; msg mrlsng35 08:04:06Z subjectSignature \"kettle-invalid-model-config\" — a THIRD, differently-keyed row for the same underlying condition). Expected behavior per coord:escalate's own documented conditionKey mechanic: re-escalating the same recurring condition with a stable conditionKey should COALESCE onto the existing open row (bump repeatCount) instead of opening a new one. Instead each kettle wake session picked its own ad-hoc phrasing/signature, so the mechanism never engaged and the owner-facing escalation queue accumulates duplicate rows for one root cause — inflating the \"aging escalations\" count (267 this wake) with redundant entries and making it harder for the owner to see this is ONE condition, not three.\n\nRoot cause: the Kettle system prompt tells each fresh-per-wake session to escalate ad-hoc without prescribing a STABLE, cross-session conditionKey naming convention for its own recurring anomaly types (e.g. \"kettle-invalid-model-config\", \"kettle-escalation-aging\", \"kettle-work-feed-stuck\"). Since each wake is a brand-new session with no memory of prior wording, the natural-language summary/signature drifts wake to wake even when the underlying detector-reported anomaly type is identical.\n\nSuggested fix: the Kettle prompt (or the anomaly's suggestedAction payload) should supply a canonical, stable conditionKey per anomaly TYPE (not per wake's prose), so every kettle session escalating e.g. \"invalid-model-config\" uses the exact same key and coalesces correctly. Alternatively, the OverwatchBrief's suggestedAction could pre-populate the exact conditionKey string to use, removing the ad-hoc naming risk entirely. (Confirmed the fix direction works: this wake's own coord:escalate call using conditionKey \"kettle-invalid-model-config\" DID coalesce onto the existing mrlsng35 row rather than creating a 4th.)",

      "title": "Kettle's invalid-model-config escalations use inconsistent conditionKey across wakes — dedup never coalesces, backlog piles up",
      "summary": "Evidence: coord:escalations (status:open) shows 4 separate OPEN rows for the same underlying \"autonomous-role spawn failed: selected model unavailable/inaccessible\" condition, each with repeatCount:1 (never coalesced):\n- mrlmxszx (05:24:11Z) subjectSignature=\"invalid-model-config-spawn-failure\"\n- mrln4bp6 (05:29:15Z) subjectSignature=\"invalid-model-config-spawn-failure\" (follow-up, still didn't coalesce onto mrlmxszx despite same signature — conditionKey apparently not passed, or passed differently)\n- mrlsng35 (08:04:06Z) subjectSignature=\"kettle-invalid-model-config\" (different signature string than the two above)\n- (this wake's own brief) count now flat at 4, no new escalation filed per backoff rule\n\nRoot cause hypothesis: successive Kettle wake-sessions (each a fresh session per this role's design) independently choose a conditionKey/subjectSignature string ad hoc instead of a documented, stable constant — so `coord:escalate { conditionKey }` dedup coalescing never fires for this drift, and 3-4 near-duplicate escalation rows accumulate for one ongoing condition. This directly feeds the OTHER standing anomaly (escalation-aging backlog growth) — the Kettle's own escalation habit is partly responsible for backlog growth it also flags.\n\nSuggested durable fix: the Kettle persona/prompt should name ONE canonical conditionKey per anomaly type (e.g. \"kettle-invalid-model-config\", \"kettle-escalation-aging\", \"kettle-work-feed-stuck-frontier-N\") so every wake-session reuses the same literal string, guaranteeing coalescing regardless of which fresh session files it. Consider hardcoding these strings in the Kettle system prompt's anomaly-action table rather than leaving the session to invent one per wake.",

    {
      "id": "EI-12727",
      "title": "Every live cut-seed force-backfill re-enqueues the ENTIRE projection into the append-only log — corestore ratcheted 237→335 MiB in one cut and never shrinks",
      "summary": "## Summary\nThe WI-4487 fix makes a live cut refresh via `backfillLocalState(..., { force: true, maxOpsPerAuthor: 0 })` before opening the store read-only. That is correct and should stay. But `force: true` re-enqueues the **entire projection** every time, the operator drains it, and each drained row is an **append to an append-only log**. So every cut permanently ratchets the corestore up by ~one full projection — the data is re-written, not de-duplicated.\n\n**This is a cost of the fix I shipped.** Flagging it against my own change rather than leaving it for whoever notices the installer got big.\n\n## Measured (2026-07-15, the 0.0.11 verification cut)\n```\ncorestore in the seed BEFORE this work    237 MiB\ncorestore in the seed AFTER one live cut  335 MiB     (+98 MiB, +41%)\ntotal seed                                458 MiB     (git 122.64 + corestore 335.36)\nown-log length   87,662 → 95,812          (+8,150 appends, one full projection)\n```\n\nThe projection that gets re-enqueued in full, per cut (verified against the live DB):\n```\nharness_features_consolidated   1,062\nharness_issues_consolidated         0\nharness_plans                   1,631\npot_settings                       15\npot_members                         2\n  BACKFILL_TARGETS subtotal      2,710\nengineer_issues (scope=harness:papercusp | operator, origin=local)\n                                5,460   ← the bulk; enqueued by the separate\n                                          second query in backfill-local-state.ts\n  TOTAL                         8,170   (was 8,092 at cut time; +78 drift in 25 min)\n```\n`8,092` enqueued → `+8,150` on the log → the delta IS the whole projection. Confirms the mechanism directly: N cuts ⇒ N × ~8.2k appends, forever.\n\n## Why it matters\n- The installer is already ~3.6 GB; the seed is 458 MiB of it and grows ~100 MiB **per cut**, monotonically. Cut 0.0.12, 0.0.13, 0.0.14 and it keeps climbing with no ceiling and no shrink path.\n- **`--sparse` cannot save us on the live path.** Trimming needs a fresh head snapshot appended via `produceLogSnapshot`, which needs the write lock the running operator holds. So the live cut warns and ships FULL history — correct, but it means the ratchet is exactly where the mitigation isn't available. Observed again on this cut: *\"no complete snapshot within the reader scan window for 5b00878b… → shipping FULL history\"*.\n- Growth is in the **log**, so it ships to every new member and is replayed on every cold catch-up, not just carried in the installer.\n\n## Do NOT \"fix\" it by dropping the refresh\nSkipping the backfill is what 0.0.9/0.0.10 effectively did (`PAPERCUSP_SEED_CORESTORE=0`) and it ships a seed missing state — the exact ships-green-does-nothing defect WI-4487 exists to fix. Correct beats small. The refresh stays.\n\n## Fix directions (unranked — needs a real design pass)\n1. **Make the head snapshot available on the live path.** The dark, P-008-gated `SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT` producer would have the operator maintain head snapshots itself, so a live sparse cut could trim with no quiesce and no write lock. That flag being off is precisely why this ratchet has no mitigation today. Most promising, and it turns the whole problem off.\n2. **Don't re-enqueue what's already federated.** The force-backfill is a blunt instrument: it exists to guarantee the projection is present, but on a store that already has 87k ops, nearly all 8.2k rows are re-statements of what's already in the log. A diff/LWW-aware backfill (enqueue only rows whose `fed_hlc` is newer than what the log already carries) would make a steady-state cut ~free. Needs care: the point of `force` is not trusting the marker.\n3. **Compact at cut time**, if a read-only compaction of the source into the seed copy is possible without the write lock (the cut already `pipeReplicate`s into a fresh store — the copy, not the source, could be the trim target).\n\n## Repro\nRun any live cut twice and diff the seed's corestore size + `manifest.json` `coreLengths`:\n`npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.ts --workspace-id papercusp-workspace --hive papercusp --out <dir>`\nEach run adds ~one projection (~8.2k ops) to the log. (Read-only against the live store; safe to run — it's not a release cut.)",

      "title": "Kettle persona prompt mandates a 15th scorecard key (\\\"context-burn\\\") the live pot-coordination-health rubric does not define — first scorecard call fails validation every turn",
      "summary": "The Kettle system prompt's turn-completion checklist lists 15 required rating keys for the pot-coordination-health scorecard, including \"context-burn\" (with a detailed model referencing loop:soak-report contextBurn fields). The LIVE rubric (rubrics:get { rubricRef: 'pot-coordination-health' }) only defines 14 criteria and does NOT include context-burn — its own description literally says \"The 14-criteria scorecard\". Calling improvements:capture with all 15 keys (as the prompt instructs) fails with: \"unexpected criterion key(s): context-burn ... A rubric scorecard must rate exactly the declared criteria.\" This means every fresh Kettle session's FIRST scorecard attempt this turn (2026-07-15T14:15Z) failed and had to be retried after discovering the mismatch via trial-and-error + a rubrics:get read — wasted a round-trip and risks a Kettle giving up / synthesizing a floor if it doesn't retry. Either (a) the rubric needs a context-burn criterion added (matching the persona's detailed model/method text, which reads like it was written for an intended 15th criterion that never shipped), or (b) the persona prompt's checklist + worked example need the context-burn entry removed to match the live 14-criteria rubric. Filed unconfirmed on root cause of the drift (which side is stale) but the mismatch itself is directly reproduced this turn.",

      "title": "Fleet-member post-compaction wake goes critical-context (111%) immediately, purely from mandated tool-preload + doc reads",
      "summary": "Third consecutive occurrence this session (su-8abfc8d3, fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-0715): each post-compaction wake, the SessionStart hook mandates a ToolSearch preload (12 tool schemas) + root/user CLAUDE.md + compaction-strategy.md reads BEFORE any real work, and context is already reported at 111% (above the 300000 soft ceiling) right after that preload, with zero new bug-drain work done. This forces an immediate re-compaction every wake, so the member never accumulates enough headroom to actually drain a work item. Likely cause: the fixed preamble (system prompt + tool catalog + mandated doc reads + carry brief) is itself large relative to the 300k soft budget for a fleet member whose session already carries a big persona/playbook.       "id": "EI-12874",
      "title": "Recurring: context measures CRITICAL (>100% of 300k soft ceiling) immediately after a single ToolSearch preload on wake, before any substantive work — costing whole wake cycles with zero drain progress",
      "summary": "Observed 5+ consecutive wakes on su-8abfc8d3 (fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-0715, member, harness papercusp, plan bug-drain-nonp2p-2026-07-11) in a tight loop:\n\n1. Wake fires (loop:arm, 600s interval).\n2. Agent loads ONE ToolSearch call (~6-13 core tool schemas: coord_orient, work_items_*, improvements_capture, coord_send, code_run, loop_*, scheduler_get_next).\n3. PostToolUse hook fires IMMEDIATELY: \"context: 331746/300000 (111%) — CRITICAL: at your soft compaction limit.\"\n4. This happens BEFORE coord:orient, scheduler:get_next, or any substantive drain-mission call can run.\n5. Agent writes loop:checkpoint (did/left/insight/next) documenting no-progress, then calls session:request-compaction { autoContinue:true }.\n6. Compaction completes, session resumes — and the SAME pattern repeats on the very next wake.\n\nThis has now happened identically across at least 5 wakes with ZERO drain-mission work accomplished in any of them (no coord:orient completed, no scheduler:get_next call, no work-item touched). Each cycle burns a full wake purely on preload→critical→checkpoint→compact, then repeats.\n\nSuspected root cause: the session's BASELINE context (persona/system-prompt + carry document/carry-brief text + injected memory recall block + CLAUDE.md ancestor chain + turn-provenance/hook injections) is itself already at or very near the 300k soft ceiling before the agent does any work this turn — so even a single minimal ToolSearch call (which itself adds real but modest tokens) tips it over 100%. This looks like either (a) a context-ceiling/token-accounting bug that overcounts, or (b) genuine baseline bloat in what's re-injected every wake (the carry-brief/carry-document + memory-recall block + hook chatter are large and repeated verbatim each wake) that isn't being trimmed/summarized across compactions.\n\nImpact: a fleet member stuck in this loop makes literally zero forward progress on its assigned mission — it is alive (loop fires, compacts, resumes) but functionally wedged, silently, for however many wake cycles this persists. This is exactly the kind of \"high load / stall with no mechanism explained\" pattern that should be treated as a real bug per platform doctrine, not shrugged off as transient.\n\nSuggested places to look: (1) whether the post-compaction carry-document assembly (SessionStart[source=compact] hook) is re-including large blocks (deferred-tools list, full compaction-strategy.md text, full CLAUDE.md chain, memory-recall block) that should be trimmed/pointer-ized per the \"Do NOT re-summarize\" rule already in compaction-strategy.md but apparently not being honored on the DELIVERY side; (2) whether the 300k soft-ceiling counter is counting something it shouldn't (e.g. double-counting the system prompt across the hook injection); (3) whether loop-wake sessions in particular (vs fresh interactive sessions) carry extra baggage that compounds each cycle.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",

    {
      "id": "EI-12889",
      "title": "Windows is the ONLY release platform with no identity/privacy audit gate — and the EI-12881 hashDir fix removed the accidental backstop that made a seed LOG leak loud",
      "summary": "Found while preparing per-platform acceptance for the 0.0.11 r7 cut (3-platform ship in flight NOW). Two facts that are each fine alone and bad together.\n\n## Fact 1 — the windows leg has NO identity/privacy gate (measured)\n`grep -cE \"audit-release-bundle|PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_AUDIT|scan-dir|findIdentityLeaks\" bin/build-windows-on-vm.sh` => **0**.\nThe only \"audit\" strings in that file are npm's unrelated `--no-audit --no-fund` (lines 689/692).\n\nCompare the siblings:\n- LINUX: `build-appimage.sh:196` — `if [ \"${PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_AUDIT:-1}\" = \"1\" ]` (defaults ON; \"an AppImage is ALWAYS a release artifact\").\n- MAC: `mac-vm-build.sh:26` exports `PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_AUDIT=\"${...:-1}\"` and :440 actually runs `python3 audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir \"$role_bundle_dir/macos/$role_label.app\"` post-build.\n- WINDOWS: nothing.\n\n`release-local.sh:501` does `export PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_AUDIT=1`, but that export is **inert for windows** — `build-windows-on-vm.sh` never reads the var. And there is no late gate: `grep -E \"audit|scan-dir|identity|leak\" bin/upload-release.sh` => none. So the windows artifact reaches r2 having passed no identity scan at any point.\n\nThis is the exact leak class WI-4736 / the 0.0.9 audit exist to prevent (\"desktop 0.0.9 audit found the shipped binaries embed the build box's identity\" — mac-vm-build.sh:29). Linux and mac are gated fail-closed; windows is ungated. 1-of-3 platforms shipping ungated is the bug.\n\n## Fact 2 — EI-12881's fix (correctly) removed the accidental backstop\n`seed-provider-corestore.ts:131` `isRocksInfoLog()` now excludes `LOG` / `LOG.old*` from `walkFiles`, so both `hashDir` (pack AND verify) and `dirSize` skip it. That fix is RIGHT and I'm not suggesting reverting it — it's what unbroke the restore.\n\nBut note what it changes, made explicit by the regression test itself (`seed-provider-corestore.test.ts:313-315`):\n```\n// (a) a store re-open regenerated LOG — it leaks the build box's identity\nwriteFileSync(join(dbDir, 'LOG'), 'Host name (Env): SOME-BUILD-BOX\\n/home/someone/abs/path\\n');\nexpect(await provider.verify(entry, payload)).toEqual({ ok: true });\n```\nThe test asserts that a **present, identity-leaking LOG now verifies `ok`**.\n\n- BEFORE the fix: LOG present => hash mismatch => verify fails => empty hive. Wrong outcome, but **LOUD**.\n- AFTER the fix: LOG present => verify ok => hive restores correctly => **the identity leak ships SILENTLY**.\n\nSo the hash used to accidentally gate the LOG leak. It no longer does — by design. That is a good trade, but it means the identity gate is now the *only* thing standing between a regenerated LOG and a shipped hostname/abs-path leak.\n\n## Why the two together are the problem\n`release-local.sh:446-448` scrubs LOG exactly once:\n```\nif [[ -d \"$ROOT/src-tauri/seed/corestore/db\" ]]; then\n  rm -f \".../db/LOG\" \".../db\"/LOG.old* 2>/dev/null || true\nfi\n```\nBest-effort (`|| true`), and the script's own comment says the risk is real: *\"a reused/as-is seed (PAPERCUSP_SKIP_SEED_CUT=1) or a later store re-open can regenerate it.\"* The windows leg is invoked at :699 with exactly `PAPERCUSP_SKIP_SEED_CUT=1`, reusing that one scrubbed seed (:696).\n\nSo on windows: if LOG is regenerated any time between the :447 scrub and packaging, **nothing catches it** — not the hash (excluded by design), not an identity gate (absent). On linux the AppDir gate catches it; on mac the `--scan-dir` gate catches it. Windows has no net.\n\nI have NOT yet proven a LOG is actually present in a windows artifact — r7 hasn't produced artifacts yet and I'm not touching the VMs. Filing the *structural* gap now because it's cheap today and expensive the day after we publish (the 0.0.9/0.0.10 lesson: both silently shipped a broken seed, unnoticed until after publication).\n\n## Proposed durable fix (not a one-off)\n1. Add the post-build `audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir` gate to `build-windows-on-vm.sh`, mirroring `mac-vm-build.sh:440`, defaulting `PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_AUDIT=1` like its two siblings. Fail-closed.\n2. Add an explicit **fail-closed \"LOG absent\" assertion on the packaged seed** for all 3 platforms, rather than relying on identity-token matching. Rationale: `--scan-dir` hunts specific tokens (aviweiss/avraham/marsh-office). It catches a LOG from *these* build boxes, but it is token-based, so it is not a general \"no diagnostic log shipped\" invariant. Since the hash deliberately no longer covers LOG, an explicit absence check is the right invariant and belongs next to the scrub.\n3. Consider making the scrub not `|| true` — or better, assert-after-scrub, so a failed scrub is loud at cut time.\n\nReuse-first note: (1) is literally the mac gate applied to the windows leg — no new surface. (2) extends the existing audit script / cut path rather than adding a parallel checker.",

    {
      "id": "EI-12895",
      "title": "Bytebot desktop-agent instances unusable: task model rejects plain string spec, and proxy route configured with literal \"dummy-key-for-proxy\"",
      "summary": "Every Bytebot browser-automation route failed, forcing a manual Xvfb + xdotool + ImageMagick fallback (~30 screenshots, pixel-coordinate clicking) to complete an owner-directed Cloudflare DNS + Google Workspace recovery task. Bytebot is the documented skill for exactly this work and was 100% unusable.\n\nThree distinct faults, all pre-browser-control (no task ever reached Chromium):\n\n1. Task model payload shape. POST /tasks with model:\"claude-sonnet-4-5\" (a plain string, the natural spec form used everywhere else in the workspace) returns:\n   400 {\"message\":\"Invalid task model payload: expected an object of shape { provider: anthropic|openai|google|proxy, name: string }\"}\n   The skill docs / callers pass the string form. Either accept the string spec (and normalize) or fix the docs+callers.\n\n2. Direct-anthropic instances pinned to a depleted balance. First task (id 46058fca-2273-490c-be74-5b9bb2b5bc7c, port 10001) FAILED before opening Cloudflare because the instance was routed at a direct Anthropic credential with no balance.\n\n3. Proxy route has a placeholder credential. Retrying via provider:\"proxy\" (the workspace inference gateway) also FAILED — the Bytebot proxy is configured with the literal string \"dummy-key-for-proxy\". So the failover path that should have rescued (2) is itself dead.\n\nNet: with direct depleted and proxy holding a dummy key, there is NO working inference route for any of the 10 Bytebot instances (probed ports 9991,10001,10011,...,10081 — all had zero COMPLETED tasks, consistent with a long-standing outage rather than a transient).\n\nCorrect state: Bytebot accepts the same model spec form as the rest of the workspace; the proxy route carries a real gateway credential; and a task that cannot obtain inference fails LOUDLY at submit time with the reason, rather than accepting the task and failing opaquely after the fact.\n\nRecurrence guard suggestion: a health check that submits a trivial no-op task per Bytebot instance and asserts it reaches COMPLETED — the \"0 COMPLETED tasks across all 10 instances\" signal above should have alarmed on its own long before an owner task hit it.\n\nNote also: the host CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can read zones but has no DNS-edit scope, and the wrangler OAuth session likewise. That is likely intentional least-privilege (not filed as a bug), but it means Bytebot/browser is the ONLY path for DNS changes — which is why the Bytebot outage was fully blocking here.",

    {
      "id": "EI-12991",
      "title": "Cupboard 503 in operator: cupboard.papercusp.com custom domain unreachable to server-side fetch while the worker is healthy on workers.dev",
      "summary": "## Symptom\nOwner's Cupboard UI: \"The Cupboard server is unavailable. Is PAPERCUSP_CUPBOARD_URL configured? (Error: HTTP 503)\". Reproduced on live :3070: GET /api/cupboard/listings -> 503 in 10.003s, body {\"error\":\"TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout\"} (the AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) in routes/cupboard.ts firing).\n\n## Healthy (ruled OUT)\n- Worker papercusp-cupboard IS deployed (CF API, modified 2026-07-14); serves 32 real listings from every network via https://papercusp-cupboard.aviynw.workers.dev/listings (200, ~0.8s).\n- Custom domain bound + enabled + cert issued: CF API /workers/domains -> cupboard.papercusp.com -> papercusp-cupboard, enabled:true, cert_id present. Zone active, not paused. CT logs: valid GTS cert covering cupboard.papercusp.com through 2026-08-24.\n- Public DNS correct (dns.google): apex/cupboard/www -> 172.67.145.145 / 104.21.73.140 (Cloudflare proxy), TTL 300.\n\n## Failure (custom domain vs workers.dev)\nThe operator's server-side fetch to cupboard.papercusp.com fails; workers.dev (which bypasses the papercusp.com ZONE) succeeds. Two contributing faults, both needing infra access a read-only token/this box lacks:\n\n1. LAN/host DNS poisoning: plaintext :53 from this box (dig @1.1.1.1, @8.8.8.8, python getaddrinfo, getent) all return papercusp.com -> 18.204.152.241 (a live but wrong Heroku router) + AAAA :: with impossible TTL 4294967295. Only DoH/:443 returns the correct Cloudflare IPs. Node fetch prefers IPv6 -> connects to :: black hole -> 10s timeout -> 503.\n2. Any Host/SNI containing papercusp.com HANGS even to the correct Cloudflare IP, on :80 and :443, from this box AND Anthropic's fetcher AND public proxies (codetabs 522, allorigins 408), while example.com on the SAME IP returns 200. Consistent with a zone WAF / bot-fight-mode / a stale proxied DNS record shadowing the Worker custom domain. Could not confirm the exact zone setting: token denied on dns_records, workers/routes, settings/ssl, settings/security_level.\n\nOPEN QUESTION: is cupboard.papercusp.com down for real browsers too, or only for automated/server-side clients (normal bot-management)? A 5-second owner check (open it in a browser) disambiguates. If browsers work, the operator's server-side fetch is being bot-challenged and the fix is a WAF/bot exception (or point the operator at workers.dev); if browsers also fail, the custom domain routing/DNS is broken zone-wide.\n\n## Product bugs (independent of the infra fault)\nA. The 503 copy falsely blamed PAPERCUSP_CUPBOARD_URL (which has a working default) and sent an hour of debugging down the wrong path. FIXED this session in CupboardErrorState.tsx: 503 now maps to reachability copy and surfaces the real upstream error; added cupboardHttpError(res) that folds the proxy's body {error} into the thrown message (the client previously threw a bare `HTTP 503`, discarding the TimeoutError). Wired listings (CupboardClient.tsx) + tools (ToolsSection.tsx). Tests green.\nB. routes/cupboard.ts collapses EVERY upstream failure into 503 with no server-side log/metric — an operator that can't reach Cupboard is invisible in logs. Consider distinguishing timeout/DNS/refused and emitting a warn.\n\n## Workaround applied (TEMPORARY — remove when the domain is fixed)\nPAPERCUSP_CUPBOARD_URL=https://papercusp-cupboard.aviynw.workers.dev appended to papercup-release/apps/operator/.env.local AND papercusp/apps/operator/.env.local, papercup-dev-api.service restarted. :3070 now returns 30 listings, 200, ~0.4s warm. This bypasses both faults but points the operator at the raw workers.dev URL instead of the canonical custom domain.\n\n## Root-cause fix (needs owner / write-scoped Cloudflare token)\n- Cloudflare dashboard: check DNS records for cupboard.papercusp.com (and apex/www) for a stale proxied A/AAAA pointing at the old Heroku origin 18.204.152.241 / ::; remove so the Worker custom domain owns the hostname.\n- Check zone WAF / Bot Fight Mode / firewall rules blocking the papercusp.com zone for non-browser clients.\n- Separately: the host's :53 resolver poisoning papercusp.com (router/middlebox) — owner network gear.",

      "id": "EI-13215",
      "title": "Cup capability_bash sandbox blocks AF_UNIX socket() (EPERM) — Xvfb/X11/GTK Tauri GUI verification structurally impossible from a cup session, contradicting agent-e2e.mdx's \"you CAN and MUST verify UI yourself\"",
      "summary": "Found while working WI-4480 (global docs-search shortcut live GUI verification). Evidence:\n\n1. `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh --boot-only` failed immediately: Xvfb :90 never came up. xvfb.log: `_XSERVTransSocketOpenCOTSServer: Unable to open socket for local/unix ... Cannot establish any listening sockets`.\n2. Root-caused with strace: `strace -f -e trace=socket,bind,listen python3 -c \"socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)\"` → `socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0) = -1 EPERM (Operation not permitted)`. A plain AF_INET TCP socket bind/listen on the SAME session succeeds fine (127.0.0.1:<port>). This is a seccomp filter (visible wrapper: `.../@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime/vendor/seccomp/x64/apply-seccomp`) that blocks AF_UNIX socket() creation specifically for tool calls made through `capability:bash` in a cup/coding-pot session.\n3. Since Xvfb, X11 client libraries, DBus, and (very likely) WebKitGTK's own internal IPC all require creating/connecting AF_UNIX sockets, NO Tauri GUI process (dev shell or packaged) can be launched from a cup's capability_bash — not just headless-Xvfb, any X11/Wayland display route hits the same wall (both use AF_UNIX sockets under /tmp/.X11-unix or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR).\n4. Separately (same session): the documented shared Rust build cache `~/.cargo-target` (symlink -> /mnt/data/relocated-builds/cargo-target) is mounted read-only in THIS sandbox (`findmnt /mnt/data` shows `ro`, though /etc/fstab declares `defaults` i.e. rw, and /tmp — bind-mounted from the same device — IS rw) — so even `cargo test`/`cargo build` fail with \"Read-only file system\" unless CARGO_TARGET_DIR is overridden to a writable path (e.g. /tmp). This looks like a deliberate per-sandbox restricted filesystem view (most of the host read-only, project dir + /tmp writable), not a real host-level XFS outage (checked `journalctl -k` for I/O errors — none found).\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS: `apps/operator-docs/.../testing/agent-e2e.mdx` and the coding-pot cup persona both assert flatly that an agent \"CAN — and therefore MUST — verify UI yourself\" via `npm run dev` + tauri-agent-tools, and frame any claim of UI being unverifiable-headless as a mistake to avoid. For a cup session with this sandbox profile, that claim is FALSE — the GUI process cannot even start. This is very likely why WI-4480's Linux live-GUI leg was never actually completed despite THREE prior cup placements on it (2 died to unrelated host-restart reaps per the WI's own notes, but the other 2 cups posted \"READY TO MARK DONE\" completion summaries that both admit, in the same breath, the live GUI/system-wide-grab check was never actually done — i.e. they hit this exact wall and glossed over it with 'structural' verification instead of surfacing the sandbox gap plainly).\n\nSUGGESTED FIX: either (a) grant cup/coding-pot sandboxes AF_UNIX socket capability + rw access to a build-cache path so `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh` actually works from a cup session, or (b) if that capability is intentionally withheld from cups for safety, update agent-e2e.mdx + the cup persona to say plainly that live GUI/Tauri E2E verification requires an su/interactive session (or human), and give cups a clear, sanctioned handoff path instead of the current blanket \"you CAN and MUST\" framing that sets cups up to either silently fail or (as happened twice on this WI) fabricate a 'structural' pass to paper over it.\n\nUnconfirmed: whether ALL cup sessions on this box have this same sandbox profile, or whether it varies by spawn config — worth confirming against another cup/su to see whether the restriction is role-scoped or session-scoped.",

      "title": "Completed work routinely lands in-tree but is never written to the work-item ledger — items sit todo/cursed and burn re-placement cycles",
      "summary": "THREE independent instances in ONE night, all found only because a fresh cup verified against ground truth instead of restarting:\n\n1. WI-4446 (cursed, failCount 3, ZERO notes): a 2026-07-15 session BUILT the release-history page and left a completion comment but never set state. Three subsequent placements were spent on already-done work; the item read as cursed. Wave-4 cup s-1784251669829 verified (87 tests green vs 64 claimed) and closed it passed.\n2. WI-3893 (todo, in the placement-recovery nag rotation): the connected_never_replicated recurrence guard was ALREADY LANDED in-tree from prior P-001/P-007 work (WI-3684/WI-4241), never closed out. Cup s-1784254503048 verified independently and closed it passed.\n3. WI-4480 (inverse failure): TWO prior sessions posted 'READY TO MARK DONE' claims that quietly admitted the live GUI check was never done. Cup s-1784251137910 re-verified fresh (5/5 cargo, 82/82 TS) and correctly blocked only the GUI leg.\n\nSO: the ledger diverges from the tree in BOTH directions — done-but-unwritten (1,2) and written-done-but-unverified (3). Cost is concrete: WI-4446 alone consumed 3 spawns + a curse; WI-3893 consumed a spawn and generated ~10 placement-recovery Mug wakes.\n\nRoot-cause shape: state-write is the LAST action of a session, so any death/end/reap between 'work landed' and 'set_state' loses it silently — and nothing reconciles tree-vs-ledger afterward. Per the owner's standing design principle (don't add a re-verify bandaid over a value that can be wrong — make the primary value right the first time): the fix is NOT a periodic reconciliation sweep. Candidates: (a) write state at the same commit boundary as the work (or make completion evidence the write, not a separate trailing verb); (b) make a session's terminal handler flush intent-to-complete durably BEFORE the work-verify step, so a death leaves 'claimed done, unverified' rather than nothing; (c) at minimum, a cup's FIRST action on any todo item should be a cheap ground-truth check against the tree (this is what caught all three) — codify it in the cup brief/persona rather than relying on a Mug remembering to write it into each brief.",

    {
      "id": "EI-13317",
      "title": "Peer-log/gossip swarm link does not re-establish after one side restarts — remote addressability goes dark until BOTH peers re-announce fresh (P-102 class, tower↔VM rig forensics)",
      "summary": "Established live on the LIVE-1 P-059 tower↔VM rig, session su-18f2f 2026-07-17 01:4x–03:2xZ (all timestamps EDT). This is the durable shape of the \"~13-min post-restart peer-log freeze\": it is NOT a bounded freeze that self-heals — it is a swarm rejoin failure that can persist indefinitely, and the earlier \"self-heals in ~13 min\" observations appear to have been transient/lucky reconnects.\n\nTimeline/evidence:\n- 22:35: tower bg-host restart + VM sidecar boot ~simultaneously → clean connect within ~100s; presence gossip + peer-log both directions verified live (V1/V2 of the presence-gossip cutover).\n- 22:51: VM sidecar reboot (only the VM restarted). The swarm link severed at ~22:49 and NEVER re-established: remote shared_presence rows frozen on BOTH sides at ~22:49; `[topic-gossip:papercusp/hive-presence] broadcast … 0 channel(s) open` continuously on BOTH the VM serve log and the tower bg-host journal; VM's inbound apply frozen (max(ts) of coord_event_log stuck at 22:50:39); zero tower↔VM sockets.\n- One TRANSIENT connection existed ~22:57 — long enough to replicate the VM's outbound backlog to the tower (looked like a \"self-heal\") — then dropped and never returned.\n- Ruled out: the isolated-DHT fixture (papercup-isolated-dht.service up since 20:11, survived every restart); a sibling tower process holding the connection (dev-api + staging-api journals carry zero topic-gossip/swarm lines).\n- 23:13: VM sidecar rebooted again (fresh dial, fresh announce) — did NOT reconnect in 6+ min of watching. So a fresh dial from one side cannot reach the stale side: the tower bg-host (up since 22:35, its own shared_presence self-rows stamped only at wire time 22:35) is not accepting/answering discovery, while ITS gossip broadcast timer keeps running with 0 channels.\n- 23:24: coordinated bg-host restart fired (dev:restart target bg-host, fence_seq 18) to recreate the both-sides-fresh configuration — the only configuration observed to connect cleanly.\n\nImpact: while severed, EVERYTHING cross-machine is dark — presence gossip (remote agents unaddressable: the marquee PRESENCE_GOSSIP capability regresses to local-only), peer-log federation (coord messages, fed events, delivery receipts, claim specs). Data is safe (backlog catch-up is lossless, proven), but availability is unbounded-bad.\n\nSuspected area: the swarm rejoin/re-announce lifecycle in the substrate host — after a peer drops, the surviving side seems to neither re-announce nor re-dial (or its DHT announce record goes stale/unreachable), so only a process restart re-primes it. Look at: announce refresh cadence vs connection lifetime, whether topic 'join' is server+client on both sides, and whether the gossip channel + hypercore replication share reconnect logic (the transient 22:57 connect carried replication but zero gossip channels — they may re-establish independently and both need fixing).\n\nCorrect state: after EITHER side restarts, the link re-establishes within ~100s (like a fresh boot pair) with no action on the surviving side; a persistent >5-min severed link on live peers should raise a loud health signal instead of silently freezing rails.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",
      "classification": "retain-fleet-pause",

      "summary": "Found while fixing an identity-keyed-state-inventory ratchet red (already independently fixed by a peer by the time I re-ran it — see the allowlist entries at identity-keyed-state-inventory.test.ts around lines 282-289).\n\nharness_shared now contains six tables with NO corresponding SQL migration file under libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/:\n  bak_20260717_unify_work_items\n  bak_20260717_unify_links\n  bak_20260717_unify_threads\n  bak_20260717_unify_posts\n  bak_20260717_unify_subs\n  bak_20260717_unify_topics\n\nThey exist only in the generated Drizzle schema (libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/schema/{schema,generated}.ts, pulled from the live DB via pull-schema.mjs) — grep across libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/*.sql finds zero hits for any of these names. This means someone ran raw CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT * FROM ... directly against harness_shared, bypassing the migration runner entirely — a direct violation of CLAUDE.md's storage policy (\"Schema = migrations only; NO runtime DDL... Never an ensureXxx()/inline CREATE TABLE\").\n\nTiming concern: the table names (\"unify_work_items\" etc.) match the WI-453 / work-item-deps-and-readiness-2026-06-22 P-010 \"unify work_items table\" initiative, which the owner (Avi, 2026-07-16 interactive) explicitly decided to park (\"Not now — keep parked\" while the drain fleet is live) — see that plan item's status (flipped todo→needs-human by me this session, aligning it to the owner's decision). The bak_ tables are dated 2026-07-17 — AFTER the owner's parking decision — strongly suggesting an agent proceeded to stage/rehearse the parked migration anyway (taking pre-migration snapshots of work_items/links/threads/posts/subs/topics) despite the explicit \"not now.\"\n\nI did NOT drop these tables (didn't want to destroy another agent's in-flight investigation data without more certainty, and it's tangential to my own assigned lane). Two things need owner/human attention:\n1. Whether an agent bypassed the owner's explicit park decision on WI-453 and should be redirected/stopped.\n2. Cleanup: these bak_ tables should either be dropped (if abandoned/no longer needed) or formalized as a real migration + classified in the identity-keyed-state-inventory allowlist (already done reactively by a peer) rather than left as stray runtime DDL. Per storage policy this is technical debt regardless of the parking-decision question.",
