    {
      "id": "EI-13623",
      "title": "Release-checkout deploy wedged 11h+ on a git-sync sweep-boundary inconsistency (new lib's workspaces entry landed before its files) — both swap AND rollback targets broken",
      "summary": "Found while debugging WI-5003 (maxturn-sweep live canary transcript-discovery failures).\n\n**Symptom:** `:3070` has been serving stale sha `f08ae73852` for 11+ hours (confirmed via `/api/health`), silently blocking every staging fix from reaching production — including an unrelated feature (WI-5002/EI-13277 owner-id pre-pin) that landed hours ago in `staging`'s `bootstrap-su.ts` but is completely absent from the release tree.\n\n**Root cause:** `/tmp/papercup-auto-deploy.log` (last write 2026-07-16 18:29, i.e. stale — not retried since) shows the release-checkout swap AND its rollback both failing identically: `FATAL: release tree cannot resolve workspace package(s): @papercusp/release-profile`. Commit `f08ae7385252a303b772b1d66e47b4d59639652d` is a git-sync sweep where root `package.json`'s `workspaces` array already lists `libs/generic/release-profile`, but the directory's actual files (package.json, src/**) hadn't landed yet — they land ONE commit later (`cd8c1e9900`). Verified directly:\n```\ngit show f08ae7385...:libs/generic/release-profile/package.json\n  → fatal: path ... does not exist in 'f08ae7385...'\ngit ls-tree HEAD -- libs/generic/release-profile\n  → present, real files (README.md, package.json, src/*.ts)\n```\nThis is a **transient sweep-boundary inconsistency inherent to git-sync's whole-tree periodic commit model**: two concurrent agents' edits (one touching root `package.json`'s workspaces array, the other adding the new lib's files) landed in two DIFFERENT sweeps instead of atomically together, leaving exactly one commit in the middle self-inconsistent (declares a workspace whose package doesn't exist yet in that same tree). The release-checkout pipeline happened to pin its target to precisely that broken commit — and because its OWN rollback logic also picked an old/broken ref, it got stuck in both directions with no automatic recovery, silently, for 11+ hours (nothing paged anyone; `/tmp/papercup-auto-deploy.log` just stopped updating).\n\n**Impact:** ANY feature added the same way (package.json workspaces edit + new lib files, landing across 2 sweeps) can wedge deploy the same way. This is a systemic gap, not a one-off.\n\n**Suggested durable fixes** (for whoever owns the release/deploy pipeline):\n1. `setup-release-checkout.sh` should retry against the NEXT-NEWER candidate commit on a workspace-resolution failure instead of just aborting + attempting a (possibly equally-broken) rollback ref — self-heal past a single bad sweep-boundary commit automatically.\n2. The deploy/checkpoint failure should be loudly surfaced (a coord:escalate / durable alert) when it's been failing for N retries or M minutes — 11 hours of silent staleness with `:3070` looking healthy (still serving fine, just OLD) is exactly the kind of failure nobody notices until they debug something unrelated.\n3. Consider whether git-sync could commit a NEW lib's manifest-registration (workspaces array edit) and its files atomically in the same sweep, or at minimum whether the release-checkout's workspace-resolution check should tolerate/skip a package whose dir doesn't exist yet rather than hard-FATAL the whole deploy.\n\n**Currently self-resolving:** `papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-1fxzuva.service` was observed running live (started ~04:58Z) against a newer, consistent candidate commit (`44bdb315`, based on `f08ae738` but past the inconsistency) — so this specific instance should clear once that lands. Filing this so the CLASS of failure gets a durable fix, not just this instance.",

      "summary": "During the P-016 generic-hive e2e: a bee produced + saved the deliverable artifact (three-sorting-algorithms.md, acceptance-complete) and posted a coord 'completion' message (\"WI-236 DONE: ... So the work-item stayed state='todo' (re-placeable), and the Queen re-placed it onto NEW bees repeatedly — each re-producing the same artifact (observed 3+ re-placements + a Queen 'cursed disposition' investigation post, all redundant). Operator workaround used: su-146bf manually called work_items:complete to flip WI-236 → passed + stop the loop.     {
      "id": "EI-15930",
      "title": "green-checkpoint's escalation open/clear pair is not pipeline-scoped — one co-hosted pot's gate can suppress OR resolve another pot's blocker escalation",
      "summary": "Same class as EI-15925 (cross-pipeline collision in `realCheckpointDeps`), but with worse consequences — that one misinformed agents, this one silently disables a safety surface.\n\nEVERY co-hosted pot runs its own green-checkpoint against its own `cfg.integrationRoot` (papercusp, oddsmith, quartermaster, … — one `~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/<pot>/` dir each). The escalation open/clear pair keys on a bare, un-namespaced `source` token:\n\n- `~2430` open-dedup: `if (open.some((e) => e.source === 'green-checkpoint')) return;`\n- `~2433` opens with `meta: { source: 'green-checkpoint' }`\n- `~2461` clear: `if (e.source === 'green-checkpoint') { … resolve … }`\n- `~2480` find: `open.find((x) => x.source === 'green-checkpoint')`\n\n`listEscalations({ status:'open' })` is not pipeline-filtered, so two failure modes across pipelines:\n\n1. **Suppression.** oddsmith's gate goes red and opens the escalation. papercusp's gate then goes red — the dedup at 2430 sees an open `green-checkpoint` row, returns early, and papercusp's blocker escalation NEVER OPENS. The owner is never paged for a genuinely held release gate.\n2. **False resolution (worse).** oddsmith's gate recovers and calls `clearEscalation`. The matcher at 2461 finds papercusp's still-red escalation and RESOLVES it. A live blocker is marked resolved by an unrelated product's recovery.\n\nBoth are silent. Neither leaves a trace that would point at the other pipeline, because the row carries no pipeline attribution at all (same root as EI-15925: the PG broadcast row for the sibling defect had `harness_slug: NULL`).\n\n## Why I did not fix it inline\n\nThe obvious fix — scope the token to `green-checkpoint:<pipeline>` at all four sites — orphans every CURRENTLY OPEN row: existing escalations carry the bare `green-checkpoint` and would no longer match the new clear-path matcher, so they would never auto-resolve and would sit open forever as stale blockers.\n\nThat needs a deliberate migration, not a drive-by. It was found during an open, owner-gated release decision (mrpcs3n5) where I judged a risky refactor of the escalation surface to be exactly the wrong thing to ship alongside a safety fix.\n\n## Suggested correct fix\n\nScope the source token per pipeline AND migrate live state in the same change:\n- write `source: 'green-checkpoint:<pipeline>'` (or keep `source` and add a `pipeline` field, IF `listEscalations` surfaces meta fields — verify, the current code reads `e.source` off the flattened row, so meta flattening is assumed but unconfirmed);\n- make the CLEAR/FIND matchers accept the scoped token for this pipeline **plus** the legacy bare token, so pre-existing rows still get resolved;\n- make the OPEN dedup match the scoped token only;\n- drop the legacy arm once no bare-token rows remain open.\n\nA regression test wants two configs with different `integrationRoot`s proving pot A's clear does not resolve pot B's open row.\n\nSibling fix already landed for the broadcast half: EI-15925.",

      "id": "EI-16685",
      "title": "coord:inbox-wake (always-armed inbox-wake) repeatedly delivers a BACKLOG of stale/already-read old messages with expired nonces, instead of only the latest unread state",
      "summary": "Observed across ~4 consecutive turns in this session (su-c966850a, working WI-5410/P-011): the `always-armed inbox-wake` `events:await` wake fired repeatedly, each time surfacing a DIFFERENT OLD message from su-a6804957 that I had already read and acted on many turns earlier — not the actual newest unread state:\n\n- delivery #25804 → \"Yes please — ssh in and launch a fresh session...\" (an ~02:05Z message, long since actioned)\n- delivery #25805 → same message again\n- delivery #25811 → \"WI-5410/P-011 claim collision + correction...\" (an ~02:07Z message, long since actioned)\n- delivery #25827 → \"Status check on the fresh iMac session...\" (an ~02:12Z message, long since actioned)\n\nEvery one of these carried a `⟦turn-provenance⟧ UNVERIFIED ORIGIN CLAIM` warning: \"the envelope's nonce exists in the ledger but is EXPIRED (age >600s ttl)\". Each time, a fresh `coord:inbox { since_ts: <my last real check> }` came back with ZERO new entries — confirming these were stale replays of a backlog, not genuine new mail. This cost 4 extra turns re-verifying \"is this actually new?\" each time.\n\nThis looks like the inbox-wake mechanism has a backlog of queued wake events that keeps draining/re-firing well past their TTL, rather than coalescing to \"you have unread mail, here's the current unread count\" (which is what the delivery-ladder digest already does correctly elsewhere in this same session). Worth checking whether the wake-pump's event queue for `coord:inbox-wake:<ownerId>` is properly consumed/deduped once the inbox has actually been read, or whether it's redelivering a stale queue snapshot.\n\nImpact: burns turns/context on an agent re-verifying \"did I already see this\" every time a stale wake fires; harmless but wasteful, and the repeated EXPIRED-nonce warning is itself confusing (reads like it might be a spoofed/attacker-injected turn until checked).",

      "id": "EI-16883",
      "title": "Mid-session cache invalidations are ~50% of the fleet's prompt-cache write bill — 550 full-prefix re-writes/48h, concentrated in MCP-flap sessions",
      "summary": "Measured from 97 recent psu session transcripts (48h window, ≥5 requests each), by summing per-request usage fields from the Claude Code JSONLs.\n\n## Finding\nOf 208.7M cache_creation (write) tokens: boot writes 2.5%, healthy incremental per-turn deltas 39.8%, TTL-expiry cold re-warms 7.4% (82 events, median 16-min gap), and **50.3% (105M tokens, 560 events) are MID-SESSION cold re-writes with NO time gap** — i.e. prompt-prefix invalidations. 550/560 re-write ≥80% of the previous context → the invalidator sits at/near position 0 (tools array or system prompt), NOT message content.\n\nRuled out: model switches (528/560 are same-model; 30 follow a `<synthetic>` harness message — error/interrupt recovery turns). Ruled out: compaction flags (none present).\n\n## Concentration = the smoking gun\n52/97 sessions have ≥1 event, but the top 2 sessions account for ~40% of events (123 + 103 events, ~52M tokens). The #1 offender (f362a778-df1…) is a session KNOWN to have suffered repeated papercusp-su MCP disconnect/reconnect cycles tonight (system-watchdog \"MCP-dark\" alerts; the session observed the server disconnect and reconnect live). An MCP reconnect that de-registers/re-registers the tool catalog mutates the `tools` block at position 0 → full-context re-write at 1.25× on the next request.\n\n## Cost\n~105M excess write tokens/48h in this SAMPLE alone (120 largest recent transcripts — the fleet total is higher). Excess cost ≈ cw×(1.25−0.1) ≈ 120M input-token-units/48h, order of $300–600/day at blended model mix. This dwarfs the ~2.5% boot-write cost that context-trimming efforts target.\n\n## Suggested fix directions (verify root cause first)\n1. Instrument: log a hash of the rendered tools-array bytes per request in afflicted sessions; confirm it changes exactly at the invalidation events.\n2. Fix the MCP flap itself (papercusp-su server stability — the watchdog has been alerting MCP-dark all night; the reconnect churn is the upstream disease).\n3. Harness mitigation: ensure the re-registered catalog serializes byte-identically (stable ordering, no per-connection nonces) so a clean reconnect does NOT invalidate; investigate whether the transient no-tools window during a flap can avoid being sent (skip/queue requests while MCP is reconnecting rather than sending a tools-array-less request that invalidates).\n4. Re-measure the read:write ratio after the fix — expected to move the fleet median from ~13.8:1 toward the ~N/2 structural ceiling (~31:1 at median session length), i.e. roughly halve the write bill.\n\nRepro/analysis scripts: cache-ratio.py, write-anatomy.py, invalidation-drill.py (job tmp dir of session su-57b6247d, conversation ffd2f730).",

    {
      "id": "EI-17287",
      "title": "work_items.attempts is 0 across ALL 20,244 papercusp rows — even via the topology-independent EI-203 bumpOrResetAttempts path in orchestrator-loop.ts (DBOS dispatch loop)",
      "summary": "While root-causing/fixing EI-13935 (setFeatureStatusPg's bumpAttempts/resetAttempts UPDATE using the unqualified `harness_features` name), I verified the theorized mechanism against the LIVE papercusp DB and it does NOT hold — but the underlying symptom (debugger auto-recovery gate effectively dead) is real and traces to a DIFFERENT, still-unexplained cause in a PROTECTED path.\n\n**What I verified (live queries against this operator's PG):**\n1. `harness_papercusp` schema DOES exist with a real, fully-writable per-harness `harness_features` view (`to_regclass('harness_papercusp.harness_features')` resolves) — so unqualified-name writes from `state-pg.ts` on THIS harness were never actually hitting the read-only fallback view as EI-13935 theorized.\n2. Migration 497's `harness_shared.harness_features` fallback view is NOT actually read-only in practice either, despite its own comment: migration 109's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA harness_shared GRANT ... TO harness_app` (run before 497 created the view) silently grants `harness_app` full INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on it (confirmed via `information_schema.role_table_grants`) — the explicit `GRANT SELECT` in 497 is a no-op überridden by the earlier default-privilege grant. **497's own doc comment is stale/incorrect and should be corrected** (a smaller, separate fix — I did not touch the SQL file itself, out of caution about editing an already-applied numbered migration).\n3. Despite both of the above, `SELECT max(attempts) FROM harness_shared.work_items WHERE harness_slug='papercusp'` → **0, across all 20,244 rows, with zero nonzero values anywhere** (`count(*) FILTER (WHERE attempts > 0) = 0`). This includes 959 `passed` + 123 `deprecated` + 49 `blocked` items — plausibly some had real retries.\n4. The CURRENT, topology-independent write path — `bumpOrResetAttempts()` in `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-loop.ts` (called from `dispatchOneHarness` whenever `ensureFeaturePipeline` genuinely starts a new pipeline for a feature whose prior status was `failing`) — writes straight to `harness_shared.work_items` with an explicit `workspace_id + harness_slug + feature_id` predicate. No qualification/permission ambiguity is possible here, yet attempts is STILL 0 everywhere.\n\n**What this means:** the debugger-auto-recovery gate (`realDebuggerHook` in `orchestrator-runner.ts`, gates on `attempts >= threshold`) is plausibly still dead on papercusp, but NOT for the reason EI-13935 filed — something in the DBOS dispatch loop itself (whether `bumpOrResetAttempts` is ever actually called with `wasFailing=true`, whether `r.started` is ever true for a feature that was previously `failing`, or something upstream in candidate selection) needs investigation. Both files are in the `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/**` protected-path pattern (human-gate per this harness's own idea-triage policy verdict D-003), so I did not modify them — filing this for a human-gated look rather than guessing at a fix in a protected, high-blast-radius dispatch loop.\n\n**Suggested next step:** instrument/log `bumpOrResetAttempts` call args + row-count for one dispatch tick on a harness with a currently-`failing` feature, to see whether it's even being reached, and whether the UPDATE actually matches a row (check for a slug/workspace_id mismatch, e.g. `activeWorkspaceId()` vs the tick's pinned `workspaceId`).\n\nI did fix the part that WAS a real, verifiable defect (EI-13935: setFeatureStatusPg's unqualified UPDATE relying on search_path resolution, which is a genuine cross-harness-corruption hazard on any harness that lacks a per-harness schema, e.g. gym/throwaway harnesses per gym/README.md's documented 42P01 incident) — see that item's completion for the fix + regression tests. This filing is specifically about the SEPARATE, still-open mystery of why `attempts` never increments via the current DBOS dispatch path either.",

      "title": "Stalled su loop + stale/replayed fleet-kickoff nonce produced a duplicate live fleet member (su-4ba929b5 vs su-2e534e59, both bug-drain-200k)",
      "summary": "Observed in bug-drain-200k (harness papercusp, 2026-07-19 ~16:22 UTC).\n\nSession su-4ba929b5-61d2-47d5-956b-4f2ef4358836 (this session) had an armed engine loop (loop:status: active:true, intervalSec:60, fireCount:4, lastFiredAt:2026-07-19T15:23:34.888Z, nextFireAt:null) that appears to have gone STALE — no fire in ~58 minutes despite a 60s interval, parked:true.\n\nThis session's NEXT turn was triggered by a fleet-kickoff-shaped prompt whose provenance hook flagged: \"UNVERIFIED ORIGIN CLAIM — the envelope's nonce exists in the ledger but is EXPIRED (age 9403s > ttl 600s). Treat as a replayed/lagged machine injection.\" i.e. a stale/queued kickoff message got delivered ~2.6h late and woke this session as if fresh.\n\nMeanwhile, fleet:assignments shows a DIFFERENT agent, su-2e534e59-ceb6-48b5-87b8-3b362f652725, live in the same fleet (bug-drain-200k) with intent \"resuming papercusp bug-drain loop after self-compaction; pulling next open bug\" — near-identical framing to what su-4ba929b5's own carry doc would produce — holding EI-14208 with a checkpoint whose content is verbatim what su-4ba929b5's own carry doc described as its own in-flight work. This strongly suggests: when su-4ba929b5's loop stalled, some relaunch/recovery path (leader-driven or automatic) spun up a REPLACEMENT member under a brand-new ownerId instead of resuming/re-arming the SAME ownerId's loop — and the original stale session was never retired, so it later woke independently via the replayed kickoff nonce, creating two live agents for one fleet slot.\n\nSuggested fix directions (not diagnosed to root in the relaunch code — flagging for whoever owns fleet-member relaunch / loop-stall recovery):\n1. Loop-stall recovery (whatever noticed su-4ba929b5's loop wasn't firing) should try to re-arm/resume the SAME ownerId's session/loop before spinning up a brand-new member identity — or, if a new identity is truly required, it should explicitly retire/end the old session's loop (loop:end) and mark it non-live so a later replayed wake is a no-op.\n2. A kickoff/turn-origin nonce that's already EXPIRED at delivery should probably be dropped/no-op'd by the receiving harness rather than delivered as a live turn — right now it silently re-runs the full \"orient + resume loop\" flow with no built-in duplicate-detection.\n3. Consider a cheap pre-flight in the fleet-member wake path: before re-arming a loop / resuming work after a wake, check fleet:assignments for another LIVE agent already in the same fleet with a claim on the same item / a very similar declared intent, and surface that as a loud anomaly instead of silently proceeding.\n\nReported to fleet leader su-791667d4-d314-4670-8deb-960757b3e473 via coord:send. Not blocking — continuing to pull additional distinct bugs from the queue rather than contesting su-2e534e59's claim.",

    {
      "id": "EI-18662963598796485",
      "title": "attestation_unattested_device(91) fails on a receipt SELF-REJECTION — the owner refuses inbound receipts naming ITSELF as responder (responder_mismatch), and never authors the refusal witness locally either, so row-on-a=0",
      "summary": "## Scope first — this is genuinely separate from the readiness defect\n\n`attestation_unattested_device` is order 91, TERMINAL. It ran at 23:13–23:14, i.e. AFTER convergence completed (`merged to 11 of 11` at 23:13:16) and after 11 consecutive scenario passes. The link was demonstrably healthy. The convergence-barrier fix (EI-18661870528779127) covers the other four failures and explicitly does NOT cover this one.\n\n## Symptom\n\nScenario output: `identity_unresolved 0→0, row-on-a=0, all reasons: receipt-apply:responder_mismatch=8`.\n\nserve-a logs exactly 8 refusals, all identical in shape:\n\n    [p2p-receipts] REFUSED inbound receipt op (responder_mismatch): responder=279242982 action=work-offer:claim hive=hello-world-pot\n\n## The key fact\n\n**279242982 is serve-a's OWN github user id.** serve-a announces itself with it at 22:48:30:\n\n    [swarm] joined topic 32ec16a4f070b438… harness=hello-world-pot (announcing as github_user_id=279242982)\n\nSo A is refusing inbound receipts that name **A itself** as the responder. (The id appears 22x on serve-a and ZERO times in serve-b's entire log — so it is A's identity, not state B was owed. An earlier reading of mine that \"b never learned a's id\" was wrong and is retracted.)\n\n## The rule being tripped\n\n`projections/p2p-receipts.ts:133`:\n\n    authorUserId = resolveIdentity(sourceLogDevice).githubUserId   // who authored the log it arrived on\n    if (authorUserId !== row.responder_github_user_id) refuse('responder_mismatch')\n\ni.e. only the responder may author their own receipt. `identity_unresolved 0→0` confirms identity resolution SUCCEEDED — it resolved and merely disagreed.\n\nSo a receipt naming A as responder arrived on a log authored by someone else (B). The check refused it. That check looks correct.\n\n## Where the real bug likely is\n\n`row-on-a=0` means A has no receipt row at all — so A never authored one LOCALLY either. Combined with the above, the refusal witness appears to be authored on the wrong side: B is emitting a receipt asserting what A did, which A then correctly rejects, while A never emits its own.\n\n**Confidence:** the symptom, the id identification, the rule, and the counters are established from logs + code. \"The witness is authored on the wrong side\" is well-grounded INFERENCE — I have not yet read the authoring path that emits a refused-op witness. Treat the fix direction as unconfirmed until that is traced.\n\n## Next step for whoever takes this\n\nTrace who authors the refused-op witness for `action=work-offer:claim` and confirm whether it is supposed to be the refuser (A, locally) or the requester (B, federating in). If the former, the authoring path is the bug; if the latter, the `responder_mismatch` invariant and the scenario's expectation are in direct conflict and one of them is wrong.\n\nRelated: WI-5779 / P-413 (attestation on a genuine second frame). Note `attestation_membership`(60) PASSED in the same run, so the attestation path is not wholly broken — it is specifically the unattested-device refused-op WITNESS leg that fails.",

      "id": "EI-18684555325410269",
      "title": "psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts: 11/22 real-pty round-trip tests time out under current host load — PRE-EXISTING, confirmed unrelated to any specific change via A/B",
      "summary": "While verifying an unrelated fix (EI-18681914950138372, psu-pty-host.mjs carry-respawn starvation), the same 11 tests in `apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts` failed identically with `Error: Test timed out in 20000-30000ms` — every failure a generic timeout on a real pty+child-process round-trip (host start / inject / recycle / discovery self-heal), never a specific assertion mismatch.\n\nVERIFIED NOT CAUSED BY MY CHANGE: ran the exact same test file against BOTH my fixed psu-pty-host.mjs (git-sync commit 569bacf406) AND the immediately-prior commit (85016ff9d1, via a scoped `git checkout <sha> -- <path>` A/B, confirmed via `locks:list` that no peer held the file first) — both runs produced the IDENTICAL 11 failed / 11 passed split, same test names, same timeout signature. This rules out my edit as the cause; it is a pre-existing condition.\n\nFailing tests (all in `hostThroughPty real round-trip`, `RECYCLE — kill + respawn`, `P-020 carry-respawn drill correlation`, `carry-respawn STALENESS guard`, `RECYCLE respawns with FRESH session args`, `RECYCLE carry-inject is retried across a budget` (x2), `WI-3455 — discovery key ownership + self-heal` (x3)):\n  - creates socket+meta on start, injects into the live child, cleans up on exit\n  - EI-153: REFUSES a control envelope addressed to a DIFFERENT ownerId\n  - replaces the child process, keeps the host alive, opens fresh process on carry-note\n  - records the fresh native id / carry path / first-prompt delivery\n  - a carry-respawn that ages past PAPERCUSP_PSU_PTY_CARRY_STALE_MS is DROPPED\n  - feeds the child the mintRecycleArgs-rewritten argv\n  - RETRIES past a fresh child that stays busy beyond one busy-cap\n  - DROPS LOUDLY when the fresh child never settles\n  - self-heals: recreates a deleted json + re-binds a deleted sock\n  - exit cleanup leaves a SUCCESSOR's registration alone\n  - stands down while a LIVE psu-marked process owns the key\n\nBy contrast, the SIBLING integration file `psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts` (10 tests, also real pty+child-process round-trips exercising the SAME host module) passed 10/10 cleanly in the same run — so this isn't \"real ptys are universally too slow on this box right now,\" it's specific to this ONE file's tests (which spawn a full host via `hostThroughPty`/RECYCLE/discovery flows — heavier setup than the turn-injection tests). Worth investigating whether this file's fixture setup (per-test host boot, `readdirSync`/socket creation, kill+respawn cycles) has a resource leak or a too-tight timeout under concurrent fleet load, rather than assuming it's simply \"the box is busy\" — per repo convention this needs root-causing, not deferring.\n\nNot investigated further here (out of scope for the task in progress + would require dedicated attention to the fixture/timeout tuning). Filing per the \"a suspected bug is always filed\" mandate — this is a real, reproducible, fleet-blocking gate risk if this file is ever load-bearing on a merge gate.",

    {
      "id": "EI-18712854461686945",
      "title": "live-federation-gate local-matrix: frame A sidecar hit 3x SIGTERM in ~1min mid-run (13:02:11-13:03:07 UTC), causing cascading PG death that explains revocation_kcut + attestation_unattested_device FAILs as infra collateral, not code regressions",
      "summary": "Gate run /tmp/live-fed-gate-20260726-083840 (HEAD=4d954e5de9, local-matrix.sh via bin/deb-hetzner-matrix.sh in BYO/docker mode), watched live. 14/17 scenarios PASSED, including replication_soak (order 87, 5x kill/restart cycles clean). Then:\n- revocation_kcut (order 90) FAILED: \"LEAK — F-RV-POST reached banned member B after the ban\". Epoch never advanced past 0 despite the WI-6043 fix's `arm papercusp-hive-rekey` calls both succeeding (confirmed in local-matrix.out: `[a] arm papercusp-hive-rekey → {\"ok\":true,...}` and same for [b]).\n- attestation_unattested_device (order 91, TERMINAL) FAILED: `responder_mismatch=5`.\n\nROOT CAUSE OF *THIS RUN's* failures (not the original WI-6043 bug recurring): frame A's sidecar (serve-a log) shows THREE separate `[serve] SIGTERM — shutting down` events at 13:02:11.121Z, 13:02:45.749Z, 13:03:07.937Z UTC — each followed by a burst of `FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command` / `FATAL: the database system is shutting down` postgres errors (dozens of connections killed per burst). This lands squarely inside revocation_kcut's ban→post-write→assert-absent window, so the owner's own hive-rekey admit operation failed mid-flight (`[hive-rekey] owner admit failed for key=7dc4d1ec: PostgresError: the database system is shutting down`) — which is sufficient on its own to explain both the epoch staying at 0 and the subsequent attestation scenario's failure (same frame, same disrupted PG).\n\nRULED OUT: I initially suspected the well-known EI-9748 cgroup-KillMode class (papercup-staging-api.service DID restart around this time) — checked precisely and it does NOT fit: `journalctl` shows the staging-api `Stopping`/SIGTERM at 09:03:41 EDT (13:03:41 UTC) and `Started` (new instance) at 09:03:48 EDT — i.e. AFTER all 3 of frame A's SIGTERMs (13:02:11-13:03:07 UTC), not before. Coincidental timing, not causal.\nAlso ruled out: `docker events` in the window (13:01-13:04:30 UTC) shows no die/kill/restart/oom event for the rig containers (pcusp-rig-a / pcusp-rig-b / the $NET-a naming) — so docker itself didn't kill the container; something sent SIGTERM to the sidecar PROCESS inside frame A's container without the container itself dying. Mechanism not yet identified (no explicit `--memory` limit is set on these containers by default, so container-level OOM is unlikely too, though host-level pressure wasn't checked).\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS: this is the standing local-release-gate's local-matrix leg, which P-402 (WI-5064) is waiting to see genuinely GREEN as this plan's first-green milestone. A collateral 3x-SIGTERM burst mid-run silently produces a real-looking FAIL (LEAK / responder_mismatch) that is indistinguishable from a genuine regression without exactly this kind of log correlation — a future triage agent could easily misattribute this to a fresh code bug (as I nearly did myself before checking the raw serve.log).\n\nNEXT STEPS for whoever picks this up: (1) identify what's sending SIGTERM directly to the sidecar's PID inside the container (check for a health-check/watchdog with a ~30s retry cadence matching the observed spacing; check host dmesg/journalctl for OOM around 13:02 UTC even without a docker-level event; check if some OTHER routine/cron on this shared host targets sidecar processes by port/name rather than container). (2) Once identified, either fix the trigger or make local-matrix.sh/the sidecar resilient to it. (3) Re-run local-matrix undisturbed to get P-402's genuine first green — 14/17 clean scenarios (incl. the historically-flaky replication_soak) is a strong signal this IS very close.\n\nNot claiming — filing for whoever has the host-level access/time to dig into the SIGTERM source; I've exhausted the log-correlation approach available to me this pass.",

      "id": "EI-18734854451629427",
      "title": "WebSearch tool hard-fails for every query: \"output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is disabled on this model\"",
      "summary": "REPRO (4/4 attempts, 100% failure rate, 2026-07-26 ~19:0x):\nAny `WebSearch { query }` call from a psu Claude Code session running effort=xhigh returns:\n\n    API Error: 400 output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is disabled on this model. Use effort 'high' or below, or enable thinking.\n\nQueries attempted (all failed identically):\n- \"Ornith model how was it trained code LLM\"\n- \"Ornith LLM training data curation announcement 2026\"\n- \"unsloth fine-tuning 2026 features GRPO full finetune multi-GPU\"\n- \"Ornith model training data\"\n\nDIAGNOSIS: WebSearch dispatches its result-summarization to a sub-model, and it appears to\nFORWARD the parent session's `output_config.effort` (xhigh) to that sub-model while the\nsub-model runs with thinking DISABLED. xhigh is only valid when thinking is enabled, so the\nsub-request 400s before any search happens. The parent session's effort setting should NOT\npropagate to the WebSearch summarizer — it should be pinned/clamped (to 'high' or below, or\nthe summarizer should enable thinking).\n\nBLAST RADIUS: every agent session running at effort=xhigh loses WebSearch entirely. This is\nsilent-ish: the failure looks like a transient API error, so agents are likely to retry it a\nfew times and then give up on web research rather than recognize a config bug. Owner set\neffort=xhigh as their DEFAULT for new sessions this session (\"saved as your default for new\nsessions\"), so this affects all their future sessions until fixed.\n\nWORKAROUND (verified working, used to complete the task): drive search through WebFetch\nagainst a text-mode search endpoint, e.g.\n  WebFetch { url: \"https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=<urlencoded query>\",\n             prompt: \"List the search result titles, URLs and snippets.\" }\nWebFetch itself is unaffected (its summarizer path does not inherit the bad effort value),\nwhich further localizes the bug to WebSearch's sub-model request construction.\n\nCORRECT STATE: WebSearch clamps/omits `output_config.effort` for its internal summarizer\ncall (or enables thinking on it), so it works at any parent effort level.</body>\n＜parameter name=\"foundDuring\">researching custom code-model fine-tuning (unsloth) for the owner",

    {
      "id": "EI-18753696723750409",
      "title": "WebSearch is 100% broken in psu Claude sessions at effort=xhigh: \"output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is disabled\"",
      "summary": "## Repro\nIn a psu Claude Code session with effort level set to `xhigh` (via `/effort`), ANY call to the native `WebSearch` tool fails immediately:\n\n```\nAPI Error: 400 output_config.effort 'xhigh' is not supported when thinking is disabled on this model. Use effort 'high' or below, or enable thinking.\n```\n\nReproduced deterministically 3/3 times with different queries. `WebFetch` on the SAME turn works fine, so this is specific to WebSearch's internal model invocation.\n\n## Diagnosis\nWebSearch dispatches to a small/fast summarizer model internally. The session's `output_config.effort` (xhigh) is being propagated to that sub-invocation, but the sub-invocation has thinking disabled — and xhigh is only valid when thinking is enabled. The sub-call should either (a) not inherit the parent session's effort setting, (b) clamp inherited effort to `high` when thinking is off, or (c) enable thinking on the sub-call.\n\n## Impact\nEvery psu session running at the `xhigh` default (which is a saved default for new sessions once a user picks it — the owner's default is now xhigh) has **zero web search capability**. This is silent and total: the agent's only signal is a 400 from the tool. Any research/lookup task in such a session either fails or forces a workaround.\n\n## Workaround (used in this session)\nRoute around WebSearch entirely via `WebFetch` against search/query APIs:\n- arXiv API: `http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=abs:%22...%22&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=40` — works well, returns structured results, WebFetch summarizes them.\n- Semantic Scholar Graph API likewise.\nThis is strictly worse than WebSearch for general-web queries (no ranking over the open web), but it is functional for academic literature.\n\n## Correct state\nWebSearch works at every effort level the session can be set to. If an effort level is genuinely incompatible with a tool's internal sub-model, the clamp belongs in the dispatch layer, not as a 400 handed to the agent.\n",

    {
      "id": "EI-18766620496523988",
      "title": "A self-relaunched claude session loses its model spec, so config:set-compaction-limit silently clamps to the 400k fleet default instead of the model's real 1M ceiling",
      "summary": "## Repro (observed live 2026-07-27, session su-8d9a671c-ccda-4aa9-b4f4-8f0d1c7a4804)\n\n1. A claude session self-relaunches (internal re-exec — TUI fullscreen switch or update relaunch). The `SessionStart` recovery hook fires and states plainly: *\"claude rebuilds argv on relaunch WITHOUT the original launch flags: the `--system-prompt-file` playbook, `--permission-mode`, `--session-id` and any `--disallowedTools` were dropped.\"*\n2. The session is an **Opus 5 (1M context)** session — real model window 1,000,000.\n3. Owner asks to raise the soft compaction limit. Call `config:set-compaction-limit { limit: 900000 }` (900k is the tool's schema maximum; 1,000,000 is rejected by the `maximum` constraint).\n4. Result:\n\n```json\n{\"ok\":true,\"compactionLimit\":400000,\"clamped\":true,\"requested\":900000,\"cap\":400000,\n \"note\":\"requested limit clamped to the model-derived ceiling (model spec unresolvable — fleet-default [1m] ceiling)\"}\n```\n\n**The limit was NOT raised.** It stayed at the 400k fleet default while the session was already at ~110% of it.\n\n## Diagnosis\n\nThe clamp is derived from the target session's resolved model spec. The self-relaunch dropped the launch argv that carries model identification, so the server cannot resolve the model and falls back to the conservative fleet default. The `note` field says exactly this — it is a correct, self-describing failure, it is just applied silently as `ok: true`.\n\nNet effect: **every self-relaunched session is permanently capped at 400k regardless of its real window**, and the only signal is a `clamped: true` flag inside an otherwise-successful response. An agent that does not read the response body closely will believe the limit was raised.\n\n## Why this matters beyond one session\n\n- Self-relaunch is not rare (TUI fullscreen toggle, update relaunch).\n- The failure is *silent* in the sense that matters: `ok: true`, no error, no warning surfaced to the owner.\n- It defeats the one lever an owner has for keeping a long session alive — which is exactly when it is reached for, i.e. the failure lands precisely at the moment it is most costly.\n- Related class: this is the second launch-flag-loss consequence hit in one session (the first being the recovery notice's own list of dropped flags).\n\n## Correct state (do not fix in this session per owner)\n\nOptions, in rough preference order:\n\n1. **Persist the model spec out of argv** — record the session's model at first contact (it is already known to the server on every request) so a relaunch cannot lose it. This fixes the whole class, not just the ceiling.\n2. **Fail loudly instead of clamping silently** when the model is unresolvable and the requested limit exceeds the fallback — return a refusal naming the cause, rather than `ok: true` with a `clamped` flag.\n3. At minimum, surface `clamped: true` + the note as a visible warning to the owner, not just a field in the payload.\n\n## Notes\n\n- `maximum: 900000` on the `limit` arg means a literal 1,000,000 request is impossible even on a healthy 1M session. Worth revisiting alongside the above — an Opus 5 1M session cannot express its own window through this tool.\n- Owner directive: **file only, do not fix from this session** [owner:Avi 2026-07-27].\n",

    {
      "id": "EI-18769415639448677",
      "title": "fed-b has NO pot_members rows for the shared hive it joined (workspace-b31a7a01/octocat-spoon-knife) — so it can admit no peer on that topic; presence is one-directional (WI-559)",
      "summary": "VERIFIED on the live rig 2026-07-27 (WI-559). This is the FUNCTIONAL defect behind WI-559; EI-18769392276881557 is the observability defect that hid it.\n\nMEASUREMENT (both VMs, same instant)\n  fed-a  select workspace_id,pot_home_slug,github_user_id from harness_shared.pot_members\n    papercusp-workspace | papercusp        | 1567022\n    papercusp-workspace | papercusp        | 279242982\n    workspace-319be5e5  | spoon-knife-pot  | 1567022     <- fed-b's device attested here\n    workspace-319be5e5  | spoon-knife-pot  | 279242982\n  fed-b  (same query)\n    papercusp-workspace | papercusp        | 1567022\n    papercusp-workspace | papercusp        | 279242982\n    (NOTHING for workspace-b31a7a01 / octocat-spoon-knife)\n\nfed-b's own wire-presence line binds the shared topic to that missing pair:\n  [wire-presence] wired workspace-b31a7a01::octocat-spoon-knife — gossipWriter=on topic=726696c069e9 pot=octocat-spoon-knife\n\nThe presence-gossip receiver resolves admissibility with listHiveMembers(binding.workspaceId, binding.potHomeSlug) — with zero rows the admitted map is EMPTY, so fed-b drops every presence frame from every peer on that topic, fail-closed. fed-a, holding the mirror rows, admits fed-b normally. Result: presence flows fed-b -> fed-a and never fed-a -> fed-b, which reads like a stale/half-open peer link and is exactly the WI-559 symptom.\n\nWHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN (the next dig, deliberately not asserted)\nWhy fed-b has no membership rows for a hive it demonstrably joined, wired, and broadcasts on. Candidates, unranked and untested:\n - the JOIN path materializes pot_members only on the hive-owner side, never on the joiner;\n - the rows were written under a different workspace_id than the one the binding later uses (each machine names this hive differently — fed-a workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife-pot vs fed-b workspace-b31a7a01/octocat-spoon-knife — so a scope mismatch at write time would leave the read empty);\n - the rows were reaped/never replicated after a VM reset.\nDO NOT conclude from a REPLICATED table which machine authored a row (that error has already burned two hypotheses on WI-559). Establish the write path first.\n\nSuggested guard once fixed: a boot-time (or wire-time) assertion that every topic registered WITH A WRITER also resolves a non-empty admitted member set — a node that can send but can admit nobody is always a misconfiguration.",

      "id": "EI-18770471131012422",
      "title": "fed-a's CURRENT device key is absent from the papercusp hive's 12-device attestation set — its presence frames are rejected on that topic too (second WI-559 cause)",
      "summary": "OBSERVED live 2026-07-27T04:27:05Z on fed-b, in the first beat after the EI-18769392276881557 instrumentation was deployed. This is a SECOND, independent cause of the WI-559 symptom, distinct from EI-18769415639448677 — it was invisible until the receiver started reporting its drops, and I had not predicted it.\n\nTHE OBSERVATION (both lines, same millisecond, two different topics):\n\n  [presence-gossip] REJECTED inbound presence frame on topic d85dc18c0bac… — signer A6zYcYobyL3u… is not an attested device of this hive (12 admitted device(s) known; 1 rejection(s) so far)\n  [presence-gossip] REJECTED inbound presence frame on topic 726696c069e9… — signer A6zYcYobyL3u… is not an attested device of this hive (0 admitted device(s) known; 1 rejection(s) so far)\n\nThe `0 admitted` case is EI-18769415639448677 (empty roster). The `12 admitted` case is this bug: fed-b's roster for the papercusp hive is POPULATED and healthy, and fed-a's frames are still rejected because the key fed-a actually signs with is not in it.\n\nCORROBORATING SQL (fed-a, its own attestation entries):\n  pot_home_slug='spoon-knife-pot', gh 279242982 -> A6zYcYobyL3u8uXH5StFwY7A6BMv7Xi9q8ZET80FMC0=   <- the key it signs with\n  pot_home_slug='papercusp',       gh 279242982 -> 8WR+//h+…, IXfGu216…, UEGDzf2w…, Vk0Rnxv…, bBRIMRjc…   (5 keys, none of them A6zY…)\n\nSo fed-a presents ONE device identity everywhere (correct — the keychain id is per-github-user, not per-hive), but its `papercusp` membership row attests five OTHER keys and never the current one. Both machines hold identical papercusp attestation sets, so this is not a replication gap on fed-b — the attestation was never updated to include the live key.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PRESENCE: the same admitted-device set gates lock authority and runner election, so a machine in this state is not merely invisible — it cannot participate in either.\n\nWHAT TO ESTABLISH FIRST (do not skip; three hypotheses on WI-559 were retracted for concluding from indirect reads):\n1. Whether A6zY… is genuinely fed-a's current device key at signing time (read it from the running operator / keychain, not inferred from the spoon-knife roster row).\n2. Whether the 5 stale keys are prior keychain generations on this VM (VM resets would produce exactly that) or another machine's.\n3. Which write path is supposed to refresh a member's `device_attestations` when a device key appears/rotates, and why it did not fire for the papercusp hive when it evidently did for spoon-knife-pot.\n\nLIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX: attestation refresh must be idempotent and self-healing at announce time — if the key I am about to sign with is not in my own attested set for a hive I am a member of, that is a self-detectable fault the node should repair (or at minimum report loudly) rather than silently sign frames every peer will discard.",

      "id": "EI-18786563572719534",
      "title": "facts:assert fails 100% with \"no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification\" — the one carry surface folded verbatim into every orient is unwritable",
      "summary": "## Symptom\n\nEvery `facts:assert` call returns:\n\n```\nhandler_error: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification\n```\n\nNo write lands. 4 consecutive attempts, 2026-07-27 ~08:35-08:45Z, from session su-e80ad977-8155-413d-ba06-36494ee85032 (harness oddsmith).\n\n## Isolation already done\n\n- NOT input-shape dependent. Fails identically with a full payload (scope/scopeRef/key/body/confidence/sourceRef/ttlSec) AND with the minimal `{ scope:'harness', scopeRef:'oddsmith', key, body }`.\n- NOT scopeRef resolution. Fails with both `oddsmith` and `oddsmith-hive`.\n- NOT a new-key vs upsert difference. Fails when creating a NEW key AND when upserting an EXISTING key (`oddsmith-loops-that-beat-but-never-report-yield`, which this same session wrote successfully ~30 min earlier).\n- READ path is healthy: `facts:list { scope:'harness', scopeRef:'oddsmith' }` returns all 6 live facts normally.\n- Regression window: this session's own facts are stamped `2026-07-27 04:05:44-04` and `04:08:18-04` (ET) and wrote fine. The breakage appeared between then and ~04:35 ET.\n\nSo the fault is in the WRITE/upsert path only, and it is recent.\n\n## Why this is major, not cosmetic\n\n`facts:assert` is the ONLY surface folded VERBATIM into every future brief/orient until retracted — the compaction/carry discipline explicitly instructs agents that a work-item comment does NOT substitute for it, because comments are never folded into orient. So while this is broken:\n\n- every agent's durable conclusions silently fail to reach successors and peers;\n- the failure is LOUD per-call (good) but there is no fallback path in the documented discipline, so an agent following instructions has nowhere compliant to put a conclusion;\n- `slot:'wall'` assertions are also blocked, which is the surface owner-gated blockers are supposed to survive on (and whose absence is explicitly not to be read as resolved).\n\nI routed this wake's conclusion to `memory:remember` (id 621d1201-7054-406a-aeff-74682a626012) plus a `loop:checkpoint` / `work_items:checkpoint` as a workaround, but neither is folded verbatim into orient the way a fact is, so the substitution is lossy.\n\n## Likely cause (a pointer, not a diagnosis — I did not read the platform source)\n\nThe message is Postgres SQLSTATE 42P10: an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (cols)` whose inferred conflict target has no matching unique/exclusion index. Typical triggers: a unique index was dropped/renamed/made partial, or the ON CONFLICT target list drifted from the index definition (e.g. the index is partial `WHERE retracted_at IS NULL` while ON CONFLICT infers a bare column tuple, which Postgres will not match). Worth diffing the facts table's live indexes against the assert statement's conflict target, and checking whether a recent migration altered that index.\n\n## Repro\n\n```\nfacts:assert { scope:'harness', scopeRef:'oddsmith', key:'probe-test', body:'x' }\n→ handler_error: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification\n```",

    {
      "id": "EI-18798652713871439",
      "title": "RELEASE BLOCKER (fix C reachability): adoptRefusedRepoKey has ONE call site, on the bootstrap DIAL path — but the superseded-repo-key refusal actually arrives every tick on the REF-ANNOUNCE receive leg, which only logs it. The self-heal rides in on a channel with no receiver, so the tower<->rig pair cannot heal.",
      "summary": "## The symptom\nThe rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:\n\n```\n[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for\nIXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:\nno git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103\n```\n\nFive of these in a single tick. The correct canonical key `gh-1223568103` is sitting in the error text. Nothing adopts it. The rig's `papercusp.git` still holds ZERO namespaces.\n\n## The root cause — reachability, not logic\n`adoptRefusedRepoKey` is correct and well-guarded. It has exactly ONE production call site:\n\n- `git-sync-action.ts:2034` — inside the BOOTSTRAP leg's dial path.\n\nBut the refusal that carries the repair arrives on a DIFFERENT leg: the ref-announce RECEIVE leg (`git-sync-action.ts:~2345`, the `cursorDecision.fetchFailed` loop). That loop has `f.stderr` containing the verbatim refusal text — and does nothing with it but `console.warn`.\n\nSo the one channel on which the repair reliably and repeatedly arrives is the one channel that cannot act on it.\n\n## Why this is the mirror image of fix D\nFix D's own comment (git-sync-action.ts:1839) says the probe must sit ABOVE the warm gate because \"a probe placed after the gate would never fire on precisely the machine that needs it: the stuck one.\" Fix C has the same defect in a different dimension: its receiver is on the cold-join path, so it never runs on the machine whose ref-announce leg is the thing actually dialing.\n\n## The fix\nCall `adoptRefusedRepoKey` from the ref-announce receive leg's fetchFailed handler, using `f.stderr` — the same fail-soft, next-tick-effective contract the bootstrap call site already uses. Adoption is idempotent (`already-canonical` is a clean no-op on every later refused dial), so calling it from both legs is safe by construction.\n\n## Broader lesson (worth keeping)\nA REFUSAL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN REPAIR ONLY HEALS IF EVERY LEG THAT CAN RECEIVE IT KNOWS HOW TO READ IT. Wiring the receiver into one leg makes the feature look done and tested while leaving it inert on the live path.",

      "id": "EI-18859147091614600",
      "title": "Dev box can't reach papercusp.com or flags.papercuspai.com — both resolve to one IP whose TLS never completes, and the /etc/hosts pin's comment names a stale origin",
      "summary": "SYMPTOM (cost ~20min on WI-6556, and it is silent — TCP connects, so it looks like a hang, not a block):\nFrom this dev box, `curl https://papercusp.com/...` and `curl https://flags.papercuspai.com/...` (PostHog) both hang until timeout. TCP connect SUCCEEDS on port 443; the TLS handshake never completes (`time_appconnect` never advances). Anthropic's WebFetch also gets ECONNRESET on papercusp.com, so it is not purely a local-egress story.\n\nEVIDENCE:\n  dig +short papercusp.com          @1.1.1.1 -> 18.204.152.241\n  dig +short flags.papercuspai.com  @1.1.1.1 -> 18.204.152.241   # SAME IP\nTwo unrelated hostnames resolving to one IP whose TLS hangs is the signature of a DNS sinkhole / interception on this host, not of either site being down. Both sites are in fact fine for real visitors.\n\nSECOND, INDEPENDENT TRAP — a stale IP in a workaround comment:\n  /etc/hosts:10  127.0.0.1 flags.papercuspai.com  # EI-16742 workaround -> SSH tunnel to PostHog box 178.156.254.244 (remove to revert)\nThe pin sends the hostname to a dead local tunnel, AND the origin IP named in its own comment (178.156.254.244) no longer answers TLS either. So an agent who does the obvious thing — read the comment, bypass the pin with `curl --resolve <host>:443:178.156.254.244` — lands on a second dead end and reasonably concludes PostHog is down. I did exactly this. Neither IP works; the comment actively misleads.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TASK: any agent verifying analytics, or verifying that a public-site deploy went live, will hit this and can wrongly conclude the SITE or PostHog is broken (a false outage report to the owner is the real risk — a previous agent's PostHog-unreachable finding nearly went to the owner as a product problem when it is purely a dev-box condition).\n\nTHE WORKAROUND THAT DOES WORK, for the next agent:\n  - Verify a Pages deploy via the deployment-specific URL (https://<id>.papercusp-com.pages.dev) — reachable from here, runs the identical Function with identical secret bindings.\n  - Confirm the custom domain authoritatively via the Cloudflare API rather than by fetching it:\n      GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<acct>/pages/projects/papercusp-com\n      -> result.domains[] and result.latest_deployment.aliases[]\n  - Do NOT trust the 178.156.254.244 in the hosts comment.\n\nDURABLE FIX (needs a decision I did not want to make unilaterally on a shared box):\n  1. Establish whether the sinkhole is deliberate (sandbox network policy) or accidental. If accidental, fix the resolver.\n  2. Either restore the EI-16742 tunnel or REMOVE the /etc/hosts line so the hostname resolves publicly — the line is currently pure breakage for every agent on the box.\n  3. At minimum, correct the stale IP in that comment, or delete the IP from it so nobody follows it into a dead end.",

      "id": "EI-19304900200711901",
      "title": "No audited escape hatch lets an agent session run a destructive git op on a provably-throwaway tree (deploy-path testing) — NOT the -C bug I first filed; see correction",
      "summary": "## What happened\nWhile validating the root fix for EI-19299565558496583 (gate submodule blindness) I needed to confirm that `setup-release-checkout.sh`'s step-1 `git reset --hard` / `git clean -fdqx` do not destroy real submodule repos. I ran both against **my own throwaway probe worktree** at `/home/marsh-office/tmp-submodule-probe`, explicitly scoped with `git -C \"$PROBE\" …`. Both were blocked by the shared-tree guard:\n\n- `git -C \"$PROBE\" reset --hard <sha>` → blocked\n- `git -C \"$PROBE\" clean -fdqx -e node_modules` → blocked\n\nThe guard's message is about \"the shared staging checkout\", but neither command targeted it — `-C` pointed at a disposable worktree I created seconds earlier.\n\n## Why it matters\nThe guard is RIGHT to be conservative and I did not route around it (I dropped the test — the script's ordering makes it moot, since step 2 `rm -rf`s and re-creates every submodule path after step 1). But the consequence is a real capability gap: **the deploy path is the one part of this repo whose correctness depends on `reset --hard` + `clean -fdqx` semantics, and it is now the one part an agent cannot empirically test.** `setup-release-checkout.sh` performs exactly these operations by design (they are correct there — it is a throwaway tree, D-004). Anyone modifying that script must reason about their behaviour instead of running it, which is precisely the \"think harder instead of running something\" failure mode that has cost this fleet repeatedly.\n\n## Evidence\nTwo consecutive blocks in this session, both `-C`-scoped to `/home/marsh-office/tmp-submodule-probe`, a worktree created via `git worktree add --detach` and not the canonical staging tree.\n\n## Suggested durable fix\nResolve the command's EFFECTIVE target before matching, rather than matching the command string:\n- parse `-C <dir>` (and a leading `cd <dir> &&`) to get the cwd, then `git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel`\n- block only when that toplevel IS the canonical staging tree\n- allow it (or warn) for any other worktree\n\nThat keeps the 2026-06-21 protection exactly as strong for the case it exists to prevent, while unblocking legitimate deploy-path testing. If full path resolution is judged too risky, a narrower version — allow when `-C`/cwd resolves under a path the caller created in this session, or an explicit `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_THROWAWAY_TREE_RESET=1` opt-out naming the tree — would also close it.\n\n## Cross-ref\nSurfaced while working EI-19299565558496583. Not a blocker for that item.</body>\n＜/invoke>\n",

      "id": "EI-19325938692618472",
      "title": "lint:tsc labelled a CLEAN file as \"COMMITTED: a standing red that WILL red the fleet\" — a false alarm that sends an agent chasing a phantom gate blocker",
      "summary": "## What happened\n\nTwo `npm run lint:tsc -- --files=...` runs ~4 minutes apart, same shared tree, disagreed about which file carries a committed standing red — and the first one named a file that is fine.\n\n**Run 1** (07:33Z) reported, unprompted and in alarming terms:\n\n```\n⚠ 1 file(s) fail to COMPILE (TS1xxx parse errors) ... \n  - packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/messages.ts\npackages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/messages.ts: 0 → 2  (+2)  ← COMMITTED: a standing red that WILL red the fleet\n```\n\nI acted on it, because that wording is a direct call to action and the fleet gate was one file from green at the time — a genuine committed parse error would have re-redded it.\n\n**It was false.** `git status --porcelain` on that path: empty (clean). Targeted re-run naming it explicitly:\n\n```\nTSC operator-core: 30 type errors across 1 file(s) [--files]\n✓ Your changed files are tsc-clean.\n⚠ 1 file(s) fail to COMPILE ... - packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/delivery-ladder-sweep.ts\ndelivery-ladder-sweep.ts: 0 → 30  (+30)  ← uncommitted, a peer is likely mid-edit\n```\n\nSo the real parse error was in a DIFFERENT file, and correctly classified the second time as *uncommitted, peer mid-edit* — the opposite disposition, requiring the opposite response (leave it alone vs. own it now).\n\n## Why it matters more than a cosmetic mislabel\n\nThe two labels are an ACTION FORK, and the tool states them with equal confidence:\n- `COMMITTED: a standing red that WILL red the fleet` ⇒ *this is yours, fix it now* (the persona treats a red gate as the reader's to green).\n- `uncommitted, a peer is likely mid-edit` ⇒ *hands off, do not collide.*\n\nA false COMMITTED sends an agent to hunt a phantom blocker in a file that is fine, and — worse on a shared tree — invites it to \"fix\" a file a peer is actively editing. I spent ~4 tool calls on the phantom before the second run contradicted the first.\n\n## Suspected mechanism (UNCONFIRMED)\n\nThe tool's own caveat is probably the cause: *\"tsc's counts for other files may be incomplete while these stay broken\"*. A TS1xxx parse error anywhere appears to corrupt attribution for other files, and the committed/uncommitted classifier then renders that corrupted attribution as a confident verdict rather than as unknown. Note the honest part is already there for the NAMED set (`--files` scoping is respected and was correct both times) — the defect is in the volunteered commentary about files the caller did NOT name.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nWhen any TS1xxx parse error is present, the committed/uncommitted verdict for files OUTSIDE the named set is not trustworthy — degrade it to an explicit \"cannot attribute while N file(s) fail to parse\" rather than emitting `COMMITTED: ... WILL red the fleet`. Same principle as the fail-closed probe in WI-6962: a determination that could not be made must not render identically to one that was.\n\n## Related\n\nAdjacent already-filed lint:tsc `--files` defects: EI-19321179234197157 (hard-fails on a TS1xxx parse error in ANY file, breaking the documented `--files` scoping) and EI-19321397364088260 (the TS1xxx hard-fail path is not scoped by --files). This is a third, distinct symptom of the same parse-error blast radius: not a hard-fail, but a confidently WRONG attribution.",

      "id": "EI-19326920187717512",
      "title": "A terminal close leaves closed_ts NULL on the sibling physical row — the same work-item id is stored TWICE under two harness_slug scopes (44 dupes measured on one title class)",
      "summary": "MEASURED 2026-08-02 while collapsing duplicate [replication-liveness] EIs (WI-6986).\n\n## The finding\n`harness_shared.work_items` stores the SAME logical work-item id as TWO physical rows under two different `harness_slug` values — `'papercusp'` and `'operator:papercusp-workspace'`.\n\nEvidence, scoped to one title class (title LIKE '[replication-liveness]%'):\n  total_rows=557, distinct feature_id=513  →  44 physical duplicate rows, harness_scopes=2\n\n## The defect\nA terminal close via `work_items:set_state` updates BOTH physical rows — `status`, `terminal_owner`, and `terminal_completion_ref` are stamped on each — but sets **`closed_ts` on only ONE**. After closing 29 open rows I was left with:\n  - 29 rows: status='dropped', closed_ts SET\n  - 25 rows: status='dropped', terminal_owner=me, terminal_completion_ref=<mine>, **closed_ts IS NULL**\nAll 25 confirmed to be from that single action (same updated_ts minute, completion ref contains 'WI-6986').\n\n## Why it matters\nAny hygiene, reporting, burn-down, or age query that keys on `closed_ts` (rather than `status`) will mis-classify these rows as never-closed — silently, and with a well-formed plausible answer. Same failure shape as the severity-accessor trap already documented in CLAUDE.md: the wrong column for the relation returns a wrong answer without erroring.\n\n## How I hit it\nCounting my own work: open rows fell 88→59 (=29) while 54 rows carried me as terminal_owner. The 25-row gap is exactly the sibling-row set. An agent trusting either number alone would have reported a wrong figure.\n\n## Not root-caused\nI did NOT determine whether the dual-scope storage is intentional (a projection/tenant artifact) or itself a bug. Two questions for whoever picks this up:\n1. Is the same feature_id under two harness_slug scopes legitimate, or is the 'operator:papercusp-workspace' row a stale/duplicate write?\n2. If legitimate, the close path must stamp closed_ts on every physical row — or closed_ts must be documented as unreliable and every consumer moved to `status`.\n\nUnverified beyond the one title class I measured; the 44-dupe figure is for that class only, not the whole table.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19331207103319339",
      "title": "Republishing an Artifact after a carry-respawn forces a full-page WebFetch, because the compaction gives the logical session a new native session id",
      "summary": "## What happened\n\nWake at 08:51Z, continuing work on an Artifact this same logical su session published ~05:00Z. Called `Artifact { file_path, url }` to update it in place and got:\n\n> This session hasn't viewed the latest version of the artifact. Read it first (WebFetch the URL), reapply your edits, then publish.\n\nThe guard is correct in intent — it prevents clobbering another session's concurrent edits. But the \"other session\" here **was me**: the pre-compaction leg of the same logical session, same coord ownerId (`su-5b23300b-…`), same loop, same work. A `session:request-compaction` carry-respawn relaunches the CLI under a NEW native session id, so from the Artifact tool's perspective the publisher and the updater are different sessions.\n\n## The cost\n\nThe forced `WebFetch` re-fetches the whole artifact — 238 KB in this case — to satisfy a viewership check on a page whose local source file I had never stopped holding and had just edited. The fetch returned the full frame-runtime preamble and the embedded base64 font before any content, i.e. the expensive part is entirely non-informational.\n\nThis is not a one-off: any long-running artifact-producing session crosses at least one compaction, so the second and every subsequent publish pays it.\n\n## Why it is worth fixing rather than routing around\n\nThe workaround (`force: true`) is exactly the wrong instinct to train — it is the flag that genuinely discards a peer's work, and reaching for it to resolve \"I am not myself anymore\" makes it habitual for the case where it is dangerous.\n\n## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)\n\nViewership/ownership should key off something that survives a carry-respawn. The coord ownerId is stable across the whole respawn chain and is already the key `sessions:search { session:'self' }` uses to reach pre-compaction transcripts (WI-5644/WI-5681) — so a session whose ownerId matches the last publisher's is arguably the same publisher. Failing that, a cheaper satisfying read than a full-page WebFetch (a version/etag check, or a hash of the last-published bytes) would remove the cost without weakening the guard.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Refusal observed 2026-08-02 ~08:56Z, artifact `78d597ee-9a24-4f5d-86e4-afd40f949fd9`.\n- Same session: `coord:orient` recovery block reports `selfSession.sessionId 00a0c27b-…` while the artifact was published pre-compaction under a different native id; `control.provenance.ownerId` is unchanged.\n- WebFetch of the URL succeeded and the subsequent identical publish call went through, confirming the only blocker was the viewership check.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19333405389004417",
      "title": "work_items:claim refuses not_claimable on a locally-filed item stamped origin:'remote' — the filer cannot claim the item it is actively fixing",
      "summary": "REPRO (observed 2026-08-02 09:33Z, su-e15fb42f):\n\n    work_items:claim { id: 'WI-7014', harness: 'papercusp' }\n    -> { ok: false, error: 'not_claimable',\n         workItem: { id:'WI-7014', state:'open', assignee:null },\n         hint: 'Item exists but the claim was refused by a trust/admission gate,\n                or it was released between the claim and this re-read' }\n\nSTATE AT REFUSAL: state='open', assignee=null, no _claimHold visible on the payload, and `assignedBy` is MY OWN ownerId (su-e15fb42f) — i.e. I filed it. The item's `origin` is **'remote'**.\n\nWHY THAT LOOKS WRONG: WI-7014 was filed from this box by me at 09:10:00Z for a local gate-blocking tsc strand, and I had already fixed and committed it (cc375043ee, 09:15:47Z). Nothing about it is remote. Per the repo docs, remote-origin is one of the two structural exclusions behind `admissibleOnly` — so an item mis-stamped `origin:'remote'` becomes permanently unclaimable through the normal path by the very agent that filed and is working it.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COSMETICS: the playbook requires holding a work-item before a code edit. An unclaimable item forces exactly the wrong behaviors — either editing with no claim held (invisible lane, so a peer duplicates the work), or filing a SECOND item for work that already has one. This is not hypothetical: while I held no claim, a peer independently filed EI-19331709872526777 for the identical bug and claimed it at 09:24:00Z, 8 minutes after my fix was already committed. An unclaimable item is a duplicate-work generator.\n\nWHAT I COULD NOT DETERMINE:\n- Whether `origin:'remote'` is the actual refusal reason, or merely correlated. The error is a bare `not_claimable` with a hint listing two possibilities and no discriminator — it does not say WHICH gate refused, nor on what field. That is itself the fixable part: a claim refusal should name the gate and the offending field, the way `scheduler:get_next` returns an `excludedBreakdown`.\n- How WI-7014 came to be stamped `origin:'remote'` at all. I did not capture the exact creation call.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX (two parts, the first is the cheap one):\n1. Make `not_claimable` self-diagnosing — return the specific floor that refused (`{ refusedBy: 'admission:remote-origin', field: 'origin', value: 'remote' }`). Today the agent cannot tell a trust gate from a claim race without guessing.\n2. Investigate why a locally-filed work-item receives `origin:'remote'`; if the stamp is wrong, fix the creation path — and if it is right, the remote-origin admission floor should still admit the item's own filer.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19395667449143812",
      "title": "Vite HMR \"RegistryDuplicateError: duplicate command id\" false-positives operator e2e console-error assertions under concurrent shared-tree edits",
      "summary": "Found while verifying EI-19373923898562595 (operator e2e ~19% red suite fix). Re-ran e2e/adv-shell-nav.spec.ts + e2e/agent-tools.spec.ts on a fresh isolated Vite dev server (OPERATOR_E2E_PORT=13101) — isolated by PORT, but the Vite server still watches the SAME shared repo tree that the whole fleet edits concurrently. 6/32 tests failed; 4 of them with an identical signature unrelated to app logic:\n\n```\n[vite] RegistryDuplicateError: duplicate command id: navigate\n  at register (packages/operator-core/lib/commands/registry.ts:23:30)\n  at packages/operator-core/lib/commands/defs/nav.ts:33:1\n[vite] Failed to reload /src/routes/__root.tsx. This could be due to syntax errors or importing non-existent modules.\n```\n\nRoot cause: `registry.ts`'s `register()` throws RegistryDuplicateError when a command id is already in the module-level `defs` Map (by design, to catch real dev bugs). Under Vite HMR, when a peer agent commits/saves a file elsewhere in the shared tree during a live e2e run, Vite invalidates and re-executes `nav.ts` (which calls `register()` at module load) while the `defs` Map singleton in `registry.ts` survives the reload (HMR module-boundary mismatch) — so re-registration throws, breaking the SPA's live-reload and cascading into a `console.error` that trips the e2e suite's `scrubConsoleErrors(consoleErrors).toEqual([])` assertions on unrelated tests (calendar/harnesses/health/frames deep-link tests, More-menu selection, ?scope=all — none of which touch the command registry).\n\nImpact: adds environmental e2e flake on this heavily-parallel shared-tree box, on top of the already-documented CPU-load flake (WI-5603) — a *different* failure signature (HMR module-invalidation race, not timeout/load), so triage that only checks for load correlation will misattribute these as genuine app regressions. Two of the 6 failures I saw (More-menu click timeout, ?scope=all duplicate \"Git\" element) are plausibly downstream of the same double-registration/double-mount, though not confirmed.\n\nSuggested fix direction: either make `register()` idempotent under HMR (e.g. `import.meta.hot.dispose` to clear `defs` before re-registration, or key registration off `import.meta.hot.data`), or have the e2e console-error scrubber (`scrubConsoleErrors`) ignore `[vite]` HMR-channel messages the way it already scrubs other known-noisy patterns.\n\nNot independently fixed by me — filing so it doesn't get re-diagnosed as a fresh app bug by the next agent triaging operator e2e reds.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19415309774723126",
      "title": "46 applied migrations have EXECUTABLE drift — DDL edited in after apply that never ran on the live DB (measurable for the first time)",
      "summary": "Filed as a FINDING, not work I did. EI-19408574209859155 shipped a classifier splitting migration `contentDrift` into `executable` (real half-landed migration) vs `comments-only` (benign). Running it against the live DB produced a number nobody had measured.\n\n## Measurement (2026-08-03, canonical staging tree vs live schema_migrations)\n\n```\nraw contentDrift : 68 applied migrations whose disk bytes != recorded sha256\n  executable     : 46   <- executable SQL differs; the edit never ran and never will\n  comments-only  : 17   <- provably benign\n  unclassified   :  5   <- applied bytes unrecoverable from git\n```\n\nReproduce: `db:check_drift` (now opts into classification), or `checkMigrationDrift({ classifyContent: true })`.\n\n## Verified, not assumed\n\nSpot-checked `151-operator-curation.sql` against the exact applied blob (`958f6da4bc83`, found by sha256-matching git history):\n\n```\n+GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON harness_shared.operator_curation_log TO harness_app;\n+DO $z$ BEGIN\n+  GRANT SELECT ON harness_shared.operator_curation_log TO harness_zero;\n```\n\nReal executable DDL added after the migration was recorded. Those GRANTs have never run here and never will.\n\nIndependent validation the classifier is not over-reporting: **`708-federate-work-item-authority.sql` is in the executable list** — the documented mig-708 hazard (EI-19365742982915607) the detector was originally built for, now identified by name rather than by hand.\n\n## NOT established\n\n- **Per-file severity.** I verified the classification is correct; I did NOT audit what each divergence costs. Several look like later-added \"(Repeatable.)\" GRANT blocks — real but low impact. Others may matter. This needs triage, not alarm.\n- **`000-baseline.sql` is a known false-positive class** — frozen/generated, regenerated by `pull-schema.mjs`, so it drifts by design. It should probably be excluded from contentDrift entirely.\n- The federated-column-completeness suite cannot catch any of this: it applies `sql/` to a FRESH testcontainer, so it validates the FILES no matter how far the live DB has diverged.\n\n## The 5 unclassified\n\nAll report `no blob in the last 1 commit(s)` — the file has exactly one commit, so the applied bytes were never committed separately (edited inside the git-sync window). Correctly counted as hazardous rather than benign.\n\n## Suggested next steps\n\n1. Exclude `000-baseline.sql` from contentDrift.\n2. Triage the remaining 45 by what the un-run DDL was — GRANTs vs columns vs constraints. GRANTs are cheap to re-apply idempotently in one new migration.\n3. Consider whether a periodic `contentDriftExecutable` check belongs in the watchdog. Deliberately NOT wired there today: classification costs a git walk (measured 12.9s for 68 files), see the cost note on `CheckMigrationDriftOptions.classifyContent`.",

      "id": "EI-19422786985734858",
      "title": "overwatch/watchdog.ts brain alerts address a concrete per-wake owner with NO durable slot fallback — the same class WI-2187/WI-963 fixed for the Mug, one role over",
      "summary": "Found while verifying WI-2187 (now closed: the Mug half is fully fixed). The Mug nudge path learned this lesson — wakeMug (pot/placement-watchdog.ts:996-1043) ALWAYS parks to the durable '@role:mug' slot OUTSIDE the `if (opts.mugOwner)` guard, so a stale/ended owner can never be the only delivery route. The overwatch brain-alert path did not.\n\nSITES: packages/operator-core/lib/overwatch/watchdog.ts:104-118 (alertMissingStartedOverwatch) and :133-157 (alertOverwatchLongStale). Both do:\n  const owner = await resolveBrainOwner(workspaceId).catch(() => null);\n  if (!owner) return;\n  await wakeRecipients([owner], {...})\nwith the whole body in a try/catch that degrades to console.warn.\n\nWHY IT IS A REAL GAP (not just style): resolveBrainOwner (harness/routines/wake-brain-action.ts:27) returns the coord_owner_id of whatever session getBrainSession(workspaceId) currently points at. Better than a stale snapshot, but still a CONCRETE per-wake id: if that brain session has ENDED (or re-launched under a new coord owner before the pointer updates), wakeRecipients resolves nothing, the catch swallows it as a warn, and the alert is LOST WITH NO DURABLE PARK. There is no '@role:'-style slot for the brain, so nothing drains it into the next brain wake.\n\nWHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: alertOverwatchLongStale is WI-3777's dead-cadence alarm, which exists precisely because scorecards:freshness masks a dead cadence. It is naturally debounced to fire ONCE per outage (comment at :130-131: once armed, live.armed is true next tick so it never re-fires for the same outage). So a single lost delivery is a PERMANENT loss of that outage's only signal — and the moment it is most likely to be lost (the session/brain layer is unhealthy) is exactly the moment it is most needed. Same shape for the missing-harness self-clear alert, which reports an irreversible state change.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX (small, reuses the existing seam — no new mechanism): give the brain the same treatment as the Mug — a BRAIN_COORD_SLOT ('@role:brain' or equivalent) parked unconditionally alongside the best-effort direct wake, drained by the brain's launch/brief gather the way pot/mug-brief-launch.ts:28 + :136 drains '@role:mug' via drainSlotMessages. severe-event-owner.ts:36-39 already establishes '@role:<slot>' as the fleet's ONE addressing convention to reuse rather than inventing a second scheme.\n\nCONFIDENCE: not blocking; I observed nothing broken live. Evidence is static (source read during the WI-2187 verification pass), so treat the runtime-loss claim as reasoned-from-source, not measured.",

      "id": "EI-19447868110362941",
      "title": "pg_read_all_stats is ASSUMED by every pg_stat_activity reader but asserted at runtime by only ONE — a deployment missing migration 733 goes silently blind fleet-wide",
      "summary": "## The gap\nEvery functional `pg_stat_activity` reader connects via `getOrgPg()` (`harness_admin`) and is CORRECT only because migration **733** granted `pg_read_all_stats` to that role. Load-bearing for: the single-primary guard (R4-2), coord furnace forensics (`gatherCoordLogActiveOffenders`), `dev-data` pgHealth/pgActiveQueries (hence the infra health panel via `compute.ts`), `pg-bounded-txn`'s blocker-hint, `db-index-bloat-reindex`.\n\n**Nothing asserts it at runtime except one function.** `countBackgroundPrimaries()` (single-primary-check.ts) checks `pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_read_all_stats','member')` and returns `null` (\"I could not look\") instead of `0`. Every OTHER reader degrades silently: PG masks other roles' backends rather than erroring — `query` → '<insufficient privilege>', `application_name` → NULL — so predicates over those columns match nothing and return a well-formed, permanent, WRONG zero.\n\n## Not theoretical\nMigration 733's own header records the sibling incident: 108 of 403 backends (~27%) carried `query='<insufficient privilege>'`, silently breaking a BINDING caller-attribution method (60 samples → 0 hits for a statement pg_stat_statements proved was firing ~2.9/s). EI-19442084790376701 is the ~10h false page from the same mechanism.\n\nOn any deployment where 733 is unapplied — fresh embedded-pg, a new pot, a restored/parallel DB — **all readers go blind AT ONCE, silently, each reporting a confident zero.** Maximally correlated, no error anywhere.\n\n## Proposed durable fix\nAssert the capability ONCE at boot/system-health (escalate loudly if `current_user` lacks `pg_read_all_stats`), converting an invisible fleet-wide false-zero into one actionable signal. Replicating the pg_has_role check per-reader is strictly worse — same invisible coupling, N times.\n\n## Explicitly NOT covered by the new static guard\n`packages/operator-core/lib/pg-stat-activity-role-visibility-guard.test.ts` stops a FUTURE reader being wired to the app role. It cannot see a MISSING GRANT at runtime. That is this item.",
