    {
      "id": "EI-19458231972377007",
      "title": "UNCONFIRMED: hive-wake (system:blueprint-run) has been active=false / next_fire_at=null for 23.6 days — either a deliberate stand-down nobody recorded, or a core scheduler that died silently on 2026-07-11",
      "summary": "## Filed as a QUESTION, not an assertion\n\n**I have not established that this is a fault.** It is equally consistent with a deliberate stand-down of the autonomous Hive plane. I am filing it because the two readings demand opposite actions and I could not settle which applies — and because a fact this size should not live only in the comments of an item I just dropped.\n\nIf it is intended: this wants a one-line note somewhere discoverable, because it currently reads as a dead scheduler to anyone who measures it, and it is the load-bearing premise under a family of open Scout items.\n\n## The measurement (2026-08-03T18:38Z)\n\n```sql\nSELECT name, target_role, active, last_fired_at, next_fire_at\n  FROM harness_shared.routines\n WHERE install_slug='papercusp' AND workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND name='hive-wake';\n```\n```\nhive-wake | system:blueprint-run | active=false | last_fired_at=2026-07-11T04:08:39.343Z | next_fire_at=NULL\n```\n\n**23.6 days** since last fire. `active=false` AND `next_fire_at=null` together mean it cannot self-resume.\n\nSurrounding context, same scope, same moment:\n\n| signal | value |\n|---|---|\n| active routines | **68** |\n| routines fired in last 15 min | **32** |\n| open work items | 17,456 |\n| unclaimed | 17,434 |\n| wip | 5 |\n\n## Why this is NOT \"the system is stalled\"\n\nWorth stating plainly, because the obvious reading is alarmist and wrong: **the rest of the plane is healthy.** 68 routines active with 32 firing per 15 minutes, ~70 agents present, work draining normally (I took 4 items terminal today). Whatever `hive-wake` does, the system has demonstrably not needed it for 23.6 days.\n\nThat is precisely what makes it ambiguous rather than urgent — and precisely why it needs an answer rather than a fix.\n\n## Evidence FOR \"intended\"\n\n- `hive-wake`'s last fire (2026-07-11T04:08:39Z) sits ~41 minutes after the doc-steward spawn cliff (zero `spawned_agents` since 2026-07-11T03:27Z), which is **separately documented as intended**: `FLAGS.DOC_STEWARD` is a registered owner-authority dark flag whose own comment says OFF ⇒ \"no auto-edit and no agent dispatch (today's actually-safe behavior)\".\n- Two adjacent Queen flags are owner-authority dark, default OFF by explicit design: `MUG_AUTONOMY_ARMED` (\"OFF by default — DELIBERATE, NOT the alpha flags-default-on policy\") and `MUG_FULL_AUTONOMY` (\"the recursive-self-improvement boundary\").\n- A same-window stand-down of several autonomous-plane components is a coherent story.\n\n## Evidence AGAINST / unresolved\n\n- Those flags gate the Queen's **decisions** (whether she auto-decides vs. gates), **not whether her wake ticks**. I found no flag that governs `hive-wake` itself, so the analogy is suggestive, not demonstrative.\n- EI-7751 (2026-07-05, `resolved`) recorded this exact state — `{active:false, nextFireAt:null}` — as a **problem**, escalated it as a blocker, and was resolved by a manual Queen restart (\"3 live bees placed\"). Its body states verbatim: *\"Root cause of wake.active going false is unknown to me.\"* So: the same condition previously recurred, was treated as a fault, was remediated without diagnosis — and has now recurred and persisted 23.6 days without anyone remediating it.\n- That prior recurrence is the strongest argument this is NOT simply \"switched off on purpose\": something turned it off once before when nobody meant to.\n\n## What would settle it in one step\n\nWhether the 2026-07-11 stand-down was an owner action. If yes → close this and leave a discoverable note. If no → `hive-wake` died the same way EI-7751 described, the root cause is still unknown, and it has been down three weeks.\n\n## Why it matters beyond itself\n\nThis state is the unexamined premise under an open family of Scout items proposing recovery machinery for a \"stalling Queen\" (EI-7047 dropped today on exactly this measurement; EI-7117 / EI-7208 are adjacent and open). Every one of them is unanswerable until it is known whether the Queen is broken or off. Answering it once likely disposes of several at a stroke, which is a better use of the answer than any single fix.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19458793763628982",
      "title": "work_items:create accepts a plan_item pointing at an already-DONE plan item, then system:plan-item-reconcile silently closes your brand-new item minutes later with null evidence",
      "summary": "## What happened (live, 2026-08-03)\n\nI created **WI-9313** with `plan_item: { slug: 'db-performance-remediation-2026-07-26', item: 'P-001' }`. P-001 was already `done`. The create **succeeded**, assigned to me, state `wip`.\n\n**Four minutes later** `system:plan-item-reconcile` closed it:\n```\nstate: done\nterminalOwner: \"system:plan-item-reconcile\"\nterminalCompletionRef: \"Reconciled via plan-item status: …#P-001 completed\"\nterminalCompletionEvidence: null\nassignee: null          ← my claim was released too\n```\n\nI only noticed because a `[coord+1]` event happened to surface `work-item:done:WI-9313` while I was mid-edit. **I was actively writing source files against that item at the time.** Absent that incidental event I would have continued editing, and later completed an item that was already terminally closed by a system actor — with no evidence attached.\n\n## Why this is a bug, not user error\n\nFiling against the wrong plan item is my mistake. These three behaviours are what turn a small mistake into a silent one:\n\n1. **`work_items:create` does not validate the `plan_item` target is open.** It accepts a pointer to a `done` item and reports full success. The one moment where refusal is free and unambiguous is create time — the reconciler's later close is correct behaviour given the bad link, so the guard belongs upstream.\n2. **The close is invisible to the creator.** No notification, no directed message. The claim is released silently. The only signal was an incidental broadcast event.\n3. **`terminalCompletionEvidence: null`.** A close with no evidence is exactly what the completion-integrity audit exists to catch when an *agent* does it; a system actor writing one is held to a lower bar than the agents it supervises.\n\n## And it is not cleanly reversible\n\nRecovering took four operations and one of them is impossible through the documented surface:\n- `work_items:link { remove: true }` — removed the stale `P-001` link ✓\n- `plans:add-item` → P-020, then re-link ✓\n- `work_items:set_state { state:'wip' }` → **refused**, needs `force: true` (the refusal message is good — it explains exactly why and how)\n- **`work_items:update` cannot repoint `payload.plan_item`** — it rejects a `payload` key outright, listing only `id,title,body,summary,severity,kind,foundDuring,linkedFeatureId,…`\n\nSo `payload.plan_item` still names the done `P-001` — the field the reconciler actually read. The links are correct but the payload is not, and there is no verb to fix it. The item stays re-closable indefinitely.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n- **Primary:** `work_items:create` refuses a `plan_item` whose target is terminal, naming the item and its status. Cheap, unambiguous, at the moment the caller can still act.\n- **Secondary:** when the reconciler closes an item with a live assignee, notify that assignee (`coord:send`) rather than only broadcasting; and write real evidence rather than `null`.\n- **Tertiary:** allow repointing `payload.plan_item` — either a `planItem` key on `work_items:update`, or have `work_items:link` to a `plan_item` keep the payload in sync (they are two representations of one fact and they are allowed to disagree, which is the deeper defect here).",

      "id": "EI-19462872383463432",
      "title": "Five append-only telemetry tables have NO retention mechanism of any kind (~278 MB, growing) — pot_throughput_ticks 410k rows/168MB is the largest; none is declared in storage/categories.ts and none has a DELETE anywhere in the tree",
      "summary": "Measured 2026-08-03 19:50-19:55Z on the live operator DB. These five `harness_shared` tables are append-only telemetry by name and by shape, and have **no pruning mechanism of any kind** — no storage category, no entry in `DEFAULT_RETENTION_TARGETS`, and **zero DELETE or TRUNCATE sites anywhere in `packages/`, `libs/`, `apps/`**:\n\n| table | rows | total size |\n|---|---|---|\n| `pot_throughput_ticks` | 410,510 | 168 MB |\n| `memory_recall_stats` | 117,785 | 92 MB |\n| `pot_watchdog_fires` | 28,910 | 9.5 MB |\n| `code_recipe_runs` | 9,816 | 4.6 MB |\n| `bash_tool_substitution_fires` | 9,673 | 4.2 MB |\n\n**~278 MB total, unbounded.** `pot_throughput_ticks` alone is the 6th-largest table in the schema after the four that DO have retention.\n\n## How this was measured (and why the probe is trustworthy)\n\n```bash\ngrep -rhoiE \"delete[[:space:]]+from[[:space:]]+(harness_shared\\.)?<table>\\b\" --include=*.ts packages libs apps | wc -l\ngrep -rhoiE \"truncate[[:space:]]+(table[[:space:]]+)?(harness_shared\\.)?<table>\\b\" --include=*.ts packages libs apps | wc -l\n```\n\nRun with **known-answer controls** so the probe could return both answers, not just the one I wanted:\n\n- zero-hits (the finding): `pot_throughput_ticks` 0/0 · `memory_recall_stats` 0/0 · `pot_watchdog_fires` 0/0 · `code_recipe_runs` 0/0 · `bash_tool_substitution_fires` 0/0\n- non-zero controls (probe demonstrably works): `test_runs` 2/0 · `system_health_ticks` 1/0 · `boot_history_events` 2/0 · `pipeline_events` 1/2 · `event_wake_deliveries` 1/1\n\nA grep-absence is weak evidence on its own, which is exactly why the control set is included — the same predicate returns non-zero for five sibling tables in the same query shape.\n\n## Why this matters beyond the disk\n\nThis is the **live, current** instance of the class EI-7518 describes (\"newly-created tables escape pruning because nobody registered them\"). That item's three cited incidents (EI-7482 / EI-7491 / EI-7499) are all remediated and both tables they named — `agent_activity`, `harness_run_output` — are now registered. That remediation is what makes this filing worth reading: **the class kept producing new instances after the named ones were fixed**, because nothing asserts coverage for a table that was never registered in the first place.\n\n## Correct fix (do NOT auto-apply a TTL)\n\nRung 1 only: each of these five needs a deliberate retention decision — a `storage/categories.ts` entry with an `ageColumn` + federation class, or an explicit \"exempt, bounded by construction\" note. `memory_recall_stats` in particular feeds recall-quality analysis and may want a longer window than the telemetry default; do not blanket-7d them.\n\n⚠ Do **not** fix this by auto-applying a default TTL to every table lacking a declared policy — see the note on EI-7518: the undeclared set also contains `work_items` (456 MB), `memory_vec_harrier` (422 MB) and `harness_plans`, which are canonical state. An auto-TTL keyed on policy-absence deletes those.\n",

    {
      "id": "EI-19468589610261889",
      "title": "The tsc-new-file-red watchdog prescribes a submodule-blind ownership test — `git status`/`git log` on a submodule path return FALSE-EMPTY from the superproject",
      "summary": "## What\n\nThe `tsc-new-file-red` watchdog (watchdogKey `tsc-new-file-red::<path>`) embeds a\n\"BEFORE CLAIMING IT, re-run the ownership test\" block in every item it files:\n\n```\ngit status --porcelain | grep <path>      # dirty => someone is editing it RIGHT NOW\ngit log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>         # minutes old => author still has context\n```\n\nBoth commands are run from the SUPERPROJECT. For any path inside a git submodule\nboth return **empty regardless of the truth** — the superproject tracks only a\ngitlink (`160000 <sha> libs/generic/search`), so it has no per-file knowledge of\nthe submodule's contents at all.\n\n## Measured, live\n\nOn EI-19466920786445299 (`libs/generic/search/src/hybrid.ts`), 2026-08-03T21:1xZ:\n\n| command (from superproject) | returned | truth (from inside the submodule) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `git status --porcelain <path>` | *(empty)* | empty — clean (correct by luck) |\n| `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>` | *(empty)* | `bf5be63 2026-08-03T16:32:23-04:00` |\n\n`git submodule status libs/generic/search` → non-empty, i.e. it IS a submodule.\n\n## Why it matters (both readings are expensive, and one is silent)\n\nThe `git log` leg is the dangerous one. An empty result there does not read as\n\"I cannot answer\" — it reads as **\"this file has no commits\"**, which invites\neither \"the file is untracked/phantom, something is broken\" or, worse, \"no\nrecent author activity, therefore definitively ownerless\". The dwell-threshold\nlogic the filing rests on (\"45min stale ⇒ the author moved on\") is *derived from\nthis timestamp*, so on a submodule path that inference is drawn from an empty\nstring every time.\n\nThe `git status` leg fails the opposite way: it can never report \"dirty\", so an\nitem whose author is actively mid-edit right now will always pass the\n\"nobody is editing it\" test and invite a colliding claim.\n\nThis is not a rare shape. `libs/generic/*` alone holds ~31 submodules (measured\n2026-08-03: 31 of 61 dirs), plus `libs/papercusp` (every harness blueprint and\nagent role prompt), `libs/agent-chat`, `libs/papercusp-db`, `libs/papercusp-shared`,\n`libs/test-config`, `libs/testing-shell`, `papercusp-desktop`. A tsc red filed for\nany of them ships the broken test.\n\nNote \"is it under `libs/generic/`?\" is NOT a usable proxy — only 31 of 61 are\nsubmodules (e.g. `libs/generic/result-encoding` is plain-tracked in the superproject).\n\n## Correct state\n\nThe filing template should DETECT the submodule case and emit commands scoped to\nthe owning repo. The detection is one command whose OUTPUT (not exit code — it\nexits 0 either way) is the test:\n\n```bash\n[ -n \"$(git submodule status <dir>)\" ]   # non-empty => submodule\n```\n\nThen, for a submodule path, emit:\n\n```bash\ncd <submodule-root>\ngit status --porcelain <path-inside-submodule>\ngit log -1 --format=%cI -- <path-inside-submodule>\n```\n\nCheapest robust alternative that needs no branching: resolve the owning repo\nfirst and run both legs there unconditionally —\n`cd \"$(dirname <path>)\" && git rev-parse --show-toplevel` gives the right root\nfor submodule and superproject paths alike.\n\nThis is the same false-empty class already documented in the repo CLAUDE.md\n(\"Checking whether your edit landed, and the path is inside a SUBMODULE?\") —\nthe watchdog's generated guidance simply predates/ignores it.",

      "id": "EI-19478108227825847",
      "title": "workspace facts scope sits AT its 50-fact cap, so every facts:assert silently evicts another agent's durable authority",
      "summary": "OBSERVED TWICE by su-07374 on 2026-08-03, both times as a side effect of an unrelated assert:\n- earlier: asserting `gate-triage-reverify-one-file-at-a-time` EVICTED peer fact `never-conclude-from-a-containment-field`\n- 23:55Z: asserting `gate-red-2026-08-03-blocker-moved-three-times` EVICTED my own `gate-triage-reverify-one-file-at-a-time` (the very fact from the first eviction)\n\nWHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A NORMAL CAP: facts are documented as THE surface folded VERBATIM into every future orient - work-items and prompts point at them as the durable authority a cold successor inherits. The tool's own note says an evicted fact is 'GONE from every future fold ... evicted by the cap, not expired and not retracted by their author'. So eviction silently revokes an authority reference that other agents/work-items still cite, with no notice to the fact's AUTHOR and no tombstone at the citation site. Same dangling-authority class as EI-19465127338264010 (7d TTL vs long-lived citations), reached by a different route - cap pressure rather than expiry.\n\nPERVERSE INCENTIVE in the tool's own eviction note: 'a SHORT TTL is what makes a fact cheap for the cap to choose, so an urgent short-lived fact is the most likely victim.' That selects AGAINST exactly the transient operational facts (live gate state, in-flight candidate) a cold wake most needs, and FOR long-TTL facts that are least time-critical.\n\nSUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (not prescriptive): (a) notify the evicted fact's author via coord instead of evicting silently; (b) leave a retrievable tombstone so a citation resolves to 'evicted at <ts>' rather than nothing; (c) evict by last-READ recency rather than TTL length; (d) make the cap per-author so one busy agent cannot drain the shared scope.\n\nEvidence: both eviction notices are in the facts:assert responses in su-07374 session 133e900a-eb28-4700-beb7-6b28234b116a, 2026-08-03.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19485284578135530",
      "title": "reclaimWedgedSpawns is structurally inert for 4 of 5 spawn classes — EI-18729995135827661 closed after fixing only its dangerous half, leaving the missing-floor half",
      "summary": "## What\n\n**EI-18729995135827661 is `done` (2026-08-02, su-5622daef), but only one of the two dependencies it names was fixed.** That item's own \"WHO DEPENDS ON IT\" list is:\n\n1. `reclaimWedgedSpawns` — the durable DB-truth reclaim floor\n2. the spawn-ceiling-jam watchdog\n\nThe landed fix (`spawn-reclaim.ts` L1286-1353, with 3 regression tests) added a spawn-CLASS filter to **`reclaimFirstOutputStalledSpawns`** — correctly and importantly, since L1353 records that without it \"this reaper would SIGTERM essentially every non-opspawn spawn in\" the fleet. That removed a live mass-false-reap hazard.\n\n**`reclaimWedgedSpawns` was not touched.** Its candidate SQL still reads (L1146):\n\n```sql\nAND last_output_at IS NOT NULL\n```\n\nwith no spawn-class predicate.\n\n## Why that matters\n\nPer EI-7215 / EI-18729995135827661, only supervised piped-child (`opspawn-`) spawns ever populate `last_output_at`; overwatch / launch / blueprint / implement never do, **by design**. Measured live 2026-08-04:\n\n- last 7 days: `last_output_at` populated for **1 of 75** spawns (98.7% NULL); `heartbeat_at` **75/75**\n- all rows ever reaped with `cancel_reason LIKE 'wedge-reap%'`: `last_output_at` **0/48**, `heartbeat_at` **48/48**\n\nSo that predicate selects ~nothing for the classes actually in use. The durable floor — documented in its own header as the restart-safe net that \"survives the in-memory wedge reaper's tracking being lost (e.g. across an operator restart)\" — **cannot fire for 4 of the 5 spawn classes**.\n\nThis is the *benign* failure direction (inert, not destructive), which is exactly why it is easy to miss and why it survived the close: nothing breaks, nothing alerts, the net simply is not there. It is the same shape as the original item's own \"why it went unnoticed\" note — a monitor watching this would be green throughout and silently meaningless.\n\nCombined with the in-memory `reapWedgedLocalSpawns` covering only the `opspawn-` class (it keys on `localSpawnOutput`, fed by the same stdout stream), the net effect is: **for overwatch / launch / blueprint / implement spawns, no wedge-reclaim path of any kind can fire.** A genuinely wedged spawn in those classes is tolerated indefinitely.\n\n## Correct state\n\nEither:\n- **(a)** apply the same per-class treatment its sibling got — so the floor either covers today's classes on a signal they produce, or *declares* itself inapplicable to them rather than silently selecting zero; or\n- **(b)** EI-18729995135827661's fix candidate 2 as written: decouple `reclaimWedgedSpawns` from `last_output_at` onto a signal that exists for today's classes.\n\nPlus the recurrence guard that item explicitly asked for and that has not landed: **any \"column must be populated\" invariant must be PER-CLASS.** A test pinning the per-class reality of *both* reapers would stop the next fix to one silently re-breaking the other — which is precisely what happened here.\n\n## Not claimed\n\nI have not established whether the closer deliberately scoped to the dangerous half and intended the floor half as follow-up; no such follow-up item was findable (`search:fulltext` scope `work_item`, 0 hits). Filing so the gap is tracked either way rather than closing with the parent.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19485505354981364",
      "title": "Triage's protected-keyword gate matches SUBSTRINGS, so items are set needsHuman by words like 'authoritative' — 5/5 'auth' gates are false positives, one of them a critical hidden for 18 days",
      "summary": "**Mechanism.** `ideaLifecycle.triageReason` gates an item to a human when the text \"mentions protected keyword\". The match is a plain substring test, not word-boundary anchored. So `authoritative`, `author`, `authored`, `authentic` all trip the `auth` gate. The item is written `payload.needsHuman = true`, which is **claim floor #6** in `harness_shared.work_item_claim_floors` — so the row becomes INVISIBLE to `scheduler:get_next` / self-select entirely. It does not fail loudly; it simply never appears in anyone's queue.\n\n**Measured 2026-08-04 (harness papercusp, open rows):**\n- 193 open rows carry `needsHuman:true`; 16 of those cite a protected keyword.\n- By keyword: `deploy` 6, **`auth` 5**, `credential` 1, `migration` 1, unattributed 3.\n- **Of the 5 `auth` gates, 5 match `auth` ONLY as a substring** — zero have a word-boundary occurrence of \"auth\" anywhere in title or body (`!~* '\\yauth\\y'`). A 100% false-positive rate for that keyword.\n- **1 of the 5 is severity `critical`: EI-13738** — \"The claim path never consults the PLAN's blockedBy\" — filed 2026-07-17, still `open`, `assignee: null`, **18 days**. Its triage reason reads verbatim: `mentions protected keyword \"auth\" -> human`. The word \"auth\" does not occur in it; \"authoritative\" and \"author\" do.\n\n**Why this is worse than a normal false positive.** The gate is SILENT and it removes the item from the pool rather than flagging it. So the louder the item (a critical), the more damage: it looks like unowned backlog nobody has prioritized, when in fact nobody CAN pick it up. EI-13738 documents a fail-open hole in the claim path — and was itself hidden by a different part of the same claim path. I only found it by claiming it BY ID as a superuser.\n\n**Fix.** Anchor the protected-keyword match to word boundaries (`\\bauth\\b` / `~* '\\yauth\\y'`), or match a token list after tokenization rather than raw `includes()`. Low risk: it strictly narrows what gets gated, and every currently-gated `auth` row is a measured false positive.\n\n**Recurrence guard.** A test asserting that a body containing only `authoritative`/`author` does NOT trip the `auth` gate, and that one containing `auth` as a word DOES. Without the negative case the narrowing can silently regress.\n\n**Second-order, worth a look but not measured:** `deploy` (6 gates) is the largest bucket and is a substring of nothing common, so it is probably genuine — but `migration` and `credential` deserve the same word-boundary check. I did not measure those.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19917150867390319",
      "title": "Editing a deployed ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/* file reports success, then is silently reverted by the release sync",
      "summary": "## What happened\nEdited `~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/ask-gate-mirror.sh` twice (adding a Stop-hook detector). Both Edit calls returned \"updated successfully\". Minutes later the file was byte-identical to before — 633 lines, zero trace of either edit. The deployed copy is re-synced from `papercup-release/apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/` (release mtime 2026-08-03; deployed copy re-stamped 16:09:28, right after my edit).\n\n## Why it is expensive\nThe failure is SILENT and shaped exactly like success:\n- Edit reports success; nothing warns that the path is a deployed artifact.\n- The only signal was a generic \"file was modified, either by the user or by a linter\" system-reminder, which reads as an acknowledgement of *your own* edit, not as \"something reverted you\".\n- I then ran an end-to-end test of the hook whose four cases returned empty output. Three of the four \"passed\" — because the hook bails early without a token, so *every* case returns empty. A vacuous test that reports PASS is worse than a failing one: only the single must-BLOCK case exposed it.\n\nSo the natural path is: edit → test → see three passes → conclude it works → ship a change that does not exist.\n\n## Correct path\nCanonical source is `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/<hook>.sh`; the `~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/` copy is deployed and takes effect only after git-sync → green-checkpoint → deploy. Same \"edit the source, never the rendered output\" rule CLAUDE.md states for prompts — but the hooks directory is not named as a projection anywhere, so it reads like an ordinary config file.\n\n## Durable fix (proposed)\n1. A PreToolUse guard on Edit/Write whose path resolves under `~/.papercusp/hooks/` — refuse and point at the canonical `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/` path. Same shape as the existing non-canonical-worktree guard.\n2. Add `~/.papercusp/hooks/` to the projections list in agent-insights/prompt-sources-canonical-vs-projections.\n3. Separately: the hook's early bail (`PAPERCUSP_SID` / token missing) is indistinguishable from \"ran and found nothing\" — a test harness cannot tell them apart. Emit a distinguishable marker on stderr when it bails so a probe can detect a vacuous run.",

    {
      "id": "EI-19952581533663549",
      "title": "Mac rig (hello-world-3-pot): SESSION_CLOSED outbox re-wire spins at ~32 Hz with no backoff — 68MB log, and the pot is permanently unreachable (H0l9YCwy dialed 463/463 = no-path over 3h)",
      "summary": "## Symptom (measured on the live Mac rig, 2026-08-09 05:35Z)\n\n`/tmp/serve-current.log` on aviweiss@172.31.44.2 (pid 24727, the current headless rig bundle) is **68,003,634 bytes** and growing at **1295 lines / 10s**. The last 4000 lines are a single repeating 4-line cycle, 988 iterations deep:\n\n```\n[outbox-drain] drain failed for papercusp-workspace::hello-world-3-pot: SESSION_CLOSED: Cannot append to a closed session\n[outbox-drain] own-log session for papercusp-workspace::hello-world-3-pot is SESSION_CLOSED — stopping this drain (no further 5000ms retries against the dead session); signaling for a re-wire\n[boot-all] un-marking outbox wiring for papercusp-workspace::hello-world-3-pot — session is SESSION_CLOSED — the next boot pass re-wires a fresh outbox loop\n[boot-history] epoch_gate_built harness=hello-world-3-pot potHomeSlug=hello-world-3-pot\n```\n\n1295 lines/10s ÷ 4 lines/iteration = **~32 iterations per second**.\n\n## Two distinct defects\n\n**(1) The re-wire loop has no backoff.** WI-3684's design intent (boot-all.ts:409-431) is that `markSendSideUnwired` clears the wired flag so *the periodic boot-all reconcile pass* re-attempts it — explicitly to stop \"the permanently-closed session's drain/announce loop blind-retrying every poll tick forever\". But the observed rate is ~32 Hz, not a periodic-reconcile rate. Note `markSendSideUnwired` only logs `if (wasWired)`, so **every one of those 988 iterations successfully re-wired and then immediately died** — i.e. the re-wire is being re-driven far faster than any reconcile cadence, and each fresh session is dead on arrival. Whatever the root cause of (2), a retry that cannot succeed must back off; this one burns CPU on the rig and 68MB of disk.\n\n**(2) The re-wire never produces a live session.** The remedy path (`un-mark → next boot pass re-wires a fresh outbox loop`) is structurally unable to recover this pot: 988 consecutive fresh wirings all landed on a SESSION_CLOSED own-log. So the own-log session for `papercusp-workspace::hello-world-3-pot` is permanently dead in a way re-wiring cannot repair. `own-log-fork-guard.ts:209` says \"a re-boot will re-open the SAME core\" — worth checking whether that is exactly the trap here (re-wiring re-opens the same dead core rather than a new one).\n\n## Consequence — this is what blocks the pot-git rig entirely\n\nTower-side census, `papercup-bg-host.service`, 3 hours (2026-08-09 02:30Z→05:30Z), all repos, all 20 candidate devices:\n\n| dial outcome | count |\n|---|---|\n| `no-path` | 5336 |\n| `backoff(no-such-repo)` | 174 |\n| `failed(pot-git …)` | 114 |\n| convergence / `advanced=`>0 | **0** |\n\nPer device: **`H0l9YCwy:no-path` 463 / 463 — zero live dials in three hours.** By contrast `Lm1ABoMR` resolved 117 times against 172 misses (~40%).\n\nThat contrast is the load-bearing part: **H0l9YCwy is NOT the intermittent-churn shape.** EI-18740968796318403 (hello channels churn at 1-30/sec ⇒ the registry is empty *at any sampled instant*) predicts intermittent success, which is exactly what Lm1ABoMR shows. It does not predict 0/463. H0l9YCwy (the Mac rig — identity settled 2026-08-09, fact `vm-rig-device-identity-h0l9ycwy-not-lm1abomr`) is simply never registered at all, permanently, which is consistent with its pot session never coming up.\n\n## Why the `no-path` token cannot be read as \"unreachable\" without this\n\n`no-path` is emitted at git-sync-action.ts:2242 when `openHiveGitDuplexToDevice` returns a duplex with `.destroyed === true`. That happens (peer-dial-registry.ts:818-851) when `resolvePotGitPeerSocket` misses AND `awaitRegistration` (4s, `DEFAULT_REGISTRATION_WAIT_MS`) also misses. A device with no recent sighting (`RECENT_SIGHTING_MS` 120_000) returns immediately. So `no-path` conflates \"mid-churn miss\" with \"never present\" — and the 463/463 vs 117/289 split is the only thing that separates them.\n\n## Repro / probes\n\n```bash\n# rig loop rate + log size\nssh aviweiss@172.31.44.2 'ls -l /tmp/serve-current.log; a=$(wc -l </tmp/serve-current.log); sleep 10; b=$(wc -l </tmp/serve-current.log); echo delta10s=$((b-a))'\nssh aviweiss@172.31.44.2 'tail -4000 /tmp/serve-current.log | grep -c \"un-marking outbox wiring\"'\n\n# tower per-device dial census\njournalctl --user -u papercup-bg-host.service --since '3 hours ago' \\\n  | grep -o '[A-Za-z0-9+/]\\{8\\}:no-path' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\njournalctl --user -u papercup-bg-host.service --since '3 hours ago' \\\n  | grep -o '[A-Za-z0-9+/]\\{8\\}:failed([^,)]*' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\n```\n\n## Suggested fix shape\n\n- **Durable, (1):** a consecutive-failure circuit breaker on the un-mark→re-wire path in `boot-all.ts` — exponential backoff keyed on `(workspace, harness, step)`, plus a loud escalation once it trips a ceiling, so an unrecoverable pot degrades to one alarm rather than a 32 Hz spin. A recurrence guard should fail if re-wire attempts for one key exceed N in a window.\n- **Root, (2):** determine why a freshly-wired own-log session for this pot is closed on arrival (does `wireOutboxForHarness` re-open the SAME closed core?). That is the actual fix; (1) is the blast-radius containment and is required either way.\n\n## Relation to other items\n\n- Blocks the end-to-end rig verification of **WI-5210** (pot-git one-sided hello loss) — with 0/463 dials there is no path over which to induce or observe a hello re-send, so WI-5210's rig leg is unexercisable for reasons unrelated to WI-5210.\n- Distinct from **EI-18740968796318403** (churn ⇒ intermittent) per the 463/463 vs 117/289 evidence above.\n- Distinct from **EI-19947344892350882** (repoKey aliasing ⇒ `no-such-repo`), which is the `Lm1ABoMR:failed(...)` leg, not this one.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20019309044931698",
      "title": "Sparse seed cut ships FULL history: the cutter's READ-ONLY corestore open races the live writer's WAL rotation (ENOENT). Root = the cross-process split; rocksdb-native binds NEITHER Checkpoint NOR secondary mode, so the fix must extract in-process [title corrected — the original \"nothing flushes the memtable\" mechanism was DISPROVEN by measurement, see checkpoint]",
      "summary": "MEASURED END-TO-END 2026-08-09T23:12-23:13Z while cutting desktop release 0.0.14-alpha (WI-37553).\nThis is the MISSING PIECE in EI-19899917753028359 / EI-19950949176340375: those explain why the cut often cannot\nGET a head snapshot (holder booted:false / holder lifetime < cut requirement). This explains why the cut still\nFAILS when it DOES get one - which is what happened on cut attempt 2 (22:04Z).\n\nTHE DIRECT EVIDENCE (probe /tmp/papercusp-release-0014/probe-fresh-snapshot-visibility.ts, log bash-2e96875e-7c6):\n  step 1  head snapshot appended OK by the live bg-host holder:\n          kind=produced pid=568520 appended=true coversUpTo=1229167 chunkCount=45 rowCount=74083 elapsedMs=56628\n  step 2  the IMMEDIATE fresh READ-ONLY Corestore open (exactly what cut-seed-cli does next) THREW:\n          Error: while stat a file for size: .../papercusp/hyperbee/db/002810.log: No such file or directory (ENOENT)\n\nMECHANISM (two faces of one problem - a read-only reader racing a live writer):\n  (a) OPEN-TIME race: RocksDB read-only enumerates the file set, then stats files the live writer has already\n      rotated/deleted -> ENOENT. cut-seed-cli already retries this up to 10x and logs it verbatim as: read-only open\n      lost a race with the live operator WAL churn (attempt 1/10). See cut log line 534. So the race is known.\n  (b) POST-OPEN STALENESS - the face nobody caught: when a retry finally WINS, the view it opened can be pinned to a\n      file set that PREDATES the just-appended snapshot. Nothing flushes the memtable after the append, so the\n      freshest blocks - the snapshot chunks written seconds earlier - are exactly the ones most likely to be invisible\n      to a read-only open. findLatestCompleteSnapshot then reports no snapshot, computeSparseFrom returns 0 (ship FULL\n      history), and seed-degradation-guard REFUSES the 5.62 GB result ~52 minutes into the cut.\n\nWHY THE PRINTED REMEDY IS ACTIVELY COUNTER-PRODUCTIVE: the guard says to append a fresh head snapshot before cutting.\nIt WAS appended moments earlier. Worse - the FRESHER the snapshot, the LESS likely it is flushed, so following the\nremedy makes the failure MORE likely. Two cut attempts (~1h each) were lost to this.\n\nWHY THE OBVIOUS SCAN-SIDE FIX DOES NOT FIX IT (built and shipped first, so this is measured, not predicted):\nWI-37553 hardened the scan to distinguish unreadable from absent and retry across 5s/20s/60s budgets (committed\ncfb6be43e0, typecheck clean, 6/6 tests pass). It makes the failure LEGIBLE and is worth keeping, but it CANNOT fix\nthis: the blocks are not SLOW, they are NOT IN THE VIEW - all three budgets fail identically. Corroborated: a\nread-only census over 12,000 tail blocks measured 0 timeouts, 0 read errors, 24ms slowest get (~200x under the 5s\nbudget), so slowness was never the cause.\n\nCANDIDATE FIX (root-cause; the primitive already exists):\n  hypercore-storage 2.9.0 exposes flush() -> this.rocks.flush() (node_modules/hypercore-storage/index.js:766-767),\n  a RocksDB memtable->SST flush. produceHeadSnapshotNow() currently appends and returns with NO flush (called at\n  substrate-head-snapshot.ts:107). Flushing after the append - before the cutter opens read-only - makes the snapshot\n  durable in SSTs and therefore visible.\n  STRONGER OPTION worth evaluating: have the holder produce a RocksDB CHECKPOINT (consistent hard-linked dir) and cut\n  from THAT. That removes the whole race class - no ENOENT, no stale view, no dependence on holder lifetime.\n\nRECURRENCE GUARD to assert: after produceHeadSnapshotNow returns appended:true, a FRESH read-only open of that store\nMUST resolve the just-appended snapshot set. Falsifiable in ~2 minutes (the probe above) instead of 52 minutes into a\nrelease cut.\n\nSCOPE: blocks the release seed path generally, not just 0.0.14 - EI-19899917753028359 records releases shipping a\n2026-07-21 seed.",

      "id": "EI-20074719498966502",
      "title": "tauri-agent-tools capture aborts ALL artifacts on a Wayland box missing grim — DOM/console/logs need no compositor but are never attempted",
      "summary": "REPRO (this box, 2026-08-10):\\n\\n  tauri-agent-tools capture --pid <pid> --output /tmp/p005-artifacts/p005-capture\\n  → [FAIL] preflight: Missing required tools:\\n      swaymsg: sudo apt install sway\\n      grim: sudo apt install grim\\n    Wrote manifest.json (0 artifacts attempted) — see fatalError.\\n\\nWHAT'S WRONG: `capture` is documented as \"screenshot + DOM + console + logs\". Only the SCREENSHOT leg needs a Wayland compositor tool (grim/swaymsg). The DOM, console and log legs go through the dev bridge's /eval and /logs endpoints and need no compositor at all — the same bridge that answered `eval` and `check` fine seconds earlier in the same session. But the preflight gates the WHOLE command, so it writes \"0 artifacts attempted\" and the agent gets nothing.\\n\\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE: this is the box's default state (platform reports `wayland`, grim not installed), and `capture` is exactly what an agent reaches for when a work-item's completion guard demands a verification artifact. The completion guard on work_items:complete REJECTS verifiedHow:'live-drove-ui' unless it can cite \"a screenshot/capture image path, or a recorded tauri-agent-tools capture/screenshot/check invocation\" — so on this box two of those three named routes are structurally unavailable, and an agent that does not know `check` is the third route will either (a) install packages on the owner's machine to satisfy a guard, or (b) honestly downgrade verifiedHow and UNDER-report verification it genuinely performed. Both are bad outcomes for a guard whose whole purpose is honest evidence.\\n\\nPROPOSED FIX: make the preflight PER-LEG rather than whole-command. Attempt every artifact whose dependencies are present, record the screenshot leg as skipped-with-reason in manifest.json, and exit non-zero only if ZERO artifacts were produced. \"0 artifacts attempted\" when 3 of 4 were attemptable is the actual defect.\\n\\nWORKAROUND that works today (and is worth documenting next to the guard's message): `tauri-agent-tools check --pid <pid> --eval \"<assertion>\"` returns [PASS]/[FAIL] with a 0/1 exit and needs no compositor. It satisfies the completion guard's third accepted form. Verified working here: [PASS], exit 0.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20077125623815751",
      "title": "The guard-of-guards' corpus test classifies by QUOTED extension mention, so it is blind in both directions — 4 guards invisible to the shrink-only baseline, and an INI-only guard sits in it",
      "summary": "## The defect\n\n`guard-string-literal-blindness.test.ts` decides which guards belong to the phantom-offender population with:\n\n```ts\nconst SCANS_CODE_FILES = /\\.tsx?['\"`]|\\.mjs['\"`]|\\.jsx['\"`]|\\.cts['\"`]|\\.mts['\"`]/;\n```\n\nIt ASKS \"does this guard scan JS/TS source?\" and MEASURES \"does its source mention a quoted extension anywhere?\". That is the SAME root defect already fixed one layer up in this very file (WI-37717 widened `NAMED_STRIPPER`, which classified strippers by NAME): a MENTION-shaped rule answering a CORPUS question. Fixing it once for the HOW question and leaving it for the WHAT question is why it recurred.\n\n## FALSE MEMBERSHIP (measured)\n\nThe regex is satisfied by any `import … from './lib/tracked-files.mjs'` — which nearly every guard has. `check-systemd-startlimit-placement.mjs` is in `SCANS_UNMASKED_SOURCE` for NO other reason: its ONLY code-extension mention in masked source is that import line (verified line-by-line). Its real corpus is `apps/operator/scripts/systemd/*.{service,conf}` — INI unit files, which contain no string or template literals at all.\n\nSame shape, weaker: `check-github-identity-terms.mjs` — only evidence is a self-exclusion `f === 'scripts/check-github-identity-terms.mjs'`; real corpus is `.md`/`.mdx`.\n\n## FALSE ABSENCE — the worse direction (measured)\n\nThe regex sees only a QUOTED extension, so it is blind to the REGEX filter form, which is how much of the tree actually filters:\n- `check-no-restart-imports`: `/\\.(ts|tsx|mjs|cjs|js|json)$/`\n- `check-constant-conditional`: `/\\.(ts|tsx)$/`\n- `check-vacuous-negative-assertions`: `/\\.(test|spec)\\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$/`\n\nThose three ARE in the baseline — but by ACCIDENT, caught via their import lines, not by measurement. A guard with a regex filter and no incidental quoted mention is invisible entirely. Measured population matching TEXT_MATCHES ∧ READS_FILES ∧ unmasked ∧ regex-filter but ABSENT from the baseline:\n\n| guard | assessment |\n|---|---|\n| `check-no-bespoke-state-read` | THE LIVE ONE — scans tool-def `.ts`, text-matches STATE_NOUNS/MUTATING_VERBS, CI-wired (CLAUDE.md cites `lint:no-bespoke-state-read` as the gate on bespoke state reads). Its evidence IS string literals (tool names), so it needs `stripCommentsOnly`, and a comment naming a tool can mint a phantom. |\n| `check-conflict-markers` | probed: bareCode=true, fires on a template literal. But CORRECTLY unmasked — a real merge conflict lands inside a template literal too (git does not respect syntax), so masking converts a phantom positive into a silent FALSE NEGATIVE on an unresolved conflict. Byte/line-level class, like check-smart-quotes. Belongs IN the baseline as a declared consideration, not fixed. |\n| `check-fleet-auth` | corpus is `/proc` cmdline/environ + config files, not source. Probably a false positive of my crude probe regex. |\n| `lint-as-committed` | a META-guard running other guards against a committed tree; corpus is package.json scripts. Probably out of population. |\n\n## RETRACTED IN FLIGHT — the obvious fix is WRONG\n\nMy first move was to NARROW the rule (ignore module specifiers and self-references as corpus evidence). Measured 26 → 16 members. I checked the 10 drops BEFORE implementing, and three of them (`check-no-restart-imports`, `check-constant-conditional`, `check-vacuous-negative-assertions`) genuinely DO scan TS via a regex filter — the narrowing would have HIDDEN real exposure while looking like a tidy-up. Do NOT re-attempt the narrowing without the regex-form widening landing first, or the baseline silently loses three real members.\n\n## The fix\n\nRecognise BOTH forms (quoted extension AND regex extension filter) AND exclude module specifiers + self-references as evidence — the two halves must land together, or the baseline moves the wrong way. Then re-seed from the corrected measurement, documenting each ADDED entry with its classification (fix vs. correctly-unmasked), on the precedent set here when the NAMED_STRIPPER widening moved `check-no-unthreaded-apply` between baselines.\n\nNote the doc comment says the set \"may SHRINK, never GROW\". That rule is about not accumulating new debt; a MEASUREMENT correction that reveals pre-existing members is a different thing and must be spelled out as such, or the next agent reads the growth as a violation and \"fixes\" it by deleting entries.\n\nAdd CONTROL fixtures (the block at the bottom of the file already has the right pattern): each must assert the OLD rule missed the shape AND the new rule catches it, so a future narrowing fails loudly.\n\n## Provenance\nProbes: /tmp/why-in-pop.mjs (per-guard evidence lines) · /tmp/narrow-classifier.mjs (the retracted narrowing) · /tmp/widen-corpus.mjs (the 4 invisible guards).",

    {
      "id": "EI-20082312471440722",
      "title": "Goal stop's placement tier is structurally inert: nothing auto-pairs a goal to a pot, so goal_pots is 0 rows and goals:update{paused} gates placement on nothing",
      "summary": "NOT a duplicate of EI-20015592992797890 (that one's root cause was agent_modes.subject, which IS fixed and verified live — this is the OTHER tier, and it survives that fix).\n\nD-014 gives the goal stop two tiers. Tier 2 (LIVE BURN — disarm loops of sessions attributed via agent_modes.mode='goal' AND subject=<goalId>) now works: goals/start.ts stamps subject:id and rolls back if setMode fails, and both post-fix goal-mode rows carry non-null subjects.\n\nTIER 1 (PLACEMENT, on pots where goal_pots.role='owner') IS FED NOTHING.\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-10 on the live operator DB (unscoped, so these are cross-tenant totals):\n  harness_shared.goal_pots             0 rows  (0 with role='owner')\n  harness_shared.goals                 4 rows  (1 active)\n  harness_shared.agent_modes mode=goal 3 rows  (2 with non-null subject)\n\nTHE CAUSE IS A MISSING CALL, NOT A MISSING WRITER. libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/goal-pots.ts:129 has a correct INSERT behind linkPot(), and it is reachable — but grep across libs/packages/apps shows exactly ONE non-test caller: packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/goals/pots.ts:75, the `goals:attach-pot` tool. Neither door that CREATES a goal calls it:\n  - goals:create (packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/goals/create.ts) — no pot reference at all\n  - goals:start (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/goals/start.ts) — creates the goal AND spawns its agent, but never pairs the agent's own pot; grep for linkPot/goal_pots/potsForGoal in that file returns nothing\n\nSo every goal created the ergonomic way owns zero pots, and `goals:update { status:'paused'|'killed' }` fans out over an empty set: it disarms attributed loops (tier 2 works) and gates placement on NOTHING.\n\nWHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE, NOT A COSMETIC GAP. This is EI-19995648221353323 one level up — the precedent where pot:pause bounded new placement, exerted zero backpressure on live sessions, and a pot read \"paused, maxBees 1\" while 73 owners drained the account pool. The goal stop was built specifically not to repeat that, and tier 2 is why it does not. But with tier 1 empty, a goal paused today stops only the sessions it can attribute; anything placing work into a pot the goal nominally drives keeps placing.\n\nTO ITS CREDIT, THE MECHANISM DOES NOT LIE ABOUT THIS: the report sets `degraded` and returns `unattributedActiveLoops`, which is exactly the detector D-014 demanded. The failure mode is a caller that renders only `status`.\n\nCANDIDATE FIX (needs a decision, hence filed not fixed): have goals:start attach the pot it spawns its agent into as role='owner' in the same transaction that stamps the mode subject — it already rolls the goal back when setMode fails, so the atomicity precedent exists. goals:create is murkier: under D-009 one goal spans many pots that may not exist yet, so an auto-pair there may be wrong and an explicit goals:attach-pot may be correct.\n\nRECURRENCE GUARD SHAPE: a test asserting that a goal created via goals:start owns >=1 goal_pots row with role='owner' — i.e. that a stop fired on a freshly started goal has a non-empty tier-1 set. Zero-because-nobody-attached is otherwise indistinguishable from zero-because-broken, which is exactly why this survived the tier-2 fix.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20108513273736336",
      "title": "Windows VM base image is the DEFAULT boot disk, so it accumulates state and silently invalidates every \"fresh overlay\" cold test",
      "summary": "## Symptom\n`/home/marsh-office/windows-vm/windows_hdd.qcow2` is the BASE image every Windows verification overlay branches from. It is supposed to be a pristine Windows with no Papercusp. As of 2026-08-10 it carries a fully warm, AUTOSTARTING Papercusp install.\n\nMeasured from a brand-new overlay created off that base:\n- `papercusp-desktop.exe` pid 2324 already RUNNING at first boot (HKCU Run entry `Papercusp Server`)\n- WSL distro `papercup-runtime` REGISTERED and Running\n- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\{Papercusp GUI, Papercusp Server, Papercusp, com.papercusp.gui}` all present\n- `%USERPROFILE%\\.papercusp\\logs\\gui.log` history back to 2026-08-01\n- NSIS uninstall keys `com.papercusp.gui_is1` / `com.papercusp.server_is1` present\n\n## Why this is a defect, not housekeeping — it INVERTS test results silently\nMy own 0014 verification at 19:03Z today, on an overlay off this SAME base, logged verbatim \"COLD box: papercup-runtime unregistered, no .papercusp, no webview data\". So the base was clean then and was polluted AFTER — someone booted the base directly instead of an overlay (base mtime 17:55 local == the guest's own `server-shell-heartbeat.json` write time, i.e. the write came from a VM running ON the base).\n\nThe resulting trap: an agent does exactly the right thing — \"make a FRESH overlay off the base for a clean read\" — and still gets a WARM box. A fresh-install test then measures an upgrade-over-existing path while believing it measured a cold install. Nothing errors.\n\nFor WI-37798 specifically (a bug about the GUI discovering the operator port, where discovery state lives INSIDE the `papercup-runtime` WSL distro) a stale registered distro would have handed me a PASS that meant nothing.\n\n## Root cause\n`boot-windows.sh` had `DISK_FILE=${DISK_FILE:-windows_hdd.qcow2}` — the BASE was the DEFAULT disk. Running the script with no env set boots and writes to the pristine base. The \"must be an overlay\" rule existed only as prose in agent notes, enforced by nothing.\n\n## Durable fix — LANDED\nAdded a base-image guard to `boot-windows.sh` that refuses to boot a base, with an `ALLOW_BASE_DISK=1` escape hatch for legitimate re-baselining. Detection is STRUCTURAL (an overlay has a qcow2 backing file, a base does not) rather than by filename, so a renamed/rebuilt base is still caught.\n\nProven falsifiable in all three directions:\n- base -> exit 2, \"it is a BASE image\"\n- in-use overlay -> exit 3, \"could not DETERMINE\" + the real qemu-img lock error\n- idle overlay -> passes the guard (proceeds to qemu)\n\nTwo bugs were found IN THE GUARD by testing it, both worth recording because they are general:\n1. The first version tested only \"did grep find a backing-filename\", which reports UNREADABLE as \"this is a base\" — a confident false statement. It fired on a healthy overlay that was merely in use (`qemu-img` cannot open a running image: 'Failed to get shared \"write\" lock'). Fixed to a three-way branch: overlay / base / undetermined. Never collapse \"could not measure\" into \"measured false\".\n2. Under `set -e`, `_info=$(failing_cmd); rc=$?` aborts the script at the assignment, BEFORE `$?` is read — so the undetermined branch was unreachable and the guard died silently with exit 1 and no message. Fixed with `if ! _info=$(...)`, which is errexit-exempt.\n\n## Residual risk\n`boot-windows.sh` lives at `/home/marsh-office/windows-vm/`, OUTSIDE the repo, so this guard is not version-controlled and not covered by git-sync. A host rebuild loses it.\n\n## Detector gap\nThe 0014 install log asserted coldness as free text (\"COLD box: ...\"). That is an assertion, not a check — it cannot fail. The purge script (/mnt/data/offload/win-vm-verify/purge-to-cold.ps1) now ends in a real gate (COLD_OK=1/0 + itemised blockers) that a caller can branch on.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",

    {
      "id": "EI-20192339459004669",
      "title": "capability:bash auto-backgrounded a 200ms script at the 120s cap, then reported it `running` for 7+ min after its process was dead and with no output file ever written — TaskOutput block:true on it would wait forever",
      "summary": "OBSERVED 2026-08-11 21:00-21:08Z, papercusp-su capability:bash, host load ~137.\n\n## What happened\nA trivial node one-liner (read data/owls.json, readdirSync /tmp/owl-src, regex over ~16 URLs — two near-identical scripts immediately before it ran in 0.2s and 0.3s) hit the 120s foreground cap and was auto-moved to background as task ksuups51w, with the standard promise: \"keeps running; you'll receive a notification with the result when it completes.\"\n\nIt never completed and never will:\n- `TaskOutput { block:false }` at +5min: status `running`.\n- The PROCESS IS GONE. Three probes: (p1) a bracketed argv grep — USELESS here, it self-matched my own wrapper because my `echo` label contained the literal target string, the exact trap CLAUDE.md documents; (p2) `node scripts/proc-guard.mjs check \"owl-src\"` — \"no external process matches /owl-src/\", the authoritative answer, and a clean demonstration that the purpose-built ancestor-excluding tool earns its place over grep; (p3) every live `node` process on the box is 3 days old, nothing young.\n- NO output file was written: newest dir under .papercusp/scratch/papercusp-workspace/capability:bash/ is 20:45Z, 15+ min before this task existed.\n- The bash door itself was healthy throughout — an unrelated `echo` returned in 0.6s at 21:06Z, so this is not door contention and not the fleet-load excuse.\n\n`TaskStop` then reported success stopping it, which is itself telling: the task-tracking layer believed it had something to stop.\n\n## Why it matters\nAn agent that follows the tool's own instruction — background it, then `TaskOutput { block:true }` — waits on a task that is dead, produced nothing, and will never notify. That is an indefinite silent hang, and it is the same failure CLASS the compaction guidance already warns about from the other direction (\"a checkpointed 'job COMPLETED' claim must be re-verified\" — EI-16611). Both directions are now observed: a dead job reported COMPLETE, and here a dead job reported RUNNING. The common root is that the task-status layer is not derived from the process's actual liveness, so its verdict is unfalsifiable from the inside.\n\n## The second question, unanswered and more interesting\nWHY did a 200ms script take >120s at all? I did not diagnose it and am not asserting load as the cause — load is a symptom, and the door answered other calls in 0.6s while this was allegedly running. Candidates I did NOT rule out: node process-start contention specific to that moment; a blocking read on /tmp/owl-src while the WI-37971 holder was rewriting a 328KB file in that directory (plausible — my parse of that same file caught a torn mid-write state at 20:55Z); or the MCP call never actually dispatching the script at all, which would explain a dead process, an absent output file, and a 120s cap-out equally well. That last one is the hypothesis I would test first, because it predicts the process never existed rather than exited.\n\n## Repro signal for whoever picks this up\nLook for capability:bash tasks whose status is `running` with no live process in their cgroup and no scratch output file. If the task layer tracked the cgroup (which the task-manager's no-escape property already gives it), an empty cgroup would settle liveness definitively instead of leaving a status nobody can falsify.\n",

      "summary": "MEASURED 2026-08-11T23:12Z via dev:pg_query over harness_shared.scout_ticks (workspace papercusp-workspace).\n\nP-003 of plan blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11 (\"diagnose + durably fix the ideator transport death\") is marked DONE. The producer is still dying.\n\nEVIDENCE — tick outcomes, last 3 days: status=ran 58 (newest 2026-08-11T21:06:34Z), status=error 18 (newest 2026-08-11T23:11:24Z), status=gated 25. In the LAST 6 HOURS: 5 error vs 2 ran. The newest error is 7 minutes old at filing time and postdates the P-003 closure.\n\nTHE SIGNATURE HAS CHANGED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY \"P-003 DID NOT WORK\". Two alternating proximate errors:\n  (a) \"rate-limit pause exceeds maxWait\" (22:38:24Z, 19:08:33Z) — the original P-003 symptom.\n  (b) \"Scout ideator constraint-removal did not receive an upstream response before the cycle deadline (left the local governor but remained queued/stalled downstream; not generation)\" (23:11:24Z, 21:41:55Z).\n\nTHE POOL SNAPSHOT IS THE ACTUAL LEAD, and it is identical across all four failures: poolSnapshotAtFire = { healthyAccounts: 0, codexHealthyAccounts: 2, codexConfigured: false }, with admissionDenial = { via: governor, reason: no-free-slot, freeSlots: 0, totalAccounts: 1, governorReason: concurrency, pausedAccounts: 0 }.\n\nRead that plainly: the governor sees ONE account, it has ZERO free slots, and it is concurrency-saturated — while TWO healthy codex accounts exist and are unreachable because codexConfigured is false. This is the \"a limit is usually a routing bug\" shape from the su playbook, not a capacity wall: pausedAccounts is 0, so nothing is rate-limit-paused; Scout is simply queued behind itself on a single-slot pool.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS TO THE BLENDER GOAL: no successful cycle since 21:06Z means the eligible-grading queue stops refilling. The steward can grade a drained queue to zero (it did, this pass: 17/17) and the loop still produces nothing. A green ungraded-count with a dead producer is the exact \"looks healthy, is dark\" failure the plan exists to prevent.\n\nDELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON: the fix most likely touches Scout ACCOUNT ROUTING, which the goal reserves to the owner (\"Preserve the existing Scout account routing\") and which the standing rule makes an explicit owner choice.     {
      "id": "EI-20204456779824251",
      "title": "Migration 797's engineer_issues terminal guard is applied to the live DB while the deployed :3070 operator still writes terminal transitions through the view — no agent on :3070 can close a bug/change item",
      "summary": "## Why this exists when EI-20200310688058514 already reports the symptom\nThat item is in the **observation lane** (`payload.lane = \"observation\"`), so it is structurally unclaimable and will never reach `scheduler:get_next` / `claim_next` — raising its severity explicitly does not change that. The fleet-wide blocker therefore had **no actionable work-item at all**. This is that item; the observation carries the full root-cause writeup as a comment.\n\n## The defect\n`harness_shared.engineer_issues_view_dml()` (migration **797**, EI-20092514168581881) refuses any terminal transition written through the `engineer_issues` compatibility **view**, directing the caller to `work_items:set_state` / `work_items:complete`. The companion code that makes those tools satisfy it — `issues-engineer.ts:2003`, updating the unified `work_items` **BASE table** — landed on staging at 23:15:51Z (`c429711ea8`).\n\n**The deployed sha `7511ab5b` serving `:3070` has ZERO references to marker `20092514168581881`.** So the guard enforces against a writer that predates it, and the error names the very tools that trip it. `done`, `resolved`, `closed`, `work_items:set_state` and `work_items:complete` all fail identically, which reads as a malformed call and invites re-trying tokens forever.\n\n## Evidence\n- `pg_proc`: the trigger function contains the raise, gated on `TG_OP='UPDATE' AND NEW.state IN ('resolved','closed','done','dropped') AND OLD.state NOT IN (...)`.\n- `harness_shared.schema_migrations`: `797-guard-engineer-issues-terminal-state.sql` applied **23:14Z**, recorded under its **bare `.sql`** name — i.e. it was armed when applied.\n- `git show 7511ab5b:packages/operator-core/lib/issues-engineer.ts | grep -c 20092514168581881` → **0**; on staging → **1**.\n- Terminal writes to issue-family items ARE succeeding continuously for other agents (00:01, 00:09, 00:14) — so this is scoped to whoever `:3070` serves, not universal. That falsified my first \"fleet-wide outage\" reading and is worth preserving.\n\n## The trap for the next diagnoser\nAfter 797 was applied, **both 797 and 798 were re-parked as `.PENDING-CODE-DEPLOY`**. The suffix makes a migration invisible to auto-apply, so the files on disk now read as *never armed* — while this database already has the guard live. Anyone reasoning from the tree alone will conclude the guard cannot possibly be in force. Migration 798 exists precisely to make this failure actionable (\"makes its stale-writer failure actionable on already-migrated databases\") and is itself parked, so we get the confusing error instead.\n\n## Nothing is lost\nThe completion **record** is still written; only the state write fails, reported honestly as `stateError`. Affected items keep their evidence and stay `open` — they need a re-flip after the deploy, not a redo.\n\n## Fix\n1. **Deploy staging to `:3070`** — carries the base-table writer and resolves it. This is the whole fix.\n2. Do **NOT** drop the guard from the live DB. It is correct; the deployed code is what is stale, and removing it re-opens the ungated-terminal-write hole 797 closed.\n3. **Durable guard against the class:** applying a `PENDING-CODE-DEPLOY`-class migration should verify its `REQUIRES-DEPLOYED` marker is present in the *deployed* sha before arming — right now the coupling is a filename convention plus a comment, enforced by nothing, and re-parking the file after the fact silently hides that the DB is ahead. That is the recurrence guard this incident is asking for.",

      "state": "open",

    {
      "id": "EI-20206285706779155",
      "title": "Vitest discovery follows a RELOCATED cargo target symlink and collects build-artifact copies of template checks as real tests — 15 phantom failures in one full local run",
      "summary": "MEASURED, not inferred. A full local run at commit 94bbdcb031857f6852bfe817912b0023fde78f60 recorded 28 failures. 15 of those 28 — over half — are the SAME file, composition-integrity.test.ts, collected from BUILD-ARTIFACT directories that are copies of templates/*/checks/, never from the canonical source.\n\nEVIDENCE (harness_shared.test_runs, commit_sha=94bbdcb0..., status='fail'): 15 rows whose file_path begins\n  papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/{universal-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin}/release/bundle/macos/Papercusp {GUI,Server}.app/Contents/Resources/sidecar/templates/{papercusp-webapp,papercusp-desktop-app,papercusp-agentic-desktop-app}/checks/composition-integrity.test.ts\nplus 3 more under papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target/darwin-sidecar/templates/.\nThese are macOS .app bundle payloads being run as tests on a Linux box.\n\nROOT CAUSE — the exclusion globs are defeated by RELOCATION, and that is why `**/target/**` does not save us:\n  1. `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target` is a SYMLINK:\n       lrwxrwxrwx papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target -> /mnt/data/relocated-builds/papercusp-desktop-src-tauri-target\n     The real bytes live OUTSIDE the repo, so any exclusion expressed as a repo-relative path under target/ can be bypassed by a walker that follows the link.\n  2. A second relocated cargo dir, `.wi3388-cargo-target/`, sits IN-tree and contains 17 *.test.ts files. Its name does not match `target/` at all, so every `**/target/**` exclusion misses it outright.\n\nDIAGNOSTIC TELL worth knowing (it is how I found the symlink): `[ -f \"<path under src-tauri/target>\" ]` answers YES while `find papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/target -name composition-integrity.test.ts` answers 0. `-f` follows symlinks; `find` does not descend them without -L. A disagreement between those two is the signature of a relocated build dir.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND NOISE: these are false failures with real, plausible-looking test names, in a suite agents read to decide whether the shared gate is safe to fire. Tonight the full-run signal was 28 failures of which at most 13 could be real; an agent triaging that list burns its context on 15 files that do not exist as source. This is the same false-signal class as EI-20203883939710354 (fixture-log false signal) and the gate-log fiction I hit earlier tonight.\n\nSCOPE NOTE: all 15 rows are source='local'. I did NOT observe these in a CI gate run, so this is a local-full-run signal-pollution bug, not (on this evidence) a gate-red cause. Do not widen that claim without CI rows.\n\nFIX DIRECTION: exclude by RESOLVED REAL PATH rather than by glob — or refuse to descend symlinks during test discovery — and add the relocated dirs (`.wi3388-cargo-target`, any `*-cargo-target`, and the resolved src-tauri/target target) to the vitest exclude set. A guard that asserts zero collected test files resolve outside the repo root would make the whole class impossible rather than enumerating names.",

      "id": "EI-20206392451210997",
      "title": "improvements:capture checkDuplicatesOnly returns ZERO duplicates for an issue the same tool then flags at 0.94 hard-semantic on the real call — the advertised cheap pre-check under-reports",
      "summary": "Measured 2026-08-12T00:50-00:52Z. Directly reproduced, twice, back to back, in one session. Both calls reported dedupCoverage lexical:ok semantic:ok degraded:false — so this is NOT a degraded-embeddings artifact, which is the obvious alternative explanation and is explicitly ruled out by the tool's own coverage field.\n\nTHE TWO CALLS:\n1. improvements:capture { title: 'db:check_drift reports executable content_drift on already-applied migrations (151, 159, 181, ...) — edits that never ran and never will', checkDuplicatesOnly: true }\n   => ok:true, created:false, reason:'check-only', possibleDuplicates: []  (ZERO)\n2. improvements:capture { kind:'bug', title: <THE SAME STRING>, body: <~2500 chars of detail> }\n   => ok:true, created:false, reason:'likely-duplicate', possibleDuplicates: 5, top hit EI-19415309774723126 '46 applied migrations have EXECUTABLE drift — DDL edited in after apply that never ran on the live DB' at similarity 0.94, semantic:'hard'. Four more at 0.87-0.89.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS: the tool's own See-also guidance says 'SYMPTOM-FIRST — improvements:capture { title, checkDuplicatesOnly:true } BEFORE you diagnose: has anyone already hit this? costs one call and a title, and creates nothing'. An agent that follows that guidance gets a clean [] and reasonably concludes the signal is unfiled. The whole purpose of the pre-check is to prevent duplicate filings and wasted diagnosis, and here it produced the exact opposite: it green-lit work on something already open as EI-19415309774723126 (major). I only avoided filing the duplicate because I happened to write the full body and let the REAL call adjudicate.\n\nLIKELY MECHANISM (hypothesis, NOT confirmed — I did not read the implementation): the title-only path appears to score against a different/weaker signal than the title+body path. A 0.94 'hard' semantic match is far above any plausible threshold, so the pre-check is probably not running the same semantic comparison at all (title-only embedding vs title+body embedding), rather than running it with a stricter cutoff. Someone should read the two code paths and confirm which before fixing — do not take my guess as the diagnosis.\n\nWHY IT IS NOT MY MISUSE: the titles were BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two calls. The only difference was the presence of kind+body. So the divergence cannot be explained by my phrasing.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: make checkDuplicatesOnly run the SAME matcher the real capture runs, or — if a title-only embedding genuinely cannot reach parity — have the pre-check say so out loud (a coverage caveat like 'title-only: weaker than the full check') instead of returning a confident empty array. An empty [] and 'no semantic signal available at this fidelity' are completely different answers to the agent reading it, and right now the tool returns the first when it means the second.\n\nRECURRENCE GUARD WORTH ADDING: a test that files a known item, then asserts checkDuplicatesOnly on its exact title returns a non-empty possibleDuplicates — i.e. pins pre-check/real-call parity so this cannot silently regress again.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20238078813478292",
      "title": "Verifying the spawner-sidecar collapse via `systemctl list-units --type=scope | grep sidecar` gives a FALSE GREEN — the scope list is not the sidecar population; only `ss -lxp` listeners are",
      "summary": "## The trap\n\nP-007 of `spawner-sidecar-cluster-fanout-2026-08-12` asks a verifier to confirm the spawner sidecars collapse from ~16 per host to 1. The obvious probe is:\n\n    systemctl --user list-units --type=scope --all | grep -i sidecar\n\nOn this box (2026-08-12T09:10Z) that returns **2** scopes, and both have an ExecStart pointing at the STAGING tree (`.../papercusp/apps/operator/bin/spawner-sidecar.ts`), i.e. the tree that CARRIES the fix. Read naively that is a textbook pass: \"2 sidecars, running fixed code, collapse confirmed.\"\n\n**It is wrong.** The real population at that same instant was **20 live spawner listeners**, 17 of which belong to a single host family:\n\n    ss -lxp | grep -oE '/tmp/papercusp-spawner-[0-9]+\\.sock' | sort -u\n\n- 1 cluster primary — pid 30305 (`node dist-host/hono-host.mjs`, ppid 4035)\n- 16 cluster workers — all with `ppid == 30305`\n- 3 unrelated hosts\n\nThat is the un-collapsed fan-out, fully intact.\n\n## Why the scope list lies\n\nThe socket is `/tmp/papercusp-spawner-<owner-pid>.sock`, where **owner-pid is the CALLING HOST process, and the listening sidecar is a DIFFERENT pid**. So sidecars are not in 1:1 correspondence with systemd scopes: most are not their own scope at all, and the handful that are tell you nothing about the total.\n\nTwo compounding reasons the naive read looks authoritative:\n\n1. **`PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT` decouples the sidecar BINARY from the HOST.** `papercup-dev-api.service` runs the RELEASE checkout (`papercup-release`, `dist-host/hono-host.mjs`) but sets `PAPERCUSP_INTEGRATION_ROOT=/…/papercusp`, so spawned sidecars execute STAGING code. The verifier sees fixed code running and concludes the fix is in effect. It is not: the socket NAME is computed **host-side**, by the unfixed release host. Fixed sidecar + unfixed caller = fan-out persists.\n2. **The count is small for an unrelated reason**, so it coincidentally matches the expected post-fix number.\n\n## Correct behavior\n\nThe acceptance probe for this plan (and any future sidecar-population question) must count **listeners**, not scopes, and must classify each socket's owner pid by `ppid` against the cluster primary. Anything that reports a sidecar population from `systemctl list-units` is measuring the wrong object.\n\nWorth considering: have `pid-keyed-socket.ts` expose a population/inventory helper so the count has ONE canonical implementation, rather than each verifier hand-rolling a shell probe and picking the wrong instrument.\n\n## Why this matters beyond one plan\n\nThis would have produced a false green on the plan's OWN acceptance criterion, at the exact moment the plan is graded — i.e. the failure lands on the surface designed to catch failures. The plan's `## Now` (rev 20) and my loop `checks` now both carry the corrected probe, but the trap is generic to \"count the sidecars\" and will outlive this plan.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "done",

    {
      "id": "EI-20386584937642609",
      "title": "fleet:launch-on-plan with count<=liveMembers is a suppressed NO-OP launch that still re-stamps the fleet claim spec — silently clobbering an authored multi-plan spec",
      "summary": "2026-08-14T00:33Z, fleet sidestage-gpt: called fleet:launch-on-plan { name:'sidestage-gpt', plan:'sidestage-standout-features-2026-08-13', count:1 } while 12 members were live. The launch itself was correctly suppressed (\"NO new terminals opened\", relaunchSuppressed:true / count<=live) — but claimSpecApplied still ran: it overwrote the AUTHORED rev17 three-plan spec (standout + checkout-shipping + red-yellow-retheme, ruled deliberate by plan Decision D-018) with a single-plan filter (rev18, plan=standout only). Every member's next scheduler:get_next pull would then scope-refuse checkout-shipping/retheme claims — su-deeb7d was mid-claim on WI-38634 (checkout-shipping) at that exact moment. Leader restored rev19 by hand at 00:34Z. FIX SHAPE: a launch call that opens ZERO terminals must not mutate the claim spec (spec application should be conditional on opened.length>0, or at minimum refuse to LOWER an authored spec's plan coverage without an explicit flag).     {
      "id": "EI-20402188135645864",
      "title": "@papercusp/dock-workbench: passing `className` silently REPLACES the dockview base theme, undefining ~29 --dv-* variables",
      "summary": "MECHANISM (verified, not inferred)\n\n`DockWorkspace` renders (libs/dock-workbench/src/DockWorkspace.tsx:294):\n\n    className={className ?? 'dockview-theme-dark'}\n\ndockview defines its ~110 `--dv-*` variables INSIDE its theme classes\n(`.dockview-theme-light { … }`), never on `:root`. So `className` is not an\nadditive hook — supplying one REPLACES the base theme and every variable the\nconsumer does not personally re-declare resolves to nothing.\n\nCSS makes this invisible: an unknown custom property is not an error, and\n`var(--undefined)` is not a warning. Nothing typechecks, nothing throws,\nnothing logs. The dock renders and merely looks slightly off.\n\nMEASURED IMPACT (SideStage seller dock, the first consumer to pass a className)\n- 47 `--dv-*` variables are read by dockview's generic (non-theme) rules.\n- 18 were declared by the consumer's token layer.\n- 29 resolved to NOTHING, including:\n    --dv-sash-color                          (the resize handles)\n    --dv-tabs-and-actions-container-height   (tab strip height)\n    --dv-tab-font-size, --dv-border-radius, --dv-tab-border-radius\n    --dv-transition-duration, --dv-active-sash-transition-*\n    --dv-overlay-z-index                     (drag overlay stacking)\n\nThe resize sash being uncoloured is the sharpest one: the dock's entire reason\nfor existing is draggable/resizable panels, and the drag affordance was\ninvisible.\n\nWHY IT IS LATENT RATHER THAN RARE\npapercusp's own HarnessDock (apps/operator/app/harness/dock/HarnessDock.tsx:159)\nwrites the SAME `className ?? 'dockview-theme-dark'` at its call site. It is\nunaffected today only because no papercusp caller actually passes a className\n(grep for `dockview-theme` in apps/operator source: zero hits outside\nnode_modules). The trap is armed for the first one that does.\n\nPROPOSED DURABLE FIX\nMake the class COMPOSE instead of replace — e.g. a `baseTheme` prop defaulting\nto `'dockview-theme-dark'`, always emitted alongside `className`:\n\n    className={`${baseTheme} ${className ?? ''}`.trim()}\n\nBackward compatible for every current consumer (HarnessDock's explicit\n'dockview-theme-dark' would merely duplicate, which is harmless), and it makes\nthe base theme impossible to drop by accident.\n\nNOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY: dock-workbench is a git submodule shared with\npapercusp (plan sidestage-seller-dockview-2026-08-14 D-012/D-013/D-014), and\nchanging its default class behaviour mid-fleet would reach papercusp's Work tab.\nFiling rather than grabbing.\n\nWORKAROUND IN PLACE (SideStage only)\nCall site now passes both classes, base first:\n`SELLER_DOCK_CLASS_NAME = 'dockview-theme-light seller-dock-theme'`\n(apps/web/src/SellerDock.tsx), pinned by apps/web/src/seller-dock-chrome.test.ts,\nwhich asserts no variable dockview reads is left undefined and carries\ndeliberately-broken controls so it cannot silently stop measuring. That guard is\nper-consumer, though — it does not protect the next consumer of the library.\n\nFound under WI-38699 / P-011.",

      "summary": "The tracked mobile store/RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md says a successful release run replaces its hashes, but the build writes provenance only after requiring a clean tree and binding current HEAD. Updating the tracked record afterward necessarily makes the tree dirty (and once committed changes HEAD), so android-release-provenance.sh verify correctly rejects the exact artifacts. Reproduced on fresh 0.1.0 candidate 1fc431d: only the candidate-doc refresh was dirty, and verify failed at assert_clean_source.     {
      "id": "EI-20445868109303312",
      "title": "Rescue/preserved copies of an uncommitted file exist ONLY on local disk — no off-machine durability, and sweeps did not capture it",
      "summary": "⚠ **RETITLED + DOWNGRADED 2026-08-14T17:19Z. The original title asserted a LOSS THAT DID NOT HAPPEN and is retracted.**\n\n## What I originally claimed (WRONG)\nThat `deploy-health-contract.test.ts` was silently lost from the live sidestage hive tree and the sole copy on Earth was the vestigial checkout.\n\n## Why it was wrong\nI had searched only the two git trees. **Two identical copies (md5 `61f151bc`) existed the whole time** — in `~/.papercusp/preserved/` and `~/.papercusp/rescue/`. My probe answered \"does it exist HERE\" when I had asked \"does it exist AT ALL\". Nothing was lost. The full source is also preserved verbatim as a comment on WI-38870 (post 64321).\n\n## What survives the correction — the real, narrower defect\n**None of the surviving copies is off-machine.**\n- rescue commit `447f6cf` is on a **local-only branch** — not on `origin/main`, not on `origin/staging`.\n- `~/.papercusp/preserved/` has **no `.git` at all**.\n- The PG comment on WI-38870 is currently the only copy outside a local filesystem.\n\nSo a single-disk event still takes all of them. That is a genuine durability gap, but it is a *latent* one, not a realised loss — hence `minor`, not `major`.\n\n## The generalisable part\nA \"rescue\" or \"preserved\" copy **feels like** a backup and is not one. Both names assert durability that neither location provides; a rescue that never leaves the machine only defends against the failure modes that were never the dangerous ones. Anything genuinely worth rescuing should land somewhere replicated — a pushed branch or a PG record — and the rescue step should say which.\n\n## Method note (the reason this was wrong for ~2h)\nThe original filing was a confident conclusion drawn from ONE probe over an incomplete search scope. `find` across two directories cannot answer an existence question about the whole machine, but its empty result reads exactly like proof of absence. Widen the scope before asserting a negative — a not-found is only as strong as the ground you searched.",
