      "title": "record-release-cli defaults --workspace to 'papercusp-workspace', so recording ANY other product's release silently pollutes Papercusp's public release page",
      "summary": "OWNER-VISIBLE. [owner:Avi 2026-08-15, interactive turn, verbatim]: \"Also remove this from our releases page I don't know how it got there\" — followed by a 0.1.0 alpha entry listing SideStage_0.1.0_android.aab / .apk, \"No changelog was written for this release\", \"427 work items across 14 plans\".\n\nWHAT HAPPENED: harness_shared.releases held (workspace_id='papercusp-workspace', channel='alpha', version='0.1.0'), cut_at 2026-08-14T23:07:13.757Z, git_sha 010a02b2678fc878c9377775eacfb497d63e7cc0, cut_by su-08298ddf-dba7-4def-9e9d-8cb75477bafe, published_at NULL, artifacts = the two SideStage ANDROID files, work_item_ids 4828, plan_slugs 33. SideStage is a DIFFERENT product; this is not a Papercusp desktop release. Because 0.1.0 sorts newest it displaced 0.0.16 as the page's \"alpha latest\".\n\nROOT CAUSE — apps/operator/lib/release/record-release-cli.ts:1259:\n    workspaceId: arg(argv, '--workspace') ?? 'papercusp-workspace',\nwhile :1253 lets the caller freely override the PRODUCT name:\n    mobileProductName: arg(argv,'--mobile-product-name') ?? env.PAPERCUSP_MOBILE_PRODUCT_NAME ?? 'Papercusp',\nSo `record-release-cli --scan-mobile --version 0.1.0 --mobile-product-name SideStage` with no --workspace writes SideStage's artifacts into PAPERCUSP's registry with no warning. The artifact basenames already said SideStage — the tool had everything it needed to refuse, and did not.\n\nFIX (durable, not just the cleanup): make a workspace default that is incoherent with the product a HARD REFUSAL rather than a silent write. If --mobile-product-name (or the resolved artifact basenames) do not match the target workspace's product, REQUIRE an explicit --workspace and exit non-zero naming both values. Recurrence guard to land with it: a test asserting that `--mobile-product-name SideStage` with no --workspace exits non-zero and writes nothing. Consider additionally refusing a release row whose artifact set is 100% mobile for a workspace whose product is a desktop app.\n\nCLEANUP ALREADY DONE 2026-08-15T17:04Z: row backed up to /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/spurious-release-0.1.0-backup-20260815T170416Z.json (108168 bytes, full row_to_json — restorable), then DELETE 1 against the exact 3-column primary key. Verified after: the registry reads 0.0.16 / 0.0.15 / 0.0.14 / 0.0.13 / 0.0.12, so 0.0.16 is correctly \"alpha latest\" again. published_at was NULL so nothing had been published to r2 — no artifact retraction was needed.\n\nSTILL WORTH CHECKING (not done): whether the same mis-scoped write hit any OTHER product's registry, and whether sidestage has its own workspace_id row this SHOULD have gone to.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20576535595925497",
      "title": "Completing a SUB-LANE work-item silently closes its parent plan item: sibling rows share one payload.plan_item stamp (126 plan items affected, 51 still live)",
      "summary": "## What happens\n\n`work_items:complete` propagates to a plan item via `finishPlanStamp()`, which reads **`payload.plan_item`**. Nothing enforces that this stamp is UNIQUE to one work-item. When a sub-lane/child row inherits its parent's stamp, completing the CHILD flips the PARENT's plan item to `done` — and `plan-item-reconcile:done` then faithfully mirrors that onto the parent work-item, which closes with acceptance criteria that were never met.\n\nThis is a false-green with an unusually clean disguise: the parent work-item's `terminal_owner` reads `system:plan-item-reconcile`, so the audit trail names the *mirroring* actor and never the *originating* one.\n\n## Measured instance (end-to-end, 2026-08-16)\n\nBoth rows carry the **identical** stamp `{item_id:'P-004', plan_slug:'release-build-vm-dev-parity-audit-2026-08-13', harness_slug:'papercusp'}`:\n\n| work-item | role |\n|---|---|\n| WI-38600 | the real P-004 item (live Windows VM install) |\n| WI-39352 | a **sub-lane** of P-004 (offline artifact inspection) |\n\nChain, each hop pinned to code:\n\n1. WI-39352 created as a P-004 sub-lane, inheriting `payload.plan_item.item_id='P-004'`.\n2. WI-39352 completed `02:19:54Z` — a legitimate close; its own offline scope was genuinely done (`terminal_owner=su-3444a9e3`, `authority='committed'`).\n3. `complete.ts:1253` `finishPlanStamp()` reads `payload.plan_item`, passes the `/^P-\\d{3,}$/` check, and `complete.ts:1312` fires `plans:set-status P-004 → done`. That is **plan revision 46 @ 02:19:55.507Z**, 1.5 s later.\n4. `reconcile-rule.ts:87` (`plan-item-reconcile:done`) fires on that `plans:set-status` and mirrors `done` onto WI-38600 @ `02:38:05Z`, `terminal_owner='system:plan-item-reconcile'`, `authority='proposed'`.\n\nCorrected at plan revision 53 (`02:45:06Z`) when the portfolio owner set P-004 back to `blocked`. P-004's real acceptance — installer exit + ProductVersion, GUI launch, in-WSL sidecar health — was unmet and *unmeetable* at the time: the Windows guest was still mid-install under WI-39356. Caught only because a human noticed an implausible close and asked directly.\n\n## Population — systemic, not a one-off\n\nOver `harness_shared.work_items` (workspace `papercusp-workspace`, harness `papercusp`), grouping by `payload->'plan_item'->>'item_id'`:\n\n```\nstamped_rows_total:          3478\ndistinct_plan_items:         3303\nplan_items_with_collision:    126   -- >1 work-item sharing one stamp\nrows_in_colliding_groups:     301\ncolliding_groups_still_live:   51   -- >=1 non-terminal row: STILL ARMED\nworst_group_size:              23   -- sidestage-public-release-testing-2026-08-14 P-009\n```\n\nFor the worst group, any **1 of 23** rows completing flips P-009. 51 groups currently hold a non-terminal row, so each is a live trigger.\n\n⚠ Honest scoping: a collision is a *necessary* condition for this failure, not proof that each of the 126 is a defect — some groups may be legitimate replicas (`work_item_replicas`) rather than sub-lanes. The causal chain is confirmed for P-004; the 126/51 figures size the exposure and should be triaged, not assumed all-bad.\n\n## The seam that makes this expensive to diagnose\n\nTwo plan-linkage surfaces exist and they DISAGREE:\n\n- `source_plan_item_ids` (column) — **NULL on both rows above**\n- `payload.plan_item` (jsonb) — the surface `finishPlanStamp` actually reads\n\nAuditing linkage via the column alone yields \"no plan-item link, so completion cannot propagate\" — wrong, and exactly the conclusion I reached one step before the correct one. `_create-core.ts:619` already carries a comment flagging that `finishPlanStamp` reads a SEPARATE surface, so the hazard was known and is still load-bearing.\n\n## Recommended durable fix\n\n1. A child/sub-lane row must not inherit the parent's `plan_item` stamp — stamp it with a `parent_plan_item` ref that `finishPlanStamp` deliberately ignores; or\n2. Make the stamp unique per plan item: refuse to create/stamp a second row claiming an already-stamped `P-NNN` in the same plan.\n\nPrefer (2) if the create path cannot reliably distinguish sub-lane from replica — it fails loudly at the point of the mistake rather than at completion time, hours later.\n\n## Recurrence guard (required)\n\nInvariant: **no two non-terminal work-items may share a `payload.plan_item` identity** within a workspace+harness. The grouping SQL above is the check verbatim (rows returned == violated), so it drops straight into `fleet:invariant` or a test over a seeded fixture. Without it, the next instance is again found only by a human noticing an implausible close.\n\nReconciling the 51 live groups is a separate remediation from the code fix — the stamp collisions already on disk do not clear themselves.\n\n## Not the cause\n\n`plan-item-reconcile` behaved exactly as written and should NOT be changed — it faithfully mirrored a plan item that really had been set to `done`. The defect is upstream, in what got stamped. Likewise `work_items:complete`'s propagation is correct by design; it is operating on bad input.\n\n## Evidence index\n\nCode: `complete.ts:1253` (finishPlanStamp reads payload.plan_item), `complete.ts:1311-1320` (fires plans:set-status), `reconcile-rule.ts:87` (mirrors onto linked work-items), `_create-core.ts:619` (pre-existing SEPARATE-surface comment). Timeline: `harness_shared.plan_revisions` seq 45 (01:59:30Z P-004 `todo`) → seq 46 (02:19:55.507Z, author su-3444a9e3, P-004 `done`) → WI-38600 closed 02:38:05Z → seq 53 (02:45:06Z, su-b9e0ec11, back to `blocked`).",

    {
      "id": "EI-20577421906951067",
      "title": "A plan-linked work-item auto-closed by plan-item-reconcile cannot be reopened by ANY documented route — the mirror is done-ward only, and work_items:set_state refuses the write while pointing at the mechanism that cannot do it",
      "summary": "## The deadlock\n\nThree behaviours are individually defensible and jointly make a state unreachable:\n\n1. **`plan-item-reconcile:done` is done-ward only.** `reconcile-rule.ts:87` registers exactly one rule, gated on `r.newStatus === 'done' && r.oldStatus !== 'done'` (`newlyDonePlanItem`, :64-72). Verified across the WHOLE module, not one file: the only other rules in `plan-items/` are `plan-item-reflect:*` (work-item → plan, the opposite direction) and `plan-item-lane-sync:blocked-by-changed`. No rule reacts to a plan item leaving `done`.\n\n2. **`work_items:set_state` refuses a direct write on a plan-linked row.** Observed verbatim: `work-item 'WI-38600' is linked to plan item(s) …#P-004; direct state:\"blocked\" writes are not durable because the plan item is the source of truth. Use plans:set-status { … } instead.`\n\n3. **`plans:set-status` off `done` fires nothing back down.**\n\nSo: the reconciler can close a work-item, and nothing can reopen it. The refusal in (2) actively misdirects — it names `plans:set-status` as the durable route, and `plans:set-status` provably cannot perform this transition.\n\n## Reproduction (live, not hypothetical)\n\n- 02:38:05Z — `plan-item-reconcile` closed **WI-38600** (`terminalOwner=system:plan-item-reconcile`, `completionAuthority='proposed'`, `terminalCompletionRef=null`).\n- 02:44Z — I corrected the source of truth: `release-build-vm-dev-parity-audit-2026-08-13#P-004` → `blocked` (rev 53).\n- 03:08Z — corrected again → `todo` (rev 55).\n- 03:10Z — `work_items:get WI-38600` → **still `state: done`**, same `closedAt`, same `terminalOwner`.\n\nTwo corrections to the declared source of truth, ~30 minutes, no propagation.\n\n## Why it matters beyond bookkeeping\n\nThe row that stays falsely `done` is the *Windows clean-install and live-drive verdict* for the 0.0.17 release. It will read `done` even after the real live-drive runs, so a reader asking \"is Windows verified?\" gets yes from the work-item and the correct answer only from the plan item. This is the same false-completion class as EI-20405552992224051, but in the direction nobody can repair.\n\nIt also makes the repair sweep on EI-20576535595925497 (126 affected plan items) **impossible via the supported path** — correcting those plan items will not release the work-items the reconciler closed behind them.\n\n## Deliberately NOT fixed here, and why\n\nThe obvious fix — a reconcile rule for `done → non-done` that reopens linked work-items — is genuinely dangerous to ship unilaterally: with 126 already-affected plan items, adding it could mass-reopen hundreds of rows, including many legitimately done, converting a silent false-positive into a loud false-negative across the fleet. That needs a deliberate migration with per-row judgement, not a reaction rule dropped in by whoever noticed.\n\nFiling it with the diagnosis instead. Related and adjacent: EI-20576535595925497 (the close-side cause; I fixed its guard asymmetry in `complete.ts` this session) and EI-20405552992224051 (reconciler closes with `proposed`/null evidence).\n\n## Interim guidance for anyone reading an auto-closed row\n\nFor a work-item whose `terminalOwner` is `system:plan-item-reconcile`, the **plan item is authoritative and the work-item row may be stale-done**. Do not read that `done` as a verdict.",

    {
      "id": "EI-20580419609576585",
      "title": "The attestation-wall \"degrade around it\" path also suppresses the .deb REPACK, so local_matrix can never pass while the owner-gated GitHub wall stands — the non-GitHub legs are not independently measurable",
      "summary": "MEASURED on the forced live-federation-gate run 2026-08-16T03:41:32Z→03:49:40Z (work dir /tmp/live-fed-gate-20260815-234132, invoker=hand, GATE_FORCE=1 RIG_WAIT=1). Filed from the p2p coordination release lane (WI-37110).\n\n## Why this matters\nThe gate was taught (2026-08-15 22:13 EDT) to DEGRADE AROUND the owner-gated GitHub attestation wall instead of aborting, so the remaining legs could still be measured. The lane has since been operating on the belief that \"the NON-GitHub legs (local_matrix, build) are now measurable\". **That belief is wrong**, and this run is the evidence: local_matrix still cannot pass while the wall stands, because the wall's skip path also suppresses an artifact local_matrix requires.\n\n## Observed\nVerdict `SKIPPED-STORM`; legs: build=**OK**, local_matrix=**FAIL**, content_matrix/from_repo/from_repo_witness=SKIPPED-ATTESTATION-WALL.\nThe build leg genuinely succeeded (`✓ sidecar built 4.8G`) and local_matrix got further than it has in weeks — cleared the sidecar-binary check, provisioned 3 frames, brought up the testnet DHT (bootstrap 10.99.0.5:49737), reached `exec deb-hetzner-matrix.sh` — then died on:\n```\n[testvm] FATAL: default_deb() picked '/home/marsh-office/.cargo-target/release/bundle/deb/Papercusp GUI_0.0.17_amd64.deb'\n — its mtime is ~0d OLDER than the newest source commit touching the bundle inputs ... REFUSING to\n silently continue on a possibly-stale artifact (EI-18160721229588594)\n=== artifact:  ===\nFATAL: .deb not found:\n```\nNo federation scenario executed. NOTE for anyone reading the verdict line: the FAIL is NOT a federation regression, and the `SKIPPED-STORM`/load-124 banner is not the cause either (the gate itself says \"frames NOT starved ... do NOT conclude 'the box was too loaded'\").\n\n## Mechanism (read in source)\n`live-federation-gate.sh` §2 rebuilds the sidecar and then REPACKS a fresh .deb, publishing it as `GATE_DEB`. That repack is gated:\n```sh\nif [ \"$SKIP_MATRIX\" != 1 ] && [ \"$FAIL_BUILD\" != 1 ]; then\n  ...  dpkg-deb -b pkg \"$GATE_DEB\" ... && log \"repacked fresh .deb (base=$BASE_DEB)\"\n```\n`SKIP_MATRIX` is the same flag the attestation-wall skip trips. With it set, no fresh `GATE_DEB` is produced — and this run's build.log contains NO repack line at all, consistent with the repack never running. `local_matrix` then falls back to `default_deb()`, which finds the last on-disk .deb and applies the staleness guard.\n\n⚠ ONE LINK NOT DIRECTLY VERIFIED: I confirmed the repack is gated on `SKIP_MATRIX != 1`, that content_matrix reported SKIPPED-ATTESTATION-WALL, and that no repack line was logged. I did NOT single-step the attestation-wall branch to watch it assign `SKIP_MATRIX=1`. Treat the coupling as strongly evidenced but confirm that assignment before shipping a fix.\n\n## The staleness guard is separately near-unsatisfiable on this box\n`papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm/lib/common.sh:227-244`:\n```sh\nouter_ts=\"$(git -C \"$outer\" log -1 --format=%ct -- apps/operator ...)\"\nif [ \"$newest_ts\" -gt \"$deb_ts\" ]; then\n  age_days=$(( (newest_ts - deb_ts) / 86400 ))\n  die \"... its mtime is ~${age_days}d OLDER ...\"\n```\nIt dies when ANY commit touching those paths is newer than the .deb mtime **by even one second**, and integer division renders that as `~0d OLDER` — a hard refusal whose own message reads like \"not stale at all\", which is actively misleading in a long boot log.\nThat interacts badly with this repo's commit model: git-sync sweeps the WHOLE tree on a schedule. Measured here: commits touching `apps/operator` have a **median gap of 563s (~9.4 min)** over the last 24h (n=29). A 1.5GB .deb takes longer than that to build, so a freshly built .deb is typically already \"stale\" by this definition before it can be used. The .deb in question was built 23:11 EDT and the newest commit was 23:34:40 EDT — a git-sync sweep (`sync(operator-core,operator-docs,tools): 4 files, +126/-3 [skip ci]`), i.e. not a change anyone made to the bundle on purpose.\n\n## Fixes (two independent, both wanted)\n1. **Decouple the repack from `SKIP_MATRIX`.** local_matrix needs a fresh .deb regardless of whether the attestation-gated content-matrix leg runs. Either repack whenever the build succeeded, or have the local_matrix leg pass an explicit `--deb=` pointing at the artifact the gate just built. Without this, \"degrading around the wall\" is only cosmetic for local_matrix.\n2. **Make the staleness guard meaningful under a sweeping committer.** Compare against commits that actually touch BUNDLE INPUTS rather than all of `apps/operator`, and/or compare content (the sidecar build already writes a freshness stamp with a serve.mjs sha — `→ wrote sidecar freshness stamp (serve.mjs d765085ca0fd…)`) instead of mtime-vs-commit-time. At minimum stop printing `~0d OLDER` — report the real delta (`23m`) so the message stops contradicting itself.\n\n## Recurrence guard\nA test asserting that with `SKIP_MATRIX=1` (attestation wall tripped) and a successful build, the local_matrix leg still receives a non-stale .deb path — i.e. the wall cannot silently disarm the leg that does not depend on GitHub.\n\n## Related\n- EI-20578660332729593 (same run class): local-matrix.sh evaluates cheap artifact preconditions AFTER evicting 24 exclusive cores and provisioning 3 frames. This run is the second consecutive demonstration — widen that fix to hoist the whole artifact-precondition class (sidecar binary AND .deb presence/freshness) above the first provisioning step.\n- The wall itself (papercupai email_unverified; aviynw no oauth_token) remains owner-gated and is NOT a code bug — do not re-diagnose it as one.",

      "summary": "`packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/related-tests-selection.test.ts` is a NEW file (the tsc baseline has never seen it) whose errors are COMMITTED — not a peer's uncommitted mid-edit — and it has now been observed red 7 times across 64 minutes without being fixed.\n\nWHY THIS WAS FILED AND MOST REDS ARE NOT.       "title": "green-checkpoint's diff-based strand guards exit 2 NOT-CHECKED in EVERY gate run — they diff against HEAD in a clean checkout, so they examine zero files and protect nothing",
      "summary": "MEASURED in two independent gate runs today (logs /tmp/papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-1fxzuva-2026-08-18T{10-37-15,14-16-33}*.log):\n\n  @papercusp/operator-core :: lint:vimock-export-strands  -> exitStatus=2  capturedBytes=1053\n  @papercusp/operator-core :: lint:required-field-strands -> exitStatus=2\n\nByte-identical captured output in BOTH runs => deterministic, not incidental.\n\nExit 2 is EXIT_NOT_CHECKED from scripts/lib/not-checked.mjs (WI-37806). Root cause: both guards resolve their candidate set with `git diff --name-status <base> -- '*.ts' '*.tsx'` where base defaults to the literal 'HEAD' (check-vimock-export-strands.mjs:428). The gate judges a PRISTINE checkout of the candidate, so the working tree is clean vs HEAD => zero files differ => zero files examined => the guard correctly refuses to issue a clean bill and exits 2.\n\nConsequence: these two guards have NEVER actually run inside the gate. Locally (dirty tree) the same guard exits 0 and prints 6 real strands on packages/operator-core/lib/agent-facts/store.ts (+previewFactCapImpact). So the protection agents believe the gate provides is absent exactly where it was meant to bite.\n\nCORRECT STATE: the gate knows both endpoints (it logs `checkpointing candidate 177ba29a (base 4824a92b)`). It should invoke these guards with `--base <base-sha>` so they diff base..candidate rather than the empty working-tree diff.\n\n⚠ RISK BEFORE FIXING: turning a silently-skipped guard into an active one will surface the whole base..candidate backlog at once (main is currently 1408 commits behind staging), which could turn the gate REDDER. Land the --base wiring together with a triage of what it then reports; do not flip it during a live red-gate incident.",

      "id": "EI-20803703725014949",
      "title": "Affected-test batch watchdog SIGKILLs live/emitting tasks instead of extending them (progress-blind kill decision, e.g. operator-core::test:lane-stateful at the 2700s floor)",
      "summary": "## Symptom\n\nA green-checkpoint run can die with the whole gate going RED for a NON-CODE reason: the affected-task watchdog SIGKILLs `@papercusp/operator-core :: test:lane-stateful` at the 2700s floor timeout. No test asserted false — the task was killed for exceeding its budget.\n\nObserved live in RUN 9 (manual run, candidate `177ba29a`, started 2026-08-18T14:16:33Z), log `/tmp/papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-1fxzuva-2026-08-18T14-16-33-048Z.log`:\n\n```\nstate=running        task=\"@papercusp/operator-core :: test:lane-stateful\" elapsedSec=2700 timeoutMs=2700000 timeoutSource=floor durationEstimateMs=572305 exitStatus=pending\nstate=watchdog-killed task=\"@papercusp/operator-core :: test:lane-stateful\" elapsedSec=2700 timeoutMs=2700000 timeoutSource=floor durationEstimateMs=572305 signal=SIGKILL\n```\n\nNote `durationEstimateMs=572305` (~9.5 min) vs the 2700s it actually consumed — the scheduler's own estimate is off by ~4.7x for this task.\n\n## The underlying distribution (n=84, measured, not inferred)\n\nAcross `~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/*.log`, parsing `state=finished ... elapsedSec=` for this one task:\n\n- min 102s, **median 2416s**, p90 2828s, max 3260s\n- buckets: 0-299s:2 · 300-599s:31 · 1200-1499s:2 · 2100-2399s:7 · 2400-2699s:23 · 2700-2999s:18 · 3000-3299s:1\n- **42 of 84 finishes (50%) took >=2400s** — within 5 minutes of the 2700s ceiling\n- 19 of 84 finishes exceeded 2700s outright\n\nThat is a strongly BIMODAL distribution: a fast mode around 102-600s (~39% of runs) and a slow mode piled up at 2100-3260s (~58%), straddling the timeout. The task is close to a coin-flip between ~7 minutes and ~45 minutes, and the timeout sits inside the slow mode rather than outside it.\n\nConsequence: any given gate run has a substantial, essentially random chance of being killed here regardless of code quality — and a manual re-fire is subject to the same coin-flip.\n\n## What this does NOT explain (checked, so it is not assumed)\n\n**It is NOT the cause of the current 26-red streak.** Watchdog kills are RARE, not chronic: across 300 checkpoint logs there are only 5 kill events (4 x lane-stateful, 1 x `@papercusp/web :: test`), dated 2026-08-15T23:34, 2026-08-16T17:26, 2026-08-17T03:30, 2026-08-17T05:26 — and ZERO in the newest 12 cron runs. Most reds in the streak are therefore real test failures owned by WI-39450, not timeouts. This is a SEPARATE reliability defect that happened to bite RUN 9.\n\nI also do not know WHY it is bimodal — test ordering, a hung PG/stateful fixture, or host contention are all candidates I did not distinguish. Filing the measurement, not a diagnosis.\n\n## Method note (so the numbers can be trusted or refuted)\n\nThe task-state vocabulary is `started | running | finished | watchdog-firing | watchdog-killed`. There is NO `succeeded` state — an initial query for `state=succeeded` returned zero rows, which looks identical to \"this task never passes\". Confirmed via a vocabulary count (`grep -ho 'AFFECTED_TASK_PROGRESS state=[a-z-]*' | sort | uniq -c`) that `finished` is the terminal-success token. Anyone re-running this analysis should use `finished`.\n\n## Suggested direction\n\nThe real fix is to find out why the slow mode exists and remove it — a task whose own scheduler estimate is 9.5 min but whose median is 40 min is mis-modelled, and `durationEstimateMs` is evidently not tracking reality. Raising the timeout alone would only convert SIGKILLs into 45+ minute gate runs, which is its own problem given the gate is on an hourly cadence. Worth deciding deliberately rather than by default.",

          "terminalCompletionRef": "✅ Auto-implement resolved (verified):\nRetitled to correct the framing (the defect is a progress-blind kill decision, not lane-stateful's timing being bimodal). The fix — a progress-aware, re-arming batch watchdog — was already landed in the tree by prior successors (scripts/lib/batch-watchdog.mjs: pure-policy `decideWatchdogExpiry` + the injectable-clock `createProgressAwareWatchdog`; wired into scripts/affected-tests.mjs so a still-emitting task's kill deadline extends instead of firing SIGKILL, monotone vs the old timer and capped at BATCH_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS so a genuinely-wedged task is still killed).       "id": "EI-20971831715218093",
      "title": "events:await timeout fallback labels intentionally idle green-checkpoint producer stalled and recommends takeover",
      "summary": "A wait on green-checkpoint:inconclusive:papercusp timed out while checkpoint production was intentionally held pending a separate, live affected-test verifier. The verified fallback returned classification=stalled and nextAction=wake-owner-or-takeover based on the checkpoint producer being inactive. Fresh evidence contradicted the implied lane stall: WI-39450 owner was live 8s ago, task 0mt1bq0z98md2ik36iq advanced cpuSec 8625->8946, its cgroup gained 7.41 CPU-seconds/5s, operator-vite finished exit 0, and the next lint task started. This false alarm could provoke duplicate checkpoint work or claim takeover. The classifier should distinguish an intentionally quiescent downstream producer from a stalled upstream blocker, using the awaited note/work-item dependency or returning unknown/expected-idle when no checkpoint candidate/run exists.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "resolved",
      "classification": "candidate-terminal-residue",
      "recommendation": "candidate-unpark",
      "basis": "The parked item itself is terminal; D-018 admits terminal residue cleanup.",
      "fullReason": "D-022 / binding fleet claim-spec revision 20 audit: loop:arm's authoritative fleet admission gate returned fleet_scope_violation. Preserve tested implementation/evidence, but do not continue or re-claim from this non-P2P drain fleet.",
      "provenance": {
        "parkedBy": "su-6b043372-ca80-43e4-bba2-1306e3d57ffe",
        "parkedAt": "2026-08-21T03:26:27.020Z",

      "evidence": {

          "seeAlso": [],
          "authority": null,
          "completionRef": null,
          "terminalOwner": "2e45e469-018e-4633-9962-a9addd782c97",
          "terminalCompletionRef": "✅ Auto-implement resolved (verified):\nRoot cause: in packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/checkpoint-verified-wait.ts, checkpointObservationState() unconditionally withheld any explicit state for a CANDIDATE-BOUND wait (details.candidateSha/runId set) whenever activeRun was a non-null observation, regardless of whether activeRun.candidate was null. That fell through to classifyVerifiedWaitTimeout()'s generic timestamp-staleness heuristic, which uses checkpointProgressAtMs() as its baseline -- and that helper's LAST fallback is routines.greenCheckpoint.lastFiredAtMs (the routine's last scheduling TICK, not evidence of in-progress work). When the checkpoint mechanism had not yet started judging ANY candidate (activeRun.candidate == null) -- e.g. because it was intentionally quiescent behind a separate, live upstream affected-test verifier task -- that stale tick timestamp got misread as producer staleness, yielding classification=stalled / nextAction=wake-owner-or-takeover for a producer that was never actually stalled (risking a duplicate checkpoint dispatch or an unwarranted ownership takeover).\n\nFix: added an explicit branch in checkpointObservationState() -- when the wait is candidate-bound AND activeRun.candidate == null, return the conservative 'unknown' state (re-await) instead of falling through to the staleness heuristic. This only withholds a positive stalled/absent verdict when there is genuinely no candidate/run for the classifier to reason about; it does NOT change behavior once a DIFFERENT candidate is actually observed as active/recent (that case still legitimately falls through to the old stalled/absent diagnosis, since it's real evidence our candidate was skipped/superseded) -- covered by a new companion test. The unaffected paths (activeRun===null -> unknown, state==='active' -> progressing, non-candidate-bound idle detection) are untouched.\n\nAlso corrected packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/checkpoint-verified-wait.test.ts: the pre-existing test 'keeps a candidate-bound wait on the stalled path when its run disappears' asserted exactly the buggy classification (stalled/wake-owner-or-takeover) for activeRun.candidate===null -- that premise (no candidate == \"the run disappeared\") was itself wrong, since it's equally the signature of \"hasn't started judging yet\". Replaced it with two tests: one reproducing this bug's exact scenario (candidate-bound wait, activeRun present with candidate:null -> now correctly classifies unknown/re-await), and one proving the narrower 'a different candidate is actually being judged' case still correctly classifies stalled/wake-owner-or-takeover.\n\nTests: testing:run { files: [\"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/checkpoint-verified-wait.test.ts\"] } -> 10 passed, 0 failed (includes the new EI-20971831715218093 regression test and the differentiating \"different candidate\" test). build:typecheck { project: \"packages/operator-core\", files: [checkpoint-verified-wait.ts, checkpoint-verified-wait.test.ts], scopeToFiles: true } -> errorsInRequestedFiles: 0 (89 pre-existing baseline errors elsewhere in the import graph, unrelated to this change).\nLanded: pending git-sync (edits left in the shared staging tree per repo convention; no commit made by this worker) (rides the release gate)",

      "id": "EI-20975165607465816",
      "title": "release-fixer agent session consumed its full deadline with zero useful activity",
      "summary": "Process-ledger task 0mt1hhh3s1mz4sa7tt8 (launchedBy orchestrator:release-fixer) remained running for ~15 minutes with no work item, no recorded tool activity, and only 11 CPU-seconds, blocking safe checkpoint serialization. At its 08:30:32 EDT deadline it finally became timed_out with exitCode 143 and exitReason=agent turn timeout. The release reconciler should detect/prevent zero-first-turn fixer sessions earlier so the shared green gate does not wait a full deadline on a non-progressing actor.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "resolved",
      "classification": "candidate-terminal-residue",
      "recommendation": "candidate-unpark",
      "basis": "The parked item itself is terminal; D-018 admits terminal residue cleanup.",
      "fullReason": "D-022: binding fleet claim-spec revision 20 excludes release-fixer titles; revision-19 receipt was invalidated. Preserved task-ledger reproduction and focused 45/45 candidate-guard tests in checkpoint; do not re-admit in this non-P2P drain.",
      "provenance": {
        "parkedBy": "su-d0ecfb62-3a6d-49e9-ba38-f5f4267ab4b5",
        "parkedAt": "2026-08-21T03:24:25.153Z",
        "ageDays": 5.918072
      },
      "responsibleParty": {

      },
      "evidence": {
        "current": {
          "lane": null,
          "origin": "local",
          "takenBy": null,
          "takenAt": null,
          "createdAt": "1787229076611",
          "updatedAt": "1787324694549",
          "parentId": null,
          "sourcePlanSlug": null,
          "sourcePlanItemIds": null,
          "redundancy": null,
          "seeAlso": [],
          "authority": null,

          "terminalOwner": "fb7fd69f-572e-4f39-822e-3798bacb8338",
          "terminalCompletionRef": "✅ Auto-implement resolved (verified):\nVerified fixed — already landed in the tree (via git-sync sweep, no further code changes needed). Root cause: spawnInvokeOnce/runChild had no bound on the time between launch and the FIRST agent-stream chunk, so a release-fixer that hung at boot (or never produced a turn) consumed the whole overall invoke deadline (~900s here) doing nothing, blocking the release gate's safe checkpoint serialization while the fixer sat non-progressing. Fix: added a role-scoped bounded first-turn silence guard (RELEASE_FIXER_FIRST_TURN_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS = 5min, packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts) applied only for role==='release-fixer' at the shared spawn chokepoint. When no non-log stdout chunk arrives within the guard window, the child tree is SIGTERM'd early and the result carries a distinct firstTurnTimedOut flag + exitReason='agent first-turn timeout' (vs the generic 'agent turn timeout'). packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/invoke-outcome.ts classifies this combination as its own infra_loss branch with a distinct diagnostic detail (\"...before producing a turn (the bounded first-turn silence guard fired before the full invoke deadline)...\"), and the existing no-turn-escalation regex in packages/operator-core/lib/release/fixer-liveness.ts (isReleaseFixerNoTurnFailure, matches \"before producing a turn\") still recognizes it, so durable-spawn.ts's escalation path is unaffected. Net effect: a hung/silent release-fixer now fails in ~5min instead of consuming the full ~15min deadline, unblocking gate serialization far sooner.       "title": "Other standalone repos may carry the same unresolvable @papercusp/test-config devDep that just froze scout-runtime's gate for 12h (papercup-db, papercup-shared, zero-harness)",
      "summary": "CLASS RISK spun out of WI-39951. Filing rather than fixing inline: these are other harnesses with their own gates, outside this dispatch's scope.\n\nCONFIRMED (scout-runtime): declaring `@papercusp/test-config` in a repo with no npm workspaces makes `npm install` die E404 (the package is private:true inside the separate papercusp monorepo, so it 404s from the public registry). node_modules then never materializes and EVERY downstream leg fails at once — build TS2688, vitest startup error. The gate reads that as RED with zero named failing tests, i.e. an unattributable red nobody can triage from the summary alone. It froze scout-runtime's deploys ~12h.\n\nSUSPECTED, NOT VERIFIED — same shape, I did not run installs in these repos:\n  papercup-db      : deps=[@papercusp/test-config] workspaces=undefined lock=absent\n  papercup-shared  : deps=[@papercusp/test-config] workspaces=undefined lock=absent\n  zero-harness     : deps=[@papercusp/test-config] workspaces=undefined lock=absent\nAlso worth a look (different package, same pattern): templates-mirror and greenfield-giftscout-templates-ref declare `@papercusp/template-kit`; both DO have lockfiles.\nNOT an issue: scout-runtime-checkpoint is the gate's own isolated copy and inherits the scout-runtime fix; sidestage and greenfield-giftscout have a real `workspaces` field, so the dep resolves locally.\n\nWhy 'suspected': the absent lockfile cuts both ways — it may mean the repo is never installed standalone (so nothing breaks), or that installs have been failing unnoticed. Deciding it is one `npm install --dry-run` per repo; I did not run them because each belongs to another harness's lane.\n\nLIKELY ORIGIN (not attributable to a person — git-sync squashes all commits under one identity, so blame proves nothing here): scout-runtime's break came from a sweep that added the monorepo's shared `sharedHostWorkerCap()` vitest convention to repos outside the monorepo. Any repo caught by that same sweep without a workspaces root has this defect.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX, per affected repo — same shape that greened scout-runtime: inline the ~15-line worker-cap helper instead of importing it, drop the cross-repo dep, and declare any type package the tsconfig's `types` array names. The guard test added at scout-runtime/src/standalone-packaging.test.ts is directly portable and is the durable prevention (it asserts no @papercusp/* dep, every tsconfig `types` entry has a declared package, and no root config file — which tsc never typechecks — imports a workspace-private package).",

          "terminalCompletionRef": "✅ Auto-implement resolved (verified):\nRoot-caused the \"generator/saturation mechanism still needs attribution\" gap and fixed the actual defect: EI-12982's `preserveIncidentCapture` forensic-evidence mechanism (packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/perf-budgets.ts) pruned `*-incident-*.json` PSI-crit snapshots to a flat newest-100-file COUNT regardless of age, even though its documented purpose is to survive \"a root-cause pass that may happen days later.\" Measured live on this box: exactly 100 incident files present, oldest dated ~13h earlier — the entire evidence budget was being consumed and evicted in under half a day given this host's real infra-crit flap rate. That is precisely why the 2026-08-20 11:15 EDT incident cited in this bug (PSI memory full avg60=12.15) could not be root-caused the next day: its raw perf-signals capture had already rotated away before anyone got to look at it, well within the \"days later\" window the mechanism was supposed to guarantee. The original historical incident itself is not independently reproducible now (its evidence is gone and cannot be recovered), but the underlying defect — count-based rather than age-based retention — is fixed so this class of unattributable incident cannot recur.\n\nFix: replaced the flat `INCIDENT_CAPTURE_KEEP=100` count cap with a pure, unit-tested retention policy (`selectIncidentFilesToPrune`) that is AGE-based first (default 14-day retention window — evidence now genuinely survives \"days later\"), with a generous count-based safety backstop (5000 files, ~2,600 headroom above the observed live churn over 14d) purely as defense-in-depth against unbounded disk growth during a sustained pathological flap. `preserveIncidentCapture` now calls this policy instead of the old `.slice(INCIDENT_CAPTURE_KEEP)`.\n\nNo protected surfaces touched (not release/deploy machinery, DBOS scheduler, git-sync, lock authority, migrations, flags, or auth) — this is a self-contained fix inside one system-health module's forensic-retention helper.\n\nTests: testing:run on perf-budgets-incident-capture.test.ts + perf-budgets.test.ts → 65/65 passed (12 in the incident-capture file: 4 new pure unit tests for selectIncidentFilesToPrune — age-keeps-all, age-prunes-old, count-safety-cap-oldest-first, never-mutates-input — plus 2 new FS-integration tests replacing the old brittle \"newest 100\" assertion, proving age governs not count, and old files get pruned). build:typecheck scoped to my 2 files → errorsInRequestedFiles: 0 (88 pre-existing unrelated project errors elsewhere). npm run test:affected (changed-paths = my 2 files) → all 12 operator-core invariant guards exitStatus=0, operator-core stateful test lane (runs perf-budgets*.test.ts) exitStatus=0; unrelated web/operator-vite workspaces still running with zero failures when I stopped monitoring.\nLanded: 47725b45ce8f275547a79afa1a8cd85dde21e770 (rides the release gate)",

      "kind": "bug",

        "current": {
          "lane": null,
          "origin": "local",

          "terminalOwner": "b9501849-b6a6-4b07-aae7-ccfaeb0e52fb",
          "terminalCompletionRef": "✅ Auto-implement resolved (verified):\nRoot cause: the infra-liveness ALARM (system-health/liveness-alarm.ts §6 catch-all) pages a `blocker` escalation for ANY `crit` infra panel — including ordinary multi-tenant host-memory PSI pressure. WI-38449/D-007 already proved (and structurally attributed, via PerfVerdict.critAttribution) that this class of PSI-memory crit is `ambient-host`, never an operator defect — and used that split to stop it from blocking the DEPLOY gate — but the infra-liveness ALARM never inherited the same distinction. So under ordinary fleet load, PSI memory full avg60 oscillating across the crit threshold (~5) repeatedly opened/resolved a `panel:infra` blocker escalation and fleet-wide paged — the \"PSI thrashing\" this item reports recurring, unrelated to WI-5471 (a genuinely different bug: bg-host event-loop/PG-pool starvation, already fixed). The huge multi-day checkpoint history on this item is consistent with that: every wake found \"no matched process/cgroup delta\" and \"root cause remains unattributed\" because there IS no operator-side root cause to attribute — it's expected ambient load the alarm was wrongly treating as an operator fault.\n\nFix: added `infraCritAmbientOnly(d: InfraHealth)` in system-health/thresholds.ts — walks every independent infra-crit leg (perf critAttribution, MCP-proxy SLO, tool-handler failures, disk, gateway reachability) explicitly (infraStatus ORs them and short-circuits, so its boolean alone can't say which leg fired) and returns true only when perf is crit with an EMPTY operatorDefect list and every other leg is clean. Fail-safe: a perf verdict with no critAttribution at all (older projection / hand-built fixture) is NOT treated as ambient-only — it still pages, the expensive-but-safe direction, matching evaluatePerfSignals' own stated fail-safe stance. Wired into liveness-alarm.ts's §6 catch-all: when panel.key==='infra' and infraCritAmbientOnly(panel.data) is true, the signal is emitted as severity 'advisory' (still recorded/visible, never enters `newBlockerSignals` so it never fleet-pages) instead of 'blocker'.       "title": "Disk 100% full on /dev/nvme0n1 (/mnt/data + bind-mounted /tmp) — breaks gate + every agent test run",
      "summary": "EVIDENCE (measured 2026-08-21 ~07:50Z, release-fixer attempt 3 on frozen candidate 875a885d1968):\n\ndf: /dev/nvme0n1 7.3T size, 7.3T used, 9.0M-9.1G avail, 100% — mounted at BOTH /mnt/data and (bind) /tmp.\n  findmnt: \"/dev/nvme0n1[/tmp] /tmp xfs\" + \"/dev/nvme0n1 /mnt/data xfs\".\n  So /tmp is a SUBDIR of the /mnt/data volume; /tmp itself is only 29G. The exhaustion is /mnt/data-wide.\n\nDIRECT IMPACT OBSERVED (not inferred):\n- My own verification run could not create its log: \"bash: /tmp/rf-final.log: No space left on device\", then \"No such file or directory\". The run produced NOTHING.\n- A prior command failed identically writing /tmp/repairfiles.txt.\n- Green-checkpoint run 2026-08-21T07-27-32Z (cand ed20de6dcb05) shows \"Terminated\" and reports ~30 workspace test tasks FAILED — including @papercusp/sse, whose own progress line reads exitStatus=0 with every test file passing. That is an ABORTED run, not 30 regressions (filed separately).\n- gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict = 15 consecutive reds.\n\nTOP CONSUMERS (/mnt/data):\n  2.0T swapfile · 910G relocated-builds · 547G back · 518G offload · 454G papercusp-backups\n  383G transformerDB · 263G papercusp-audit-inputs · 174G Debug · 140G db · 86G MEMORYSTORE\n  54G tmp-offload · 34G Backup · 20G tmp\n\nWHY THIS IS A BUG NOT WEATHER: agents write scratch to /tmp constantly; at <10G headroom on a 7.3T volume shared with backups/DBs, test runs fail nondeterministically across unrelated packages. There is no headroom guard and no alarm — the gate simply goes red with misleading per-package failures.\n\nDURABLE FIX NEEDED (beyond reclaiming space):\n1. Give /tmp its own quota/filesystem (or XFS project quota) so agent scratch cannot be starved by, and cannot starve, /mnt/data data.\n2. A free-space precondition + alarm on the green-checkpoint gate: refuse/abort loudly with \"disk exhausted\" rather than emitting a per-package red list.\n3. Retention/reaping for the Papercusp-generated growers: relocated-builds (910G), papercusp-backups (454G), papercusp-audit-inputs (263G), tmp-offload (54G).\n\nNOT self-fixed: reclaiming space here means deleting owner-owned backups/DB/build data — irreversible and outside my authority.       "id": "EI-21048549665261701",
      "title": "/dev/nvme0n1 100% full: per-directory breakdown of /mnt/data — ~2.3TB is papercusp-generated build/backup/audit scratch",
      "summary": "Actionable follow-up data for escalations mt2nmgqj (disk full) and mt2noai4 (swapfile hazard). Filed as a durable, addressable record because coord:escalate COALESCED my attempt to update mt2nmgqj (bodyDiscarded:true), so new evidence cannot reach that thread.\n\n## Measured: du -x -d1 /mnt/data (KB)\n```\n5850410212  /mnt/data            (TOTAL, includes the 2TB swapfile as a direct file)\n 953840212  relocated-builds     ~953 GB\n 573259364  back                 ~573 GB\n 542975304  offload              ~543 GB\n 475822308  papercusp-backups    ~476 GB\n 400776212  transformerDB        ~401 GB\n 275045100  papercusp-audit-inputs ~275 GB\n 182398512  Debug                ~182 GB\n 146537384  db (mongodb)         ~147 GB\n  89190436  MEMORYSTORE           ~89 GB\n  55839320  tmp-offload           ~56 GB\n  35411020  Backup                ~35 GB\n  20266624  tmp  (== /tmp)        ~20 GB\n   1895864  Debug_ELI\n       540  Debug_BEN\n```\nArithmetic check: subdirs sum to 3,753,258,200 KB; total minus that = 2,097,152,012 KB = exactly the 2 TB swapfile, confirming it is counted.\n\n## Honest gap\ndu exited 1 (EXIT=1 recorded in the log) — it ran as marsh-office and hit permission-denied paths (Debug_JAMES and parts of mongodb-owned db report 0). So du accounts for ~5.45 TB of the 7.3 TB df reports USED; ~1.85 TB is UNATTRIBUTED and likely sits behind those denials. A root-run du would close that gap. Do not treat 5.45 TB as the complete picture.\n\n## Why this matters\n/dev/nvme0n1 is mounted at BOTH /mnt/data and /tmp (/tmp is the subdir /mnt/data/tmp). At 100% full every agent's /tmp scratch write ENOSPCs, including the Claude harness's own task-output file — it broke a routine Bash call during this run.\n\n## Largest plausibly-reclaimable, all papercusp-generated (~2.3 TB)\n- relocated-builds ~953 GB\n- papercusp-backups ~476 GB\n- papercusp-audit-inputs ~275 GB\n- offload + tmp-offload ~599 GB\nThese four groups alone are ~2.3 TB, which dwarfs the ~25 GB of /tmp scratch everyone reaches for first. They are OURS, not the owner's mongodb/Backup/Debug trees, so they are the right place to look for a retention policy.\n\n## Do NOT\nTouch /mnt/data/swapfile — it is ACTIVE swap, 89.2 GB in use, 8 GB RAM free; swapoff would likely OOM the host. See fact mnt-data-swapfile-is-active-swap and escalation mt2noai4.\n\n## Proposed durable fix\n1. A retention policy + reaper for relocated-builds / papercusp-backups / papercusp-audit-inputs / offload (they grow unbounded with no expiry today).\n2. Give /tmp its own filesystem or an xfs project quota on /mnt/data/tmp, so a data-volume fill can NEVER again ENOSPC every agent's scratch. That is the class fix; sweeping /tmp is only an instance fix worth hours.\n\nI deleted nothing — all of this is destructive and owner-authority on a shared box.",

      "id": "EI-21053570719607951",
      "title": "Shared /mnt/data volume chronically at 96% (4.64% free) starves /tmp — ENOSPC misreported by green-checkpoint as thousands of failing tests",
      "summary": "EVIDENCE (gate run ~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/2026-08-21T08-36-27-584Z-...-cand-09f2b5fc7b60.log):\n\n1. /tmp is a BIND MOUNT of /mnt/data/tmp on /dev/nvme0n1 (findmnt: '/dev/nvme0n1[/tmp]'), a shared 7.3T XFS volume. /tmp itself holds only 11G; the volume is consumed by /mnt/data: 2.0T swapfile, 547G back, 540G relocated-builds, 518G offload, 450G papercusp-backups, 383G transformerDB, 263G papercusp-audit-inputs.\n\n2. Measured now: free=346.0 GiB, freePct=4.64%. DEFAULT_DISK_POLICY in packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-space-alarm.ts is freePctMin=0.1 (10%) with `detectLowSpace` tripping on `freeBytes < 5GiB || freePct < 0.10`. So the alarm IS firing (4.64% < 10%) and watchedPaths() DOES include tmpdir(). This is NOT a missing detector — it is a correctly-firing alarm that has gone unactioned, with the volume chronically at 95-96%.\n\n3. During the run the remaining headroom hit zero. All 11 genuinely-failed tests in operator-core read 'ENOSPC: no space left on device' under /tmp/pcv (affected-tests-stdout-ordering, identity-gate-authorised-product-strings, restore-hive-seed). scripts/__tests__/papercup-backup-health-check.test.ts failed its 'disk-headroom discrimination' self-test and its retry died with ENOSPC too.\n\n4. THE EXPENSIVE PART — the misreport. The run reported 'Test Files 2242 failed | 313 passed' then 'Test Files 2556 failed (2556)' and 'Test Files 1763 failed (1763)', while the SAME summaries reported only 'Tests 11 failed | 12044 passed' and 'Tests 1 failed | 5021 passed'. The whole-workspace collapses are vitest 'Test Run Error' + 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token is not valid JSON' — truncated worker/reporter JSON, the signature of a write hitting ENOSPC. A reader sees ~4,300 FAIL lines and concludes a catastrophic code regression; the truth is 11 disk errors. This has now consumed three release-fixer dispatches.\n\nPROPOSED DURABLE FIX (two parts, neither of which I have authority to do unilaterally):\n(a) RECLAIM/RESIZE: the 2.0T swapfile plus ~2.5T of backups/relocated-builds/offload on the same spindle as /tmp need a retention policy or their own volume. Needs owner authority — deleting backups is irreversible.\n(b) ATTRIBUTE, don't misreport: green-checkpoint should statfs the test tmpdir before and after the suite and, when a run hits ENOSPC or crosses the low-space floor, emit a distinct INFRA-FAULT verdict instead of a RED that names thousands of test files. A red that says 'the box ran out of disk' costs minutes; one that says '2,556 test files failed' costs dispatches.",

    {
      "id": "EI-21107607735220636",
      "title": "Online raw Docker-volume rescue aborts on expected file-changed tar status after authoritative logical dumps",
      "summary": "WI-40334's mesh rescue runs tar across all live Docker volumes under set -Eeuo pipefail. During the volume stream, Defguard PostgreSQL rotated or modified a WAL segment and GNU tar emitted `file changed as we read it`. Tar normally exits 1 for this condition, so the wrapper can abort before exporting exact container images and writing SHA256SUMS even though the authoritative PostgreSQL logical dumps and 84-table ClickHouse FREEZE/shadow are already complete. Durable fix: make the online raw-volume stage explicitly best-effort/non-authoritative, record warnings and its pipeline status in the manifest, validate any completed archive, and never let expected live-file churn suppress the later image and checksum stages. A stopped-consistent volume snapshot would be a separate operation, not something to claim from the online tar.",

    {
      "id": "EI-21109934479293631",
      "title": "Oddsmith's alarms have no delivery path off the box: cron-alarm fired 142x in 24h into journald + an error_events table inside the very sidecar that was down",
      "summary": "DISCOVERED 2026-08-22 while fixing WI-39503 under an owner-directed oddsmith recovery.\n\n## The failure this caused\noddsmith's paper-cycle cron failed 298 CONSECUTIVE runs (last success 2026-08-18T21:30:08Z, ~74h) and the owner only learned of it by asking me directly. Separately the sidecar sat stopped for 14.6h. Neither reached a human.\n\n## The detection is NOT missing — WI-39503's title (\"and nothing alarms\") is stale and I corrected it on close\n`apps/desktop/scripts/cron-alarm.sh` (dated 2026-08-16 17:34) works correctly and was firing the whole time:\n- `journalctl --user -t oddsmith-alert --since '24 hours ago'` => 589 lines, 142 of them cron-streak alarms.\n- Verbatim: `CRON-DOWN: paper-cycle has failed 298 consecutive run(s) (rc=1)`.\n- It even emitted the recovery correctly once I fixed the build: `CRON: paper-cycle RECOVERED after 298 consecutive failure(s)` at 20:06:33.\n- The liveness watcher likewise fired `LIVENESS: sidecar unit is inactive (not active) (I-004 watcher)` every 2 minutes for 14.6h.\n\nSo this is a DELIVERY defect, not a detection defect. Filing it as detection-missing would produce the wrong fix (another alarm).\n\n## Root cause: both sinks are dead ends, and one is circular\ncron-alarm.sh has exactly two sinks (see its header comment, lines 26-27, and the SQL at line 89):\n1. `logger -t oddsmith-alert` — journald on this box. Nothing watches it. No human, no papercusp fleet surface, no error_events bridge.\n2. an `error_events` row in the ODDSMITH EMBEDDED POSTGRES.\n\nSink 2 is the interesting one: that Postgres runs INSIDE papercup-oddsmith-sidecar.service (ODDSMITH_PG_PORT=5544, embedded-pg-data under ~/.oddsmith). So when the sidecar is down, :5544 is closed and the durable alarm sink is down TOO — precisely when the alarm matters most. Verified directly: with the sidecar stopped, `error-triage.log` shows `error-triage(ingest): pg localhost:5544 down — skipping` every 14 minutes. A circular dependency: the alarm about the dead service needs the dead service to record it.\n\n## Why this class is nastier than it looks\nThe same shape is present in the engine's OTHER alarms. `analyst-mix-collapse` fires a textually excellent alarm — \"Forecasts keep being written at the normal rate, so every liveness surface stays green while the edge they carry is the zero-edge fallback\" — and it too lands only in journald + the embedded pg. The alarm literally describes a silent-degradation trap while itself being silently trapped.\n\n## Proposed durable fix (not implemented — filing, not fixing, to keep tonight's scope honest)\nGive oddsmith alarms ONE sink that is outside the failing blast radius. Preference order:\n1. Best: emit to the PAPERCUSP operator (:3070) error_events / supervision surface, which is a different process on a different port with a different lifecycle. Supervision ALREADY knows about this unit — it emitted `supervision: papercup-oddsmith-sidecar is down (report-only: entry.autoRestart:false)` into the coord feed tonight, so the bridge partly exists; the cron-streak alarms just do not use it.\n2. Or a `coord:send { to:['human'] }` / owner-escalation hop on threshold crossing.\nWhichever is chosen, the acceptance test is falsifiable and cheap: stop the sidecar, let a cron streak cross CRON_MAX_FAILS, and assert the alarm is READABLE from a surface that does not depend on the sidecar being up.\n\n## Also worth noting for whoever takes this\n`entry.autoRestart:false` on the supervision registry entry means nothing ever brings the sidecar back. Combined with the above, oddsmith can go fully dark and stay dark indefinitely with every alarm firing correctly into a void. That combination — correct detection + no delivery + no auto-recovery — is the actual reason tonight's outage lasted as long as it did.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "needs-human",

    {
      "id": "EI-21146949285164737",
      "title": "work_items:complete returns ok:true but leaves the item `wip` — a false success on the documented completion path",
      "summary": "## What I observed (hard evidence, reproduced twice)\n\nWhile closing WI-40581 (a content-fixer quarantine repair) on build a2d69cef50:\n\n1. `work_items:complete { id:'WI-40581', summary:'...' }` -> `ok:true`, `counts:{ok:1,failed:0}`.\n2. Immediately after, `work_items:get { id:'WI-40581' }` -> `state:\"wip\"`, `closedAt:null`.\n3. Called `work_items:complete` AGAIN -> `ok:true`, `counts:{ok:1,failed:0}` again, and its OWN response body carried `results[0].workItem.state = \"wip\"` right next to `ok:true`.\n4. `work_items:set_state { state:'done' }` then REFUSED loudly and correctly, twice, until I supplied the real gate args: first `completionRef` ('a terminal state REQUIRES completionRef'), then `assumptions` ('a terminal close requires assumptions ... or the literal \"none\"' - D-016/D-050).\n5. With `completionRef` + `assumptions:'none'` + `decision`, set_state returned `state:\"done\"`, `closedAt` populated, `terminalOwner` + `terminalCompletionRef` set.\n\nSo the terminal-close gate demonstrably EXISTS and is enforced by set_state, while complete either bypasses it or silently fails it - and reports success either way.\n\n## Why this matters more than a usability nit\n\nThe agent persona text states plainly: \"not done until `work_items:complete`\". An agent following that documented contract calls complete, receives ok:true, and reports the work finished - while the item stays `wip` in the shared queue forever. That is the exact class the platform elsewhere treats as unacceptable: EI-10883's own error text says an undeclared arg is rejected rather than ignored precisely because \"passing an arg a tool does not declare used to return ok:true while quietly doing something else, which is indistinguishable from success.\" This is that failure, on the completion path itself.\n\nSecondary harm: it also silently skips the D-016/D-050 assumptions capture that set_state enforces, so items closed via complete (if it ever does close them) would carry no assumptions record.\n\n## What I could NOT determine\n\n- Whether `work_items:complete` requires additional args (e.g. completionRef/assumptions/completionEvidence) that it accepted-and-ignored rather than refusing, OR whether it is a genuine no-op that reports ok:true, OR whether it writes a completion *report* by design and was never meant to flip state. I did not read its handler source; this is filed from black-box behaviour only.\n- Whether this affects other terminal verbs.\n- Whether `summary` is even its correct arg name - it did not refuse it, but per EI-10883 non-refusal is not evidence of acceptance here.\n\nAny of those still leaves the same defect: ok:true with unchanged state and no signal to the caller.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nMake complete route through the SAME terminal-close gate as set_state - refuse with the identical actionable errors when completionRef/assumptions are missing, and never return ok:true unless closedAt actually moved. A cheap recurrence guard: assert post-state is terminal in complete's own success path, and a test that calls complete with no completionRef and asserts a refusal (not ok:true).\n\n## Side finding (separate, lower severity, same session)\n\n`work_items:list { q }` with a MULTI-WORD query returns `[]` for an item that definitively exists: `q:'unterminated quotes deb-hetzner-concurrent'` -> `[]`, while `q:'unterminated'` -> returns WI-40581 with that exact phrase in its title. A dedup search is the documented pre-filing step, so a multi-word q silently returning empty manufactures false 'no duplicate exists' conclusions. Positive-control caught it here; nothing in the tool's output flags it.",

      "id": "EI-21186779946952865",
      "title": "OMP --no-tools run can still exceed Gemini's 512-function limit because MCP tools remain exposed",
      "summary": "A bounded OMP 17.3.5 native-tool disable probe ran `omp --no-tools --print --mode=json --no-session` on Gemini 3.1 Pro. The request failed before inference with Google 400 `tools[0].function_declarations: At most 512 function declarations can be specified`. `--no-tools` removes built-ins but leaves the large MCP inventory, so the advertised no-tools mode is not sufficient to produce a valid Gemini request in this managed environment.     {
      "id": "EI-21244248918276621",
      "title": "projection pick on plans:items silently no-ops when given a results[]-rooted path, returning a truncated unprojected body that reads like the real answer",
      "summary": "SYMPTOM\\nA `projection: { pick: [...] }` whose paths do not match the body's root shape is treated as \"no projection\", and the door then returns the UNPROJECTED body truncated to fit the cap. The result looks like a normal bounded answer, so the natural reading is \"this is the data, truncated\" rather than \"my filter did not apply\".\\n\\nREPRO (verbatim, this session)\\n1. tools:invoke { name:'plans:items', args:{ slug:'orchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22', harness:'papercusp', projection:{ pick:['results[].items[].id','results[].items[].effectiveStatus','results[].items[].unresolvedBlockers'] } } }\\n   -> returned FULL item objects (each with the complete multi-hundred-char `text` field) for 5 of 29 items, \"showing 5 of 29\", 5,764 of 28,904 chars. No warning that pick matched nothing.\\n2. Same call with the CORRECT root shape: projection:{ pick:['items[].item.id','items[].item.effectiveStatus','items[].item.blockedBy','items[].item.unresolvedBlockers'] }\\n   -> returned ALL 29 items, 5,685 of 28,396 chars, \"80% saved\". Complete answer, comparable byte count.\\n\\nWHY THE WRONG PATH IS THE NATURAL ONE\\nplans:items roots its body at `items[]` with the payload nested under `.item`, i.e. `items[].item.id`. Sibling tools I had used minutes earlier in the same turn — work_items:get, work_items:claim, plans:get — all root at `results[]`. So `results[].items[].id` is exactly what you write after using those, and it is wrong here in TWO ways at once (wrong root key, and the doubled `items[].item` nesting is easy to miss).\\n\\nWHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO\\nThe two failure modes are not symmetric. `pipe` on a JSON body returns an EMPTY result, which is loud. A bad `pick` returns a PARTIAL result, which is quiet — and worse, the partial is truncated by the SAME cap the projection existed to avoid, so the caller both loses the data and pays the context they were trying to save. In my case call 1 cost ~5.7KB of context and answered nothing; call 2 answered completely for the same bytes.\\n\\nThe door ALREADY has the right behaviour and applies it inconsistently: on a LATER call in the same session, `pick` including a path that matched nothing emitted a clear warning — \"pick path(s) matched nothing: results[].priorWorkWarning — those field(s) are ABSENT from the body below\". That is exactly the signal missing from case 1. The difference appears to be partial-match (some paths hit, warn) vs total-match-failure (no paths hit, silently skip projection).\\n\\nCORRECT STATE\\nWhen NO pick path matches the body at all, say so as loudly as the partial-match case already does — e.g. \"pick matched 0 of N paths; projection NOT applied\" plus the body's actual root key(s), which the door already computes and prints elsewhere (\"The body is an OBJECT with key(s): ok, results, counts\"). Naming the real root turns a silent re-read into a one-line correction. Total-match-failure is strictly MORE suspicious than partial and should not be the quieter of the two.\\n\\nThis is the same false-absence class the repo guide warns about: an empty/short result that is indistinguishable from a real measurement. Here the instrument silently did not run.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "blocked",
      "classification": "retain-other-unresolved",
      "recommendation": "retain-park",

      "fullReason": "implementation lane must land the total-pick-mismatch diagnostic and rerun validation",

    {
      "id": "EI-21255990089512953",
      "title": "psu-pty-host managed kickoff gates on TUI prompt-ready (injectTurnAtPrompt requireInitialOutput), not on MCP registration",
      "summary": "UNCONFIRMED residual, split out of EI-7042 so the umbrella can close on its (now-fixed) primary mechanism.\n\n## What is fixed (EI-7042's actual subject)\nA FRESH OMP launch no longer receives its kickoff as a spawn-time positional argv token. `routeFreshKickoff` (apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs) returns for `backend === 'omp'`:\n  { positionalArgs: [], managedKickoff: tagged[0], kickoffSeeded: true }\nso the prompt goes through the managed pty instead. Credited in-source to EI-20339142329504181. Committed: HEAD blob == staging blob 3ecb1e4cf9692b9e06c31e121101fd2affd32f6b.\n\n## The residual (this item)\nThe managed path delivers via psu-pty-host.mjs:3566\n  injectTurnAtPrompt({ text: launchKickoff, label, requireInitialOutput: true })\nThat barrier waits for the TUI to reach a ready prompt and emit initial output. It does NOT consult any MCP-registration readiness signal — a grep of psu-launcher.mjs for mcp[-_ ]?(ready|registered|registration|handshake)|awaitMcp|waitForMcp|mcpReady returns ZERO hits (positive control: \"kickoff\" returns 108 in the same file). So prompt-ready is being used as a proxy for tools-registered.\n\nIf OMP can render an interactive prompt while asynchronous MCP discovery is still settling, a kickoff injected at that moment still lands on a toolless first turn — the original EI-7042 symptom, through a later and much narrower window.\n\n## Why UNCONFIRMED\nNot reproduced. Proving it needs a live OMP launch observed across the prompt-ready -> MCP-settled interval. I did not run one: OMP is dormant (208 turns / 77 sessions lifetime = 0.03% of 637k turns; last OMP turn 2026-08-19T01:42:59Z), and the routing changed 2026-08-22, so ZERO OMP sessions have exercised the current code path.\n\n## If someone does confirm it\nThe pty host already parses TUI state closed-loop for the mcp-reconnect macro (psu-pty-host.mjs ~1927-1937, drives the /mcp dialog). That existing parser is the reuse-first seam for an MCP-ready predicate — extend it, do not add a pre-spawn health probe: four prior EI-7042 investigations rejected a health-gate specifically because of the documented defaultMcpProxyProbe transient-blip regression (mcp-outage-triage-2026-07-02).\n\nNot worth speculative work at 0.03% usage; filed so the analysis is not lost if OMP is ever revived.",

      "state": "open",

    {
      "id": "EI-21275523571820186",
      "title": "A cold wake can deliver a SUPERSEDED loop carry-note, and the successor's loop:checkpoint then silently destroys the newer one (single-slot, no compare-and-swap)",
      "summary": "## Symptom\n\nMy cold wake (fire #10) was delivered carrying a carry-note written at 2026-08-23T19:36:10Z. A NEWER note ('Wake #11', contentHash 315d65469ec5) had already been written at 19:52:20.719Z — roughly 19 seconds BEFORE my first real turn (loop:status lastRealTurnAt=19:52:39.771Z). I never saw it. At ~20:01Z I wrote my own loop:checkpoint (contentHash f83e042d756a), which replaced did/left/insight/next wholesale and destroyed the 19:52 note's content.\n\nThe 19:52 note's content only reached me BY ACCIDENT: a queued/staged replay wake (EI-10935 class) delivered ~20:02Z happened to carry the 19:52 snapshot text in its preamble. Without that coincidence the thread was gone.\n\n## What was nearly lost\n\nThe 19:52 note carried the only record of a live investigation: su-48397c83 had been queued as 'probably effectively dead, ignoring three required wakes', and Wake #11 had established that was wrong on every count (parked+wakeable, contextPressure ok, holds WI-40022, presence/ledger intentDivergent). I re-verified and confirmed it this turn (WI-40022 is state=blocked; the member's silence is CORRECT), and preserved it as fact 13080 — but only because the replay handed it back.\n\n## Mechanism\n\n1. The loop carry-note is SINGLE-SLOT, keyed by ownerId.\n2. did/left/insight/next are full REPLACEMENTS on write (unlike `checks`/`walls`, which have rowsMode:'merge' and upsert by id).\n3. loop:checkpoint takes no expected-contentHash / compare-and-swap argument, so a writer holding a stale read overwrites a newer note unconditionally and reports ok+verified:true.\n4. The wake delivery itself can carry a superseded snapshot — the delivery preamble even warns the text 'can be a stale snapshot from when the wake FIRED', but there is no signal that a NEWER note exists.\n\nSo the hazard is not merely 'you were shown stale text'. It is 'you were shown stale text, and your own next write is what destroys the current text'.\n\n## Distinct from the known stale-delivery class\n\nEI-10935 / EI-20230529647745311 cover a QUEUED/STAGED DELIVERY arriving late with stale content — a READ-side staleness problem. This is the WRITE-side consequence: unconditional clobber of a newer note by a reader who was handed an older one. The live-recheck banner mitigates the read side and does nothing for the write side.\n\n## Suggested durable fix\n\nGive loop:checkpoint an optional expected contentHash (the value it already returns) and refuse/merge on mismatch, the way work_items writes guard concurrent claims — or surface 'a newer note exists (hash X, written T)' in the wake preamble so the reader can reconcile before writing. Reusing the existing rowsMode:'merge' semantics already proven on checks/walls is likely the smallest change.\n\n## Workaround in the meantime\n\nDurable conclusions go to facts:assert, which is keyed, superseding and multi-row, so it ACCUMULATES rather than clobbers. Treat the loop note as lossy scratch.",

    {
      "id": "EI-21285199425229320",
      "title": "fleet:leader-brief bench_suggested recommends benching parked no-self-wake members, inverting what fleet:bench is for (suppressing a live-looping lane)",
      "summary": "## Symptom\n\nOn fleet `byoc-alpha-max-2026-08-23`, `fleet:leader-brief { include_stale:true }` returned (2026-08-23T22:32Z):\n\n```\nsummary: members 18, speaking 0, dead 7, dormant 7,\n         laneless_idle 7, bench_suggested 7, claimable_now 0\n```\n\n`bench_suggested: 7` while `speaking: 0`. Every member visible in `members[]` read `sessionState:'parked'` with `verdict:'first-turn-done'` and `idleVerdict.cause:'no-self-wake'` — they took one turn and stopped, with no wake source, `lastToolCallAgeMs` 18–57 minutes.\n\n## Why I think the suggestion is pointed the wrong way\n\n`fleet:bench { member, wakeEvent }` parks a member on a wake event so a lane blocked-waiting on a peer's critical path stops LIVE-LOOPING. Its value is suppressing wake/token burn by a member that is spinning. But:\n\n- `speaking: 0` is the population-complete field, so nothing on this fleet is spinning. There is nothing to suppress.\n- A `no-self-wake` parked member is already maximally quiet. Benching it ADDS a wake source, raising future cost rather than lowering it.\n- It also buys nothing unavailable later: a `parked` member stays wakeable on demand, so a single `coord:wake` when work actually arrives beats pre-benching 7 members and re-benching all 7 every 30 minutes (the bench TTL) against a `claimable_now: 0` pool.\n\nFollowing the suggestion literally is a standing treadmill of 7 calls per 30 minutes that makes the fleet more expensive, not less. I had in fact been running exactly that treadmill for several wakes off a carried instruction before noticing.\n\n## Explicitly NOT confirmed\n\nI did not read `bench_suggested`'s writer, so I cannot say what it is intended to mean. If it means \"these lanes lack a wake source\" rather than \"these lanes are spinning\", then the counter is correct and only the ACTION implied by its name is wrong — which would make this a naming/guidance defect rather than a logic one. Either way a leader reading it at face value is led to the wrong action, which is why I am filing it rather than just ruling locally.\n\nI have ruled locally in the meantime: `byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-091` — do not bench while `summary.speaking == 0`; re-arm benching only if `speaking > 0` AND `laneless_idle > 0`.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nGate `bench_suggested` on the member actually being awake-and-looping (`speaking`/`monitorState` evidence of repeated wakes), or rename it to say what it observes (`laneless_no_wake_source`) and pair it with the action that fits an inert member — which is \"leave it parked and wake it on arrival\", not \"bench it\".\n\n## Secondary observation from the same read (separate, already known to me)\n\n`members[]` returned 7 of 18 even at `payloadTier:'full'` WITH `include_stale:true`, carrying a `membersTruncated` marker. Any count or absence derived from `members[]` is a FLOOR, never a population finding — `summary.*` is the population-complete surface. This previously produced two false claims in a decision I had to amend within 3 minutes.",

            "summary": "The outer Codex exec_command CreateProcess guard rejects a bounded mktemp EXIT-trap rm -rf cleanup before execution; the guard is outside the Papercusp repository and cannot be changed by this work-item.",
            "evidence": "At HEAD 2df82de292605afbfbdb338324766fc03db304c2, the exact command was rejected before execution with `rm -f style commands are not permitted. Use a safer approach`.     {
      "id": "EI-21302020922691074",
      "title": "Monkey-patching node:child_process in a vitest setup file cannot bound sync spawns — ESM named imports keep the original binding, so the \"safety net\" is a silent no-op",
      "summary": "## Why anyone would try this\n\nWI-41180 established that an unbounded sync spawn (`execFileSync`/`spawnSync`/`execSync` with no\n`timeout:`) blocks the worker event loop inside libuv's `uv_spawn_sync`. No vitest timeout can fire,\nbecause `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` are timers and timers cannot run on a blocked loop. In the pure\nlane (`isolate:false`, ~2,740 files sharing one fork) that wedges the whole lane until the 2700s\nwatchdog.\n\nThere are 224 such call sites across 91 files (measured 2026-08-24). Bounding them one at a time is\nslow, so the obvious lever is a GLOBAL default: `libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts:303` already\ncomposes a setup chain (`HERMETIC_ENV_SETUP`, `TESTING_LIBRARY_TIMEOUT_SETUP`, ...), so adding a\n`BOUNDED_SYNC_SPAWN_SETUP` that patches `child_process` to inject a default `timeout` looks like a\none-file fix for all 224 landmines.\n\n## It does not work, and it fails SILENTLY\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-24, plain node ESM, two shapes:\n\n    // setup.mjs\n    import cp from 'node:child_process';\n    const orig = cp.execFileSync;\n    cp.execFileSync = function patched(...a) { process.stdout.write('PATCH-HIT '); return orig.apply(this, a); };\n\n    // consumer, static:   import './setup.mjs'; import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';\n    // consumer, dynamic:  await import('./setup.mjs'); const { execFileSync } = await import('node:child_process');\n\nBOTH consumers called the ORIGINAL function — no `PATCH-HIT` printed on either — and an identity\ncheck reported `DIFFERENT(unpatched)`: the named import is not the same function object as the\n(patched) property on the default export.\n\nNode generates the ESM named exports for a builtin from the CJS exports when the facade is\ninstantiated. Mutating a property on the default-export object afterwards does not rebind the\nalready-generated named export. Since essentially every call site in this repo uses\n`import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'`, such a setup file would patch nothing.\n\n## Why this is worth a filing rather than a shrug\n\nThe failure mode is the dangerous direction: the patch installs without error, the setup file looks\npresent and correct in the config, and every wedge it was supposed to prevent still happens. It\nwould read as \"the class is defended\" while defending nothing — strictly worse than no net at all,\nbecause it removes the pressure to do the real per-call fix.\n\n## What actually works\n\n1. An explicit `timeout:` (+ `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'`) on each call — what the WI-41180 ratchet guard\n   `packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/pure-lane-unbounded-sync-spawn.test.ts` detects and drives.\n   This is the path being taken in WI-41223.\n2. If a global lever is ever genuinely needed, the mechanism would have to be a vitest\n   `resolve.alias` remapping `node:child_process` to a bounding shim (the specifier resolves to the\n   shim, so named imports DO bind to it; the shim reaches the real builtin via\n   `createRequire(import.meta.url)('child_process')` to avoid aliasing itself). NOT ATTEMPTED here:\n   aliasing a core module across 2,759 files is a large blast radius, and re-exporting every\n   `child_process` symbol with four overload shapes per sync function is easy to get subtly wrong.\n   Recording it only so the next person evaluates the RIGHT mechanism rather than re-testing the\n   broken one.\n\n## Corrective for the next agent\n\nBefore wiring any global monkey-patch of a Node builtin into test setup, run the 6-line probe above\nand confirm a `PATCH-HIT` actually prints through a NAMED import. If it does not, the net is a no-op.\n",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",
