    {
      "id": "EI-21304382115507204",
      "title": "turn-start context injection is ~100% semantically degraded: embed exceeds the 1200ms budget on :3070 despite a warm sidecar answering in 0.94ms",
      "summary": "SYMPTOM: every UserPromptSubmit related-context injection returns lexical-only, on essentially every turn, for at least 8 hours. The hook line reads: \"semantic leg blocked: query embed failed: query embed exceeded 1200ms budget\". Consequence is worse than poor ranking — improvements:capture reports dedupCoverage.semantic='unavailable', so \"possibleDuplicates: []\" means NO LEXICAL MATCH only, and agents read an empty result as real absence.\n\nWHERE IT COMES FROM (established): the string is raised by libs/generic/search/src/hybrid.ts:313, `new EmbedTimeoutError(budgetMs)`. Line 318 documents it as bounding the EMBED CALL ITSELF (\"await embedder(query) but give up after budgetMs\") — NOT the acquisition. So the embedder handed to hybrid search is taking >1200ms per query embed.\n\nTHE PATH (established): ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/userpromptsubmit-memory.sh execs ~/.papercusp/hooks/inject/index.mjs, which POSTs to OPERATOR_URL defaulting to localhost:3070 (core.mjs:43), routes /api/agent-mcp/turn-start-memory and /api/agent-mcp/mid-turn-context (ports.mjs:67,74). :3070 is papercup-dev-api, running papercup-release/apps/operator/dist-host/hono-host.mjs.\n\nTHE CONTRADICTION THAT REMAINS UNEXPLAINED — this is the whole question:\n- The sidecar is warm and fast. /healthz 200 in 0.5ms; POST /embed {\"texts\":[...],\"kind\":\"query\",\"model\":\"local\"} returns real vectors in 0.94ms; uptime 3.4 days; models gemma:{document,query}, harrier:{document,query}, local:query all \"warm\".\n- dev-api HAS PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3384 (drop-in 97-harrier-embed-sidecar.conf).\n- Its bundle is FRESH (built 2026-08-23 21:44Z) and CONTAINS the wiring (16x buildSidecarAwareEmbedder, 5x resolveProcessSidecarUrl, 9x EMBED_SIDECAR_URL).\n- The write path is healthy: 3,049 rows embedded mode='gemma' in 12h.\nYet the query embed on this route exceeds 1200ms. A sidecar-backed embed at 0.94ms cannot. So on this route the embedder is NOT sidecar-backed — and why is unknown.\n\nRULED OUT, each with evidence (do NOT re-test these):\n1. Per-worker ONNX cold-start that warms after first use — FALSIFIED: 278 failures/6h spread evenly across ~11 dev-api workers, each failing continuously for 5h15m-5h30m. Nothing warms. Query latencies also do not decrease across successive calls (4098, 4086, 53, 4178 ms).\n2. OpenAI quota exhaustion — FALSE. No key exists: OPENAI_API_KEY unset on dev-api and staging-api, and operator_credentials has openai_api_key absent (payload ? 'openai_api_key' = false) for both workspaces. That cascade branch is unreachable. (My earlier \"79x 429\" claim was a grep artifact matching `readFileSync @ node:fs:429` — a stack-trace line number.)\n3. DB pool contention on the credentials read — WEAK/NO: dev:pg_health shows 258 idle, 17 active of 512 max.\n4. The transformers import in localAvailable() — NO: `@huggingface/transformers` cold-imports in 143ms, not seconds.\n5. Duplicated non-sidecar-aware search cascade — NO: agent-tools/search/embedder.ts also calls buildSidecarAwareEmbedder for local/gemma/harrier ('query' prompt).\n6. Frozen main / stale release SOURCE — NO: release and staging embed-sidecar-wiring.ts and agent-tools/search/embedder.ts are identical.\n7. Stale release BUNDLE — NO: built 21:44Z today, contains the wiring.\n8. papercup-mcp-proxy missing PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL — REAL CONFIG GAP, BUT NOT THIS BUG. It was the only unit lacking the drop-in its three siblings have, and I added papercup-mcp-proxy.service.d/70-embed-sidecar.conf and restarted (verified live, pid 99681). Injection did NOT recover. It is the wrong process — injection posts to :3070, not :9071. The drop-in is harmless and closes a genuine inconsistency, so it was left in place; REVERT is `rm` + daemon-reload + restart if unwanted.\n\nWHERE TO START NEXT (the narrow question): instrument which branch resolveProcessSidecarUrl takes INSIDE dev-api for the turn-start/mid-turn route specifically. Candidates not yet tested: (a) verifySidecarFitness rejecting for the requiredCapabilities that route asks for, returning null and silently falling to in-process (the fitness check is per-capability and the sidecar advertises only route-level [\"GET /healthz\",\"POST /embed\",\"POST /rerank\"]); (b) the route resolving a mode whose model is NOT warm on the sidecar — note local:document is ABSENT from the sidecar's warm model list while local:query is present; (c) a per-route embedder built before/outside the sidecar-aware path.\n\nNOTE ON MEASUREMENT: there is no durable success/fail counter to query. readLegHealth() is an in-process ring buffer read only by retrieval-degradation-watchdog.ts, which states plainly that a cross-process aggregate \"would need a durable sink and is deliberately not built here\". That watchdog is also not registered as an active routine (routines query returned 0 rows), so nothing escalates this condition — which is why it ran for hours unnoticed. Related prior filing: EI-20008037133036474 (same degradation, marked done while the condition is live).",

    {
      "id": "EI-21308269358666878",
      "title": "A psu session whose MCP tool list loads EMPTY goes silently toolless for its whole life — no self-check, still reports healthy",
      "summary": "SYMPTOM\nA psu agent session can come up with ZERO papercusp MCP tools and never notice. It keeps heartbeating, keeps presence 'live', and looks completely normal to coord:presence / fleet:assignments — while being unable to claim, checkpoint, complete, release, or control its own loop. It is a live agent that cannot coordinate.\n\nOBSERVED (this session, su-e40dceb1, 2026-08-24T04:36Z)\nMy carry-respawn started a fresh Claude CLI whose papercusp-su MCP client connected through :9071 during a proxy WEDGED window. The handshake HALF-completed: the server's `instructions` block WAS delivered (so connect+initialize succeeded — it rendered into my context) but tools/list returned nothing. Claude Code caches the tool list at connect time and never re-lists, so when the watchdog restarted the proxy at 04:39:20Z and :9071 went healthy again (tools/list 200 in 1.73s), my session stayed empty. Repeated ToolSearch `select:mcp__papercusp-su__coord_orient,...` returned 'No matching deferred tools found' throughout; keyword searches returned only other servers' tools.\n\nWHY THIS IS A DETECTOR BUG, NOT JUST THE PROXY'S BUG\nThe proxy cause is EI-21306673196653484 (owned, being worked). This is the separable half: NOTHING asserts 'my MCP tool list is non-empty'. That makes the failure silent and indefinite rather than loud and transient, and it generalizes past this proxy — any cause of an empty/partial tools/list (transport blip at connect, upstream restart mid-handshake, a bad tools= filter, an auth edge) produces the same invisible cripple.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE FLEET\nA silently-toolless agent is worse than a dead one. A dead agent is reaped and its claims are freed; this one stays 'live', so any claim it holds is never released (it cannot call work_items:release) and peers correctly refuse to contest a live holder. That is a livelock generator — the same class as the WI-38602 hot potato, but with no way for the holder to park the item.\n\nPROPOSED DURABLE FIX (a guard, not a restart)\n1. Session-side assertion at first turn: if the papercusp tool surface is empty/absent, say so LOUDLY in-context (the agent can then use the documented direct-operator fallback) rather than letting the agent discover it by failing calls one at a time.\n2. Make it visible fleet-side: presence should carry a toolSurfaceOk signal so a toolless-but-live agent is distinguishable from a working one, and its claims are reclaimable.\n3. Recurrence guard: a test asserting that an empty tools/list at connect is surfaced as a hard, named condition rather than an empty catalog.\n\nEVIDENCE\n- journal: 04:39:13-04:39:20Z in-flight 31->34 each held 30s; 04:39:20Z 'WEDGED -> restarting papercup-mcp-proxy ... while upstream :3070 serves tools'; 04:39:41Z new pid 238905 listening.\n- Same tools/list against :3070 throughout: HTTP 200, 271,930 bytes, 3.9s. So the catalog was always available; only this session's cached view was empty.\n- Last 3h: 5 proxy starts, 3 WEDGED verdicts — so the window that produces this is recurring, not a one-off.\n\nSCOPE OF MY CLAIM: n=1, directly observed in my own session, Claude CLI client. I have NOT verified whether other MCP client implementations cache the same way or would re-list on recovery.",

      "id": "EI-21319539684841627",
      "title": "Standing tsc red with no owner: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/author-refresh.test.ts (50min, 2 errors)",
      "summary": "`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/author-refresh.test.ts` is a NEW file (the tsc baseline has never seen it) whose errors are COMMITTED — not a peer's uncommitted mid-edit — and it has now been observed red 2 times across 50 minutes without being fixed.\n\nWHY THIS WAS FILED AND MOST REDS ARE NOT. Committed new-file reds are dominated by self-healing (measured 2026-08-02: 4 of 5 cleared unaided within ~15 minutes), so the sweep files only reds that OUTLIVE the 45-minute dwell threshold — i.e. ones whose author has most likely moved on. That makes this one unusual: it is very likely OWNERLESS rather than in progress.\n\nIMPACT: a committed non-baselined red reds the shared green-checkpoint, so it blocks the whole fleet's promotion path, not just this file's author.\n\nBEFORE CLAIMING IT, re-run the ownership test — the red may have been fixed between this filing and your reading it:\n  git status --porcelain | grep packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/author-refresh.test.ts   # dirty => someone is editing it RIGHT NOW\n  git log -1 --format=%cI -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/author-refresh.test.ts      # minutes old => author still has context\n  npm run lint:tsc -- --files=packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/author-refresh.test.ts\n\nObservation window: first seen 2026-08-24T06:54:25.000Z, last seen 2026-08-24T07:44:48.000Z.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "blocked",

      "title": "Green checkpoint materialization exceeds 900s and starves queued writers",
      "summary": "CORRECTION / RETRACTION (2026-08-24 04:38 EDT): the initial filing called the exclusive writer lock stale. That was wrong. A direct fuser/process-tree read found live holder PID 2611473 (`setup-release-checkout.sh` for candidate 014b057d...) started 04:20, with active `find`/`sha256sum` descendants still advancing at 04:37.       "title": "dev:pg_query tenant advisory recommends the active workspace for coordination-pinned carry_notes rows",
      "summary": "While reading the canonical AUTO-loop carry note during WI-40086 monitoring, an intentionally cross-workspace query on harness_shared.carry_notes returned the correct loop row under workspace_id='default', but dev:pg_query advised adding workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'. Source packages/operator-core/lib/carry-note.ts pins loop carry rows to DEFAULT_COORD_WORKSPACE and reads newest across workspaces with default only as the tie-breaker.       "id": "EI-21338411229452662",
      "title": "events:await newest-only semantics permit duplicate simultaneous waits for one subscriber and exact key",
      "summary": "Direct event-ledger evidence contradicts events:await's stated newest-only one-shot behavior. On harness:papercusp:wi-40086-qualified-current-tip generation 3, events:status at 2026-08-24T12:43Z showed the same subscriber with multiple state=registered waits on the same exact key: su-6c343 await 88244 and 88231; su-171c await 88255 and 88230; su-3cc77 await 88241 and 88229; su-6362 await 88254 and 88228. The leader wake then delivered two coalesced timeout expiries for the same key. Registering a newer exact-key wait should retire every older live wait for that subscriber regardless of whether registration came from fleet:bench, direct events:await, or auto-arm.     {
      "id": "EI-21339862163229768",
      "title": "check-mock-cast-escape is 36 over its shrink-only baseline (1123 vs 1087), so the ratchet cannot pass and a NEW cast hides in the debt",
      "summary": "MEASURED, not inferred — `node scripts/check-mock-cast-escape.mjs` at 2026-08-24T12:58Z:\n\n    ❌ mock-cast-escape count exceeded baseline: 1123 > 1087 (+36).\n\nThe baseline is documented shrink-only, so a +36 overshoot means the guard is currently RED for every agent who runs it, and — the part that matters — a genuinely NEW `as never` cast is now indistinguishable from the 36 already sitting above the line. The guard's whole value is that it fires on the new one.\n\n## What this is NOT\n- NOT the gate red. `gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict` reads red-current with 39 consecutive reds, HELD-LIVE by su-d9211d54 on WI-40086, and `gate_health.failingTests` is `[]`. I did not establish that this leg is the one holding the gate and am not claiming it. Filed separately on purpose.\n- NOT mine. My change (WI-41323) added 2 casts to send.test.ts, the PostToolUse hook flagged them (78 → 80), and I replaced both with `mockResolvedTyped`. send.test.ts is back at its baseline 78, so this change's net contribution is zero.\n- NOT already covered by the existing filings. The 54 rows matching \"mock-cast-escape\" are about the SCRIPT's behaviour (EI-21063955147138003 stdout truncation — done; EI-21063878935940047 ENOSPC — done; EI-21064443379113471 the gate names the script not a vitest file; EI-21064374337636420 the failure dumps 25 files of baselined debt instead of naming the new one). None of them is \"the count is over the line\".\n\n## Why it recurs\nThe PostToolUse hook is excellent at the moment of authorship — it named my two casts, in my file, with the typed-helper remedy, before I ran anything. So the +36 did not arrive through that door in a session that read it. Either those casts predate the hook, or they were added where the hook does not fire. Worth measuring which before hand-fixing 36 sites: `git log -S'as never' --since` over the offending files would separate \"old debt the baseline was seeded above\" from \"new breaches leaking past the hook\", and only the second is a fix worth doing twice.\n\n## Cheapest honest next step\n`node scripts/check-mock-cast-escape.mjs` prints the offender files but not the delta per file against the baseline — EI-21064374337636420 already asks for exactly that (\"it has everything needed to just name it\"). Landing that first turns this 36-site cleanup from an archaeology exercise into a list.",

    {
      "id": "EI-21340355513221785",
      "title": "checkpoint in-flight oracle misses pre-run-lock exclusive materialization",
      "summary": "Live 2026-08-24 reproduction: dev:pipeline_position/release:deploy reported checkpointRunInFlight.active=false and gateCandidate=no-active-run while pid 4188979 was already running pc-heavy.sh --exclusive-all-slots -- setup-release-checkout and its child held exclusive-materialization.lock FLOCK WRITE. Materialization precedes acquisition/publication of the current run-lock, so the in-flight oracle has a blind window in which callers are told no checkpoint is active even though a checkpoint/deploy materializer is live. This can authorize a second release:checkpoint-run that kills or collides with the first materialization. Root fix: include the exclusive materialization writer/run marker in the in-flight oracle and the checkpoint-run proactive guard, with a recurrence test for the pre-run-lock phase. No concurrent force/replace was attempted during this observation.",

      "summary": "Measured 2026-08-25 during WI-41607: in every log-quiet (9–35h) agent-session scope autopsied, the codex vendor binary (@openai/codex codex-linux-x64) sat at a constant 8.3–8.5% CPU while every other process in the scope was 0.0% and the session log had not been written for 9+ hours. 53 of 58 quiet scopes showed ~840ms CPU per 6s window — i.e. an IDLE parked codex session burns ~1/12 core forever.     {
      "id": "EI-21438635768335146",
      "title": "Cold engine-loop driving claims self-wake on every session-end release, bypassing the configured cadence",
      "summary": "A cold loop bound to driving work item WI-40939 auto-claims the item on each wake. When the cold turn ends, session-death cleanup releases that claim; armWorkItemHolderInterests has unconditionally registered one-shot claim:released:WI-40939, so the release immediately re-invokes the same session instead of respecting the 1200s blocked cadence or waiting on the real green/red/inconclusive producer. Reproduced across multiple consecutive turns; each reclaim created a fresh auto-arm, latest await_id 96917 (created 15:14:04Z) and each end produced an immediate claim-release wake. Read of packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts:2164-2183 confirms the unconditional lifecycle auto-arm and returned cancel handle. Manual cancellation of only 96917 stopped the redundant edge while preserving verdict awaits 96683-96685, WI-40086 await 96690, and inbox wake. Durable fix: suppress or auto-retire the claim-release wake for cold loop-owned claims whose release is the expected turn lifecycle, without weakening genuine unexpected-claim-loss recovery; add a cold-loop recurrence proving configured cadence/event awaits are not bypassed.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",

      "id": "EI-21463647841760959",
      "title": "Artifact publish/read/watch silently breaks mid-session when the inference gateway rotates the pool account — a live artifact reads as \"not found\" / \"deleted\"",
      "summary": "MEASURED 2026-08-25 ~19:50-20:05 UTC, this session (su-13973086), single unbroken session, no respawn.\n\n## Symptom\nAn artifact I published and verified live became unreadable and unwritable ~10 minutes later, and BOTH the watch subsystem and the Artifact tool reported it in language that means \"deleted\":\n\n- `artifact-watch-lifecycle` task notification: \"Stopped watching Artifact ... no such artifact for this account (it was deleted, or it has not been shared with the user).\"\n- `Artifact { action:'read', url }` -> \"artifact not found - it may have been deleted, or it has not been shared with you\"\n- `Artifact { file_path, url }` (update) -> `<artifact-deleted url=...>` \"the artifact you're updating was deleted, or you no longer have write access to it.\"\n\nNothing was deleted.\n\n## Root cause (evidence, not inference)\nThe Artifact connector's ACCOUNT IDENTITY changed between turns. The gallery listing swapped wholesale:\n\n- T1 (publish turn), `Artifact action:'list'` -> 23 artifacts, unmistakably this workspace's own: \"PaperCusp - Architecture\" (08-25), \"Learning Loop Backlog Audit\", \"SideStage Submission Packet\", \"Feature flags currently OFF - Papercusp\", \"CLAUDE.md classification map - P-002\". My new artifact appeared at the top of this list and was verified present.\n- T2 (~10 min later, SAME session), `Artifact action:'list'` -> 5 artifacts, a fully DISJOINT set: \"RTX Screen Flight Plan\" (08-19), \"The 340 Megabyte Hour\", \"The 4 GB Cage\", \"Swap Line\", \"The SQL Escape Hatch\". Newest is 08-19, i.e. older than several artifacts from the T1 list.\n\nA single account cannot lose 23 artifacts and gain 5 different older ones in 10 minutes. The session was re-routed to a different pool account.\n\n`accounts:status` confirms the pool and the pressure that would drive failover: claude-provider accounts `aviynw` (rate.pausedUntil set, penaltyCount 1, utilization7d 0.92), `aviynw3` (usageWalled:true, sustainedlyLimited:true, edgeThrottled:true), `avistorewolf.com` (usageWalled:true), `aviynw10` (usageWalled:true, sustainedlyLimited:true), plus `aviynw2` and others. So mid-session failover between pool accounts is expected behaviour of the gateway.\n\n## Why this is worse than an inconvenience\n1. The error text asserts DELETION. An agent that trusts it will tell the owner their artifact was deleted - a false statement about data loss. I nearly did.\n2. The update path is unrecoverable-by-design once it flips: the tool instructs \"do not pass its url to the Artifact tool again\" and says republishing creates a NEW artifact. An agent following that instruction FORKS the artifact onto whichever stray pool account is currently serving it - orphaning the real one on the owner's account and putting the new copy somewhere the owner may not be able to see.\n3. It is silent and non-deterministic. Nothing announces the rotation; the same call succeeds and then fails with no state change by the caller.\n4. It defeats the existing \"re-resolve before citing a URL as delivered\" discipline: I DID re-resolve, at publish time, and got a true positive that went stale ~10 minutes later for reasons unrelated to the artifact.\n\n## Correct state\nAt minimum, the failure must be distinguishable from deletion. Options, cheapest first:\n- Have the Artifact tool surface the account identity it resolved against (id or hash) in `list`/`read`/publish results, so an agent can detect rotation itself and say \"different account\" instead of \"deleted\".\n- Make the not-found/deleted message conditional: if the current account differs from the account that served the publish in this session, say so explicitly and do NOT advise republishing without a url.\n- Consider pinning the Artifact connector's account for a session's lifetime independently of LLM-inference failover - the two do not need to share a routing decision, and artifact identity is durable state while inference routing is not.\n\n## Repro\n1. Publish an artifact; confirm via `Artifact action:'list'` that it is present.\n2. Continue the session across enough turns/time for gateway failover to occur (pool under usage pressure makes this likely).\n3. `Artifact action:'read'` the same url -> \"not found\". `action:'list'` -> a different account's gallery.\n\n## Scope\nAffects EVERY agent in this workspace that publishes an artifact and later updates it, and every artifact URL an agent writes into a durable surface (checkpoint, plan, report) - the URL stays valid for the owner but becomes unverifiable and un-updatable from the agent side without warning.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",
      "classification": "retain-unresolved-condition",
      "recommendation": "retain-park",
      "basis": "The reason names a condition, but the condition is not deterministically proven satisfied.",
      "fullReason": "External-owner surface: the failing text is claude.ai's artifact-store response (zero occurrences in papercusp code — premise re-check on the item thread); the connector/account routing belongs to the harness+gateway lane. Rescue mechanics already documented in agent-insights/recovering-a-deleted-claude-artifact; rotation-distinction guidance recorded on the item thread for the doc-steward. Unpark when the harness exposes artifact-account identity or pins the connector's account.",

      "id": "EI-21509610544515350",
      "title": "Resilient MCP proxy (:9071) restart window surfaces one hard transport error per attached session — candidate fix: systemd socket activation",
      "summary": "CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (was mis-filed as per-role hosts; :9071 is the resilient MCP PROXY, systemd unit papercup-mcp-proxy, :9071 -> :3070 — the dev-box steady state whose purpose is making operator restarts invisible to sessions).\n\nEvidence timeline (EI-21508819301042644, resolved as transient): plans:get transport failure at 09:53:24Z connecting to http://127.0.0.1:9071/api/mcp; the current proxy listener pid 702723 started 09:53:09 UTC — the failure landed ~16s INTO the proxy's own startup. One occurrence; exact call verified healthy immediately after through the same URL class.\n\nWHY the window exists: between proxy process death and the replacement binding its listen socket, :9071 accepts nothing -> clients get ECONNREFUSED phrased by their harness as 'Transport send error: HTTP request failed'. The proxy cannot absorb its OWN death from inside; the :3070-side BOOT_WINDOW absorption (apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts BOOT_WINDOW_STATUSES) only covers UPSTREAM blips, not proxy-process restarts. Related: WI-41257 (proxy refusal path logs nothing).\n\nCANDIDATE FIXES (design lane — deliberately NOT patched in a drain unit):\n1. systemd socket activation (.socket unit owns the LISTEN fd; proxy inherits it via sd_listen_fds-style FD passing) — zero refused window across restarts; touches the deliberately dependency-free proxy.ts.\n2. SO_REUSEPORT dual-process handshake during deploys.\n3. Client-side guidance only (retry via tools:invoke worked) — status quo.\n\nRecovered-in-place evidence: single occurrence, self-healed, canonical path healthy. Severity minor until frequency data says otherwise.",

      "id": "EI-21543657511391052",
      "title": "capability:bash — a background job started from the su surface cannot be killed: su exposes no capability:bash_kill, and the papercusp-surface one refuses with missing_capability for principal system:judge",
      "summary": "## Symptom\nAn su session can START a background job (`capability:bash { run_in_background: true }`) and can READ it (`capability:bash_output`, which reattaches by durable task_id after a carry — that half works well). But it has no working way to STOP it.\n\n## Direct evidence, both sides\n1. `ToolSearch { query: \"select:mcp__papercusp-su__capability_bash_kill\" }` → \"No matching deferred tools found\". The su surface exposes capability_bash and capability_bash_output but NOT capability_bash_kill.\n2. `mcp__papercusp__capability_bash_kill { task_id: \"0mtafkiv916b9wk4oo1\" }` → `missing_capability: Principal \"system:judge\" lacks capability \"capability:bash\" (tool: capability:bash_kill)`.\n\nSo the surface that can start the job cannot kill it, and the surface that exposes the kill verb runs under a principal that lacks the underlying capability. Neither path completes.\n\n## Why it matters beyond inconvenience\nThe documented escapes are both closed to the agent. CLAUDE.md is explicit that you must never `pkill -f` (it has twice killed the owner's live desktop and peers' Xvfb) and must use `processes:kill { taskId }` instead. When neither typed kill verb resolves, the only remaining lever is exactly the one the repo forbids — so the correct behavior is to leave the job running and let its deadline reap it, which is what I did.\n\nConcretely this cost real resource: my run was redundant (the gate's own suite is authoritative) and was competing for the 3 clamped pc-heavy slots with a release gate that was actively judging, during a ~6-day main freeze. Freeing that slot was the right call and was not available to me.\n\n## Repro\nFrom an su session: start any long job with `capability:bash { run_in_background: true }`, then attempt to stop it via either path above.\n\n## Expected\nEither the su surface exposes `capability:bash_kill` (symmetric with bash/bash_output, which it already has), or `processes:kill { taskId }` resolves for the su principal. Whoever can start and read a job should be able to stop it.",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",
      "classification": "retain-unresolved-condition",
      "recommendation": "retain-park",
      "basis": "The reason names a condition, but the condition is not deterministically proven satisfied.",
      "fullReason": "UNPARK WHEN: the green-checkpoint gate is green and the prompt-weight ratchet passes (tools:find currently 1513 vs the 1500-char budget). Reason for the park: the obvious fix adds a tool to the su surface, which adds description+guidance prompt weight while that shrink-only ratchet is already RED, during a ~6-day main freeze with 43 consecutive reds. Prefer the alternative fix in the checkpoint — make processes:kill { taskId } resolve for the su principal, which adds NO new tool description. Sti",

      "id": "EI-2470",
      "title": "hive:survey (no-arg) from a member-having hive's Queen resolves home→operator-home (papercusp) + members=[], surfacing another fleet's workspace-wide frontier as this hive's",
      "summary": "Repro: as the sb-devboard-hive Queen (session scoped to sb-devboard-hive; hive:get and hive:add-member both correctly resolved sb-devboard-hive), a no-arg `hive:survey` returned home=\"papercusp\", members=[], scope=\"workspace\", and a 50-item frontier of papercusp PLATFORM work-items (WI-323..342) — i.e. another fleet's backlog presented as this hive's frontier. The member IS wired: hive:add-member{hive:sb-devboard-hive,member:sb-devboard} returned changed:false. hive:get{slug:sb-devboard-hive} correctly shows the hive with frontier todo_depth:0. So the defect is hive:survey's no-arg home-resolution falling back to the operator home (papercusp) instead of the caller's actual hive home, which then triggers the workspace-wide membership fallback. Danger: a Queen acting on that frontier without verifying scope would place bees on a different fleet's work (the highest-severity placement error). Workaround for now: verify scope with hive:get{slug:<own>} / work_items:list{harness:<member>} before trusting a no-arg hive:survey frontier; pass the explicit hive home where the API allows.",

      "id": "EI-2614",
      "title": "Implement-worker assembled prompt overflows model context window on boot (\"Prompt is too long\" DOA)",
      "summary": "The auto-implement lane's worker dies dead-on-arrival with \"Prompt is too long\" because its assembled boot prompt exceeds the model input window. Confirmed recurring across the dispatch ledger: EI-2609 (84s, exit 1, \"Prompt is too long\"), EI-1425 (\"dead-on-arrival … Prompt is too long\"), EI-1443 & EI-235 (\"Autocompact is thrashing … too large for the context window\").\n\nRoot cause (deeper fix #2 from EI-2613's diagnosis): the spawned implement worker's assembled context — blueprint worker prompt + base preamble + spliced CLAUDE.md + identity/memory + large tool outputs — is too large to fit the model context on boot, so the worker can never do work. This is the load-bearing reason the implement lane is actually broken, distinct from the misclassification noise (EI-2613).\n\nPROTECTED SURFACE — operator-core / self-improvement-loop prompt assembly, fleet-wide (affects every spawned worker). Needs a human/owner decision on how to shrink the worker context budget. Also pairs with the classifier-handling decision in EI-2613: a \"Prompt is too long\" death must NOT be charged as a real attempt (it says nothing about the item), but classifying it env-only would create a silent infinite re-dispatch loop — so the handling (route-to-human-on-overflow vs env-rollback) is a design call, not an auto-fix.\n\nSurfaces: packages/operator-core/lib/prompt-assembly.ts (assembly + budget), packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/implement-worker-exit.ts (the env-failure classifier that currently misclassifies overflow deaths).",

      "title": "[change] Owner-gated asks recorded as ## Now prose are invisible to every inbox surface — no canonical owner-decisions view",
      "summary": "An audit of all 100 non-shipped plans found ~22 items genuinely blocked on the owner (decisions, sign-offs, creds). The other ~12 exist ONLY as prose in the plan's `## Now` block (\"Owner: decide D-002…\", \"human greenlights a phase\", \"Owner: provide FCM/APNS creds\"), so no inbox surface can ever show them; the owner only discovers them by reading every Now line (which is what the audit had to do).\n\nCompounding it: (a) the attention feed mixes the 10 real needs-human items into ~580 items (145 todo + 48 blocked + 100 coord messages + alerts) with no owner-decisions-first default view; (b) needs-human items on already-shipped plans (e.g. close-the-self-improvement-loop P-007, dbos-pipeline-prompt-reconciliation P-001/P-002) drop out of any open-plans view; (c) the unified human inbox is itself an unshipped plan (inbox-cards-unification-2026-05-31, ready, untouched).\n\nDesired state: one convention + one surface.     {
      "id": "EI-5240",
      "title": "git-sync commits syntactically-broken code (no pre-commit transform gate) → crash-loops the bg-host",
      "summary": "EVIDENCE (2026-06-30 08:49–08:52): the bg-host (papercup-bg-host.service, the DBOS routines/git-sync/substrate PRIMARY) crash-looped — NRestarts climbing every ~10s, `Main process exited status=1/FAILURE` — because a fresh boot loaded `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts:1242` which had a BACKTICK inside a `sql\\`...\\`` tagged template (in a SQL comment: `the \\`hive-placement\\` tag`), prematurely closing the template literal → esbuild `Transform failed: Expected \";\" but found \"hive\"`. The bg-host runs the shared tree via tsx, so ANY agent's syntax error that git-sync auto-commits takes down the WHOLE background engine (routines, git-sync, substrate, queen) on the next restart — and the freeze-restart loop means a restart is never more than ~7min away, so a broken commit is a guaranteed host-down. I fixed the one backtick (host recovered), but the CLASS is open.\n\nROOT CAUSE: git-sync has NO pre-commit transform/typecheck gate — it commits whatever is in the tree, including non-transforming code.\n\nCORRECT STATE: before git-sync commits, run a cheap syntax/transform smoke over the CHANGED .ts files (e.g. esbuild transform --no-bundle, or `tsc --noEmit` scoped, or even `node --check` after a strip) and BLOCK the commit (or quarantine the offending file + escalate) if the tree won't transform — so broken code can never reach the shared tree and crash-loop the host. Pairs with the bg-host watchdog: a host that won't boot due to a transform error should surface THAT, not silently restart-loop. Related: the WI-344 ③ spawner-sidecar + the broader bg-host-freeze incident (plan bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30).",

      "summary": "Split out from EI-77 (post 57 \"Major new evidence\"). EI-77's ROOT bug — the signed-spawn MCP URL carried no stable coord owner (no `client=`) — is FIXED and regression-tested (identity.test.ts fleet-spawn branch + EI-318, spawn-mcp.test.ts, operator-spawn.test.ts all green). This is the DISTINCT, still-open failure mode that survives that fix.\n\nMECHANISM: a live fleet:spawn bee reaches the operator over an MCP umbilical that resolves the host via the shared `endpoint-ipc.json` discovery file (packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-ipc-discovery.ts). When :3170 (staging) restarts during a bee's lifetime, the endpoint-ipc.json rewrite poisons the spawned bee's already-resolved umbilical mid-flight → the bee's coord:* / plans:* MCP calls hit transport errors and it silently degrades to output_tail-only (claim/ack/early-report protocol gone). Evidence: 21:02 re-fan batch (5 bees) all voice-severed with zero coord writes despite completing their work; R2's tail shows MCP transport errors; timeline matches :3170 restarts at ~20:33 and ~20:58.       "id": "EI-7042",
      "title": "psu/omp launch during operator warmup delivers the kickoff BEFORE MCP registration — toolless first turn → eval doom-loop",
      "summary": "Session 10012 (omp, ornith) was launched ~3.5 min after a :3070 deploy restart. The papercusp-coord.ts extension's session_start handler hit the still-warming operator, blocked the UI loop 43.6s and timed out (30s cap); the plan kickoff turn was delivered at 18:10:37.540Z while papercusp-su MCP registration completed at 18:10:38.889 — one second AFTER the model's first turn began. Result: the model's toolset contained only omp builtins (bash/eval/read) for the whole session; it never saw a single papercusp tool and doom-looped 12+ eval httpx attempts against PI_TOOL_BRIDGE_URL plus bash 'tools:find'/'plans:get' command-not-found calls, then stalled. This is indistinguishable-from-model-failure noise in behaviour scoring, and any fleet member launched in a deploy window will hit it. Durable fix: gate kickoff delivery on MCP-ready — psu launcher (or the omp session_start extension) should verify the papercusp-su handshake completed (retry with backoff, fail loudly after N) BEFORE injecting the first turn; also the extension timeout should not silently strand the session.       "summary": "Existing signal systems emit unconditionally and rely on humans/agents to notice; EI-7347's registry is proposed as documentation, not enforcement. This makes the effector binding a PRECONDITION of emission and adds an affinity-threshold gate so noise self-suppresses until repetition proves it actionable — a demand-coupled emission contract rather than a supply-side firehose. Nothing today ties a signal's right to occupy the digest to a physically dispatchable work-item plus dedupe-on-open.\n\n**Mechanism:** A signal-effector binding table (the 'antigen registry'). Each monitoring/freshness criterion must register an effector before it may emit: a concrete work-item template + a dispatch verb + a suppression predicate. At emission time the emitter calls bindEffector(signalId). If no bound effector exists, OR the bound effector's last dispatch is still open, the signal is DOWNGRADED to a silent counter that increments an 'affinity score' instead of hitting the digest. When affinity crosses a threshold (repeated recognition = confirmed antigen), clonal expansion fires: auto-spawn the bound effector work-item exactly once, tagged with signalId so subsequent re-fires dedupe against the open item. CI fails on any actor-less signal (hard gate implementing EI-7347). Auto-synth 'floor' emissions with no live agent turn are classified SELF/benign and never expand.\n\n**The bet:** Digest volume from monitoring/freshness criteria drops sharply (target >60% fewer orphan emissions per wake) while genuine recurring problems surface louder via clonal expansion into real work-items. Lower rendering/token cost per wake, and every surviving signal is guaranteed to have an owner — eliminating the actor-less-signal class entirely.\n\n**Cheap experiment (D-006):**\n- Hypothesis: A majority of current monitoring/freshness digest emissions are orphans (no bound effector) and would be silently downgraded, cutting digest volume substantially without dropping any signal that leads to real action.\n- Method: Instrument the emit path read-only for one week of wakes (or replay the last N wake logs): for each of EI-7593/7579/7577/7543/7526 and siblings, check whether a plausible effector exists (a real work-item template + dispatch verb). Classify each emission as bound / orphan / self-synth. Count what fraction would be downgraded and simulate affinity thresholds to see how many would eventually clonal-expand.\n- Falsified if: Prove WRONG if fewer than ~30% of monitoring/freshness emissions are orphans (i.e. most already have live effectors, so the gate saves little), OR if simulated downgrading suppresses signals that historically DID trigger useful human/agent action within one wake — meaning the affinity threshold introduces harmful latency rather than filtering noise.\n\n_Scout-generated. Source ideas: scout-idea-analogical-0-0._",

            "terminalOwner": "su-37977cd5-5e70-4704-a7da-8d191db427d4",
            "terminalCompletionRef": "Root cause: the D-003 \"every nudge/escalate ALSO drops a companion observation\" write for a persisting anomaly (e.g. escalation-aging) never threaded the anomaly's stable conditionKey into the improvements:capture{lane:'observation'} call, and observations skip dedup entirely by design (D-005) — so each wake minted a fresh open work-item forever for one unresolved condition (7k+ open items).\n\nFix (root-cause, not a mitigation): capture-core.ts now COALESCES onto the existing OPEN observation sharing the same watchdogKey (bump repeatCount + lastSeenAt via mergeIssuePayload, refresh title/body via updateIssue silent+confirmShrink) instead of inserting a new row; a call without a key keeps the original always-re-file behavior (correct for one-off readings). brief-types.ts/compute-brief.ts surface conditionKey on EVERY suggestedAction (not just escalate) and teach the agent to pass it to both coord:escalate AND improvements:capture. capture.ts (the tool) exposes a new conditionKey arg (lane:observation only) threaded to watchdogKey. kettle.md's OBSERVE guidance (both the per-anomaly section and the TURN-COMPLETION CHECKLIST) now instructs passing `[conditionKey: …]` verbatim to improvements:capture for the OBSERVE action and the D-003 companion observation alongside a NUDGE/ESCALATE.\n\nAlso fixed in this pass: the new instructional preamble text in renderOverwatchBrief embedded the literal string \"escalation-aging\" ahead of the anomaly list, which broke compute-brief.test.ts's severity-ordering assertion (it does out.indexOf('escalation-aging') to check rendering order) — reworded to describe the bug generically without repeating the anomaly-kind literal.\n\nDeliberately NOT doing: mass-closing the ~474+ existing flood rows already in the DB (filed by live peer loops; a blind tree-wide close risks clobbering in-flight peer/digest signal) — the fix is upstream generation only, per the bug's own filing.",

      "id": "EI-7651",
      "title": "Watchdog routine-failure: suppress reaper self-heal phantom via last_fired_at/reaped_count, not only concrete-future next_fire_at",
      "summary": "The routine-failure collector (`routineFailureSignalsFromRows`, `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/watchdog.ts` ~L1074-1095) is source-aware but STILL re-files reaper self-heal phantoms through a timing race — this is the root cause of the recurring \"Background routine <name> is failing\" EIs (EI-7544 filed 2026-07-04 AFTER the source-aware fix landed; 25+ prior instances: EI-5950/6061/6081/6083/…).\n\nROOT CAUSE: for a non-loop reaper-marked routine (`last_error_source='dbos-executor-reaper'`), suppression fires ONLY when `next_fire_at` is a concrete FUTURE timestamp (isConcreteFuture). But between the reaper stamping `metadata.last_error` and `claimDueRoutine` advancing `next_fire_at` + `clearStaleReaperLastError` wiping the marker, there is a window where `next_fire_at` is momentarily stale-in-the-PAST while the reaper breadcrumb is still present. A watchdog tick landing in that window reads (reaper marker + past next_fire_at) → emits the signal → mints a phantom bug EI. EI-7544 is exactly this: all 10 git-sync installs now show last_error=null / 0 reaper-marked / firing on schedule — it self-healed within minutes.\n\nDURABLE FIX (add to the same non-loop suppression branch, so it treats a proven-recovered routine as a phantom regardless of the next_fire_at race): also suppress when EITHER\n  (a) last_fired_at > last_error_at (the routine already fired successfully after the marker — the doc's proven-recovered criterion), OR\n  (b) reaped_count is BELOW the wedge threshold the git-sync-stall-watchdog already uses (a genuinely wedged routine keeps reaping ≥N times and never self-heals; a single self-heal should never file).\nKeep the genuine-wedge escape intact: `reaped_count >= N` (git-sync-stall-watchdog threshold) must STILL surface. Extend `collectRoutineFailureSignals`'s SELECT to project `metadata->>'last_error_at'` + `metadata->>'reaped_count'` and thread them into `RoutineFailureRow`. Add a `routineFailureSignalsFromRows` unit case for the (reaper marker + stale-past next_fire_at + last_fired_at>last_error_at) row asserting NO signal.\n\nPROTECTED SURFACE — human gate: this is the self-improvement loop's own code (watchdog.ts). Do NOT auto-implement. The doc `agent-insights/routine-failure-ei-is-usually-a-reaper-self-heal-phantom.mdx` already flags this class fix as a STOP surface.",

      "id": "EI-7694",
      "title": "Fleet idle-member auto-re-drive: engine wakes a 0-claim member when its claim-spec view is nonempty",
      "summary": "PROBLEM (backlog-drain-0705, both waves): interactive fleet members finish a turn and PARK; they never self-pull the next item even when the fleet claim-spec view has claimable work. The leader becomes a manual pump — every wake, census idle members and coord:send wake-nudges (\"pull via scheduler:get_next\"). Two incidents: ~8/13 members idle with 5 unowned open bugs; f5241 ACKed a pointed item then idled without claiming (ACK-without-claim leaves the item unowned — a second face of the same gap). SKETCH: extend the fleet-sentinel/claim-spec machinery — when a fleet has an active claim spec whose view resolves nonempty AND a member presence row shows sessionState live/parked with 0 claims for >N sec, the engine fires a targeted wake carrying the scheduler:get_next directive (rate-limited per member; leader-configurable via spec field e.g. spec.redrive:{idleSec,maxPerHour}; off when the fleet is winding down). REUSE: fleet-sentinel already tracks fresh ownerIds for spec inheritance; loop-stuck-backstop (WI-2714) is the wedged-loop sibling — this is the idle-session sibling. Together they close both halves of \"work exists but nobody is moving\". Leader wake-nudges today = TEMPORARY MITIGATION; this is the durable fix.\n\n---\nTRIAGE (su-fd5d3ca8, 2026-07-05 ~17:00Z): reviewed the claim-spec machinery (packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/claim-spec-store.ts, claim-spec.ts, get-next.ts) to scope this. Confirmed genuine and not yet implemented (no existing \"redrive\"/idle-wake logic found in scheduler/ or fleet-membership-store).\n\nSizing: this is a real multi-file feature, not a quick fix — it needs (a) a `redrive` field added to the ClaimSpec zod schema, (b) a periodic sweep correlating presence (sessionState + idle duration) against each fleet's resolved claim-spec view being nonempty WITHOUT claiming (a \"peek\" read), (c) rate-limited targeted wake delivery, (d) an off-switch for wind-down. The sweep MUST hook into the routine-tick machinery (packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/**), which is a D-003 protected path (human-gated for the auto-implement lane) and also operator-core/system-level per the standing fleet directive to notify su-8dc11e75/su-9e92d366 before any change there — both currently unreachable (unknown_recipient, confirmed twice this session).\n\nDISPOSITION: leaving OPEN, not implementing now. This deserves a dedicated engineering pass (its own plan/session) rather than a partial/rushed implementation squeezed into an opportunistic backlog-drain claim on protected scheduling infra. The existing leader wake-nudge workaround remains an acceptable interim mitigation per the item's own text. Not resolving/closing — this is a real, well-scoped, un-actioned feature request; re-claim it if you have bandwidth for the full build + tests.",

      "title": "Green-checkpoint progress surface: phase + elapsed + median-ETA on release:checkpoint-run status (stop the fleet tailing /tmp logs)",
      "summary": "PROBLEM: a running green-checkpoint verdict is a ~55-min black box. Today BOTH the drain leader and su-03650 independently resorted to systemctl is-active + tail /tmp/papercup-green-checkpoint-manual-*.log, and the only signal is one static line (\"checkpointing candidate X (base Y)\") — no phase, no per-workspace progress, no ETA. Agents burn wakes polling and guess ETAs from folklore (~53min). WI-2978 covers the STALE-CANDIDATE status bug; this is the missing PROGRESS capability on the same surface. SKETCH: green-checkpoint.ts already runs discrete phases (per-workspace test suites) — have it write a small progress row (phase, workspace, startedAt, workspacesDone/total) to PG (storage policy) as it advances; release:checkpoint-run { op:\"status\" } and release:deploy { op:\"status\" } fold in { phase, elapsedSec, etaSec: median-of-last-N-runs }, and emit a checkpoint:progress event so consumers events:await instead of polling. REUSE: extends the existing checkpoint unit + release:deploy status read; the run-history table already exists for verdicts — add duration columns rather than a new system.\n\n---\nTRIAGE (su-fd5d3ca8, 2026-07-05 ~17:15Z): confirmed scope — apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts is the file to extend, exactly as the sketch says. This is the SAME file that runs the release gate the whole fleet depends on, and is `apps/operator/lib/release/**`, THE most protected path in the D-003 policy (\"the deploy machinery — never auto-touch what ships the fleet\"). It's also currently under an active standing directive: only su-f0afe8f2 may fire/stop/touch the green-checkpoint gate (currently HELD pending WI-2932 rename churn landing per the day's coordination). Given (a) protected-path status, (b) the active hold + single-driver directive on this exact subsystem right now, and (c) the standing notify-before-operator-core-change requirement (su-8dc11e75/su-9e92d366, both confirmed unreachable this session) -- this is not something to touch opportunistically mid-backlog-drain, even though the feature itself is well-scoped and reasonable.\n\nDISPOSITION: leaving OPEN, not implementing. A genuinely good idea (agents are visibly burning wakes polling for gate status) but belongs to a dedicated pass coordinated with su-f0afe8f2 (the sole gate owner), not a drive-by edit to release/** while the gate is actively held for other work.",

      "id": "EI-7745",
      "title": "Checkpoint-anchored work-item ownership: claim conflicts when another LIVE agent holds a fresh checkpoint",
      "summary": "PATTERN MINED FROM WAVE-3: placement churn hit 3 items — EI-7474 had THREE simultaneous holders (fd5d3 mid-fix, e958e scheduler-pull, 3c289 assignee-of-record), WI-2990 double-claimed, WI-2955 re-placed while actively held. Root: assignee/takenAt fields were untrustworthy at read time (WI-2990 read-side bug, now fixed) AND two placement channels race (leader push-placement vs scheduler:get_next pull). But one signal was ALWAYS truthful: the freshest work_items:checkpoint — every collision agent had written one. PROPOSAL: work_items:claim (and scheduler:get_next) returns claim_conflict when the item carries a checkpoint newer than N minutes authored by a DIFFERENT agent whose coord:presence is live — ownership follows the freshest live checkpoint, not the assignee column. Override with {force:true} for leader reclaims. This would have prevented all 3 collisions this wave even WITH the read-side bug unpatched, because it keys on write-side evidence (checkpoints) not read-side projections. REUSE: extends existing claim path + classifyItemActivity, no new table.",

    {
      "id": "EI-7759",
      "title": "Rubric staleness → automatic re-ratify trigger: persistently-unknown criteria should open a queen↔scout re-ratification cycle (hive-coordination-health has 6 criteria 68–96% unknown)",
      "summary": "## Evidence (rubrics:trend { rubricRef: 'hive-coordination-health' }, verified live 2026-07-05 ~13:30 EDT)\n\nThe staleness signal (P-011) shipped in rubrics:trend now surfaces exactly the condition it was designed to catch, at scale — 6 of the rubric's criteria are persistently unassessable:\n\n- ideation-quality: 96% unknown (376/390 scorecards)\n- bee-observation-quality: 90% (352/390)\n- queen-plan-selection: 90% (352/390)\n- parallel-distribution: 86% (337/390)\n- scheduler-usage: 69% (260/376)\n- bee-execution: 68% (264/391)\n\n(idle-prefixed unknowns are already excluded by the trend aggregation, so these are genuine \"the rater could not map reality onto the criterion\" unknowns — the rubric's model has drifted from how the hive actually works, e.g. post pot-rename / scheduler-tier changes.)\n\n## The gap\n\nThe staleness DETECTOR exists (rubrics:trend → staleness.stale) but nothing CONSUMES it. A stale criterion just sits there generating \"unknown\" ratings forever; the documented remedy (\"re-ratify via the queen↔scout loop\") relies on someone happening to run rubrics:trend and act on it. That's a dead-end signal — same failure shape as a dark flag: built, correct, and doing nothing.\n\n## Proposal\n\nClose the loop: when a rubric criterion crosses a staleness threshold (e.g. >60% unknown over ≥50 non-idle scorecards in 7 days), automatically open a re-ratification work-unit:\n\n1. A periodic sweep (tier:ephemeral blueprint schedule, or fold into the existing scorecard/curation pulse) runs scorecardTrend per active rubric and evaluates staleness.\n2. On breach, file ONE deduped work-item per rubric (not per criterion): \"re-ratify <rubric>: criteria X,Y,Z persistently unknown\", tagged for the queen↔scout loop, carrying the trend evidence inline.\n3. The re-ratify flow is the existing one: revise template_data → rubrics:ratify; the sweep auto-resolves the item when unknown-share drops below threshold.\n4. Immediate concrete instance: hive-coordination-health should get that re-ratify pass NOW with the 6 criteria above — whoever claims this can use it as the pilot.\n\n## Paths / prior art\n- packages/operator-core/lib/scorecards.ts (scorecardTrend + staleness computation — the detector)\n- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/rubrics/trend.ts (the read surface)\n- rubrics:propose / rubrics:ratify (the existing re-ratify mechanism)\n\nFound during: EI-7553/deploy-verify arc, IDEATE pass on rubric freshness (su-36dab, AUTO+IDEATE).",

      "id": "EI-7847",
      "title": "backlog-drain claim-spec keeps serving already-fixed watchdog/bug tickets to multiple agents (repeated re-verify waste)",
      "summary": "3rd+ occurrence this session (per su-fd5d3's own flag on EI-7717/EI-7734, now mine on EI-7806/WI-3070): work_items:claim_next repeatedly serves tickets whose underlying code was ALREADY fixed (by a different agent, sometimes minutes/hours earlier) but the work-item itself was never terminalized. Each occurrence costs a full re-investigation (read code, run tests) just to discover 'already fixed, closing.' Root cause is probably upstream of the claim-spec itself: whoever lands a fix for a watchdog-filed ticket (EI-*) or a WI-* spinoff isn't reliably closing the originating ticket in the same motion, so it sits in todo/open indefinitely looking claimable. A worthwhile fix: (a) when a fix references a WI-/EI- id in its commit/completion, auto-close the referenced id (or at least auto-comment + flag for a cheap re-verify-only pass), or (b) have claim_next itself do a cheap pre-check (e.g. 'does the referenced test/path already pass on HEAD?') before handing the item to an agent as fresh work, short-circuiting to a fast-close path. Low severity (each incident only costs one test run + a completion write, not real rework) but recurring and fleet-wide.",

    {
      "id": "EI-8214",
      "title": "Recurring stalls (recurring 3–32×) stay open because stall handling is binary: either ignore the wedged cell or reap it. Reaping a slow-but-live cell discards in-flight work and re-triggers the same f",
      "summary": "Current stall handling is a single binary threshold (watchdog → kill). No existing rung uses cheap in-band liveness probes or neighbor-peek-at-checkpoint before spawning, and none auto-de-escalates on resumed progress. The benign-tolerance tag for known self-clearing pauses is also absent — today they trigger the same reap path as true wedges.\n\n**Mechanism:** A graduated escalation ladder for cells classified 'wedged self', keyed on stall-severity and blast radius: rung 1 = near-zero-cost in-band 'still there?' probe; rung 2 = recruit a neighbor to inspect the cell's checkpoint/log instead of cold-spawning; rung 3 = warm-inject a re-drive into the existing claim if a fresh checkpoint exists; rung 4 = supersede+reap+re-place. Each rung has a timeout and auto-de-escalation: if the cell's progress counter resumes advancing, drop back to rung 0 (tolerate). Signals matching known-benign self-clearing patterns are tagged tolerated and never escalate past rung 1.\n\n**The bet:** Cheap remedies resolve the majority of recurring stalls without discarding work, cutting expensive re-spawns and reducing MTTSH regression. Preserves partial progress on slow-but-live cells and stops benign RPM pauses from consuming reap/replace budget.\n\n**Cheap experiment (D-006):**\n- Hypothesis: For recurring stalls, a large fraction resolve via rungs 1–3 (probe / neighbor-peek / warm re-drive) without ever needing rung 4 reap, and benign RPM pauses self-clear at rung 1.\n- Method: Instrument the existing stall path in shadow mode: on each 'wedged self' classification, log what a rung-1 probe WOULD return and whether the cell's progress counter advances within the rung timeout — without changing behavior. Replay against the ~6 known benign EIs plus a sample of genuine wedges over one week of stall events.\n- Falsified if: If <20% of wedged cells resume progress within the rung-1/2 timeouts (i.e. the cheap probe almost never distinguishes live-but-slow from dead), the ladder buys nothing over binary reap and the idea is wrong. Also falsified if benign RPM EIs do NOT reliably self-clear at rung 1 within their timeout.\n\n_Scout-generated. Source ideas: scout-idea-analogical-0-1._",

    {
      "id": "EI-8299",
      "title": "Separate auto-filed watchdog/telemetry work-items from the actionable drain queue",
      "summary": "ROOT CAUSE of several fleet-drain frictions. System watchdogs (system:p2p-perf, critical-severity-alert, MTTSH, etc.) AUTO-FILE new bug/change items at roughly the fleet drain rate, so the NONTERMINAL backlog count is NET-FLAT (~189 for papercusp) even as members close real work — a leader watching the obvious burn-down metric sees no progress and must instead track TERMINAL delta manually. Worse, these auto-filed items land in the SAME claimable queue as owner-reported bugs, so a fleet gets served telemetry noise: e.g. p2p-perf regressions EI-8022 (532% worse) then EI-8024 (2808% worse) were handed to a p2p-EXCLUDED fleet member back-to-back; each release is wasted round-trips, and the ballooning merge.delta-tick numbers are likely FLEET-CONTENTION ARTIFACTS (the watchdog measuring degradation caused by the very fleet draining the queue), not real regressions. PROPOSAL: (1) stamp auto-filed items with origin=watchdog/auto (the origin column already exists); (2) default the human/fleet drain queue and claim-spec to EXCLUDE origin=auto unless explicitly opted in; (3) split burn-down reporting into human-filed vs auto-filed so leaders see real progress; (4) dedupe/debounce re-filing the same regression signature and suppress perf-watchdogs during known heavy-fleet-load windows. EVIDENCE: this session, harness papercusp + operator:papercusp-workspace.",

    {
      "id": "EI-8574",
      "title": "Command-output tee parser panics on a multibyte char at the truncation byte-offset (loses the whole output)",
      "summary": "REPRO: run a Bash command whose stdout is large-ish and contains a non-ASCII char (e.g. an em-dash `—`) near an internal truncation offset. The output-persistence/tee layer panics instead of returning output:\\n\\n  thread 'main' panicked at src/parser/mod.rs:191:39:\\n  end byte index 60354 is not a char boundary; it is inside '—' (bytes 60353..60356 of string)\\n\\nHit deterministically running `npx vitest run <two inference-gateway test files>` (vitest's summary + comment text is full of em-dashes). The panic replaced ALL command output — I could not see pass/fail.\\n\\nCAUSE: the parser slices the captured output at a raw BYTE index (191:39, `end byte index … is not a char boundary`) without snapping to a UTF-8 char boundary — Rust `String` slicing panics mid-multibyte. Any agent running a Unicode-heavy command (this codebase's comments/test names are em-dash-dense) can lose their output.\\n\\nWORKAROUND that worked: redirect to a file inside the command (`… > out.log 2>&1; echo exit=$?`) then read the file with grep — the redirect bypasses the tee-parser truncation path.\\n\\nFIX DIRECTION: in the tee/persist parser, clamp/snap any byte-offset truncation to `str::floor_char_boundary` (or operate on chars/grapheme boundaries) before slicing, so a multibyte char straddling the cut degrades to a shorter-but-valid slice instead of a panic.",

      "title": "Integration tests that mock getOrgPg but not withWorkspace silently write to the REAL org PG — add a guard (env pin or db-org test-mode assert) so an unmocked withWorkspace under vitest fails loud instead of escaping",
      "summary": "Hit while building rubrics-first-party-seed.integration.test.ts (WI-3320). The established fixture pattern (_org-test-db.ts doc, rubrics-seed.integration.test.ts) mocks `getOrgPg` and — when the code under test only reads — everything looks hermetic. But any WRITE path routed through `withWorkspace` (e.g. withPlanLock, and everything built on it) uses the REAL db-org connection: my test's proposeRubric writes escaped the testcontainer and content-rewrote two live harness_plans rubric rows (workspace papercusp-workspace) while the test itself FAILED with a confusing \"did not resolve after write\" (write landed live, read-back hit the test DB). Damage was benign only by luck (the seeded content had been generated from those very rows).\n\nThe failure mode is silent, live-data-mutating, and the doc-comment prescription (\"mock withWorkspace too\") is easy to miss — a guard beats a doc. Options: (a) db-org detects `process.env.VITEST` and throws from the real withWorkspace/getOrgPg unless an explicit opt-in env (PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_REAL_PG_IN_TESTS) is set; (b) vitest setup file that stubs db-org's real connection factory to throw; (c) at minimum, a lint rule flagging `vi.mock('@papercusp/db-org')` factories that patch getOrgPg without withWorkspace.\n\nMitigation already landed for the rubric seed specifically: loadAllRubrics guards the auto-seed off under VITEST, and the new test mocks withWorkspace per the prescribed pattern.       "id": "EI-8611",
      "title": "scheduler:get_next self-selects human-gated (triageDecision:gate) and origin-mismatched items into autonomous self-pull, forcing manual per-item claimHold",
      "summary": "FRICTION (repeatable, hits every autonomous self-puller): scheduler:get_next keeps returning, at the TOP of the claim-spec rank, work-items the caller cannot or should-not action autonomously — so each wake I burn calls pulling them, diagnosing, and manually setting release{claimHold:true} one at a time.\n\nConcrete instances this wake (su55e-v1-self-pull-no-p2p rev2, harness:papercusp):\n1. HUMAN-GATED changes: EI-8575 (kind=change) has ideaLifecycle.triageDecision=\"gate\", triageReason \"kind=change is not auto-eligible (autoKinds:[bug]) → human — human gate per policy verdict D-003\". A change that triage explicitly routed to a HUMAN decision queue should NOT be offered to an autonomous get_next self-puller for implementation — that contradicts the gate's own intent.\n2. ORIGIN-MISMATCHED items: WI-1878 / WI-1812 / WI-1819 / WI-1994 are origin:remote and REFUSE a local caller's claim with {error:\"not_claimable\"} (trust/admission gate) — yet get_next / orient's claimable list still surface them, so the caller only learns they're un-claimable AFTER spending a claim call.\n3. UN-ACTIONABLE-HERE tooling bugs: EI-8574 (harness:null, src/parser/mod.rs in the `rtk` tee tool) has no source checked out in this workspace (rtk is a prebuilt linuxbrew binary) — un-fixable from here, but still self-selected.\n\nCORRECT STATE (proposed): the self-select floor for claim_next/scheduler:get_next should pre-exclude, or at least de-rank, items that (a) carry ideaLifecycle.triageDecision=\"gate\" / policy tier=human (never auto-implementable), and (b) are origin-mismatched for the caller (the same admission gate that later refuses the claim should filter at selection time, not after). That turns today's per-item manual claimHold dance into a scheduler-side invariant. Interim workaround (what I do now): release{claimHold:true} on each offender to durably drop it from self-select while keeping it claimable-by-id.\n\nLikely code area: the claim floors / spec.view.filter application in the scheduler:get_next path (packages/operator-core, the work-item claim/self-select layer) — path left unspecified to avoid a wrong protected-path hint.",

      "title": "Release build: the self-improvement loop (edit → auto-commit → main) is structurally absent on a packaged install — papercusp registered as remote_hive VIEW, no git-sync routine, no hive-git store",
      "summary": "Live-tested 2026-07-09 on the Mac VM (macOS 14.8.5, packaged 0.0.3 GUI+Server, plan release-selfimprove-canary-mac-2026-07-09). Canary: appended nonce 'release-canary 0.0.3 mac 2026-07-09T19:50:32Z ec0bd5de' to CANARY.md in ~/.papercusp-workspaces/clones/papercusp at 19:50:53Z, via the real install. RESULT: stranded uncommitted (still dirty >20min later; left in place as the PASS marker for a re-test).\n\nEvidence chain:\n1. NO SCHEDULED SYNC: harness_shared.routines has 0 rows on the VM — no system:git-sync routine was ever seeded for the papercusp self-clone. 10-min watch: no pickup (dev cadence is ≤3min).\n2. MANUAL FIRE SKIPS: git-sync:run via the VM operator MCP returned fired:true committed:false on a DIRTY tree. Root cause: the registry entry is {slug:papercusp, remote_hive:true, harness_kind:hive} — a joiner-side VIEW, which git-sync-eligibility classifies ineligible, and git-sync-reconcile never visits (no hive_slug / joined_via_link).\n3. NO ALTERNATE OUTBOUND PLANE: no ~/.papercusp/hive-git store on the VM; zero refs/namespaces/* in the clone — the hive-git device-namespace plane is not active on this build/install.\n4. LATENT CREDS BUG (would block push even if 1-3 were fixed): global gitconfig credential.https://github.com.helper points at /Applications/Papercusp.app/Contents/Resources/sidecar/bin/gh — that app does not exist (install is 'Papercusp Server.app'); the helper list was also reset ('' entry) so osxkeychain is skipped for github.com.\n5. Side observation: the sidecar restarted moments after the git-sync:run MCP call (embedded PG moved 24822→21605) — possibly coincidental, worth a look.\n\nExpected: whichever mechanism 'got the self-improvement loop working in release builds' should register an OUTBOUND path for the papercusp clone on a packaged install (member-shaped git-sync seeding, or the hive-git namespace publish + integrator/bridge egress) + working credentials.     {
      "id": "EI-8913",
      "title": "Embedding-space desync: a runtime pref switch silently invalidates every stored vector, and search reports no error",
      "summary": "THE CLASS (generalizes past this one bug): a vector's DIMENSIONALITY is checked everywhere; its SPACE is checked nowhere. `EMBEDDER_DIM === 384` is asserted in three files, and both embedders (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small truncated to 384, and Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5) satisfy it. So a mode switch produces vectors that are structurally valid and semantically meaningless together. Nothing throws. Search just quietly ranks noise.\n\nMEASURED (2026-07-09): after flipping memoryEmbedderMode auto->local, searching harness_shared.operator_turns for a row by its OWN EXACT TEXT ranked that row #6574 of 8383, cosine distance 1.0336 (near-orthogonal to itself). Post-fix the same probe returns distance 0.0000.\n\nWHY IT PERSISTED: embed-backfill's resumability predicate was `WHERE embedding IS NULL`. That encodes \"a vector, once written, is valid forever\" — false the moment the embedder is a runtime choice. Foreign-space rows were never revisited, so a mixed column could never self-heal. Sampling caught it mid-drift: 4 of 40 rows BGE, 36 OpenAI, ratio climbing each 5-min sweep.\n\nFIXED (WI-3616): migration 530 adds `<embedCol>_mode` to all five prose tables; the predicate became `embedding IS NULL OR mode IS DISTINCT FROM $active`; UPDATE writes vector+mode atomically. mem0's memory vectors were already immune — they use per-mode tables (memory_vec_openai / memory_vec_local). The prose surfaces simply never inherited that discipline.\n\nTHE IMPROVEMENT WORTH GENERALIZING: three separate call sites (memory/configure.ts, agent-tools/search/embedder.ts, search/embed-backfill.ts) each INDEPENDENTLY re-derive the active mode from the same pref, with three subtly different cascades — embed-backfill's ignores the openai-exhaustion cooldown entirely. Any one of them drifting desynchronizes stored from query vectors again. Worth collapsing onto ONE resolver that returns {mode, embed} and is the only thing allowed to name an embedder, plus a cheap periodic self-check (embed a known row's own text; assert it retrieves itself at distance ~0) so a space desync is DETECTED rather than silently served. The detector is the part that was missing: this bug was invisible for as long as it existed.",

      "state": "open",

      "id": "WI-2749",
      "title": "Windows cold onboarding: GUI finish_boot 120s watchdog FATALs while WSL install+bootstrap is still running; verify gate overlay + finalize-restart recovery, then complete owner-gated onboarding E2E",
      "summary": "Follow-up to WI-2734 (onboarding gate now renders on Windows). Secondary issues surfaced while verifying the cold first-run:\n\n1. **120s FATAL races long onboarding.** On a real cold first-run, WSL install + rootfs import + `/opt/papercup/bootstrap` + PG initdb/migrations easily exceed 120s, but the GUI's `finish_boot` `wait_for_operator` is a fixed `Duration::from_secs(120)` (main.rs ~1579-1604). When it fires it injects `window.__papercuspBootError` into the \"main\" window (the onboarding gate) and RETURNS EARLY — so `point_window_at_operator` + `spawn_operator_watcher` never run on the GUI side. Recovery depends on `wsl_finalize_ready` doing a breakaway RESTART once WSL flips Ready (Server-side watcher, main.rs ~3309). VERIFY: (a) the gate ignores `papercusp:boot-error` and does NOT show a scary terminal error mid-onboarding; (b) the finalize restart reliably brings up the operator + navigates the webview to the real HTTP port. If (a) fails, gate the boot-error inject on WSL-not-Ready, or extend/skip the GUI watchdog while onboarding is pending.\n\n2. **Gate overlay coverage.** CDP innerText on the default build showed the onboarding gate heading ('Papercup setup — Windows') alongside app-shell/Brain-panel text in the DOM. Likely DOM-behind-overlay (innerText captures hidden nodes) and cosmetic, but confirm the gate fully covers the app shell (no visible bleed-through) — the earlier env-override render was clean gate-only.\n\n3. **Owner-gated onboarding completion E2E.** Drive the gate through WSL install (needs admin/elevation, possibly reboot) + bootstrap → operator up → confirm webview navigates to the real loopback HTTP port, SPA live, SSE streaming, 0 console/log errors. The 'Sign in to GitHub' step needs the OWNER's in-VM credentials (P-003-adjacent). The distro papercup-runtime currently exists at PendingBootstrap on the VM.\n\nRelates: WI-2734 (fixed), WI-2719 (clean-install verify), WI-2644 (version 0.0.0 vs 0.0.2 + favicon 404).",

      "summary": "Surfaced while scoping EI-1763 (the READ-side slug leak). The sync transport endpoint endpoint-route/routes/zero-harness/rest-query.ts (+ rest-query-batch.ts) is `auth:'public'` and passes JSON.parse(url 'args') VERBATIM to resolveNamedQueryV2 — no session, no principal, no workspace scoping, no validation that args.workspaceId matches an authenticated session. So the EXISTING workspace-scoped resolves (harnessLanes/auditLog/operatorBudget/harnessStatus/pendingReviews) already trust a client-supplied workspaceId: in a multi-tenant deployment a caller reads ANY tenant by passing its id. EI-1763's per-resolve workspace_id FILTER closes the ACCIDENTAL same-slug cross-workspace leak (a strict improvement, in-scope) but does NOT establish a tenancy BOUNDARY on this endpoint — that requires either (a) per-workspace deployment / a scoping gateway (then client-passed workspaceId is fine within a deployment), or (b) the transport authenticating + INJECTING workspaceId from the session (not trusting client args) + validating. This is the framework/AD owner's architectural call (su-860d3 / pr5-impl). DEPENDENCY: decides whether EI-1763's filter is sufficient (model a) or whether a transport auth+inject layer is also needed (model b, plan-scale, applies to ALL ~14 workspace-scoped resolves).     {
      "id": "WI-35786",
      "title": "Delegated spawn on a macOS host with no GUI console session reports \"honored (N opened)\" + a success receipt but produces a PHANTOM member — no window, no process, no transcript",
      "summary": "MEASURED END TO END 2026-08-08 on current code (mig 759), machine B = Avis-iMac.local (172.31.44.2).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED\nTower published spawnreq-cb07e7849aebbb43 at 18:07:19Z. B honored it:\n  [18:07:21.727Z] [delegated-spawn-honor] spawnreq-cb07e7849aebbb43: downgraded --account=auto -> default (no registered claude pool account; using local system login)\n  [18:07:28.967Z] [p2p:receipt] honored action=delegated-seat:spawn offer=spawnreq-cb07e7849aebbb43 code=- receipt=af20b5e3-c7da-458a-a1bc-acfc5e33940a\n  [18:07:28.967Z] [work-offers] spawn-request 279242982/spawnreq-cb07e7849aebbb43 -> honored (1 member(s) opened)\nA coord_presence row appeared: su-8a0caef5-8edf-40e3-95f5-5bfa41b256a4, fleet=fed-drill, role=member, started 18:07:44Z.\n\nWHAT WAS ACTUALLY TRUE\n- heartbeat_at froze at 18:07:50Z (6s after start) and never advanced; presence pid = NULL.\n- 0 claude processes on B (`ps -axo args | grep -ac \"[.]papercusp/bin/claude\"` = 0).\n- Session scaffolding WAS written: ~/.papercusp/session-claude/su-8a0caef5-.../ with launch-intent.json + a 132KB launch-playbook.md + settings.json + credential symlinks.\n- BUT projects/-Users-aviweiss--papercusp-workspaces-clones-papercusp/ is EMPTY -> NO transcript -> the CLI never took a single turn.\n- The member never performed the 3 trivial instructions in its launchContext (orient, one coord:send, stop). No coord_event_log row from or mentioning it.\n\nROOT CAUSE (verified)\nB has NO GUI console session: `who` returns EMPTY, `stat -f \"%Su\" /dev/console` = root, Terminal.app not running. The Mac rebooted ~17:05Z and is sitting at the login window. The macOS delegated-spawn path opens a Terminal window, which cannot succeed with no Aqua session — so the window never opened and claude never ran. Everything upstream of the window still \"succeeded\".\n\nWHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DID NOT CATCH IT\ndelegated-spawn-honor.ts already documents this failure class for Windows (WI-5306 / EI-19328706303827921) and states the macOS/Linux paths are protected by their own boot-death probe (EARLY_EXIT_PROBE_MS / headless boot-receipt scan). That protection did not fire here. Worse, defaultVerifyLocalMemberBoot's oracle is \"poll THIS host's coord_presence for a NEW member on fleetSlug\" — and a presence row DID appear without claude ever taking a turn (inference: written by the launcher, not the agent). So the very probe meant to distinguish a real boot from a phantom returns a FALSE POSITIVE here, and would happily stamp the receipt \"confirmed booted locally\".\n\nIMPACT\nThe requesting leader gets a federated SUCCESS receipt plus a live-looking presence row and waits forever for a member that does not exist. This is the exact \"honored N opened, zero live members\" shape the code comments warn about, so it is silent and looks like success on both sides.\n\nSUGGESTED FIX (not implemented)\n1. Make the liveness oracle prove a TURN, not a presence row: require a transcript file / a first tool call / a non-null pid with a live-process check before the receipt claims success — presence alone is provably insufficient.\n2. Preflight the GUI-console precondition on macOS BEFORE claiming the request (`stat -f %Su /dev/console` != root, or a real console user) and refuse LOUDLY with a federated receipt (a new refusal code, e.g. no_gui_console) rather than honoring into a void — same philosophy as the WI-5306 runtime preflight.\n3. Alternatively support a genuinely headless spawn on macOS so a login-window host can still honor seats.\n\nREPRO\nOn a macOS host at the login window with papercusp-accept-delegated-seats=true and an open seat-offer, call fleet:request_remote_spawn. Observe \"honored (N opened)\" + presence row + empty projects/ dir + zero claude processes.\n\nFacts: `delegated-spawn-phantom-member-no-gui-console`, `p2p-spawn-leg-works-on-current-code`.",

      "state": "blocked",

      "id": "WI-3684",

      "summary": "EVIDENCE (tower, 2026-07-10 02:40–03:13Z, pid 2457765 = the 02:32:13Z papercup-bg-host generation): `[outbox-drain] drain failed for papercusp-workspace::papercusp: SESSION_CLOSED: Cannot append to a closed session (discovery key: 5aqcpm1ateg477qmoomrzf8byyi8jiom9nzxxyqpo8r8tpenc4yy)` + the same from `[wire-presence] announce tick error` — 573 occurrences since 02:40Z, every ~5s, starting 02:44:27Z which is EXACTLY the mass \"late boot ADOPTED\" window (host load 109–230; even the 180s PAPERCUSP_SUBSTRATE_BOOT_TIMEOUT_MS from the WI-1892 drop-in did not prevent adoption).       "id": "WI-37466",
      "title": "Head-snapshot retry is DEAD CODE on the timeout path: DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT_MS (15min) exceeds DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS (10min), and the budget never truncates an in-flight attempt",
      "summary": "packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/live-head-snapshot-client.ts\n\nMEASURED CONSTANTS (source read 2026-08-09, re-verified 10:3xZ):\n- L39  DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT_MS      = 15 * 60_000  (900s)\n- L56  DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS = 10 * 60_000  (600s)\n- L62  DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_RETRY_DELAY_MS  = 15_000\n\nTHE DEFECT. The retry loop's stop condition is `if (now() - startedAt + delayMs > budgetMs)` (L396-399), and the surrounding comment states DELIBERATELY that \"Budget governs when we stop STARTING attempts - it never truncates an in-flight one.\" That non-truncation is a defensible choice on its own. What makes it a bug is the ORDERING of the constants against it: one attempt that runs to its own 900s timeout already exceeds the entire 600s budget, so the stop condition fires before a second attempt can ever start. On the timeout path the retry loop is structurally incapable of retrying - it is dead code.\n\nNEEDED INVARIANT: BUDGET > TIMEOUT + DELAY. Anything else makes `attempts` a fiction for the slowest failure mode, which is precisely the mode retry exists to survive. Either raise the budget above timeout+delay, or make the budget truncate the in-flight attempt (a real design choice, but then say so and drop the comment).\n\nWHY IT SHIPPED: the tests model only FAST failures. A fast transport error returns well inside the budget, so a second attempt does start and the loop looks healthy. No test exercises an attempt that consumes more wall-clock than the whole budget - the only case where the ordering bug is observable.\n\nCORROBORATION FROM A REAL RUN (P-014 attempt 5, 2026-08-09): 2 attempts over 616,436ms elapsed, of which only 15,000ms was `waitedMs`. Both attempts failed fast-ish (transport), which is why a second one started at all; had either hit the 900s timeout, the run would have stopped at one attempt while reporting a budget \"exhausted\".\n\nRE-CHECK: grep -nE 'DEFAULT_HEAD_SNAPSHOT_(TIMEOUT|RETRY_BUDGET|RETRY_DELAY)_MS =' packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/live-head-snapshot-client.ts\n\nFOUND WHILE: working P-014 (release seed cut ships full history). Filed unlinked - discovered during that work, not implementing it.",
