      "id": "WI-37476",
      "title": "UNEXPLAINED mass desktop death: 3 desktops died in one launch, 2 of them on ISOLATED target dirs that build never touched — mechanism undetermined, and the obvious explanation is ruled out",
      "summary": "## Why this is separate from WI-37452 (the dedup guard flagged 0.93 similarity — deliberately overridden)\n\nWI-37452 was filed for this same incident, but its DEFECT (the target-dir slot guard deciding on an argv spelling) is fixed, tested and CLOSED. What is *not* fixed is the observation that started it: three desktops died at once. Left as a comment on a closed item, that question goes terminal and invisible. It is an open question with no known fix, so it gets its own open item.\n\n## The observation (2026-08-09 ~09:33Z, my launch, evidence real)\n\n`cd papercusp-desktop && OPERATOR_DEV_PORT=3170 npm run tauri -- dev --config '{...}'`. Three desktops were running:\n\n| app pid | target dir |\n|---|---|\n| 172711  | `~/.cargo-target`      (slot 0) |\n| 3621374 | `~/.cargo-target-dev2` (slot 1) |\n| 2487732 | `~/.cargo-target-dev3` (slot 2) — mine |\n\nImmediately after, a pid probe showed 172711, 3621374, 2487732, 164271, 3621185, 2486714 all GONE. Two of those windows were peers'.\n\n## RULED OUT — do not re-derive these\n\n1. **Shared-target-dir corruption (WI-7101) cannot explain two of the three.** My build wrote only to `~/.cargo-target`. The desktops on `-dev2` and `-dev3` were on *isolated* dirs it never touched.\n2. **`bin/dev-operator-ifneeded.sh` did NOT kill a squatter on this launch.** I originally filed this as the cause; it is wrong. The incident log (`/tmp/papercusp-capability/scratch/bash-628855cd-ea6.log` line 12) reads verbatim `[tauri] operator already serving on :3170 — reusing`, and there is no `terminating squatter pid(s)` line anywhere in it.\n3. **The staging-api restarts were not caused by my launch.** `journalctl --user -u papercup-staging-api` shows `Stopping…` at 05:25:35 and 05:35:39 local, and `[memory-watchdog] RSS high-water mark tripped … { rssMb: 6076, rssLimitMb: 3200 }` at 05:39:29 — the watchdog recycling on its own schedule.\n4. **\"The slot lock dies with the build\" is FALSE** (measured at length under WI-37452: the lock is held by the launcher for the whole dev session and survives `exec`). Do not resurrect that story.\n\n## Remaining live hypothesis — UNVERIFIED, and I refuse to promote it\n\nA cgroup reap. EI-9748 records headless children being reaped by a service's cgroup on restart, and this box bounces `papercup-staging-api` constantly. If those desktops were spawned from agent sessions parented into a service cgroup that bounced then, all three die together regardless of target dir — which is the one property the observation actually has: they died *together*, across unrelated dirs.\n\nI could not confirm it. The processes were already gone when I looked, so their cgroup membership was unreadable, and a plausible story is not a cause.\n\n## How to settle it, cheaply, if you catch it live\n\nRecord cgroup membership for every running desktop BEFORE a launch:\n\n```bash\nfor p in $(pgrep -f 'debug/papercusp-desktop'); do echo \"$p $(cat /proc/$p/cgroup)\"; done\n```\n\nIf a mass death correlates with one cgroup bouncing, that is the answer — and the fix belongs wherever agent-launched desktops are parented into a service cgroup, NOT in the target-dir slot machinery, which is now doing its job correctly.\n\n## Why filed rather than dropped\n\nThe seductive explanation (\"a second build corrupted the shared dir\") is written down in CLAUDE.md *and* in the slot script's own header, so anyone seeing desktops die during a launch will reach for it — as I did — and it is provably insufficient here. Leaving that trap unmarked is how the same wrong diagnosis gets made a third time.\n\nSeverity minor: no known ongoing loss. Unclaimed on purpose — whoever next observes a live mass-death is far better placed to settle it than someone re-reading this cold.",

    {
      "id": "WI-37480",
      "title": "produceLogSnapshot starves the bg-host event loop for its whole duration, so the freeze watchdog restarts the host and kills the snapshot — the snapshot cannot survive its own process (root cause of WI-36770's recycle cadence)",
      "summary": "## Mechanism\n\n`produceLogSnapshot`'s read loop (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/log-snapshot.ts`) awaits only on `ownLog.get()` promises. A block already resident in the store resolves **within the current tick**, so `await` yields to the MICROTASK queue and the loop **never reaches the event loop's TIMER phase**. Every `setInterval` in the process is starved for the entire read: the DBOS routines ticker, git-sync, and wake delivery.\n\n`bghost-watchdog.mjs` restarts `papercup-bg-host` when `MAX(last_fired_at)` across active routines is >240s stale while the unit is active. So the snapshot induces exactly the signal that gets its own host killed. **No timeout budget on either side could ever have fixed this** — the process that had to survive the operation was being restarted *because of* the operation. That is why five successive release cuts failed at this same wall.\n\n## Measured (2026-08-09, live 461,475-block own log)\n\n- Head-snapshot POST ran 11:45:26Z → 11:53:02Z (455s, `http=000` — connection killed).\n- `harness_shared.routines` fires: 11:45 (4), then **ZERO from 11:46 through 11:54**, resuming 11:55. A 9-minute hole exactly spanning the POST.\n- `~/.papercusp/bghost-watchdog.log` 11:53:01.961Z: `FROZEN -> restarting papercup-bg-host … routine fires 417s stale AND scheduler (routinesTick) 422s ago (> 240s) while active`.\n\n**The watchdog is CORRECT and is not the thing to change.** The ticker really was frozen.\n\n## Corrects a widely-carried claim\n\n\"bg-host self-recycles every ~8.5 min\" is **not** an unconditional property. Its own watchdog log shows **41 minutes healthy with zero restarts (10:54:29Z → 11:35:01Z)**. It recycles on that cadence **only while a head-snapshot is in flight**. Prior observations of the \"cadence\" were all taken while snapshots were being attempted. Do not treat the recycle as an independent standing defect.\n\n## Fix\n\nOne yield per read window, at the end of the window loop:\n\n```ts\nawait new Promise<void>((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve));\n```\n\n`setImmediate` runs in the check phase, which the loop reaches only after giving timers their turn. At `SNAPSHOT_READ_CONCURRENCY=256` that is ~1.8k turns for this corpus — negligible against the read, and it changes nothing about what is folded or in what order.\n\n## Guard\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/log-snapshot-event-loop-yield.test.ts` (5 tests, green). Instrument: a `setTimeout(…,0)` armed before the read fires from the TIMER phase, so whether it lands DURING or AFTER the read is a direct, wall-clock-independent read of \"did this operation yield\".\n\nFalsifiability follows the repo's tier-1 discipline for an imported module — a permanently-resident deliberately-wrong implementation (`foldWithoutYielding`, the pre-fix loop shape) that the same instrument must report as STARVED, plus a calibration case. No tree mutation.\n\nNote the calibration needs **more than one** yield: `setImmediate` resolves in the check phase of the current iteration without having passed back through timers, so a single yield can land before the armed timer gets a turn (measured — a one-shot version reported `after`).\n\n## Why the two prior fixes did not catch it\n\nBoth prior halves made the read faster/leaner and neither touched the starvation, so each looked like progress and still hit the same wall:\n- half 1: bounded read pipeline (serial `get` was RTT-bound)\n- half 2: incremental fold (materialising 461,475 decoded ops peaked at 20.1GB and died with SIGABRT)\n\n## Transferable diagnostic\n\nA routine-fire histogram over an operation's window; a HOLE matching the operation's span is event-loop starvation, not slowness:\n\n```sql\nSELECT date_trunc('minute', last_fired_at), count(*)\n  FROM harness_shared.routines\n WHERE workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace'\n   AND last_fired_at BETWEEN <start> AND <end>\n GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;\n```\n\nAlso: bg-host logs NOTHING before its stop (it is an external `systemctl restart`), so the journal alone makes the restart look causeless. `~/.papercusp/bghost-watchdog.log` is the authoritative record of who restarts it and why.\n\n## Status\n\nFix + guard in tree, `lint:tsc` clean (`LINT_TSC_RESULT label=operator-core scope=files exit=0 status=clean`), 5 new tests green, 65 passed across the 9 existing snapshot suites. Real-corpus re-probe with the fix loaded is IN FLIGHT; P-014 closes only on a measured `coreSparseFrom > 0` from a fresh sparse cut.",

      "id": "WI-37494",
      "title": "LAZY_SUBSTRATE_BOOT's owner-ratified staging constraint names a venue (:3170) that CANNOT execute it — the cutover has been structurally un-stageable since it was written",
      "summary": "Found while working EI-13795 (hyperbee FD leak), 2026-08-09. No code changed.\n\n`FLAGS.LAZY_SUBSTRATE_BOOT` (`papercusp-lazy-substrate-boot`) is `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS` `case:'cutover'` (libs/flags/src/types.ts:2420). Its entry records an owner-ratified BINDING execution constraint (D-005/D-006, plan shared-hive-cross-machine-scale-10k-2026-06-29 P-010): **stage on :3170 first**, attended verify, owner/leader flips.\n\n## The defect\n**:3170 cannot perform that verify, by construction.** Three independent findings, each sufficient:\n\n1. **:3170 boots NO substrate.** `boot-all.ts:263-269` (`defaultInProcessBootAllowed` → `backgroundWorkersEnabled`) refuses the default boot path on a request-only host. `boot-all.ts:850` says it verbatim: *\"substrate default boot disabled on request-only host (PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 / :3170); bg-host owns corestore\"*. `systemctl --user cat papercup-staging-api.service` confirms `PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0`. So there is nothing on :3170 for lazy-boot or the eviction reaper to act on — a verify there measures zero work and returns green. That is the zero-work false-green class CLAUDE.md already documents three times (`tsc -p .`, `test:affected`, `-t` no-match).\n\n2. **The flag cannot be scoped to a target.** Overrides are ONE shared PG row (`operator_flag_overrides` via `readOperatorState`/`writeOperatorState`, `flag-override-store.ts:35`) plus a deliberate cross-process `flag_override_changed` NOTIFY to every listening process (WI-6793). A flip reaches :3070, :3170 **and bg-host** — and bg-host is the corestore owner holding the FDs. \"Flip it on staging\" IS the production flip.\n\n3. **A throwaway-workspace rehearsal doesn't substitute.** The override is workspace-keyed by `cacheKey: () => activeWorkspaceId()` (`flag-override-store.ts:88`) — the READING process's active workspace, not the workspace being booted. bg-host's active workspace is papercusp-workspace, so an override set for `generic-test` is never read when bg-host boots generic-test's harnesses. Corroborated independently by EI-1831.\n\n## Why it matters\nThe flag has sat dark ~6 weeks with the eviction reaper, the outbox keepalive and the P-010 activation planner all BUILT and tested (`substrate-eviction-reaper.ts`, `substrate-boot-wrapper.ts`, `planSubstrateActivation` wired at boot-all.ts:1188-1200). The mechanical explanation is not reluctance — the venue the constraint names cannot run the test. Meanwhile the behaviour it would fix is live: 2038 hyperbee fds across 92 harness stores in one process (measured pid 2388036, 2026-08-09).\n\nThis is the same shape as the module-pin/detector class this repo has hit repeatedly: **the instrument was narrower than the property it was meant to measure, and its silence read as \"not done yet\" rather than \"cannot be done here.\"**\n\n## Proposed fix (needs the owner — the constraint is owner-ratified, so only the owner can amend it)\n- **(A)** Stage on an ISOLATED operator stack — its own `HOME` + `PAPERCUSP_HOME` + workspace + PG, running `PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=1` so it genuinely owns a corestore. Reproduces the affected topology with zero fleet blast radius. (D-012 isolated-stack recipe; needs the three env pins.)\n- **(B)** Amend D-005/D-006 to name **bg-host** as the venue with an explicit rollback (flip OFF + restart bg-host restores eager boot; the flag's own text calls OFF \"definitively-safe … cannot diverge\"), attended by the owner.\n\n🚫 Do NOT \"fix\" this by giving :3170 background workers — that creates a SECOND corestore owner and breaks the EI-126 single-writer invariant the request-only guard exists to protect.\n\nFull evidence and probes: EI-13795 checkpoint + post 56637.",

      "id": "WI-37576",
      "title": "shipped-seed-artifact.test.ts is RED on 3 assertions — the bundled corestore payload is 1,529,554 bytes LARGER than its manifest declares, and epoch-keys.json is absent from the shipped seed",
      "summary": "Found incidentally while running the full `@papercusp/operator-core` suite as the regression set for WI-37571 (an unrelated loop-transitions change). **I do NOT hold this item and have not investigated the cause** — filing it because it is a live red that nothing else had filed, not because I diagnosed it.\n\n## The failures\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/shipped-seed-artifact.test.ts` — \"shipped seed artifact (integrity of the real bundled seed)\", 3 failing assertions:\n\n1. **`every declared payload exists on disk at its declared size (catches a truncated/partial ship)`** — `:123`\n   ```\n   AssertionError: corestore: payload size drifted from the manifest:\n     expected 6031427350 to be 6029897796\n   ```\n   Actual on disk is **1,529,554 bytes LARGER** than the manifest declares. Note the direction: the test's own comment frames this check as catching a TRUNCATED/partial ship, but what is observed is a payload that OVERSHOOTS its manifest — so the manifest and the payload were produced at different times, rather than a transfer being cut short.\n\n2. **`ships the bundled epoch keys — the offline path for the DEFERRED git restore`** — `:132`\n   ```\n   AssertionError: epoch-keys.json missing — offline git restore cannot resolve a key:\n     expected false to be true\n   ```\n   `existsSync(join(SEED_DIR, 'epoch-keys.json'))` is false.\n\n3. A third assertion in the same file (truncated in my captured log tail — re-run the file to see it).\n\n## Evidence\n\nFull suite run 2026-08-09 ~22:0xZ, `npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-core run test`:\n\n```\nTest Files  1 failed | 3909 passed | 6 skipped (3916)\n     Tests  3 failed | 52083 passed | 2 expected fail | 24 skipped | 7 todo (52119)\n```\n\n**This file is the ONLY failing file in the entire workspace** — 3,909 other test files passed. So this is an isolated, well-bounded red, not a symptom of broad breakage.\n\nReproduce:\n```bash\nnpm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/shipped-seed-artifact.test.ts\n```\n\n## Why I did not claim or fix it\n\n- The subject is a **~6GB bundled binary artifact** plus its manifest. Reconciling them plausibly means regenerating the seed bundle, which is heavy and easy to get wrong blind.\n- Both symptoms together (payload larger than declared, a key file absent) read like a **seed rebuild that is in flight or was left half-finished** rather than a code defect. If a peer is mid-regeneration this may resolve on its own — and a second agent regenerating a 6GB artifact concurrently would be actively harmful.\n\n**Whoever picks this up: establish first whether the manifest or the payload is the stale side, and check for an in-flight seed rebuild before regenerating anything.**\n\n## Not a duplicate (checked)\n\n`work_items:search` returned 0 hits but its semantic leg ERRORED (`degraded: true`), so that result is not evidence of absence. Re-checked with a direct lexical query over `harness_shared.work_items`: the only related rows are **EI-19458472116740526** (done), **WI-5179** (resolved) and **WI-4920** (done) — all closed and about different aspects of the seed/epoch-key path. No open item covers this.\n\n## Ruled out as the cause: WI-37571\n\nMy change (loop-transition disarm logging) cannot be responsible. The test imports only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` and seed-bundle modules (`@papercusp/seed-bundle`, `restore-hive-seed`, `bundled-epoch-key-provider`, `deferred-git-restore`), and contains **zero** references to routines/loop code (grep count 0). It asserts over bytes on disk, which nothing in that change writes.",

      "id": "WI-37578",
      "title": "The macOS rig GUEST is hung/dark (VM process alive, guest not answering ARP) — every p2p-git item is unmeasurable until it is recovered, and nothing on the tower detects it",
      "summary": "## The condition (measured 2026-08-09 ~22:05Z)\n\nThe rig VM **process** is healthy and has been up 21h36m (started Sat Aug 8 20:32:32; it IS the rig — OpenCoreBoot + MacHDD on `mactap0`/`macbr0`). The **guest OS inside it is not servicing the network at all.**\n\nThree independent layers agree:\n- `papercusp-desktop/bin/vm-rig/preflight-login.sh` → **`FAIL(4)` VM unreachable over SSH**. Note this is NOT the kcpassword/loginwindow class (which is exit 2) — it is worse.\n- `ip neigh show dev macbr0` → **`172.31.44.2 FAILED`** — the guest does not answer **ARP**. A Mac sitting at the loginwindow still answers L2, so this is not \"auto-login didn't fire\"; the guest is hung, panicked, or halted.\n- the independent hostfwd path `127.0.0.1:2222` (QEMU **is** LISTENing) → **`Connection timed out during banner exchange`** — QEMU accepts the TCP, the guest never replies.\n\nTower-side symptom, consistent with the above: bg-host reports **`0 channel(s) open`**, **0** `channel CLOSED` events, and **20 dial-registry devices ALL `no-path`** for **~605-655 minutes** across many installs. So the guest died roughly 10-11h into the VM's 21.6h run.\n\n## Why this is critical\n\nEvery open p2p-git investigation is **unmeasurable** while this holds — there is no peer to open a channel with. It has already consumed real fleet time: EI-18808621019872598's Q1 (socket lifetime) was re-derived as \"blocked\" by hand on two consecutive wakes before the cause was pinned to the rig rather than to papercusp. That item is now `blocked` with the evidence attached.\n\n## The second defect: nothing NOTICES\n\nThe tower has no detector for \"the peer side went dark\". The bootstrap-tick escalation (WI-37226) fires correctly and honestly, but by design names no cause and hands the reader three checks to run. WI-37574 has since folded discriminator (2) in-band; discriminator (1) — the rig preflight — still runs only when a human/agent thinks to run it. That is **EI-19942866777863544** (\"a guard that exists but is never invoked is not a guard\"), which is currently filed at severity `nit` and unassigned despite guarding a class its own body says costs DAYS each time.\n\n## Recovery — deliberately NOT attempted this wake, and why\n\nRecovery needs a VM reset/boot. I did not do it blind, for a stated reason rather than timidity: the documented next state after a reset is that macOS auto-login may fail (kcpassword drift), which lands the rig at the loginwindow needing a **human GUI login** (`spice://127.0.0.1:5930`) because Secure Token blocks a headless password reset. Turning a hung-but-possibly-recoverable guest into a state that provably requires a human is a worse position, and a hard reset of a hung guest also risks the disk. Whoever takes this should decide reset-vs-console-first with eyes open:\n- console first: SPICE at `127.0.0.1:5930` will show whether it is panicked, halted, or wedged — that is the read that makes the reset decision informed rather than blind.\n- then `bin/vm-rig/boot-headless-current.sh` (runs ON the VM; the operator runs headless at the loginwindow) once SSH is back.\n\n## Standing fact\nAsserted as `p2p-rig-guest-dark-2026-08-09` (workspace scope, 12h TTL) so peers stop re-deriving it. **Retract it the moment `preflight-login.sh` exits 0.**",

      "id": "WI-38341",
      "title": "A peer's git-sync hold is honored on the happy path but silently bypassed two ways — acquireLocks 'error' has NO caller branch, and CLAUDE.md's tier-3 probe recipe hands out a 600s TTL with no heartbeat while git-sync heartbeats its own",
      "summary": "Filed by su-dc8f5691 2026-08-12. Found while VERIFYING a claim I was about to file as a doc defect — the verification inverted my premise, so the framing below is deliberately the opposite of what I set out to write.\n\n## First, the correction: CLAUDE.md is RIGHT, and a widely-carried agent belief is WRONG\n\nThe repo CLAUDE.md tier-3 mutation-probe recipe (CLAUDE.md:786-792) says git-sync's own tick takes `git-sync:<slug>` and **skips when a peer holds it**. I carried a standing check asserting the opposite (\"the lock is advisory and the sweep commits anyway\"). **The doc is correct; my check was wrong, and I have retracted it.**\n\nVerified in source at tip, `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/git-sync/git-sync-action.ts`:\n- `:447-452` — a not-ok `tryAcquireResource` returns `{ state:'held', blockedOn, blockedReason }`.\n- `:1514-1526` — the caller returns `{ status:'skipped', reason:'lock_held', blockedOn }` and logs `a peer holds <resource> — skipping this tick`.\n\n**Where the wrong belief comes from — worth recording, because it will recur.** The resource is registered with `enforcement: 'advisory'` (`:310`), and `locks:list` renders that word. \"Advisory\" there is a REGISTRY classification (no hook enforces the lock against arbitrary shell commands); it does NOT mean the routine ignores it. git-sync honors it **voluntarily**, which is exactly what advisory means in the cooperative sense. Reading the registry word as \"the sweep ignores your hold\" is the trap.\n\n## But the hold is NOT airtight — two real bypasses, both of which produce the exact symptom \"commits landed while I held the lock\"\n\n### (A) `state:'error'` has no caller branch — git-sync proceeds and commits UNLOCKED\n\n`acquireLocks` returns `{ state:'error' }` on a thrown acquire (`:435-446`): workspace-lock contention that outlasted `acquireWithContentionRetry`, or the SU-lock DB being unreachable/not bootstrapped. The caller at `:1513` branches on `'held'` only. There is no `'error'` branch — control falls through to the sync body. The only downstream uses are `:1556` (`lock.state === 'acquired'` gates the heartbeat) and `:1571` (gates the release), so an `'error'` run does the whole commit → submodule-push → pointer-bump → push sequence **holding nothing**, while a peer believes it holds the lock.\n\nThe in-code comment at `:437-438` states the intent explicitly (\"proceed unlocked (best-effort)\"), so this is deliberate for the DB-unreachable case. The problem is that the same return value also covers **contention after retries** — a load-driven condition, not an infra outage. This box is 128 cores at load ~117 with 165 active agents; that is the routine operating point, not an edge case. It logs a `console.warn`, but nothing signals the peer, and the probe's `status` is never `skipped`, so no caller can distinguish \"I was protected\" from \"I was bypassed\".\n\n### (B) The recipe's `ttl_sec: 600` expires mid-probe, and the doc never says to heartbeat\n\nCLAUDE.md:790-791 hands the agent:\n\n    locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'git-sync:papercusp', mode: 'exclusive',\n                             ttl_sec: 600, reason: 'mutation probe' }\n\nwith no instruction to heartbeat it. **git-sync does not make that mistake for its own hold** — `LOCK_TTL_SEC = 600` at `:155`, and `:1556-1557` starts `startLockHeartbeat(...)` for the whole run, stopped at `:1570`. So the routine keeps its lease alive indefinitely while the agent's identical 600s lease silently expires after ten minutes.\n\nThat asymmetry is the sharp part: tier 3 exists for a probe that must hold the tree mutated **for as long as the suite runs**, and the suite this protects can run ~55 min. Under the documented recipe the mutant is exposed for ~45 of those minutes, and the exposure begins silently — the agent gets no signal that its lease lapsed. This alone is sufficient to produce a \"six commits landed while I held the lock\" observation without any bug in the skip logic at all.\n\n## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)\n\n- (A) Give `'error'` an explicit branch. At minimum, separate contention-exhausted from infra-unavailable: skipping the tick is the safe default when a lock the peer may be holding could not be evaluated, and \"proceed unlocked\" should be reserved for a provably-unbootstrapped lock store. Whatever the choice, it should be legible in the returned outcome so a probe can tell it was bypassed.\n- (B) Fix the recipe: either raise the TTL to exceed the longest protected suite, or (better) document `locks:heartbeat_resource` alongside it so the agent's hold behaves like git-sync's own. The generated CLAUDE.md is projected from `harness_shared.harness_doc_parts` — edit the PART and re-project with `node scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs --write`, never the rendered file.\n- Consider also correcting the \"advisory\" reading where `locks:list` surfaces it, since that single word is what manufactures the wrong belief.\n\n## NOT claimed\n\nI did NOT measure how often (A) fires — the code path is proven, its frequency is not. I did NOT reproduce either bypass empirically this session; both findings are source-verified at tip. The prior \"six commits during an exclusive hold\" observation I carried is second-hand recall from 2026-07-26 that I could not re-run, and I am explicitly NOT offering it as evidence — (A) and (B) are simply the two mechanisms that would explain such an observation without contradicting the verified skip logic.\n\nSkip-on-held is not new: the `:447-452` region traces back through 8c2e3910 (2026-06-12) and 941ca283 (2026-06-03), predating that observation.",

      "id": "WI-38342",
      "title": ":3070's pinned PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_WATCHDOG_LIMIT_MB=12288 puts 16 request workers permanently between the GC trigger and an unreachable recycle — ~350 useless full GCs/hour, and the one lever that reclaims never fires",
      "summary": "Found while measuring :3070 memory for WI-38221. Config-level, no code change needed to reproduce — read the unit env and the journal.\n\n## The two thresholds\n\n`papercup-dev-api.service` pins `Environment=PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_WATCHDOG_LIMIT_MB=12288` while also setting `PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=16` and `PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0`.\n\n- `resolveMemoryWatchdogLimitMb()` (packages/operator-core/lib/memory-watchdog.ts) returns the explicit env value first, so all 16 REQUEST workers get the BACKGROUND recycle limit of 12,288 MB rather than `MEMORY_WATCHDOG_LIMIT_MB_REQUEST` = 3,200.\n- The proactive-GC threshold is deliberately NOT derived from that override (EI-20237116358190923, correctly — raising the recycle backstop must not silently move the GC trigger out of reach). So GC still fires at the REQUEST tier: 3,200 x 0.6 = **1,920 MB**.\n\n## Why the combination is the worst of both\n\nEvery worker's steady-state RSS is ABOVE 1,920 MB and far BELOW 12,288 MB. So the cluster sits permanently in the band where the GC always fires and the recycle never can:\n\n- **Measured 2026-08-12 over a 6h journal window: 2,120 proactive full GCs, mean reclaim 7.3 MB from a mean 2,580 MB heap = 0.28%.** That is ~350 full stop-the-world mark-compacts per hour across the cluster, buying essentially nothing. The GC is not broken — the heap is genuinely live (one sample in the same set reclaimed 707 MB, which proves the page-return path works, so a 0.28% mean means there is nothing to collect).\n- Meanwhile the recycle — the ONLY mechanism that sheds a growing live set — is unreachable. 16 workers x 12,288 MB is 196 GB of nominal headroom on a 251 GB box that had 38 GB free at the time of measurement. The box would OOM long before a single worker tripped its limit.\n\nConsequence, from systemd's own accounting for the service lifetime that ended at 19:06 EDT: `Consumed 1d 19h 54min CPU time, 60.8G memory peak, 8.6G memory swap peak.` In practice the leak is bounded only by how often a deploy restarts the cluster.\n\n## Why the limit is probably pinned at all\n\n12,288 is `MEMORY_WATCHDOG_LIMIT_MB_BACKGROUND`, which strongly suggests it was copied from the bg-host drop-in (the EI-1613 class of fix — bg-host boots the substrate and legitimately needs it). :3070's cluster workers are BG=0 and, per the source comment, are supposed to be the \"plain request-only worker ... stays light, so 3200 fits it\" case. They are not light — a 13-minute-old worker is already ~1.6 GB — so 3,200 is also wrong for them. That is the real question this bug has to answer, and it is NOT simply \"unpin the env\".\n\n## Suggested shape of the fix (not yet decided — needs the WI-38221 leak result first)\n\n1. The tier is cluster-blind. A per-PROCESS recycle limit is the wrong unit when a single service runs N workers; the meaningful budget is per-SERVICE. Consider deriving the effective per-worker limit from a service-wide budget divided by the resolved worker count, so `PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=16` cannot silently multiply the ceiling by 16.\n2. Give the :3070 cluster worker its own measured tier the way :3170 and :3270 already got one, instead of inheriting BACKGROUND by a pinned env var.\n3. Either way, the GC trigger and the recycle limit should be resolved from the SAME tier decision, so they can never end up straddling the steady state as they do now.\n\n## Recurrence guard to add with the fix\n\nA test asserting the invariant directly: for any resolved role, `proactiveGcMb < recycleLimitMb` AND the expected steady-state band is not entirely between them. Plus an assertion that resolved recycle limit x worker count does not exceed the host's memory. Nothing today fails when a config puts a whole cluster permanently in the dead band, which is why this survived unnoticed.\n\n## Evidence\n- `systemctl --user cat papercup-dev-api.service | grep -E 'WATCHDOG|CLUSTER|BACKGROUND'`\n- `journalctl --user -u papercup-dev-api.service --since '-6h' | grep -A3 'proactive GC'` — pair rssMbBefore/rssMbAfter and aggregate\n- `resolveMemoryWatchdogLimitMb` + the `MEMORY_WATCHDOG_PROACTIVE_GC_MB_*` constants in packages/operator-core/lib/memory-watchdog.ts",

      "id": "WI-39540",
      "title": "Memory settings page shows a hard 300-row cap that reads as the corpus size — real reachable corpus is ~2,465 active rows",
      "summary": "OWNER REPORT (Avi, 2026-08-16): \"I only see like 300 memories, I thought we had a lot more than that.\"\n\nThe owner is right about the corpus and the page is technically working-as-coded — which is exactly the problem: the cap is indistinguishable from a measurement.\n\nMECHANISM (read the writer):\n  - apps/operator/app/settings/user/memory/page.tsx:27 — `export const DEFAULT_MEMORY_PAGE_LIMIT = 300;`\n  - :256 — the useSyncQuery args pass `limit: 300` unless `showAll`.\n  - packages/operator-core/lib/memory/list-user-memories.ts — `listUserMemories(userId, {limit})` fetches the user pool + one pool per registered harness, sorts newest-first, then applies the limit as a FINAL slice. So 300 = most-recent-300 across all pools, not a total.\n\nMEASURED CORPUS (harness_shared.memory_canonical, row_kind='memory', 2026-08-16):\n  - user pool (120f421b-…): 567 rows total / 513 active\n  - harness:papercusp pool: 2,194 rows / 1,907 active\n  - all pools the page reads (user + harness:%): 2,465 active, 383 broken_anchor, 415 forgotten, 1 archived\nSo the page shows 300 of ~2,465 active.\n\n(Aside worth keeping: memory_canonical ALSO holds 50,159 row_kind='entity' graph nodes. A raw table count is NOT a memory count — don't quote it as one.)\n\nWHY IT MISLEADS: `possiblyMoreThanShown` (=rows.length>=300) does render a 'Show all' affordance, but the page never states the TOTAL. The search placeholder reads \"Search your 300 most recent memories…\" — which parses as \"you have 300 memories\". This is the documented saturated-count-reads-as-a-measurement failure: a cap rendered without its denominator.\n\nDURABLE FIX: surface the denominator — a cheap COUNT alongside the capped page so the UI can say \"300 of 2,465\" (and label the Show-all button with the real remainder). Keep the 300 cap (EI-12937 added it for a real 2MB payload reason); the bug is the missing total, not the pagination.",

      "id": "WI-39886",
      "title": "Promote @papercusp/db-org into the full-replacement-mocks registry — it caused a collection-breaking gate red and is the #2 unprotected exposure (154 bare factories to convert)",
      "summary": "Split out of EI-20836231573383362 (guard-verdict fix, shipped). This is the half that was DELIBERATELY deferred, with its cost measured — not dropped.\n\n## Why it is real work, not tidying\n`@papercusp/db-org` has ALREADY cost an incident. A bare `vi.mock('@papercusp/db-org', () => ({ getOrgPg: ... }))` in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/learning-knowledge-scout.test.ts` broke COLLECTION of that whole file (`No \"setAdminPoolStatementTimeoutProvider\" export is defined on the \"@papercusp/db-org\" mock`, reached via agent-tools/locks/configure.ts:38 -> locks/su-lock-store.ts:11) and was named by green-checkpoint run 13. A peer fixed that ONE file at 2026-08-18T23:10:03Z. The other 153 remain.\n\n\"Modules that have actually cost us an incident\" is the registry's own documented admission criterion (scripts/check-full-replacement-mocks.mjs, docblock l.26-28). db-org meets it. It is not in the registry.\n\n## Measured cost of promotion (this is the whole reason it was deferred)\nImported the guard's real analyzer over the live corpus, 2026-08-19 01:5xZ:\n- `@papercusp/db-org`: **154 test files** carry a bare full-replacement factory. Every one must be converted to the import-actual spread BEFORE the entry is added, or the guard goes red on 154 violations immediately.\n- For scale, the whole unprotected population is 1,399 modules / 5,216 factories; db-org is #2 behind `packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-registry` (271).\n\n## Why it was not done in the same pass (disclosed, not hidden)\n1. The conversion is mechanical but NOT semantically free: spreading the real module changes what the test sees. A test that relied on an export being absent/undefined, or on the real module NOT being imported (side effects at import time — and db-org opens pools), can flip from green to red. 154 files is a real blast radius on a shared tree.\n2. It cannot be verified this wake: `npm run test:affected` is REFUSED (exit 75) by scripts/pc-heavy.sh while the release gate is isolating, and that refusal is CORRECT — overriding it can flip the gate's real-break-vs-load-flake verdict fleet-wide. A 154-file test change needs a full sweep, not `test:file`.\n\n## What shipped already (so this item is not blocked on discovery)\nEI-20836231573383362 made the guard's PASS verdict scope-honest, and it now NAMES db-org as the #2 unprotected exposure on every run. The gap is discoverable instead of invisible — which is exactly what made it sit for weeks.\n\n## Suggested approach\n1. `node scripts/check-full-replacement-mocks.mjs --list` — the census is now printed, top 25.\n2. Convert the 154 factory heads to `async (orig) => ({ ...(await orig<typeof import('@papercusp/db-org')>()), ...overrides })`. Mechanical; the guard's error text prints the exact target shape.\n3. Run the FULL sweep (not test:file) once the gate is out of its isolating phase — spreading a real module can change collection behaviour in files whose tests you did not touch.\n4. Only then add the `{ module: '@papercusp/db-org', why: ... }` entry, and confirm `--list` reports `0 full-replacement` for it.\n\nConsider `packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-registry` (271) as the follow-on, same method.",

    {
      "id": "WI-40435",
      "title": "Android 16KB-page emulator image (sdk_gphone16k_x86_64) cannot resolve ANY third-party launcher activity — install succeeds, `am start` returns START_CLASS_NOT_FOUND (-92)",
      "summary": "FOUND DURING: WI-40367 (P-018 Stonebrook Android greenfield launch proof).\n\nOn a fully-booted 16KB-page-size emulator image, a correctly-built and correctly-installed third-party APK CANNOT be launched: `am start` fails START_CLASS_NOT_FOUND (-92) / \"Error type 3\", with no crash and no logcat FATAL. This consumed ~8 hypotheses and several hours before a device-level positive control isolated it to the IMAGE, not the app.\n\nAFFECTED\n- AVD `stonebrook-p018`, serial emulator-5560, image `sdk_gphone16k_x86_64`, `getconf PAGE_SIZE` = 16384, booted (sys.boot_completed=1).\n- Install succeeds; `pm path` resolves. The class IS in classes3.dex; `<activity android:exported=\"true\">` IS in the merged manifest; aapt2 xmltree shows the fully-qualified `com.stonebrook.ledger.MainActivity` (no unexpanded `.MainActivity`).\n- `cmd package resolve-activity -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER <pkg>` -> no activity. `am start` -> START_CLASS_NOT_FOUND (-92).\n\nTHE DECISIVE POSITIVE CONTROL (what makes this an image defect, not an app defect)\nA known-good UNRELATED third-party APK (`com.papercuspai.operator.mobile`, 114,275,631 B, pulled read-only from a peer's emulator-5554) installed on the SAME emulator-5560 ALSO failed to resolve. `cmd package query-activities -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER` returned only 4 SYSTEM activities and zero third-party ones. The Activity Resolver Table on this image never admits third-party launcher entries.\n\nFIX / WORKAROUND\nUse a STANDARD (non-16KB) AVD. `stonebrook-p018-std` on port 5566 launched the BYTE-IDENTICAL APK (md5 734624bea22d6e3595b4950c3179beb7) first try:\n  resolve-activity -> com.stonebrook.ledger/.MainActivity\n  am start -W      -> Status: ok / LaunchState: COLD / TotalTime: 2245\n  ResumedActivity  -> com.stonebrook.ledger/.MainActivity ; FATAL count 0\nThat AVD then carried the whole WI-40367 release-APK acceptance to green.\n\nHYPOTHESES THIS KILLED (all disproved — recorded so nobody re-walks them)\nmissing android:exported (already present) · unexpanded .MainActivity (already fully qualified) · 16KB .so ALIGNMENT (`zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4` verified all 12 .so OK) · install corruption (a genuinely clean uninstall+reinstall, ceDataInode=0, failed identically) · \"Missing permission state for package ... on user 0\" (red herring) · system_server instability (probed 8x: 8/8 healthy, 0 watchdog kills) · missing libstonebrook.so in /proc/PID/maps (a REAL zero but EXPECTED — extractNativeLibs=false maps the .so from inside base.apk, so no separate path ever appears; a positive control of 3037 total maps lines proved run-as worked and the zero was genuine).\n\nTWO INSTRUMENT TRAPS HIT WHILE DIAGNOSING (same warning applies)\n1. `cmd package resolve-activity <package>` takes an INTENT, not a package name — the first \"No activity found\" was a self-generated false signal.\n2. The serial is `emulator-5554`, not `5554`. A wrong `adb -s` produces an authentic-looking \"does not exist\" from a device that never had the app.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS: 16KB-page images are the forward-looking Android target, so any future agent doing an emulator launch proof will hit this. The symptom (install OK, launch fails, no crash) reads exactly like an app packaging defect, which is why it cost hours.",

    {
      "id": "WI-40537",
      "title": "revocation_kcut FAILS on the 2-frame rig: after the ban, an epoch-1 key wrapped to the BANNED member's OWN device pubkey exists on both frames — mechanism (re-key vs key-distribution) NOT localized",
      "summary": "## The failure\n\nLive-federation matrix run `m1787374736` (local-matrix, 2-frame BYO rig, private testnet DHT), 2026-08-22T05:10:29Z, `===LOCAL_MATRIX_EXIT:1===`:\n\n```\nFAIL  revocation_kcut  (rc=1; log has no OVERALL:/✗ line)\nrevocation: K-CUT FAILED — banned member B still holds an epoch-1 key wrapped\nto its OWN device (iwRKqTp0myBNiSC6XxjA8wYV5mPxPiUnlvcuKc+NwDM=);\nthe re-key did not cut it off\n```\n\nRun roll-call: **15 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped of 18 registered.** OVERALL: FAIL.\n\n## Why this is filed critical\n\nThe K-cut is the cryptographic containment boundary: banning a member is supposed to re-key the pot so the banned device can no longer decrypt. This run says the banned device retains a valid epoch-1 key wrapped to its own pubkey. If that is what it appears to be, a ban does not actually revoke read access.\n\nThis lands directly on GOAL `shared-pot-p2p-is-ready-for-public-release-flip--fa8a26`. A public release flip with a non-functioning revocation cut is the kind of thing that is very expensive to discover after the flip.\n\n## The coverage trap this exposes — read this before concluding revocation is covered\n\n`fed_reap` PASSED in the same run, and it is the leg most likely to be mistaken for covering this. Its own PASS line bounds itself explicitly:\n\n> \"Session was seeded, not spawned — see header scope note; proves wind-down, NOT containment of a hostile session.\"\n\nSo: the leg that proves *wind-down* passed, and the leg that proves the *cryptographic cut* failed. Those two must not be read as covering each other, and a summary that reports \"revocation federates correctly\" from `fed_reap` alone would be wrong in exactly the direction that matters.\n\n## Bounded claims — what this item does and does NOT establish\n\n- **Does establish:** on this run, on this artifact, the k-cut assertion failed with the banned device still holding an epoch-1 key wrapped to its own pubkey.\n- **Does NOT establish** whether the root cause is in the re-key mechanism, in key distribution/propagation, or in the scenario's own teardown. I am reporting the run's verdict; I did not read the re-key implementation. Do not cite this item as having localized the defect.\n- **Does NOT establish** reproduction on current HEAD. Per D-037 the run used the gate's deb repacked from HEAD `b889f196af` at 2026-08-22T01:49Z — NOT current HEAD. First triage step should be confirming it still reproduces on a current build.\n- **n=1.** One run. It has not been repeated.\n\n## Upstream-contamination check (done, and it comes out clean)\n\n`attestation_unattested_device` (order 79) FAILED in the same run, and order 90 depends on it, so contamination is the obvious first suspicion. It does not hold: order 79's failure was that it could not HOLD its attestation strip, and its log line records that it *restored* B's device_attestations on frame a (\"2 attestation(s) — revocation_kcut(90) needs them to resolve B's pubkeys\"). So order 90's precondition was satisfied and its failure is its own.\n\nOrder 79 is separately NOT a product defect — it self-declares \"PRECONDITION UNHOLDABLE, so this leg CANNOT score the feature (NOT a product defect)\". See WI-40534's completion for the fingerprint reading on that one (frame a's restore is the ADMISSION path, WI-1585, so the log's suggested reordering fix will not hold there).\n\n## Evidence location + a durability warning\n\n`/tmp/local-matrix-wall1-run2.log` (roll-call at lines 179-200; the failure at line 160). Per-scenario logs were written to `/tmp/deb-hzfed.aJiyyE`. **The rig frames have already been destroyed** (teardown ran at end of run) and both paths are `/tmp`, so this evidence is not durable — the quoted lines above are the surviving record.       "summary": "P-006 of social-platform-integrations-2026-08-23, on the P-004 seam, binding on D-004 and D-006.\n\nWHAT: the create-shaped half of the social:* family. Unlike social:reply (P-005) there is no parent post to resolve from, so the destination is CALLER-SUPPLIED — which is exactly the shape D-020 rail 2 governs.\n\nDESIGN COMMITMENT (extends D-006 ruling (a) rather than contradicting it): the platform is still never a free-standing caller argument. The destination is ONE opaque token \"<platform>:<destination>\" parsed at the seam by the same first-colon rule, so the platform half selects the credential and is never trusted as an instruction; the destination half goes through assertTrustedSocialDestination, which refuses a body-only provenance.\n\nFLAG: per D-004 ruling (b) this ships behind a REGISTERED owner-authority flag, default OFF, with a KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS entry carrying its justification and a review-by date. This is the repo's second legitimate default-OFF category (an outward-facing publish surface the owner must personally ratify), not the parking-lot abuse — the verb is fully built and fully tested behind it and flipping it is one owner decision.\n\nACCEPTANCE: tests proving (1) a body-only destination is refused, (2) the flag OFF refuses to publish but still returns the resolution echo per D-004(b), (3) an AT-URI-shaped destination survives the first-colon parse, (4) a write-unverified platform (bluesky) is refused by the registry gate before the adapter lookup, (5) idempotency key is derived, never caller-supplied.       "id": "WI-41042",
      "title": ":3070 /api/mcp data-plane stalls silently for 8000ms with no response headers while /api/health stays 200 — the upstream root cause WI-35737 explicitly left open",
      "summary": "## Reopening what WI-35737 closed only half of\n\nWI-35737 fixed `papercup-mcp-proxy` **self-saturation** (proxy-side request amplification against its 200 in-flight cap) and states in its own resolution that **the root cause is upstream and remains open**. Nobody reopened it. This is that item.\n\n## The defect\n`:3070`'s `/api/mcp` goes **completely silent for ~8000ms — no response headers at all**, then the client times out and retries. Measured during the 2026-08-23 residue investigation: **151 `handshake_timeout_retry` events on `/api/mcp` in a 30-minute window**, while `/api/health` on the SAME process returned 200 throughout.\n\n## Why this keeps being misdiagnosed (I made this error myself)\n`/api/health` being green is **not** evidence the operator is healthy. It is served on the control plane and does not touch whatever the MCP data plane blocks on. I told the owner \"upstream isn't slow\" on exactly that reasoning earlier in this investigation and was wrong — WI-35737 had already falsified it. **Any triage of this item that leans on `/api/health` is measuring the wrong plane.**\n\nThe proxy is a **victim**, not the cause. Fixing the proxy again will not help.\n\n## Blast radius (why critical)\nA silent 8s stall on the MCP data plane is what agents experience as `mcp_proxy_overloaded` / `request_rejected`. During this investigation it **blocked ledger writes and a work-item claim outright** — the claim on EI-21268871278252116 was refused and the item was picked up by a different agent. Under fleet load this silently drops coordination writes fleet-wide.\n\n## What to determine\n1. What blocks inside `:3070`'s `/api/mcp` handler for 8s with headers unsent — the handler has not yet written a status line, so it is blocked *before* response start (event-loop block, a synchronous await on a saturated pool, or an unbounded queue).\n2. Whether it correlates with PG pool exhaustion (6-connection-per-host cap) or the `bg-host`/routines tick.\n3. Why no timeout fires server-side — an 8s silent hold with no 504 means nothing is bounding it.\n\n## Evidence\n- 151 `handshake_timeout_retry` / 30min on `/api/mcp`, `/api/health` 200 throughout (2026-08-23).\n- WI-35737 resolution text: root cause upstream, remains open.\n- Sibling already filed: EI-21266597359411650 (the psu-launcher 429 half).\n\nFiled from the EI-21268871278252116 residue investigation.",

      "title": "Package CONSTRUCTOR function [owner:Avi 2026-08-23]: a goal/plan package MAY carry `construct` — a sandboxed, PURE `(typedInputs) => spec` …",
      "summary": "Package CONSTRUCTOR function [owner:Avi 2026-08-23]: a goal/plan package MAY carry `construct` — a sandboxed, PURE `(typedInputs) => spec` run at START (never at install — P-006's install-is-inert discipline holds), so a template can build its plan/goal deterministically instead of static-content-plus-substitution. Determinism contract: output is a pure function of (package content, typed inputs); anything live it needs is resolved INTO the inputs by the start door (pickers → values), never read ambiently — which is what makes a dry-run PREVIEW possible at the start door before anything is created. Output is validated through the SAME create seam as hand-authored content (insertGoalRow / plans content validation — one writer seam, no drift). Executes in the existing code:run sandbox: time-boxed, no network/db/secrets (Cupboard-distributed code is third-party code). Consumes P-021's input schema; surfaced via P-017.",

    {
      "id": "WI-41764",
      "title": "BEFORE stamping any real item to pilot arm B: verify the work_items:complete self-review gate end-to-end against a live operator",
      "summary": "## Why this is a gate on P-007, not a nice-to-have\n\nD-021 deferred arm B's enforcement wiring specifically because it \"could not be tested end-to-end, only unit-tested against a marker no real item carries\". P-006 has now landed the wiring AND the assignment protocol that produces the marker — so the end-to-end test D-021 wanted has become possible for the first time. It has NOT been run.\n\nThe wiring is unit-tested (12 gate tests + 27 self-review tests green, and the 289-test existing completion suite confirms no regression), but every one of those exercises the decision functions, not the live verb against a real row with a real ledger read.\n\n## Why it must happen BEFORE the first stamp\n\nThe gate lives in `work_items:complete` — the one verb no agent in the fleet can route around. It refuses `not-claimed`, so the moment an item carries `payload.pilotArm:'B'`, whichever agent picks it up gets refused at close time until they supply `completion.selfReview`. If the ledger query, the identity resolution, or the window bound is wrong in the live path, that agent is wedged on a real work item and the failure surfaces as someone else's incident.\n\nRight now there is NO live risk: nothing is stamped, so `itemIsArmB` returns false everywhere and the gate is inert. That is exactly why this is cheap to do now and expensive to discover later.\n\n## What to verify\n\n1. **The code under test is actually running.** Two-port model: the wiring is in the staging tree and the Hono host has no file-watch, so confirm the serving operator was restarted since the change landed (`dev:pipeline_position` on `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts`, then `serving.startedSinceCodeChange`). A green e2e result against an operator running the OLD code is indistinguishable from a working gate — the gate would simply be absent.\n2. **Refusal path**: scratch item stamped `pilotArm:'B'`, close it with no `selfReview` → expect refusal naming verdict `not-claimed`, and confirm the item is STILL OPEN with no recorded completion (the atomicity D-021 §2 requires, per EI-20962416980274656).\n3. **Acceptance path**: same item, perform a real `capability:read`/`capability:git` on the changed file, then close WITH `selfReview` → expect acceptance.\n4. **Zero-findings path**: `selfReview` with `findings: []` → MUST be accepted (D-020). Refusing this would teach agents to invent findings.\n5. **Stale path**: review recorded BEFORE the last edit → expect `stale-review`.\n6. **The control that matters most**: an UNSTAMPED scratch item closes normally, unchanged. This is the fleet-wide regression, not a pilot concern.\n7. **Ledger scoping**: confirm the query finds this session's rows. A workspace-scoped su session files under `harness_slug='*'`, which has previously made ledger rows read as zero under a harness-scoped query — `selfReviewLedgerQuery` filters on workspace + coord_owner only, so verify that holds in practice rather than assuming it.\n\nRestarting the shared operator interrupts peers mid-work, so prefer letting the normal pipeline carry the change and verifying afterwards over forcing a restart.",

    {
      "id": "WI-4236",
      "title": "Add single-instance advisory lock to own-log Corestore (prevents concurrent-process key contention)",
      "summary": "Corrected scope for the \"Q1 keypair persistence\" fix originally hypothesized under WI-4070/WI-2105 — filed as its own item since WI-2105 (resolved) is UNRELATED (its fix was a no-hiveHome admission-list bug) and WI-4070 is the network-connectivity investigation, not this storage-layer fix.\n\nORIGINAL HYPOTHESIS (never verified): the own-log Corestore keypair does NOT persist across a process restart — each boot regenerates a fresh key, explaining the observed fed_hlc author-node-id oscillation (ef7a8160 / 660eb73a / b58a40fe) on the VM leg of the p2p rig.\n\nDIRECT EVIDENCE (2026-07-11/12, gathered while recovering the VM operator for WI-4070 P1/P2): inspected the VM's harness Corestore dir (/Users/aviweiss/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/papercusp/hyperbee/) before and after a full clean stop/restart of the packaged operator (launchctl bootout -> bootstrap -> kickstart -k, 2026-07-11 21:13 EDT). The CORESTORE primary-key metadata file's mtime was UNCHANGED (Jul 9 18:59, predating every restart including this one) — the on-disk keypair IS durably persisted; it is NOT regenerated on boot. The original Q1 \"persist the keypair\" fix would fix nothing — persistence already works for a simple restart.\n\nACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: the oscillation is caused by MULTIPLE CONCURRENT PROCESSES opening the SAME Corestore storage root at once — observed twice in one evening on the VM: a wedged/stale packaged-app process tree + a competing `tauri dev` instance from a separate checkout (papercup-build-mac) racing for the same default PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACES_ROOT; killed once, then a FRESH `tauri dev` cluster reappeared ~2min later and was killed again. Two live processes opening the same 'peer-log' Hypercore produces exactly the observed identity churn (one wins, the other's writes fork/orphan). Kill-on-sight is not durable — it already recurred same-session.\n\nDURABLE FIX: add a SINGLE-INSTANCE GUARD on the Corestore/own-log storage root — an advisory/exclusive lock (flock-style lockfile, or an OS-level file lock) taken when openOwnLog(store) first opens the 'peer-log' core, held for the process's lifetime, and checked/refused with a loud actionable error by any second process opening the SAME storage root. Converts silent corruption into a fast, diagnosable failure — cheaper than the existing WI-2136 orphan-tail / WI-3535 own-log-fork-guard detectors, which only catch the damage after the fact.\n\nWhere to look: packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/peer-log.ts (openOwnLog), corestore.ts (getHarnessStore/storagePath), and whatever single-instance enforcement (if any) exists today at the Tauri/launchd layer — it did not prevent this.",

      "id": "WI-4701",
      "title": "Heavy-command admission is a load-triggered TRIPWIRE, not a real cap: route the documented `npm run test:affected` (and other heavy npm scripts) through the pc-heavy.sh semaphore by default (Part 2 of EI-10913)",
      "summary": "Split from EI-10913 (Part 1 — the guard-blocks-its-own-remedy defect — is FIXED; this is the deeper design follow-up it also raised).\n\nPROBLEM: pc-heavy.sh has a host-wide flock counting semaphore that would prevent N agents' concurrent vitest/tsc runs from saturating the shared 128-core box. But it is OPT-IN, and CLAUDE.md instructs every agent to run `npm run test:affected` / `test:affected:integration` DIRECTLY, bypassing the semaphore. So the fleet's documented, universal workflow never engages the limiter; the only thing that engages is the PreToolUse admission gate (pretooluse-bash-resource-gate.sh), which fires only AFTER host load1 is already past ~1.5x cores. Measured live during the WI-4545 audit: 70 concurrent vitest processes, load 219/128 cores. A concurrency limiter that only activates after the concurrency has already melted the host isn't limiting concurrency — it's a tripwire that refuses whoever arrives last while the 70 runs that caused the saturation churn on unimpeded.\n\nFIX OPTIONS (from the item, in preference order):\n1. Route the DOCUMENTED path through the semaphore: make `npm run test:affected` (and the other heavy npm scripts) acquire a pc-heavy slot internally, so the cap is enforced by default and the admission gate rarely fires. Then no agent has to know pc-heavy.sh exists.\n2. Or: have the admission hook AUTO-WRAP a heavy command in pc-heavy.sh instead of rejecting it (queue, don't refuse). NOTE a caveat: a PreToolUse hook decides allow/deny then exits BEFORE the command runs, so it cannot itself hold a slot — auto-wrap would require rewriting the tool_input command (uncertain hook-protocol support + shell-quoting risk), so Option 1 is the cleaner path.\n\nWHY human-reviewed (not auto-implemented): this is a host-wide admission-policy change touching interactive runs, the green-checkpoint/capability exemptions, nested-invocation/bypass semantics, timeout behavior, and the package.json test workflow — a shared-safety-surface design decision, well beyond a self-inline fix. Needs a deliberate design pass, not an auto-fix.\n\nThe lesson worth internalising (sibling of WI-4541): when you build an admission gate, test what it does at the moment it actually fires — including whether the remedy it prints still works, and whether the documented happy-path even reaches the limiter.",

      "title": "psu resume: cross-backend PORT — resume a Claude session under Codex/OMP (seed a fresh session with prior conversation)",
      "summary": "⛔ AWAITING OWNER (Avi) GO — DO NOT implement until Avi answers the OPEN QUESTION (trigger mechanism) below AND gives an explicit go. This is a design-shape, multi-file feature; plan-first discipline applies.\n\nFull handoff brief: apps/operator/docs/plans/BRIEF-psu-resume-cross-backend-port-2026-07-14.md\n\nPROVENANCE: [owner:Avi 2026-07-14, verbatim] \"this was a claude opus session originally, but I wanted to resume it as a chatgpt session, I should be able to do that, no?\"\n\nWHAT: let `psu --resume` of a session continue the CONVERSATION under a DIFFERENT backend (e.g. a Claude/opus session → a Codex/GPT session). A native cross-backend resume is impossible (claude jsonl vs codex rollout vs omp thread — none parses another's format), so this is a cross-backend PORT: mint a FRESH native session (new id) seeded with the source session's conversation as context. Feasible because papercusp stores turns backend-agnostically (session_turns recall + packages/operator-core/lib/session-archive-read.ts + adv-session-search.ts).\n\nPRIOR WORK: WI-4889 (resolved) = the two-step resume menu (RESUME_MODEL_MENU/RESUME_EFFORT_MENU/composeResumeModelSpec/chooseResumeModel in apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs). WI-4891 (resolved) = scoped that menu to session.agent's backend to block a broken `claude -m sol`. This feature INTENTIONALLY reworks WI-4891's hard-scoping so cross-backend WORKS (via port) instead of being blocked.\n\nOPEN QUESTION FOR OWNER (blocks build): trigger mechanism — (A, recommended) auto: picking a different-backend model triggers the port; or (B) an explicit \"Switch backend…\" menu row. Avi has NOT chosen.\n\nVERIFY (per brief): node --check psu-launcher.mjs; npm run test:file -- apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts; npm run lint:tsc -- --mine. Keep port logic (history extraction + fit-vs-summarize) in PURE exported functions (the @inquirer flow can't be driven headlessly).",

      "title": "pot-git cross-machine repoKey NEVER rendezvouses: each device keys the store + wire req by its LOCAL install slug — G-8 fetch asks the peer for a repo name the peer doesn't have",
      "summary": "Live-caught on the P-302 Leg A rig (WI-3496, 2026-07-17 ~04:45Z), the first genuine cross-machine bootstrap ever attempted.\n\nEVIDENCE: tower created its store as (potHomeSlug='hello-world-3-pot', repoKey='hello-world-3' — ITS local member install slug); the VM joined the same pot but its local install slug for the same repo is 'hello-world', so runBootstrapLeg dials the tower and sends wire req { repoKey:'hello-world' } (serve-wiring.ts wire slot 0 carries the repoKey literally); the tower's handleReq resolves hiveGitRepoPath('hello-world-3-pot','hello-world') → no such store. Proven by experiment: symlinking hello-world.git → hello-world-3.git on the tower is what let the fetch proceed. Same defect in runOwnHeadPublishLeg/announce (repoKey = local slug everywhere in git-sync-action.ts): two devices publish the SAME logical repo under DIFFERENT (potHomeSlug, repoKey) stores and announce refs for repo keys peers can't correlate.\n\nROOT CAUSE (design, WI-5146's sibling): p2p-git-research G-1..G-8 never pinned a CANONICAL cross-machine repo key. The install slug is machine-local (join-pot derives it from the local registry — tower got 'hello-world-3', VM got 'hello-world' for octocat/Hello-World).\n\nFIX DIRECTION: derive the wire+store repoKey from a federated identity both sides share — the memberLink's github repo_id (e.g. 'gh-1296269') or the hive-directory member slug — with the local slug kept only as a registry-side alias; migrate hiveGitRepoPath callers in git-sync-action (own-head, bootstrap, announce, integrator, worktree-bridge) + serve-wiring resolution together, in one breaking change (alpha: no compat shim). Scope-repos already solved this with scope: wire keys (scope-repo.ts) — extend the same idea to member repos.\n\nBLOCKS real-world G-8 for any two devices whose install slugs differ (i.e. nearly always — slug collisions/dedup make them differ even for the same repo URL).",

    {
      "id": "WI-5395",
      "title": "Hive-git integrator election is not repo-aware: a member elected authority for a repo it has no bare store for stalls that repo hive-wide (silently)",
      "summary": "FOUND 2026-07-18 (su-71c69) while baselining the P-402 soak on the bridged canary. This is the ROOT CAUSE behind the canary's ~22h silent GitHub-origin freeze.\n\n## The defect\n`lockAuthorityForHive(potSlug)` elects ONE integrator per HIVE (HRW over live presence). But integration is per (hive, REPO), and a hive binds several repos. A member machine can legitimately hold bare stores for only SOME of them. When the elected authority does not hold a given repo's store, that repo is never integrated by anyone:\n  - the authority cannot (no store, and in this case no git-sync routine for the install either);\n  - every other member correctly declines at `if (!authority.isSelf) return;` (git-sync-action.ts, runIntegratorLeg).\nCanonical `refs/hive/staging` for that repo therefore never advances. Downstream, the GitHub bridge has nothing new to egress, so origin silently freezes.\n\n## Evidence (live, this session)\n- Hive `hello-world-3-pot`, mode `bridged` (pot_settings, since 2026-07-17 19:52).\n- In-process probe of the real election: `lockAuthorityForHive('hello-world-3-pot')` -> `{isSelf:false, liveCount:2, peer: Avis-iMac Lm1ABoMRKVoo...}`. The MAC holds the lease.\n- The mac's `~/.papercusp/pot-git/hello-world-3-pot/` holds ONLY `hello-world-3.git` and `hello-world.git` — there is NO `hello-world-3-pot.git`.\n- The mac's `harness_shared.routines` has `system:git-sync` rows for ONLY `hello-world` and `papercusp` — no install/binding for `hello-world-3-pot` at all, so no tick ever runs its bootstrap/integrator legs there.\n- The tower HAS the store + routine, and correctly declines as non-authority.\n- Live consequence: wrote a heartbeat -> git-sync committed d367c05a -> own_head_publish advanced the tower's member namespace. Canonical stayed pinned at 301d0687 across further ticks. Bridge read `lag unpushed=1`.\n\n## Why it was invisible\n`metadata.integrator` is written ONLY on a successful announcement, and every early return in runIntegratorLeg was a bare `return`. So \"authority elsewhere and incapable\" was byte-identical to \"nothing to integrate\". Partially addressed by the diagnostics landed under WI-5394 (`metadata.integrator_status` now records `not_authority` WITH the lease holder, plus a new `authority_without_store` decline that logs loudly) — that makes it DIAGNOSABLE but does not fix it.\n\n## Recommended fix (needs a design call — deliberately NOT hand-rolled under release pressure)\nConstrain election to CAPABLE members: exclude from the candidate set any peer that does not hold the repo's bare store. `lockAuthorityForHive` already threads an `excluded` set (`evictionExclusions`) into both `selectAuthorityRendezvous` and `selectAuthorityFromRows`, so the seam exists. The blocker is that per-repo store capability is NOT advertised today — presence rows carry no repo inventory, so a machine cannot locally determine a peer's capability. That needs a capability field in presence/gossip, which is a real feature with a federation-format implication, not a patch.\n\nInterim alternatives if a fix is needed sooner: (a) propagate hive repo bindings to every member so all members hold every bound repo (makes election-capability moot, but forces stores onto machines that may not want them); (b) pin integration of a hive-home's own self_repo to its home machine.\n\n## Blast radius\nAny bridged/p2p hive with heterogeneous repo bindings across members. Not a data-corruption risk (nothing is force-pushed; refs simply stop advancing) — but it is SILENT, and it stalls the GitHub bridge, which is the release-facing surface. Blocks a meaningful P-402 soak on the affected repo.",

    {
      "id": "WI-5441",
      "title": "Boot-window capture hole: rows written between the backfill sweep stamping backfill_done:&lt;table&gt; and the capture trigger becoming effective NEVER federate (silent permanent loss) — reproduces as the item-assignments backfill red on every live-fed-gate run",
      "summary": "DEMONSTRATED LIVE with timestamps on the 214246 local lane pair (frame B = joiner, PG :18632, still running at filing time):\n\n- B backfill marker `backfill_done:plan_item_assignments` (harness hello-world) stamped **21:54:17**.\n- B row `plan-mx-seed:P-001` (the backfill probe) created **21:54:18.217** — ONE SECOND AFTER the marker, origin='local'.\n- B `substrate_outbox` for plan_item_assignments contains ONLY `plan-mx-ba:P-002` (21:55:58, the later incremental probe). The seed row has NO outbox entry, ever.\n\nSo the seed row fell into a hole: too LATE for the boot sweep (per-table marker already stamped done → never re-swept, by design since WI-971 gap 2), and NOT captured by the trigger. Net effect: a local write is silently and permanently non-federating, with no error and no stall-detector fire (the row simply never enters the outbox).\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE TEST: this is not only a probe-timing artifact. Any real local write landing in that same boot window is silently lost to peers — directly relevant to shared-pot plan/work-item editing reliability (owner asked about exactly this). The window is small but it is a correctness hole, not a latency issue.\n\nSUB-MECHANISM NOT YET PINNED (two candidates, needs one more step):\n(a) the capture trigger was not yet attached at 21:54:18 (fresh install — migrations create triggers during the same boot the sweep runs in), or\n(b) a guard inside capture_substrate_outbox no-ops the write while the harness is not yet federation-online. Read of capture_substrate_outbox shows an echo-loop guard (skips origin<>'local') but no obvious online guard in the first ~40 lines — so (a) is currently the stronger candidate. Confirm by comparing trigger creation time (pg_trigger/migration apply log) against the row's created_at on a fresh frame.\n\nDISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE (rules out the classes already fixed): NOT the WI-5399 workspace mis-stamp class (that is fixed; every other table's backfill AND every incremental leg, both directions, PASS on this run). NOT WI-971 gap 1 (plan_item_assignments IS registered in BACKFILL_TARGETS since 2026-07-17) and NOT the legacy-marker path (LEGACY_MARKER_TABLES correctly excludes it). NOT WI-5167 (different table, feature_audit_consolidated).\n\nREPRODUCTION: it is the sole remaining content-matrix red on live-fed-gate runs 200519 AND 214246 (`item-assignments backfill NEVER crossed (src outbox=0/1)` + backfill-late 0/2), i.e. reproduces across consecutive fully fix-bearing runs.\n\nLIKELY FIX DIRECTIONS (design needed, do not just widen the sweep): order boot so the capture trigger is provably effective BEFORE the sweep stamps its marker (close the window), and/or have the sweep stamp its marker only after capture is live, and/or a post-online reconciliation pass that enqueues any local-origin row with no corresponding outbox history. A pure \"re-run the sweep later\" patch re-opens the WI-971 gap-2 idempotency problem, so it is not the answer on its own.",

      "id": "WI-5446",
      "title": "Cross-machine seat-offers do not federate between tower and iMac: donor delegate succeeds locally but the offer never reaches the spender; zero p2p receipts on BOTH machines for the papercusp pot",
      "summary": "This is the actual blocker behind WI-5410 / P-011 (live two-machine seat-pool verify). It is NOT a cooperation or staffing problem — it is a federation delivery gap, and it is reproducible.\n\nWhat I did (2026-07-19 ~02:45-02:52Z), as pot-seat-pools leader:\n1. Staged the drill CORRECTLY for the first time: fired the donor-side delegation ON THE IMAC (via ssh 172.31.44.2 -> its local MCP door at 127.0.0.1:3070), not on the tower. It succeeded: `{ok:true, action:'set', allotment:{fleetSlug:'pot-seat-pools', resourceKind:'agent_slot', resourceRef:'sonnet:medium:AUTO', quantity:1, status:'active', createdByGithubUserId:1567022}}`. Note `hive:'papercusp'` WAS passed, so EI-16667's silent-skip-on-ambiguous-hive does not apply here.\n2. Fired `fleet:request_remote_spawn {fleet:'pot-seat-pools', plan:'pot-seat-pools-prose-ux-2026-07-18', count:1, hive:'papercusp'}` from the tower, repeatedly over the following ~7 minutes.\n\nEvery attempt refused with: \"seat-offer seat-ec799e00fa1c9725 is this machine's OWN delegation\".\n\nWhy that single refusal is conclusive. Read `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/request-remote-spawn.ts` around lines 157-169: when the fleet has MORE than one open seat-offer the tool refuses with \"fleet '<slug>' has N open seat-offers — pass publisher + offer to pick one\", and it only auto-selects when `seatOffers.length === 1`. It auto-selected. Therefore the tower can see exactly ONE seat-offer for this fleet — its own. The iMac's offer is absent, not merely deprioritized or sorted behind it.\n\nCorroborating evidence: `p2p:trace {pot:'papercusp'}` returns `receipts: []` and `refusedOpCounters: []` on BOTH machines, and `SELECT ... FROM harness_shared.p2p_receipts WHERE created_at > now() - interval '2 hours'` returns zero rows on the tower. There is no P2P traffic for this pot in either direction — not refused traffic, no traffic.\n\nSo the seat-offer publish is succeeding locally on the donor and never being delivered to the peer. Suspect areas: whether the two operators are actually peered on the papercusp hive home log, and whether a repo-less hive home requires the gh-authed announce + joiner restart described in the existing memory on the WI-560 fed-a/fed-b rig (a joiner only peers a HOME its operator booted at STARTUP). Worth checking that both operators booted the papercusp hive home before concluding the publish path itself is broken.\n\nImpact: no pot-scoped or fleet-scoped seat donation can ever be spent across machines while this holds, which makes the entire feature unverifiable live even though its logic is unit- and integration-green (12 of 14 items on pot-seat-pools-prose-ux-2026-07-18).\n\nRepro: delegate an agent_slot from machine A naming the hive; from machine B call fleet:request_remote_spawn for the same fleet+hive; observe B never sees A's offer, and p2p:trace stays empty on both.",

      "id": "WI-5457",
      "title": "Timeout-killed bees never trigger fleet:supervise's restart_strategy — completeSpawn doesn't auto-report a timedOut death for restart",
      "summary": "Split off from EI-361 (resolved 2026-07-19). EI-361 reported 3 compounding failures for the 2026-06-11 timeout-SIGTERM incident: (1) fleet:spawn/cup:spawn missing a per-spawn timeoutMs override, (2) the nursery row recording an empty error_message on a timeout kill (indistinguishable from a crash), (3) restart_strategy one_for_one not restarting the killed bee.\n\n(1) was already fixed prior to this session via EI-350 (cup/spawn.ts exposes `timeoutMs`, threaded through operator-spawn.ts's SpawnInput → spawnInvokeOnceWithFallback). The default PAPERCUSP_DBOS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MS was also already raised from 600_000ms to 2_700_000ms (45min) per orchestrator-runner.ts's D-010 comment. (2) was fixed this session: operator-spawn.ts's completeSpawn call now checks `r.timedOut` (already returned by runChild/spawnInvokeOnceWithFallback but previously ignored) and writes an explicit `invoke timeout after <N>ms — SIGTERM'd (EI-361)` errorMessage instead of falling back to empty stderr → null.\n\n(3) remains OPEN and is the reason for this follow-up: `fleet:supervise` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/supervise.ts) implements the one_for_one/one_for_all/rest_for_one restart-intensity logic, but it is a TOOL that must be explicitly CALLED with the crashed spawn_id(s) — nothing in operator-spawn.ts's completeSpawn path (or elsewhere) automatically invokes it when a spawn finishes with status='failed'/timedOut:true. So a timeout-killed bee simply sits dead unless some external caller (a parent agent, a watchdog) happens to notice and call fleet:supervise itself.\n\nThis is a genuine supervision-POLICY decision (should EVERY failed spawn auto-trigger its restart strategy? only timeout deaths? is there a risk of restart storms/loops if done unconditionally from completeSpawn?) that touches the protected packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/** neighborhood's failure-handling semantics — deliberately left to a human/architectural call rather than being folded into EI-361's fix, per that item's own D-003 human-gate triage. Investigate whether completeSpawn (or a watchdog tick) should call fleet:supervise-equivalent logic automatically on a timedOut/failed terminal status, respecting each spawn's configured restart_strategy and restart-intensity budget.",

      "id": "WI-5501",
      "title": "Loop engine: leader-wake session-limit/auth-wall deaths should attempt account failover via the inference gateway (EI-13818 item (b), deferred)",
      "summary": "Follow-up to EI-13818 (resolved). EI-13818 fixed (a) misclassification — classifyResumeTurnExit now correctly detects a session-limit/auth-wall wedge instead of treating exit-0 as always-success (so the failure-streak circuit now opens correctly) — and (c) alerting — loop-turn-outcome.ts now raises a debounced captureImprovement + overwatch-wake the first time a loop dies on a surfaceToUser wedge class.\n\nItem (b) from the original ask was explicitly deferred as \"a substantially larger, separate undertaking\": when a loop-driving leader/agent session's wake dies on a detected session-limit or org-auth-wall wedge (classifyWedgeText in session-end-reason.ts), the loop engine should attempt ACCOUNT FAILOVER via the inference gateway (re-arm the next wake routed through a different, healthy account/pool) instead of only backing off and re-firing into the same wall / alerting a human. Today (a)+(c) mean the failure is loud and the retry cadence backs off correctly, but a leader loop pinned to (or auto-routed onto) an exhausted account still has no automatic path to a working account short of an owner/operator manually re-pinning it.\n\nScope for whoever picks this up: thread a failover hook through loop:arm's account resolution (see the `account` routing knobs — pool id / `auto` / `default` — documented in the su playbook's spawn-announcement section) so a wedge-classified death can request the gateway's next-best account on the NEXT fire, and surface which account it failed over to in the loop's carry-note / checkpoint so a human auditing the loop can see the substitution happened. Coordinate with whoever owns the inference-gateway account-pool code (gateway auto-routing / `dev:rate_governor_status` area) before implementing — this crosses the loop-engine / gateway boundary EI-13818 deliberately stayed out of.\n\nFiled while reconciling a stale/lagged self-compaction carry injection that referenced EI-13818 as still in-flight (it was actually already resolved) — closing the loose end its own completion note called out (terminalCompletionRef: \"...should be filed as its own follow-up bug referencing EI-13818\").",
      "kind": "bug",
      "state": "open",
      "classification": "retain-other-unresolved",
      "recommendation": "retain-park",
      "basis": "No D-018-authorized release proof is present; retain conservatively.",
      "fullReason": "feature/design-shaped (new account concept + spawn-path + gateway coordination), not a drain-lane bug — needs a plan, not a single-session fix; see comment",
