      "title": "replication_soak: WI-183-class zombie-connection recovery still misses 90s SLA on fresh, correctly-built .deb (collision-storm + build-staleness both ruled out)",
      "summary": "Follow-up from WI-5634 (now closed as diagnostic-complete). A clean verification run of `bash bin/local-matrix.sh --only=replication_soak` on a FRESH, explicitly-correct build (Papercusp Server_0.0.12_amd64.deb, mtime 06:25 EDT 2026-07-20, has the grace-ms fix; confirmed no staleness WARN) still failed 1 of 5 cycles (2 of 10 directional legs would have been the worry; only cycle 2 A→B actually failed):\n\n  ✗ cycle 2 A→B FAIL: F-RLSOAK-1784545384-2-AM did not land on member within 90s (WI-183 zombie-connection class) — loadavg at failure: a=86.03 b=86.03 (vs ~55-81 on passing cycles)\n  Cycles 1, 3, 4, 5 and the B→A leg of cycle 2 all passed comfortably inside the 90s SLA (6-68s).\n\nThis rules out BOTH confounds already investigated:\n  - Build staleness: WI-5634 caught a first attempt that silently used a stale pre-fix .deb (EI-18160721229588594); this run used the confirmed-fresh artifact.\n  - Collision-storm (WI-5631's fix): WI-5634's own two prior runs already disconfirmed this as the cause even with the collision storm present or fully eliminated.\n\nDetector correctness confirmed: WI-1840's replication_stalled/replication_frozen detector correctly fired in both frames' serve.log during the failure window (`✓ detector fire-path pin` in the scenario's own self-check) — NOT a detector-blind regression.\n\nEvidence banked at /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/live-fed-gate/triage/{scn.replication_soak,serve-a,serve-b,load}-070954.* (this run, stamp=070954). Serve logs show the classic WI-183 signature repeatedly across the run: `replication_stalled (connected_never_replicated)` / `(no_replicator)` / `replication_frozen (frozen) ... no progress for 31s`, interleaved with `[event-loop-lag] high loop delay — host is CPU-bound` bursts (maxMs up to ~1047ms) and one `zombie window entered after 'boot timeout after 30000ms'` on frame b. Most of these self-recover within the SLA via `repair-on-detect: re-attached replica session ... after Ns swarm-connected-but-dead` (typically 15-20s); cycle 2's A→B leg is the one where recovery didn't complete before the 90s window closed.\n\nNOTE: WI-183 itself is marked state=done, but its closing checkpoint documents a DIFFERENT, inconclusive forensic thread (git-export hydrate.ts provenance theory, never confirmed) — it was not actually resolved with a landed fix; this is the SAME symptom class recurring under matrix-rig conditions. Treat this item as the live tracking issue for the zombie-connection-recovery-exceeds-SLA problem; WI-183 is prior art/context, not a landed fix to re-verify against.\n\nNEXT STEPS (from WI-5634): root-cause why the zombie-connection repair path (`repair-exhausted: forcing topic rejoin` → `repair-on-detect: re-attached replica session`) occasionally takes >90s instead of the usual 15-20s. Candidates to rule in/out with fresh evidence: (a) genuine host-CPU contention on the SLA-missing leg specifically (loadavg was highest — 86 — at the one failure, vs 55-81 on passes, so this is plausible but not yet proven causal on a 128-core box); (b) a bounded-retry/backoff ceiling in the repair path that can exceed 90s in the worst case even when healthy; (c) run-to-run variance in an inherently racy detect→repair→reattach cycle. A useful next experiment: instrument/log the repair attempt timestamps relative to the restart, and run several more soak passes to see if failure correlates with loadavg crossing some threshold.",

      "id": "WI-5673",
      "title": "live-federation-gate content-matrix: incr-B→A intermittently NEVER crosses for the FIRST 4/10 TYPES-list entries (features/conversations/messages/threads) — likely a post-join warm-up-latency window on B's outbound path, NOT a capture miss (misdiagnosed initially)",
      "summary": "Gate run /tmp/live-fed-gate-20260720-153839 (15:38 EDT, dirty=0 clean build, head=2f68428826). BACKFILL: all 10 types PASS. INCREMENTAL A→B: all 10 types PASS. INCREMENTAL B→A: features/conversations/messages/threads FAIL \"NEVER crossed (src outbox=0/1)\" — B's own write for these 4 types never even entered B's outbox (0 of 1 captured, not a delivery/apply-side miss). The other 6 types (thread-posts/plans/plan-parts/item-assignments/hive-settings/hive-members) B→A all PASS.\n\nNotably item-assignments B→A now PASSES cleanly (2nd consecutive clean run for that leg — corroborates WI-5667's fix for WI-5666's symptom).\n\nKEY EVIDENCE this is NON-DETERMINISTIC / a race, not a fresh code regression: the immediately-prior gate run (/tmp/live-fed-gate-20260720-143812, 14:44 EDT) used build head=ab75e58a86, and this run's head=2f68428826 — but `git diff ab75e58a86 2f68428826 -- libs/papercusp` is EMPTY (identical submodule pin, i.e. byte-identical server code). That prior run's INCREMENTAL B→A leg was a FULL PASS on all 10 types. So the EXACT SAME CODE produced a full B→A pass in one run and a 4/10 B→A capture-miss in the very next run — this is not explained by any commit between the two runs (superproject diff only touches unrelated files: gym/account-workspace, loop-fire, github-bridge escalation doc, pot-git storage — nothing on the outbox/projection/federation path).\n\nHost was under heavy load at capture time (loadavg 46.62/45.59/49.75 per `uptime`, consistent with WI-5672's host-contention hypothesis for the local-matrix roster-convergence failures on this same run's local-matrix leg). Working hypothesis: B's outbox-capture trigger/write path for these 4 specific content types is timing/scheduling-sensitive under contention (e.g. a captured-but-not-yet-flushed write racing the smoke script's probe-and-declare-outbox=0 check), OR there's a narrower structural gap specific to features/conversations/messages/threads (vs. the 6 that always pass) worth checking independently of load.\n\nThis run's OVERALL content-matrix verdict is INCOMPLETE, so it does NOT qualify as a P-402 first-green candidate on its own (blocks WI-5137).\n\nNot yet live-traced (PAPERCUSP_A003_TRACE=1) — the pair for this run is left running for Brief E/G per its own convention (ports in ~/.papercusp-lane-a-fed/instances.env), so a live psql/trace pass is possible without a fresh run if picked up soon.\n\nNext steps for whoever picks this up: (1) live DB check on B's outbox table for these 4 types' captured-but-undrained rows (mirrors the WI-5666 investigation pattern) — is the op captured at all, or does drain fail post-capture; (2) check whether this 4-type set shares a projection/outbox-wiring code path distinct from the 6 passing types; (3) re-run under lower host load to test the contention hypothesis directly; (4) cross-reference WI-5672 (same run's local-matrix roster-convergence failures) — if both symptoms clear together on a quiet-host re-run, that's strong evidence for one shared host-contention root cause rather than two separate bugs.\n\nBlocks: WI-5137 (P-402 gate-first-green).",

      "id": "WI-5680",
      "title": "REGRESSION on WI-5355 (already \"done\"): topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts 2/7 tests failing deterministically — socket.destroyed:true when expected false",
      "summary": "## What\n\nFound during an unrelated `npm run test:affected` full regression sweep (verifying EI-52's fix). `lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts` fails 2 of its 7 tests deterministically — reproduced twice (the affected-tests runner's own flake-absorbing fresh-process re-run hit the identical 2 failures both times), and the test uses `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` (fake timers), so this is not a wall-clock/host-load flake — it's a deterministic logic mismatch:\n\n```\nFAIL lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts > createTopicGossip severed-link escalation ladder (EI-13317) > WI-5355: never evicts a socket still paired on a DIFFERENT healthy topic\nAssertionError: expected true to be false\n  expect(socket.destroyed).toBe(false); // must survive — still serving TOPIC2\n  → received true (the socket WAS destroyed)\n\nFAIL lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts > WI-5355 iteration 3: re-attempts CHANNEL-level pairing on a surviving socket after the forced leave+rejoin\nAssertionError: expected true to be false\n  expect(socket.destroyed).toBe(false); // survives — still serving the OTHER topic\n  → received true\n```\n\nThe other 5 tests in the same file (including the adjacent \"WI-5355: evicts a zombie socket... before rejoining on escalation\" case) PASS — so this isn't a suite-wide setup issue, it's specific to the \"socket paired on a different healthy topic must survive severed-link escalation on THIS topic\" invariant.\n\n## Why this is a regression, not new\n\n`WI-5355` (title: \"Hive-directory topic pairing... never re-completes after a forced leave+rejoin\") is already marked **`done`** in the tracker, with completion evidence citing a live 2-machine rig fix (\"Protomux channel re-invoke on surviving deduped sockets, topic-gossip.ts\") that specifically targeted **not evicting a socket still serving a different healthy topic** during the severed-link escalation/forced-rejoin path — which is EXACTLY what these 2 unit tests assert and are now failing. So either:\n- a later edit to `topic-gossip.ts` (or its escalation ladder) regressed the fix, or\n- the live-rig verification that closed WI-5355 never had unit-test coverage keeping it green (the unit test may have been failing for a while unnoticed — this sweep is the first time I've seen it).\n\n## Scope note\n\nUnrelated to my own task (EI-52, `*.integration.test.ts` reachability hardening in `su-locks-http-mcp`/`power-user-e2e`/`mint-roundtrip`/`ui-control`) and to files I touched — filing rather than fixing, since it's a different subsystem (hyperbee p2p/DHT discovery) that deserves an owner familiar with that escalation ladder, not a drive-by fix from an unrelated task.\n\n## Repro\n\n```\nnpm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts\n```\n(2/7 fail, reproduced twice via fresh-process re-run, 2026-07-20)\n\n## Cross-refs\n\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip.ts`\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/topic-gossip-severed-link-escalation.test.ts`\n- WI-5355 (marked done; this looks like its regression)",

This is a SEPARATE concern from WI-971/WI-5628 (WI-5775's actual scope, which PASSED) — filing distinctly per the script's own comment (\"a separate concern per WI-280/WI-1666... worth confirming\").\n\nSYMPTOM: after `pot:ban_member { pot, githubUserId: B, revoke: false }` (policy-only ban — B stays admitted, NOT revoked) + a 3s settle sleep, B writes F-AKBAN and it DOES land on A:\n  AK ban (B's op DROPPED on A, EN-4): FAIL (probe=1 hello-world A_count=1)\ni.e. banprobe first-word=1 (federated/materialized) and akban_a=1 (row present) — the op should have been DROPPED, per policy-admission.ts's `decidePolicyOp` EN-4 ban rule (author's bannedGithubIds membership → `policy_banned`, admit:false).\n\nFull run log: /tmp/wi5775-fromrepo-gateflags.log (grep \"AK ban\\|AK0\\|AK unban\").       "id": "WI-5861",
      "title": "P-409 follow-up: find the actual post-connection timer behind the ~13.0s p2p socket death (UDX-native retransmission or dht-rpc keepalive, not hyperdht handshake)",
      "summary": "Follow-up to WI-5837 (done). WI-5837 decisively ruled out all 4 named hyperdht handshake-layer constants (HANDSHAKE_INITIAL_TIMEOUT, HANDSHAKE_CLEAR_WAIT, passiveConnectTimeout, relayTimeout) as the cause of the ~13.0s p2p socket death seen in the live federation rig (a->b join never converges, 92s/420s timeout, 0 membership rows).\n\nKEY FINDING FROM WI-5837: the ageMs measurement (packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/swarm.ts:1188-1220, the 'swarm-churn close' log) starts INSIDE hyperswarm's 'connection' event handler, which only fires AFTER the DHT handshake already succeeded (hyperswarm/index.js conn.on('open') -> emit('connection'), :235-244 client / :403 server). So the real ~13s timer that kills an ESTABLISHED connection must live at a POST-connection layer -- none of WI-5837's 4 candidates could structurally have been it.\n\nLEADS TO INVESTIGATE (untested):\n1. UDX-native's own retransmission-exhaustion (native C binding, not JS source in node_modules -- rtoCount/retransmits counters ARE exposed at node_modules/udx-native/lib/stream.js:101-106; could instrument these at the socket 'close' event to see if rtoCount saturates right before the ~13s death, or look for the native default RTO/max-retransmit constant in libudx's actual source).\n2. dht-rpc's per-request keepalive/timeout (node_modules/dht-rpc/lib/io.js:458 references a per-request `this.timeout`; hyperswarm calls existing.sendKeepAlive() on duplicate-connection handling, packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/swarm.ts:364 -- worth checking whether there's a companion \"keepalive not acked\" timeout that would explain a fixed ~13s established-connection death).\n3. The error string precededByError:'connection timed out' (182x in one run's banked log) is NOT found anywhere in the JS source of hyperdht/hyperswarm/@hyperswarm/secret-stream/udx-native/dht-rpc (all searched) -- it is almost certainly emitted by the native udx binding. Locating/instrumenting that would directly confirm or refute the UDX-retransmission-timeout hypothesis.\n\nThis is still fully consistent with the standing NAT-hairpin theory (mem0 2bf014f5, packet-proven 2026-06-24: fed-a/fed-b share NAT egress IP 10.31.1.15) -- an established connection whose packets silently vanish post-handshake would be killed by whichever post-connection liveness/retransmission timer exists, at a fixed deterministic offset (explains the observed 9ms ageMs spread). Confirming the exact mechanism would let the team distinguish \"durable fix = make bootstrap/relay actually route between co-NATed peers\" from any other actionable option.\n\nEvidence/banked logs from WI-5837 (all 4 candidate runs + baseline): /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/live-fed-gate/triage/serve-{a,b}-{224842,230320,230923,231427}.log",

      "title": "live-federation-gate revocation_kcut: post-ban content LEAK — F-RV-POST reached banned member B after the ban (cut-off failed)",
      "summary": "Gate run /tmp/live-fed-gate-20260726-074510 (HEAD=bbb4404626, real 2-frame containerized rig, local-matrix leg, hourly-timer-fired) hit revocation_kcut (order 90, b3-revocation.sh scn_revocation_kcut) with:\n\n  ✗ FAIL revocation_kcut (rc=1) — revocation: LEAK — F-RV-POST-m1785067454 reached banned member B after the ban (cut-off failed)\n\nThis is the OPPOSITE symptom from the historically-documented revocation_kcut baseline FAIL (EI-15535, done: \"owner→B pre-ban federation broken\") — that was pre-ban content NOT reaching B. This is POST-ban content (F-RV-POST, a feature created after the ban) INCORRECTLY reaching the banned member B — a real security-relevant cut-off leak, not a false negative.\n\nNot the known cascade case either: papercusp-desktop/bin/live-federation-gate.sh's revocation_kcut CASCADE CARVE-OUT (WI-5616) only tolerates a revocation_kcut FAIL when replication_soak ALSO failed in the same run (attributed to frame-CPU starvation). In THIS run replication_soak PASSED cleanly (5/5 kill-restart cycles, detector quiet), so this is an ISOLATED, non-starvation revocation_kcut FAIL — not covered by any existing downgrade/tolerance path. It did NOT stop local-matrix from otherwise completing (15/16 scenarios passed) but the gate's overall verdict should be RED on this leg.\n\nEvidence banked at /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/live-fed-gate/triage/, stamp 081054-revocation_kcut (and a near-duplicate stamp 081136 ~40s later, same message — likely the scenario's own retry/recheck before declaring FAIL): scn.revocation_kcut-081054-revocation_kcut.log (98 bytes, just the one-line verdict), serve-a-081054-revocation_kcut.log + serve-b-081054-revocation_kcut.log (~1.1MB each, full sidecar logs for both frames across the whole matrix run — the revocation/K-cut mechanics will be in the tail).\n\nFor contrast: two PRIOR runs from 2026-07-25 (stamps 182058, 191900) banked \"revocation + K-cut OK — B federated pre-ban, then after the ban B stopped receiving post-ban content (pre-ban stayed readable)\" — i.e. the SAME scenario passed cleanly less than a day earlier on presumably-older builds. Whether this is a genuine regression introduced between those builds and HEAD=bbb4404626, or an intermittent/load-sensitive race in the K-cut enforcement path, is not yet determined — next step is diffing what changed and/or re-running --only=revocation_kcut in isolation to check reproducibility.\n\nScenario source: papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/scenarios/b3-revocation.sh (scn_revocation_kcut, matrix_register revocation_kcut 90).       "id": "WI-6046",
      "title": "live-federation-gate: the failing scenarios harden their MEASUREMENTS but not their SETUP — b9-attestation.sh strips B's attestation with errors swallowed (line 183), so a disturbed frame A silently converts a real test into a FALSE FAIL",
      "summary": "MECHANISM FOUND — this supersedes the item's original \"no settle barrier after the soak\" framing, which was a symptom-level guess built partly on a miscount (see checkpoint). Claimed by fleet leader su-e3b21216. WI-6043 (the revocation leak) stays su-48ed7aaf's.\n\n=== THE DEFECT ===\n`bin/lib/scenarios/b9-attestation.sh` scores its leg on a counter that only bumps if its SETUP mutation actually applied — and that mutation swallows every error:\n\n  183:  drv_psql a \"UPDATE harness_shared.pot_members SET device_attestations='[]'::jsonb\n                    WHERE pot_home_slug='$RIG_HIVE_ID' AND github_user_id=$b_gh_id;\" >/dev/null 2>&1\n\nNo rc check. No read-back. If frame a's PG is unavailable or degraded when this runs, the strip silently no-ops, B's device still resolves to a member, A never refuses with `identity_unresolved`, and the leg then fails at line 201 reporting EXACTLY the signature we observed in run 083840:\n\n  FAIL — identity_unresolved 0→0, row-on-a=0, all reasons: receipt-apply:responder_mismatch=5\n\nThat is not \"A failed to refuse an unattested device\". It is \"the device was never made unattested, so there was nothing to refuse\" — a FALSE FAIL.\n\nSame unguarded shape at lines 102, 123 and 187 (the pending-join insert, the LEG3 receipt insert, and this leg's own probe receipt). Four setup mutations, zero verified.\n\n=== WHY THIS IS PARTICULARLY SHARP HERE ===\nThe file's authors hardened the MEASUREMENTS with real care and documented why:\n- WI-5779 scoped the assert to the EXACT reason `receipt-apply:identity_unresolved`, because a loose `LIKE 'receipt-apply:%'` total could go true from a stray responder_mismatch re-bump — \"a guaranteed-nonzero baseline plus an unrelated further bump is a false PASS\".\n- WI-5788 made an UNMEASURED baseline a hard FAIL rather than coercing to 0 (line 179), and did the same for the post-probe read (line 198), explicitly noting this leg \"runs LAST (order 91) after four invasive scenarios ... that can leave frame a briefly unreachable\".\n\nSo the risk of a disturbed frame a was KNOWN and defended against — on the read path only. The write path that establishes the test's precondition was left completely unverified. The guard and the hole sit twelve lines apart.\n\n=== THE UPSTREAM DISTURBANCE IS REAL ===\nFrame a took 3 SIGTERMs (13:02:11.121Z / 13:02:45.749Z / 13:03:07.937Z — 3 events, double-logged as 6 lines), and su-48ed7aaf documented the resulting PG \"administrator command\"/\"shutting down\" cascade. attestation banked its FAIL at 13:06:23Z, i.e. squarely in the recovery window. What SENT those SIGTERMs is still open (not the staging-api restart at 13:03:41Z — that postdates all three; not papercup-dev-api, last started 12:33:48Z).\n\n=== SCOPE: THIS EXPLAINS ATTESTATION, NOT REVOCATION ===\n`b3-revocation.sh` does NOT carry the swallowed-error pattern — checked. revocation_kcut's failure remains WI-6043's epoch-never-advances problem. But the two share ONE ROOT CLASS through different sites: **a setup action assumed to have taken effect because the call returned.**\n- attestation: an UPDATE whose errors go to /dev/null.\n- revocation: `rig_arm_hive_rekey` (bin/lib/deb-hetzner-rig.sh:930) POSTs to /api/flags/set and only `fed_log`s the response string — it never asserts the flag resolved true. The sidecar cannot even read that write (EI-18712738949489735), so the arming is a no-op that reports success.\n\nThat is the same bug wearing two costumes, and it is why both post-soak scenarios are unreliable.\n\n=== FIX (mine) ===\n1. Verify the attestation strip: read `device_attestations` back after line 183 and hard-FAIL if it is not empty — matching the treatment the read path already gets. Same for the pending-join and receipt inserts (assert the row exists where it should).\n2. Make `drv_psql` mutations non-silent by default in scenario setup, so a new scenario cannot inherit this hole.\n3. Generalize: any rig setup step must READ BACK its effect, never trust the call's return. Same rule already asserted for flags (fact `rig-sidecar-ignores-runtime-flag-overrides`).\n4. THEN reconsider ordering/settle-barrier work — with setup verified, a disturbed frame produces an honest ERROR instead of a false FAIL, which is most of the value. The settle barrier is a nice-to-have after that, not before.\n\n=== FALSIFIER ===\nIf the strip DID apply in run 083840, this is wrong. Check frame a's `pot_members.device_attestations` for B's github_user_id in the banked state, or re-run the leg with the read-back added and see whether it FAILs at setup rather than at scoring.\n\n=== CAUTION ===\nFilesystem/gate timestamps on this box are LOCAL = UTC-4 and read 4h early vs coord/WI timestamps (fact `gate-artifact-timestamps-are-local-utc-minus-4`). Two agents mislabelled runs from this today. Use `git merge-base --is-ancestor` + provenance `dirty=` for build ordering — timezone-free.",

      "id": "WI-6076",
      "title": "Shared peer socket + per-harness Corestores: the 2nd store's replicate() clobbers the 1st's protomux hypercore/alpha pairing, making its COLD cores permanently unservable (proven, controlled unit repro)",
      "summary": "PROVEN WITH CONTROLS (packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/shared-socket-multi-corestore-clobber.test.ts, 4/4 green).\n\nTHE DEFECT\n`store.replicate(stream)` -> hypercore/index.js:181 registers the lazy serve callback via `noiseStream.userData.pair({ protocol: 'hypercore/alpha' }, ondiscoverykey)`. protomux `pair()` is `this._notify.set(toKey(protocol,id), notify)` (protomux/index.js:407) — a Map SET, ONE slot per protocol, last writer wins. So when a SECOND corestore replicates the SAME socket, it silently overwrites the first store's `_attachMaybe`. Every core belonging to the losing store that is NOT already open becomes structurally unservable on that connection — while the socket stays fully handshaken and live.\n\nTHIS IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN-TREE, AND HONOURED ONLY FOR THE SCOPED STORE. scope-cores.ts:13-15 (\"verified against corestore 7.9.2 / hypercore 11 / protomux source\"): \"protomux pair() is a Map SET keyed (protocol,id): a second corestore's replicate() on the same stream CLOBBERS the first's hypercore/alpha pairing — so the scoped store must never replicate() a shared socket.\" The MAIN path violates the same invariant.\n\nTHE PRODUCTION TOPOLOGY THAT TRIPS IT (all three in tree today)\n1. ONE process-wide Hyperswarm (`_sharedSwarm`, swarm.ts:3163), so ONE peer socket is muxed across EVERY harness sharing that peer — \"the live-fed rig runs hello-world-pot + hello-world + papercusp over a single connection\" (swarm.ts:2702-2704).\n2. Each harness has its OWN Corestore (corestore.ts, cached per `${workspaceRoot}::${harnessSlug}`).\n3. Each harness's connection handler calls `opts.store.replicate(socket)` on that shared socket (swarm.ts:2519).\n=> N corestores, one protomux, ONE hypercore/alpha notify slot.\n\nEVIDENCE MATRIX (the controls are what make this conclusive — only the 2nd store differs between rows 3 and 4)\n| serve stores on socket | serve-side core | attached |\n| 1 | open | PASS |\n| 2 | open | PASS (both) — eager attachAll at replicate() covers open cores, which is why this hid for so long |\n| 1 | COLD (on disk, not open) | PASS |\n| 2 | COLD (on disk, not open) | FAIL — peersCount 0 forever on a live connection |\n\nWHY IT MATCHES THE OBSERVED SYMPTOM CLASS: live connection (swarmConnections>0) yet peersCount==0; ORDER-dependent hence non-deterministic run to run; DIRECTION-selective (each side has its own pair() winner); and a handle to a core nobody serves sits at 0 forever (separately verified — fact wi-5673-lead-peerscount-requires-remote-to-serve).\n\nSCOPE / HONESTY: the MECHANISM is proven. That it is WI-5673's production trigger is NOT yet established — that needs a cold serve-side core on the real rig, which is what the EI-18726252562537043 discriminator would show in one line.\n\nCANDIDATE FIXES (not yet chosen)\n(a) ONE corestore per peer socket — a single root store with per-harness namespaces, so exactly one replicate() per socket (matches what corestore namespacing is for);\n(b) keep per-harness stores but ensure only ONE of them replicates the socket and the others attach their cores explicitly per-core x connection (the scope-cores.ts fail-closed primitive, already written and tested);\n(c) a shared multiplexing ondiscoverykey handler that consults EVERY store on the socket instead of the last one to register.\n(a) or (b) are structural; (c) is the smallest change but keeps N stores on one mux.\n\nThe characterization test currently asserts the BROKEN behaviour on purpose so the shared green gate is not red-pinned; it carries an explicit \"INVERT WHEN FIXED\" instruction.",

      "id": "WI-6140",
      "title": "RELEASE-BLOCKER: the two gates can run heavy phases concurrently — live-federation's exclusive cpuset vs green-checkpoint's new nice-10 throttle, against a 60m WALL-CLOCK reaper, is a complete path to reaping a healthy checkpoint",
      "summary": "MINE (p2p-release lane leader). Rig/gate mutual-exclusion scope. Synthesized 2026-07-26 from three independently-verified findings that are individually benign and jointly a live failure path.\n\nTHE CHAIN (every link verified at source by one of us, none inferred):\n1. live-federation-gate's local-matrix leg takes a cgroup-v2 EXCLUSIVE core partition (rig_frame_exclusive), evicting other work off 16-24 cores.\n2. As of ~2026-07-26 14:12 (EI-78), green-checkpoint's three heavy legs run at nice 10 + ionice best-effort 7. Verified live by su-055aef7f in a real run: 23 procs at ni=10 vs 5 at ni=0, nice propagating through pc-heavy -> npm -> vitest -> every worker fork.\n3. So the two policies compose in one bad direction: green-checkpoint is now DELIBERATELY deferential to a process that takes cores by force. Before EI-78 they competed as equals.\n4. The DBOS reaper cancels a routineFire whose CREATION time is older than 60m and that has checkpointed no DBOS step output. su-055aef7f verified this is a WALL-CLOCK CAP, not a no-output timer: the predicate is `created_at < staleRoutineFireNoOutputAt` (dbos-executor-reaper.ts ~L199) with an explicit \"Use created_at, not started_at_epoch_ms or updated_at\" (~L190), and operation_outputs is a checkpoint table that records no start row. green-checkpoint does a single runScript with no intermediate DBOS checkpoint, so it can log continuously for 90 minutes and the timer is unaffected.\n5. GREEN_CHECKPOINT_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS is 120m against that 60m reaper — the inverted invariant of WI-6112.\n\nRESULT: gate takes exclusive cores -> concurrent green-checkpoint starves -> suite leg stretches past 60m wall-clock -> reaper cancels it as stale -> presents as an infra flake / \"green-checkpoint mysteriously wedged\". That is the 2026-06-29 \"reaper kills a healthy checkpoint\" incident shape, reachable by a route that did not exist this morning.\n\nWHY IT IS LIVE NOW AND WAS NOT BEFORE — I re-armed it myself, disclosed:\nThe hazard was MASKED for the last several hours because the live-federation gate was NOT actually taking exclusive cores: its own gate-cycle probe detected its own parent process and degraded every run to affinity-only (WI-6133, the self-detection bug I fixed this wake). My fix correctly restores the exclusive partition for the gate's own local-matrix leg — which is the right measurement condition and must NOT be reverted — but it means link 1 of this chain is active again on the next full cycle. su-055aef7f flagged the interaction as theoretical before knowing this; it is no longer theoretical.\n\nDURABLE FIX (this item): the two gates must not run heavy phases CONCURRENTLY. Correct scope is the rig-flock / gate-singleton layer, not either gate's internals. Candidate: green-checkpoint takes a shared lock on the same resource local-matrix takes exclusively, or a registered named resource lock both honour. Explicitly NOT the fix: reverting EI-78's throttle (its measurement stands — 395s vs 707s unthrottled median, and it is a different pipeline from WI-6133), and NOT raising LOAD_GATE (owner decision D-003, 2026-07-17: the durable fix for the load path is isolation).\n\nSEQUENCING: WI-6112 first — raising the reaper above the suite budget breaks the LAST link and is the cheap mitigation. This item removes the FIRST link and is the durable fix.\n\nDETECTORS to add with the fix (su-055aef7f's, and they are the right two): a green-checkpoint suite leg falling outside the 274-2773s baseline band, AND correlating in time with a local-matrix run.\n\nCONTEXT: over the last 24h the live-federation gate is 14 RED and ~10 SKIPPED (e.g. 14:41 today: \"GATE: SKIPPED (load 165.71 > 108)\"), so the pipeline is currently neither verifying nor reporting reliably. attestation_unattested_device also fails in all 4 recent runs and is the standing long-pole for gate-first-green (WI-5137 / P-402) independent of everything above.",

      "id": "WI-6186",
      "title": "vm-federation.sh step 9 cannot handle a from-repo response of {existing:…} — every RE-RUN against the same repo hard-fails with \"A from-repo create failed\"",
      "summary": "Surfaced on WI-760 once the two boot blockers (WI-6176, WI-6180) were fixed and\nthe 2-VM rig reached step 9 for the first time.\n\nPOST /api/harness/pots/from-repo is IDEMPOTENT: when a hive for the repo already\nexists it returns `{ok:true, existing:{…}}` instead of `{ok:true, created:{…}}`.\nbin/vm-federation.sh:394-403 only ever indexes `d['created']`:\n\n    HIVE_SLUG=\"$(fed_json \"$a_resp\" \"d['created'].get('potSlug') or d['created'].get('hiveSlug') or ''\")\"\n    MEMBER_SLUG=\"$(fed_json \"$a_resp\" \"d['created']['memberSlug']\")\"\n\nso both come back empty and the driver exits 6 \"✗ A from-repo create failed\"\neven though the call SUCCEEDED (ok:true).\n\nACTUAL RESPONSE SHAPE, read live off fed-a (the driver truncates the body to 400\nchars with `head -c 400`, which is why the log never showed this):\n\n    TOP KEYS: ['ok', 'existing']\n      existing KEYS: ['kind', 'coords', 'hive', 'source', 'bindingUnverified']\n        kind = hive\n        source = cupboard\n        bindingUnverified = False\n        coords KEYS: ['owner','repo','githubRepositoryId','private','identityResolved']\n        hive  KEYS: ['potId','title','ownerGithubLogin','hivePubkey','memberLinks','claimStatus']\n\nNOTE THE REAL DIFFICULTY: `existing.hive` carries potId (\"octocat/Hello-World\"),\nhivePubkey and memberLinks — but NO `memberSlug`, and potId is a repo coordinate,\nnot the pot slug the driver needs. So this is not a one-line `.get('created') or\n.get('existing')`: the member harness slug has to be resolved separately (e.g.\nfrom harness_shared.pot_members on A, or from the directory row) before steps\n11-12's merge probes can seed a write on A's member harness.\n\nIMPACT: the default repo is the fixed https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World, so\nthe FIRST run on a machine creates the hive and every SUBSEQUENT run against that\nrepo fails at step 9 — the rig is effectively single-use per repo. Combined with\nWI-6180 (which meant no run ever REACHED step 9), this has been latent.\n\nWORKAROUND IN USE meanwhile (explicitly a workaround, not the fix): set\nPAPERCUSP_FED_REPO_URL to a repo with no existing hive so the create genuinely\ncreates. That is what I am doing to unblock WI-760's drop/re-peer verification —\nit does not resolve this item.\n\nFIX: accept the `existing` shape and resolve potSlug + memberSlug for it, so a\nre-run is a supported path rather than a hard fail. Also stop truncating the body\nto 400 chars on the FAILURE branch — the truncation actively hid the shape here.",

      "summary": "FOUND DURING WI-760 (2-VM federation rig). The driver's discover/join leg (bin/vm-federation.sh ~L406-427) polls B's /api/discovery/pots for memberLinks and, on a miss, FALLS BACK to `fed_hive_dir_row a \"$HIVE_SLUG\"` — A's own listing. That fallback is structurally impossible to satisfy.\n\nWHY: /api/discovery/pots -> buildHiveDirectoryRows (packages/operator-core/lib/discovery-hive-rows.ts) returns ONLY (a) getHiveDirectory().listDiscoveredHives() — pots learned over the wire from OTHER peers — plus (b) joined REMOTE pots (project.remote_hive === true).       "id": "WI-6216",
      "title": "Federated pot harness ingests into TWO different local workspaces on the same node (papercusp-workspace/spoon-knife AND workspace-b31a7a01/spoon-knife on fed-b)",
      "summary": "Found while root-causing WI-6209 on the fed-a/fed-b federation rig (isolated DHT, both VMs on identical bundle e3d05f765ee4).\n\n## Observation\nfed-b holds the SAME remote pot harness under two different local workspace_ids:\n\n    workspace_id         | harness_slug        | origin | count\n    papercusp-workspace  | spoon-knife         | remote |     1   <-- leaked into the PLATFORM workspace\n    workspace-b31a7a01   | spoon-knife         | remote |     4   <-- the correct local pot workspace\n\nBoth are BOOTED substrate bindings (GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status on fed-b lists\npapercusp-workspace/spoon-knife as a live binding).\n\nfed-a shows no equivalent split — it has only workspace-319be5e5/spoon-knife.\n\n## Why this looks wrong\n`papercusp-workspace` is fed-b's OWN platform workspace (it is where the `papercusp` pot lives). A remote\npeer pot's harness replicating INTO the local platform workspace crosses a tenant boundary: every\nmulti-tenant table here keys on (workspace_id, harness_slug), so a row landing under the wrong workspace is\nexactly the mis-scoping hazard documented in\n/internal/docs/agent-insights/raw-sql-plan-slug-needs-workspace-harness-scope.\n\nConsequence observed directly: the 5 rows fed-a wrote to its spoon-knife harness arrived on fed-b SPLIT across\nthe two workspaces (4 + 1), so neither workspace holds the complete set. A reader scoped to either workspace\nsees a silently-partial view of the harness.\n\n## Evidence\n- fed-b: SELECT workspace_id, harness_slug, coalesce(origin,'local'), count(*) FROM harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated GROUP BY 1,2,3\n- fed-b: GET /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-status -> booted includes BOTH papercusp-workspace/spoon-knife and workspace-b31a7a01/spoon-knife\n- pot identity is shared: harness_shared.pots.public_key = 2006cba7cd231fd4dd5085e6ee81f1a674b59aac5cf6c85623f0e1f6a8872b14 on BOTH VMs\n\n## Status\nUNCONFIRMED as to root cause — I have not traced which admit/bind path chose papercusp-workspace. Filed so the\nobservation is not lost; not blocking WI-6209 (which is resolved by the build fix, and whose bidirectional\nreplication verifies healthy against the workspace-b31a7a01 binding).",

      "id": "WI-6335",
      "title": "ALL THREE squid egress proxies are DEAD (TCP timeout) — gateway was in proxy-pool mode routing ~half of all upstream attempts into a 12s timeout, surfacing as 529/overloaded to every gateway-routed session",
      "summary": "Owner-reported 2026-07-27: \"529 error in any new sessions I start even though prior sessions continue working.\"\n\n## MEASURED: every egress proxy is down\n```\n199.182.115.224:3128  http=000 t=12.0s   TCP-REFUSED/TIMEOUT\n209.163.116.244:3128  http=000 t=12.0s   TCP-REFUSED/TIMEOUT\n216.213.24.64:3128    http=000 t=12.0s   TCP-REFUSED/TIMEOUT\n```\nRaw `</dev/tcp/<ip>/3128` times out on all three. Meanwhile the BOX's own egress is healthy: a direct `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` from the box returned **401 in 0.13s** — a real round-trip rejected only for missing auth, so the box IP is NOT edge-blocked at the transport level right now.\n\n## Why it produced 529s\nEvery claude account's `egressPool` is `[{proxyUrl: <dead squid>}, {}]` — a proxy entry plus a box-direct entry. `pickEgress()` round-robins across them, so roughly HALF of all upstream attempts were dialing a dead proxy and burning a 12s transport timeout before failing. The gateway surfaced that as:\n```\ngateway 503: {\"type\":\"overloaded_error\",\n  \"message\":\"inference-gateway: egress proxy transport error on 'aviynw'; retry shortly\"}\n```\nObserved live in the oddsmith live-loop. Intermittent-by-design (round-robin), which is why it hit NEW sessions hardest — a session's first call has ~50% odds of landing on the dead leg — while long-running sessions that had already succeeded kept going.\n\nAccount state before the fix: 3 of 4 claude accounts `available:false`; `aviynw` edgeThrottled with penaltyCount 17; `aviynw10` penaltyCount 19; `avistorewolf.com` penaltyCount 26. Those penalties were being manufactured by the dead-proxy timeouts, not by real upstream limiting.\n\n## MITIGATION APPLIED (not a fix)\nFlipped the purpose-built, live, reversible kill-switch (egress-proxy-toggle-2026-06-30):\n```\nPOST http://127.0.0.1:8788/admin/egress-mode?proxy=off\n-> {\"ok\":true,\"proxyEgressDisabled\":true,\"mode\":\"box-ip-only\"}\n```\n`effectiveEgressEntries()` then filters out every `proxyUrl` entry, so all accounts egress via the box IP (always reachable by design).\n\nImmediate measured effect: `aviynw` went `available:false -> true`, `edgeThrottled:true -> false`, `edgeThrottleBare429Streak:2 -> 0`; `sustainedlyLimited` cleared on `avistorewolf.com` and `aviynw10` (penaltyCount 26->2 and 19->2).\n\n⚠ THIS IS A TEMPORARY MITIGATION, not the durable fix. Two reasons:\n1. The proxies are still dead — nothing has been repaired.\n2. Box-IP-only is the exact condition the proxy pool exists to escape. Within a minute of the flip, `avistorewolf.com` and `aviynw10` began accruing fresh bare-429 streaks (5 and 7) on the box IP — the Cloudflare per-IP edge throttle, under the load of ~51 live gateway-routed sessions. `aviynw`'s own label records this history: \"box IP CF-throttled; penalties were edge-429s, 2026-07-06\".\n\nSo this trades a hard transport failure for a per-IP edge-throttle ceiling. Better, but it will degrade under fleet load.\n\n## Durable fix needed\n- Restore the squid egress proxies (they are EXTERNAL hosts — three public IPs; nothing in this repo provisions them, so this likely needs the owner: provider outage, expiry, billing, or firewall). Then flip `?proxy=on`.\n- Independently: the gateway should NOT keep round-robining onto an egress that is hard-down. A dead proxy should be cooled and DROPPED from rotation quickly (the per-IP cooldown exists — `IP_TRANSPORT_COOLDOWN_MS` / `PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_EGRESS_CIRCUIT_MS=90000` — but a 90s circuit against a permanently-dead host still readmits it every 90s, re-inflicting a 12s timeout on whichever request draws it). Consider escalating the per-IP cooldown on repeated transport failure (like the bare-429 escalation already does) so a dead proxy backs off toward \"effectively removed\" instead of being retried forever at a fixed interval.\n- Add a health signal: nothing alerted that all three proxies were down. `accounts:status` showed the SYMPTOM (accounts unavailable) but not the CAUSE.\n\n## NOT the cause — checked and cleared\n`--account default` still correctly SKIPS the gateway. Verified three ways: (1) `resolveAccountPin` returns no gateway env for ''/default/none/system; (2) the launcher's `accountRoutingMode()` mirrors it; (3) LIVE env of running sessions — every recent default session, including the su session doing this investigation, has `PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ROUTING_MODE=default` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9073` (the transparent cache proxy, which forwards to api.anthropic.com directly, NOT to :8788). Route split across live procs: 51 on :8788, 8 on :9073. The cache proxy is healthy: 76,913 requests / 83 upstream errors (0.1%), up since Jul 19 with 0 restarts.",

      "id": "WI-6561",
      "title": "Verify the WI-6522 coord:send fix against live traffic (~24h post-deploy soak) — difference-in-differences, and do NOT count the old signatures",
      "summary": "FOLLOW-UP to WI-6522, covering exactly what that item deliberately left undone: its step 3 (\"re-measure afterwards — this bug carries its own before-numbers, so the fix is verifiable rather than asserted\"). Split out so the verification sits in the CLAIMABLE QUEUE with a real trigger, rather than surviving as a paragraph attached to a closed item. WI-6522's code half is done, verified and committed; this is the verification half. Filed by su-bf586921 at the direction of su-8d9a671c.\n\nPREREQUISITE: the fix must be DEPLOYED, plus ~24h of soak. Check with dev:pipeline_position { path: 'packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/send.ts', marker: 'STRING \"true\" is NOT the boolean true' } — proceed only when positions.deployed is true, and record the deploy timestamp as DEPLOY_TS. At ~380 coord:send calls/day, a window shorter than ~24h has no statistical power; the retry-success metric wants longer.\n\n════ ⚠ READ FIRST — THE OBVIOUS METRIC IS WRONG, AND IT FAILS IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION ════\n\nThe WI-6522 fix changed REFUSAL TEXT. It did NOT change what the schema ACCEPTS. A caller who forgets `summary` is still refused — they are now merely TOLD it is `summary`.\n\nSo if you re-run the original query and count the old strings, both fixed signatures collapse toward zero. THAT IS A TAUTOLOGY OF THE STRINGS HAVING CHANGED, NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. Reporting it as a ~95% reduction would be a fabricated success, and it is exactly the shape of result that gets believed. Do not do it.\n\nBASELINE (pre-fix, captured 2026-07-28T04:12Z by su-bf586921, deployed sha then 3b51a647; 14-day window; NOT scoped by workspace_id/harness_slug — deliberately, to reproduce the bug's original measurement; scope BOTH sides identically if you change that):\n  OK                                4,786 calls / 450 distinct senders\n  A: {to,summary} menu   (TREATED)    344 calls / 137 distinct senders\n  B: wake \"Invalid input\"(TREATED)    196 calls /  80 distinct senders\n  C: expects             (CONTROL)     19 calls /  15 distinct senders\n  D: other                              6 calls /   6 distinct senders\n  non-ok = 565 / 5,351 = 10.6% failure rate. A+B = 540/565 = 95.6% of failures.\n\n════ DESIGN: DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES, USING C AS A FREE CONTROL ════\n\nA plain before/after on one population inherits every confound that moves between windows — fleet composition, a model change, a new agent onboarding and fumbling coord:send, a traffic-mix shift. A drop from 10.6% to 8% could be the fix or could be three chatty agents going offline, and you could not tell.\n\nSignature C (`expects`) is the control: its refusal text ALREADY named its accepted values before this fix and was NOT touched by it. C being ~11x rarer than B is the very evidence the bug rests on. So measure A+B (text became actionable) AND C (text unchanged) across the SAME two windows:\n  · A+B retry-success RISES while C stays flat  -> the fix did it.\n  · BOTH rise                                   -> something environmental moved; the effect is NOT yours.\n  · NEITHER moves                               -> the hypothesis is wrong. A real finding, to be reported as such, not buried.\nCAVEAT (su-8d9a671c, preserve it): C is small (19 events / 15 senders), so as a control it is noisy and may not reach significance on 24h. Treat a flat C as WEAK confirmation, never proof — but a C moving IN STEP with A+B is STRONG disconfirmation even at that N. That asymmetry is worth having for free.\n\n════ EXACT SQL — CROSS-ERA CLASSIFIER (matches BOTH old and new wording) ════\n\nClassify by FAMILY, never by the old literal string:\n  CASE\n    WHEN status = 'ok' THEN 'OK'\n    WHEN error_message ILIKE '%for many distinct messages%'\n      OR error_message ILIKE '%needs `summary`%'\n      OR error_message ILIKE '%needs `to`%'\n      OR error_message ILIKE '%`items` is an EMPTY array%'  THEN 'A: single-send shape (TREATED)'\n    WHEN error_message ILIKE '%wake%Invalid input%'\n      OR error_message ILIKE '%`wake` accepts%'             THEN 'B: wake (TREATED)'\n    WHEN error_message ILIKE '%needs `expects`%'            THEN 'C: expects (CONTROL)'\n    ELSE 'D: other'\n  END AS sig\n\nQ1 — overall failure rate (once per window):\n  SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status='ok') AS ok,\n         count(*) FILTER (WHERE status<>'ok') AS non_ok,\n         round(100.0*count(*) FILTER (WHERE status<>'ok')/nullif(count(*),0),2) AS non_ok_pct\n  FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations\n  WHERE tool_name='coord:send' AND invoked_at >= :ws AND invoked_at < :we;\n\nQ2 — per-signature volume + breadth (once per window), using the CASE above:\n  SELECT sig, count(*) AS calls, count(DISTINCT coord_owner_id) AS distinct_senders\n  FROM (SELECT status, error_message, coord_owner_id, <CASE> AS sig\n        FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations\n        WHERE tool_name='coord:send' AND invoked_at >= :ws AND invoked_at < :we) t\n  GROUP BY sig ORDER BY calls DESC;\n\nQ3 — THE PRIMARY METRIC: retry-success per signature.\n  WITH calls AS (\n    SELECT id, coord_owner_id, invoked_at, status, error_message, <CASE> AS sig\n    FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations\n    WHERE tool_name='coord:send' AND coord_owner_id IS NOT NULL\n      AND invoked_at >= :ws AND invoked_at < :we\n  ), seq AS (\n    SELECT *, lead(status)     OVER (PARTITION BY coord_owner_id ORDER BY invoked_at) AS next_status,\n              lead(invoked_at) OVER (PARTITION BY coord_owner_id ORDER BY invoked_at) AS next_at\n    FROM calls\n  )\n  SELECT sig,\n    count(*) AS refusals,\n    count(*) FILTER (WHERE next_at IS NOT NULL AND next_at <= invoked_at + interval '10 minutes') AS with_retry,\n    count(*) FILTER (WHERE next_at <= invoked_at + interval '10 minutes' AND next_status='ok') AS corrected,\n    round(100.0*count(*) FILTER (WHERE next_at <= invoked_at + interval '10 minutes' AND next_status='ok')\n          /nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE next_at IS NOT NULL AND next_at <= invoked_at + interval '10 minutes'),0),1) AS retry_success_pct\n  FROM seq WHERE sig <> 'OK' GROUP BY sig ORDER BY refusals DESC;\n\nRETRY DEFINITION — STATE IT, DO NOT RE-INVENT IT (su-8d9a671c): \"corrects on the next call\" is only computable with a bound. The rule is the same sender's NEXT coord:send WITHIN 10 MINUTES. A next call later than that is neither a retry nor a repeat-failure and DROPS OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR (that is what `with_retry` counts). A different bound gives a different answer — say which you used.\n\nWINDOWING: never \"last 14 days\" post-deploy — that MIXES pre- and post-fix traffic and washes the effect out. Use two equal-length windows either side of DEPLOY_TS: pre = [DEPLOY_TS - 24h, DEPLOY_TS), post = [DEPLOY_TS, DEPLOY_TS + 24h).\n\nREPORT: the DiD table (A+B vs C, pre vs post, retry_success_pct), the overall non-ok rate for both windows, and an explicit verdict — confirmed / environmental / hypothesis-refuted. A null or negative result is a legitimate outcome and should be reported plainly; this exists to be verifiable, not to be vindicated. Then link the result back to WI-6522 to close its verification debt.",

    {
      "id": "WI-6821",
      "title": "OWNER-REPORTED 2026-08-02: HUD \"+ new session\" popup sits on \"Starting up — waiting for this session to come online…\" — the launch dies and NOTHING ever marks it failed, so the roster advertises a dead launch as \"starting\" indefinitely",
      "summary": "Owner report (verbatim, 2026-08-02 ~02:26Z): \"clicking new session is still showing 'Starting up — waiting for this session to come online…' in the popup that comes up\"\n\n== TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS. The second one is the one the owner SEES, and it is fixable independently of the first. ==\n\n--- DEFECT B (the reporting lie — MINE TO FIX, do this one first) ---\nWhen a terminal launch dies, `harness_shared.adv_sessions.ended_at` / `exit_code` are NEVER stamped. `listStartingTerminalLaunches` (packages/operator-core/lib/adv-sessions.ts:314) selects on `display = DISPLAY_TERMINAL_LAUNCH AND ended_at IS NULL AND started_at > now() - STARTING_LAUNCH_WINDOW_SEC`, so a launch that died 3 seconds in stays in the roster's `starting` tier for the WHOLE window. SessionChatModal's `startingUp` (SessionChatModal.tsx:641) is fed by exactly that tier, so the popup says \"Starting up — waiting for this session to come online…\".\n\n⚠ A DEAD LAUNCH AND A STILL-BOOTING LAUNCH ARE CURRENTLY INDISTINGUISHABLE. The 60s `STARTUP_GRACE_MS` fallback is the only thing that ever corrects the copy, and it is a client-side timer, not an observation — nothing ever reconciles the ROW. This is the same class of fabricated-diagnosis bug as WI-6745 (the launch banner that blamed the user for an unreachable DB), just in the hopeful direction.\n\nVERIFIED EVIDENCE (row 14444, the owner's 22:25:08 click):\n  argv  [\"/home/marsh-office/.local/bin/psu\",\"--no-picker\",\"--agent=claude\",\"--owner-id=su-f4093966-0b57-4be7-86a3-d07911e0aad2\",\"--no-plan\",\"--account=default\"]\n  terminal_bin gnome-terminal · display 'terminal' · pid 3267523\n  pid 3267523 GONE by 02:28Z · session_id NULL · ended_at NULL · exit_code NULL\n  coord:presence → sessionState 'recorded', source 'session-log', lastActiveSecAgo null — it NEVER came online.\nNot a one-off: row 14434 (15:59:52, su-6d7e0b74) is the only other `display='terminal'` launch in 48h and failed identically.\n\n--- DEFECT A (the launch death — root cause NOT yet established) ---\nThe launch genuinely dies before registering. I could NOT reproduce the death; every path I drove works:\n  1. `gnome-terminal --wait --window -- bash -c '<harmless>'` with DISPLAY/DBUS/XAUTHORITY taken from the live gnome-terminal-server (pid 2039560) → window opened, command ran. Terminal spawning is HEALTHY.\n  2. psu-launcher.mjs with the owner's EXACT argv + a stub `claude` on PATH → ran clean end-to-end, reached the agent exec. `node --check` + import clean. psu is HEALTHY. (Flags all supported; `--harness` is NOT required — selectionsFromArgs falls back to server defaults, only `--agent` throws.)\n  3. Real psu, owner's exact argv shape, in a real gnome-terminal under `script` (PTY preserved), owner-id su-PROBE3-f49eb-diag → came up **sessionState 'live'** and stayed up 70s. THE OWNER'S ARGV SHAPE WORKS.\n  4. `capability:launch-agent` (the same `launchAgent` entry point NewSessionLauncher.tsx:32 calls) via the :3070 operator → gnome-terminal pid 3595742 still alive after 25s.\n\n⚠⚠ FALSE LEAD — DO NOT REPEAT IT. My first repro wrapped the command in `exec > >(tee …)` and produced:\n    \"Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print\"  (psu exit 1)\nThat is an ARTIFACT OF THE HARNESS, not the bug: claude switches to --print mode when stdout is not a TTY, then errors for want of a prompt. Re-running under `script -q -e -c` (real PTY) the SAME command stayed alive. Any repro of this item MUST preserve a PTY or it manufactures this error.\n(It is still worth checking whether the desktop sidecar's spawn hands the child a non-TTY stdio — that would produce this exact instant-exit for real. console-spawn.ts:1252-1254 shows the headless path deliberately compensates via usePtyHost + PAPERCUSP_PSU_HEADLESS=1; confirm the TERMINAL path cannot land in the same non-TTY state.)\n\nKEY REMAINING LEAD: the owner's click goes through their Tauri desktop app's OWN sidecar operator, NOT :3070 — nothing appears in papercup-dev-api/papercup-staging-api logs for 22:24:30–22:27:00. That sidecar is a different process with a different env. Note :3270's listener (pid 3529191) started 22:33:46, i.e. the sidecar restarted ~8min AFTER this launch — a restart reaps spawned children (EI-9748 class), but it does NOT explain THIS instance, because the pid was already gone at 02:28Z, before that restart. Do not assert the restart as the cause without evidence of an earlier one.\n\n== NEXT ACTIONS ==\n1. Fix DEFECT B: reconcile the row. A launch whose recorded pid is gone and which never registered must be stamped ended (with a reason) so the roster stops advertising it and the popup can say what actually happened instead of \"waiting\". `gnome-terminal --wait` means the recorded pid IS a valid liveness handle for the window's lifetime — that is the observation to reconcile against, not a timer.\n2. For DEFECT A: capture the desktop sidecar's own stderr around a failing click, and confirm the terminal path's child stdio is a PTY.\n3. Owner question outstanding: does a terminal window flash open and close on click, or does nothing visible happen at all? That single answer splits \"spawned and died\" from \"never spawned\".",

      "id": "WI-6936",
      "title": "FLEET-WIDE OUTAGE: all 3 egress forward-proxies are dead (TCP connect timeout), collapsing every claude account onto the box's Cloudflare-throttled IP — usableAccounts:0, and every fresh agent spawn dies on its first inference call",
      "summary": "## Verified evidence (2026-08-02T05:32Z)\n\nDirect curl through each owner-provisioned proxy TIMES OUT on TCP connect, while direct egress from the box is healthy:\n\n```\n199.182.115.224:3128   http=000 curl_rc=28   (timeout)\n209.163.116.244:3128   http=000 curl_rc=28   (timeout)\n216.213.24.64:3128     http=000 curl_rc=28   (timeout)\ndirect (box IP)        http=405 curl_rc=0    (expected: GET on /v1/messages)\n```\n\n`http=405` direct proves the box has working internet + DNS + TLS to api.anthropic.com. The proxies themselves are unreachable.\n\n## Blast radius\n\nWith no proxy, all 4 claude accounts egress from ONE shared box IP that Cloudflare has rate-limited:\n\n- `accounts:status`: 4/4 claude accounts `edgeThrottled:true`. aviynw `usageWalled:true`+`sustainedlyLimited`; aviynw10 `sustainedlyLimited`, penaltyCount 12; avistorewolf.com + aviynw3 rate-paused with `edgeThrottleBare429Streak` 0 and 4.\n- `fleet:capacity`: `usableAccounts:0`, `poolExhausted:true`, `factor:0`, `healthyAccounts:1`, queueDepth 13. Its own advice names the cause: \"4/4 edge-throttled (a live per-IP/Cloudflare bare-429 cooldown, NOT account quota) ... the egress path itself is broken (a down/unreachable forward-proxy forcing accounts onto one shared, already-throttled IP)\".\n- `dev:rate_governor_status`: liveAgents 130 against an admission `maxConcurrent` of 4.\n\n## Confirmed downstream failure — silent spawn death\n\n`fleet:respawn-member` on su-00cb5bbb returned **ok:true** with a launched pid, and the launcher genuinely ran (it assembled and wrote the 92KB launch prompt `~/.papercusp/launch-context/session-14457.md` at 05:20Z). But the CLI died before taking a single turn: terminal pid 101775 is now `/bin/bash -l` with no children and no `claude`/`psu-launcher` descendant — the wrapper script's `exec \"$SHELL\" -l` fallthrough. The fleet roster shows the member as never having joined; p2p-release is down to 1 live member (the leader) with 19 unowned criticals and 158 claimable.\n\nThis is `fleet:capacity`'s \"fresh spawns will die on their first call\", observed live.\n\n## Fix\n\nOwner-gated: the egress proxies are owner-provisioned infra. Restore/replace the three squid endpoints (or provision new ones via `egress:provision`), then `gateway:reload` and confirm `fleet:capacity` reports `usableAccounts > 0` and `poolExhausted:false` before resuming any placement.\n\n## Secondary defect worth fixing separately\n\n`fleet:respawn-member` reports `ok:true` on a launch that produced no agent. It should verify the replacement actually joined (a session row / first tool call) before reporting success, or at minimum consult `fleet:capacity` and refuse-with-reason when `poolExhausted:true`. As it stands a leader gets a false success and only discovers the truth by hand-inspecting the process tree.",

      "id": "WI-8848",
      "title": "connect-phase-deadline is PER-POOL slot starvation on a healthy server — measured at a real failure instant; the both-causes fix is COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED, so the fleet still reads the old single-cause text",
      "summary": "## CORRECTION TO MY OWN FILING (made minutes after filing it)\nI first titled this \"the error string asserts a cause measurement falsifies\". That is TRUE of the\nDEPLOYED binary and FALSE of the tree. libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/connect-retry.ts at HEAD already\nsays \"Two causes present identically here, so check both: (a) ... DEAD or unreachable ... (b) the\nCLIENT pool is saturated while the endpoint is perfectly healthy\". I derived the defect from the\nerror text I RECEIVED, which is the old pre-10479ae8 string still running on :3070. Verify against\nthe TREE, not the running system. The remaining defect is a DEPLOYMENT gap, not a code gap.\n\n## WHAT IS ACTUALLY MEASURED AND NEW (this is the contribution)\nAt a real failure instant (~16:38Z, my own dev:pg_query died on the 45s deadline) I captured the\nserver-side correlation nobody had. su-3a5df explicitly flagged it as undetermined:\n\"what pool in-use/waiting was at each failure instant\" — they could not answer it; this does.\n\nBOTH of the causes the error names are FALSIFIED for this instant:\n  (a) DEAD ENDPOINT — ruled out. ~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json -> postgresql://...@localhost:5432,\n      127.0.0.1:5432 IS listening, and I queried successfully through it seconds later.\n  (b) SERVER exhaustion — ruled out. 307/512 conns (205 FREE), active=32, idle-in-txn=14\n      (oldest 14.3s), active-Lock waits=21 (oldest 0.6s).\n\nTHE SUPPORTED MECHANISM IS A THIRD ONE: PER-POOL starvation on an IDLE server.\nConnections are concentrated per PROCESS, and the pools are wildly uneven:\n  pcusp:org-app:p1993413    50 conns,  0 active (hoarding), oldest 56.2s\n  pcusp:org-admin:p1275480  40 conns, 14 active,            oldest 95.1s\n  the :3070 pools my calls ride (p623*):  only 5-10 conns EACH\nA 5-10 slot pool is emptied by a handful of slow queries. Measured slot-hogs\n(pg_stat_statements, papercusp db, 24.5d window):\n  coord_event_log \"WITH directed AS ...\"  11,737 calls  mean 21,822ms  MAX 62,204ms      71.1h\n  tool_invocations adoption (variant 1)    1,341 calls  mean 38,601ms  MAX 3,348,389ms   14.4h  (55.8 MINUTES)\n  tool_invocations adoption (variant 2)   15,773 calls  mean  8,742ms  MAX 28,348ms      38.3h\n  plans read                               1.87M calls  mean    297ms                   154.3h  (#1 by total time)\npostgres-js retries connect forever when connect_timeout is unset, so a caller waiting on a FULL\npool waits until the 45s wrapper fires. This reproduces EVERY observed symptom: a healthy server,\nsome calls fine and others dead, reads AND writes hit, and the non-determinism where a write\nCOMMITS and still errors (handler commits on pool A, a later acquisition on starved pool B\ndeadlines) — which is precisely the multi-connection case the committed message fix warns about.\n\n## DISCONFIRMING PROBE — NOT YET RUN, so treat the mechanism as a hypothesis\nAt a failure instant, snapshot pg_stat_activity filtered to the FAILING process's own\napplication_name and show ITS slots all held. I have the server-wide snapshot, not the per-pool\none for the exact failing pool. If that pool shows free slots at the instant, this is WRONG.\n\n## BURSTINESS CORRECTION (engineer_issues, for WI-6993)\nsu-3a5df measured 1,648 calls/min (37.4% of a core) at 16:31Z; I measured 54 calls/min (1.1%) at\n16:37Z, same regex, same single database (per-dbid split confirms engineer_issues real-FROM reads\nexist in exactly ONE db, so it is NOT a scoping artifact). The since-stats_reset average over\n35,244 minutes (24.5 days) is 477 calls/min and 50.7% of one core = 297.96h = 12.2 core-hours/day.\nSo the load swings ~30x within six minutes: NEITHER spot sample is \"the rate\". su-3a5df's\nCONCLUSION stands and is understated (12.2 core-h/day vs their ~9); only their number was a burst.\n\n## NEXT LEVER\nThe both-causes fix (10479ae8, in the libs/papercusp SUBMODULE) is committed and NOT deployed;\nevery agent still reads the old single-cause text. Deployment is the fix that helps the fleet now.",

      "id": "WI-953",
      "title": "Shared-hive DIRECTORY ANNOUNCE never reaches the joiner — peers connect but published-hive announce doesn't land in joiner's /api/discovery/hives (no discover→join→content)",
      "summary": "The consistent core blocker behind \"shared hive content doesn't federate\" across BOTH the 2-VM rig and the canonical host smoke (see shared-hive-member-content-federation-2026-06-20 D-024/D-025). The content-APPLY code is proven correct (faithful 2-boot hermetic repro passes). The failure is UPSTREAM at the directory-announce/peering layer:\n\nSYMPTOMS (live, su 2026-06-29):\n- VM rig: fed-b shows peer_connected for the hive topic but ZERO [A-003] slug-filter lines → it processes no peer ANNOUNCE → never admits the owner's home core → 0 content.\n- Host smoke (two-instance-content-matrix, ISOLATED testnet DHT, 128 cores/no load): owner A create+publish hello-world-hive announced=True, but joiner B's /api/discovery/hives stays count=0 (\"rows=0 after 40 tries\") → join fails (no hiveId) → no content.\n\nWHAT'S RULED OUT: apply guard/merge (hermetic green); load (0.21/core); identity (device key 5cWxDY present+correct); admission gist gate (WI-797 fixed). Membership rows that DID federate are days-stale (persisted), not live.\n\nLIKELY CONTRIBUTORS / NEXT STEPS:\n1. Same-host NAT hairpin on the persistent fed VMs (public DHT) — they don't directly peer; a local testnet DHT (PAPERCUSP_DHT_BOOTSTRAP) is required and was never configured on those VMs.\n2. Host smoke on this dev box isn't truly isolated: the \"fresh\" instances inherited the host workspace's hives (B joined oddsmith/hive-canary/team-offsite topics) → host-operator swarm pollution; A peers a 3rd node (the host op, serves oddsmith) instead of B.\n3. The directory-announce processing itself: even when peers connect, the published-hive descriptor doesn't propagate into the joiner's hive_directory_cache / /api/discovery/hives. Trace whether the joiner JOINS the hive-DIRECTORY topic, peers the OWNER on it, RECEIVES the verifyHiveAnnounce descriptor, and why it doesn't land.\n\nREPRO for a CLEAN signal: run on a QUIESCED box (no host operator) OR the separate-machine bin/deb-hetzner-federation.sh. Files: hive-directory-boot.ts (wireHiveDirectoryForWorkspace), read-admission.ts (decideAdmission/slug-filter), boot.ts drainAdmissionQueue, swarm.ts (bootstrap isolation). Diagnostic toolkit: agent-insights/shared-hive-federation-diagnosis-toolkit.",
